The Uṇādi numeral and the words marked [?] are clotted.

[…] पतेस्थ च । उ. ४-१०[३?] [?] । इतीनिप्रत्ययस्थकारान्तादेशश्च । जसि पथिमथ्यृभुक्षामादिति व्यत्ययेनात्त्वम् । अज्झेरसुक् । यद्वा । पन्थान इत्यत्र वर्णव्यापत्त्या [?] नकारस्य सकारः । पथिमथोः सर्वनामस्थान इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । ससहिः । षह अभिभवे । उत्सर्गश्छन्दसीति वचनाद् आदृगमहनेति किप्रत्ययः । लिड्वद्भावाद् द्विर्वचनम् ॥ […] pateṣṭha ca | U. 4-10[3?] [?] | itīnipratyayasthakārāntādeśaś ca | jasi pathimathyṛbhukṣām ād iti vyatyayenātvam | ajjhe[?]rasuk | yadvā | panthāna ity atra varṇavyāpattyā [?] nakārasya sakāraḥ | pathimathoḥ sarvanāmasthāna ity ādyudāttatvam | sasahiḥ | ṣaha abhibhave | utsargaś chandasīti vacanād ādṛgamahaneti kipratyayaḥ | liḍvadbhāvād dvirvacanam ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"yasya — of which Indra; śavasā — endowed with strength; aparītāḥ — (by enemies) not to be approached; panthāsaḥ — rays of splendour; divo na — like the rays of the shining sun (which make rain), from the sky [like the rays of the sun going out from the sky]; retasaḥ — the waters of rain; dughānāḥ — pouring; yanti — spread from the world of heaven in all directions; taraddveṣāḥ — one who overcomes such enemies, [and]; pauṃsyebhiḥ — [with his] prowess; sasahiḥ — victorious in fighting [with enemies]; marutvān — one joined with the Maruts; indraḥ — Indra; naḥ — our; ūtī — for protection; bhavatu — may [he] be."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"May Indra — whose rays of splendour, joined with strength and not to be approached by enemies, pour down the waters of rain like the rays of the shining sun, and spread from the heavenly world to every side — who overcomes such enemies, and is victorious in battle with enemies by his prowess, and who is joined with the Maruts, give us protection."

English Translation (as printed)

May he, whose rays, powerful and unattainable, issue forth like those of the sun, milking (the clouds) ; he who is victorious over is [sic] adversaries triumphant by his manly energies ; may Indra, associated with the Muruts [sic] be our protection.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.3 (Kannada)

"In explaining this Ṛk, between Sāyaṇa's bhāṣya and Skandasvāmin's bhāṣya there is a difference in the order of construction (anvayakrama) and in the explanation of the meaning, but the main intention is the same. In Sāyaṇa's bhāṣya, for the word panthāsaḥ is given 'raśmayaḥ' — 'rays'; Skandasvāmin has mārgāḥ — 'paths'" continues on p. 183

original p. 183

"[— 'paths'] and so explains. From this difference of meaning there is a difference in the construction too. As in the first explanation:

Yasya — indrasya; panthāsaḥ — raśmayaḥ, 'rays'; retasaḥ — vṛṣṭyudakāni, 'waters of rain'; dughānāḥ — pravarṣantaḥ, 'pouring'; yanti — nirgacchanti dyulokād itas tataḥ prasaranti, 'they issue forth, they spread from the heavenly world hither and thither' — that is, the sense is that they spread in all directions from the heavenly world. Divo na — 'yathā dyotamānasya sūryasya kiraṇā vṛṣṭiṃ kurvanto nabhaḥsthalān nirgacchanti tadvat': as the rays of the shining sun, making rain, go out from the sky — that is, 'as these go out from the sky and spread to all the world', this is said as a simile showing the capacity for splendour of Indra and of the sun. Then the two words śavasā and aparītāḥ are adjectives to panthāsaḥ: śavasā is 'endowed with strength', and aparītāḥ is 'not to be approached by enemies'.

According to the second explanation: 'diva iti pañcamī | na śabdaḥ upariṣṭād upacāraḥ' [as printed, the second clause doubtful [?]]: 'dyulokāt yasyendrasya balena retasaḥ vṛṣṭilakṣaṇāny udakāni | dughānāḥ kṣarantaḥ | panthāsaḥ vṛṣṭipatanamārgāḥ | yanti pṛthivīṃ prati gacchanti': by Indra's power the paths of the falling of rain go from the world of the gods towards the earth, pouring out. In this, divaḥ means 'from the world of the gods', in the fifth case; and na is understood with the sense of saṃprati — 'now', 'in the present case' — and not only as a particle of comparison. In this construction śavasā means indrasya balena, 'by Indra's strength', and aparītāḥ means vṛṣṭipratibandhakarair asurādibhir aprāptāḥ — 'not approached by the Asuras and the like that hold back the rain'; and it serves as an adjective to panthāsaḥ as well.

Retasaḥ — since ārṇaḥ, kṣodaḥ, kṣadma and the like are read among the names of water (Ni. [1-?]3 as read [?]), retasaḥ means 'rain-waters'.

Taraddveṣāḥ — dveṣāṃsi śatrūn taran jitaśatrukaḥ iti arthaḥ: one who has crossed [overcome] the enemies, the sense is, one who has conquered enemies.

Pauṃsyebhiḥ — since ojaḥ, pājaḥ and the like are read among the twenty-eight names of strength (Ni. 2-9 as read [?]), and also among the [forty-six, as read, ?] names of battle, such as raṇaḥ, vivāk, vikhādaḥ, the word has the two senses 'strength' and 'battle'. Here it means 'by strengths'; 'prowess endowed with manly capacity' is the sense. This epithet is used very often of Indra —" Glosses, editorial and tentative: "[The Maruts] tore Vṛtra limb from limb, [they scattered] the mountains, doing manly deeds, bull-like"; "Much you have done with us, with equal [companions], O bull, by your manly powers".

original p. 184

वि वृत्रं पर्वशो ययुर्वि पर्वताँ अराजिनः [as read, ?] । चक्राणा वृष्णि पौंस्यम् । vi vṛtraṃ parvaśo yayur vi parvatāṃ arājinaḥ [as read, ?] | cakrāṇā vṛṣṇi pauṃsyam | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[7?]-3[3?] as read [?])

भूरि चकर्थ युज्येभिरस्मे समानेभिर्वृषभ पौंस्येभिः । bhūri cakartha yujyebhir asme samānebhir vṛṣabha pauṃsyebhiḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-185-8 as read [?])

"— so describing Indra's deeds of valour, this epithet, which indicates capacity, shows Indra's own real power. In the same way in [Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-3[?]-3 and 6-66-3, as read [?]] and other Ṛks it is used also of the Maruts and of other deities.

Sasahiḥ — śatrūṇām abhibhavitā: one who has the power to overcome enemies; this epithet too is mostly used of Indra."

केमुत्स्नवे [?] च प्रसवे च सासहिमिन्द्रं देवासः कवसामदन्ननु [?] । kemutsnave [?] ca prasave ca sāsahim indraṃ devāsaḥ kavasāmadann anu [?] | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-103-1 as read [?]; clotted in print)

त्वां देवेषु प्रथमं हवामहे त्वं बभूथ पृतनासु सासहिः । tvāṃ deveṣu prathamaṃ havāmahe tvaṃ babhūtha pṛtanāsu sāsahiḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-102-9 as read [?])

सुप्रकेतेभिः सासहिर्दधानो [?] विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुम् । suprakete­bhiḥ sāsahir dadhāno [?] vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[2?]0-6 as read [?])

"— in such places this epithet shows Indra's capacity." Reading note: the Pada and the bhāṣya of 100.3, on p. 181, were read as sasahiḥ with a short a; the Saṃhitā, the quotations above and the grammar below all give sāsahiḥ, with the long ā. The Pada's reading is therefore doubtful [?].

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.3) grammar pages, pp. 184–185, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?]

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: divaḥ (the ending acute by ūḍidaṃpadādi [Pā. Sū. 6-1-171 as read]); retasaḥ (reta is a name of water; rīyate gacchatīti retaḥ, root rī gatireṣaṇayoḥ; asun by sphurībhyāṃ tuṭ ca [as read, Uṇ. Sū. 4-[?]10 [?]] with the augment tuṭ; guṇa of the root vowel; acute on the first syllable by ñnityādir nityam; the jas-substitute for śas by the statement supāṃ suluk…, read in the print as supāṃ suṣo bhavanti [?]); dughānāḥ (root duh prapūraṇe; śānac for laṭ in the active; luk of śap by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ; gh for h by vyatyayo bahulam [Pā. Sū. 3-1-85 as read], even though no cause for it is present; the final acute that the c-marked affix would give is replaced by the first-syllable acute, since vṛṣa etc. is an open list [ākṛtigaṇa], by vṛṣādīnāṃ ca [Pā. Sū. 6-1-203 as read]); panthāsaḥ (patanti iti panthāno raśmayaḥ; root patḷ gatau; ini by pateṣṭh ca [Uṇ. Sū. 4-[?]]; the word pathin; jas: a for i by pathimathyṛbhukṣām āt [Pā. Sū. 7-1-85 as read]; the augment asuk by ajjhaser asuk [Pā. Sū. 7-1-50 as read]; or, in the Vedic manner, n → s by letter-interchange; th → nth by tho nthaḥ [Pā. Sū. 7-1-87 as read]; s → ru → visarga; acute on the first syllable by pathimathoḥ sarvanāmasthāne [Pā. Sū. 6-1-199 as read]).

original p. 185

The grammar of Rik 100.3 continues: yanti (root iṇ gatau, adādi; laṭ, third person plural, jhi; anta by jho 'ntaḥ [Pā. Sū. 7-1-3 as read]; yaṇ for the vowel of the root before an affix beginning with a vowel, by iṇo yaṇ [Pā. Sū. 6-4-81 as read]; no nighāta, because of the relative [yad] before it; the verb being adyudātta by its affix); taraddveṣāḥ (root dviṣ aprītau; asun of the Uṇādi class; dveṣāṃsi taran yaḥ saḥ taraddveṣāḥ — the member that is the object is placed last because the compound belongs to the rājadantādi class); sasahiḥ (root ṣah abhibhave; ki by ādṛgamahanajanaḥ kikinau liṭ ca [Pā. Sū. 3-2-171 as read] by the rule utsargaś chandasi, even without a cause for it; doubling as if liṭ followed; ādihalśeṣa in the reduplicative; lengthening of the reduplicative syllable by anyeṣām api dṛśyate [Pā. Sū. 6-3-137 as read]; final acute by the affix); pauṃsyebhiḥ (puṃsaḥ bhāvaḥ pauṃsyam; ṣyañ in the sense of 'state' under the heading strīpuṃsābhyām [Pā. Sū. 4-1-87 as read]; vṛddhi by taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ; since the affix is ñit, acute on the first syllable; bhis follows, and ais does not appear because of bahulaṃ chandasi). The Rik is closed with ‖ 3 ‖ and a rule of dashes.

saḥ | aṅgiraḥ-bhiḥ | aṅgiraḥ-tamaḥ | bhūt | vṛṣā | vṛṣa-bhiḥ | sakhi-bhiḥ | sakhā | san | ṛgmi-bhiḥ | ṛgmī | gātu-bhiḥ | jyeṣṭhaḥ | marutvān | naḥ | bhavatu | indraḥ | ūtī ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.4)

स इन्द्रोऽङ्गिरोभिः । अङ्गन्ति गच्छन्तीत्यङ्गिरसो गन्तारः । तेभ्योऽप्यङ्गिरस्तमोऽभूत् । अतिशयेन गन्ता भवति । वृषभिर्वृषा वर्षित्रभ्योऽप्यतिशयेन वर्षिता । सखिभिः समानख्यानेभ्यो मित्रभूतेभ्योऽपि सखातिशयेन हितकारी । एवंभूतः सन् ऋग्मिभिरर्चनीयेभ्योऽपि ऋग्मी अर्चनीयो भवति । गातुभिर्गातव्येभ्यः स्तोतव्येभ्योऽपि ज्येष्ठोऽतिशयेन स्तोतव्यः । एवंगुणविशिष्टो मरुत्वानिन्द्रो रक्षणाय भवतु ॥ sa indro 'ṅgirobhiḥ | aṅganti gacchantīty aṅgiraso gantāraḥ | tebhyo 'py aṅgirastamo 'bhūt | atiśayena gantā bhavati | vṛṣabhir vṛṣā varṣitrabhyo 'py atiśayena varṣitā | sakhibhiḥ samānakhyānebhyo mitrabhūtebhyo 'pi sakhātiśayena hitakārī | evaṃbhūtaḥ san ṛgmibhir arcanīyebhyo 'pi ṛgmī arcanīyo bhavati | gātubhir gātavyebhyaḥ stotavyebhyo 'pi jyeṣṭho 'tiśayena stotavyaḥ | evaṃguṇaviśiṣṭo marutvān indro rakṣaṇāya bhavatu ‖

"That Indra — aṅgirobhiḥ: those who move, go (aṅganti), are aṅgirasaḥ, 'goers'; he became aṅgirastamaḥ even among them, that is, the one who is the greatest goer. Vṛṣabhiḥ vṛṣā — among the showerers, the greatest showerer. Sakhibhiḥ — among those of equal standing, who are friends, the friend who does good to the highest degree. Being such, ṛgmibhiḥ ṛgmī — he is worshipful even among the worshipful ones. Gātubhiḥ jyeṣṭhaḥ — even among those who are to be praised, to be sung, he is the most excellent, to be praised most. Indra, thus endowed, accompanied by the Maruts — may he be for our protection."

Bhāṣya's grammatical tail (characterized, partly transcribed) Characterized: the roots agi, ragi, lagi in the sense of going; aṅgirās is formed with asun by an Uṇādi rule [numeral clotted, ?], with the feminine/the word apsarās treated together [as read, ?]; ṛgmin from ṛc 'to praise', with the kvip of the class sampad and the possessive mini, the k and g by the word's status as pada; gātu from gā 'to sing' with tu by kamimanijani…. The words marked [?] are clotted.

U. 4-[?] [?] | ity auṇādiko 'sun [?] stryo [?] nipātyate | idānādiṣu sarvatra pañcamyarthe tṛtīyā [?] | ṛgmibhiḥ | ṛca stutau | sampadādilakṣaṇo bhāve kvip | matvarthīyo miniḥ | padatvāt kutvaṃ jaśtvaṃ ca | gātubhiḥ | gā stutau | kamimanijanītyādinā karmaṇi tupratyayaḥ ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"saḥ — Indra; aṅgirobhiḥ — among those who go about (swiftly); aṅgirastamaḥ — the one who goes about most swiftly; bhūt — was; vṛṣabhiḥ — among those who shower desired objects; vṛṣā — the giver who is the most generous of desired objects; sakhibhiḥ — among friends; sakhā san — being a friend (the most beneficent); ṛgmibhiḥ — among the worshipful; ṛgmī — (the most praiseworthy) the worshipful one; gātubhiḥ — among all those who deserve to be praised; jyeṣṭhaḥ — the most excellent; marutvān — together with the Maruts; indraḥ — Indra; naḥ — our; ūtī — for protection; bhavatu — may he be."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"May Indra — who among those who go swiftly goes most swiftly; among those who shower desired objects is the most generous giver of the desired; among friends is the most beneficent friend; among the worshipful is the most worshipful; and among those worthy of praise is the most excellent — together with the Maruts be for our protection."

English Translation (as printed)

He is the swiftest among the swift, most bountiful amongst the bountiful, a friend with friends, venerable among those who claim veneration, and pre-eminent among those deserving of praise : may Indra associated with the Maruts, be our protection.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.4 (Kannada)

"Aṅgirobhiḥ aṅgirastamaḥ — aṅganti gacchantīti aṅgiraso gantāraḥ, tebhyo 'py aṅgirastamaḥ — atiśayena gantā: 'among those who go about, he who goes about most swiftly' — Sāyaṇa has given this meaning. This way of explaining is also acceptable in one respect. For, in the explanation of the second Ṛk of this same sūkta, quoting Śruti sentences in praise of the speed of Indra's movement, it was shown how horses swifter than the speed of the mind carry his chariot; and the above meaning, which describes such swift movement of Indra, is also borne out from that point of view. But Skandasvāmin says:"

स इन्द्रोऽङ्गिरोभिः ऋषिभिः अङ्गिरस्तमः । सोऽयमङ्गिरोभिः सम्बन्धादङ्गिरःसम्बन्धिस्यमङ्गिरःशब्दोऽत्र द्रष्टव्यः [?] । अतिशयेन अङ्गिरसां स्तुत्यतया सम्बन्धी भवति ॥ sa indro 'ṅgirobhiḥ ṛṣibhiḥ aṅgirastamaḥ | so 'yam aṅgirobhiḥ sambandhād aṅgiraḥsambandhisyam aṅgiraḥśabdo 'tra draṣṭavyaḥ [?] | atiśayena aṅgirasāṃ stutyatayā sambandhī bhavati ‖ (Skandasvāmin, as read; the middle clause clotted [?])

"[— that is: 'among the Aṅgiras seers Indra is the most Aṅgiras'; here the word aṅgiras is to be seen as 'connected with Aṅgirases'; he is connected, to the highest degree, with the Aṅgirases by being praiseworthy.] In the first" continues on p. 188

original p. 188

"[In the first aṅgirobhiḥ] the word aṅgiras means the seers called Aṅgirases; in the second aṅgirastamaḥ the word aṅgiras is used in the sense 'he too is one [of them]' — just as, in showing an extremely close relation by identity (tādātmya), here too, because of extreme worthiness of reverence, he is said to be one very near to the Aṅgirases: thus [Skandasvāmin] has given the meaning. Who the Aṅgiras seers are, what their greatness is, and what the relation is between Agni and the Aṅgirases — all these matters were explained in the Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, part 1, pp. 641–642 [as printed in the Kannada original series]. Continuing that explanation, let us here learn what relation Indra has with the Aṅgirases; or whether Indra can be addressed as 'Aṅgiras'.

The word Aṅgiras is a title-name; it is also the name of a line of seers; and it is also the name of a group of deities; in three places this word has [separate] application.

First: the title-name Aṅgiras is used as the name of a single person, and in many places his power is described. For example —"

अङ्गिरस्वन्महिव्रत [print: …न्नमहिव्रत, ?] प्रस्कण्वस्य श्रुधी हवम् । aṅgirasvan mahivrata [print: …nnamahivrata, ?] praskaṇvasya śrudhī havam | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[4?]5-3 as read [?])

तमु त्वा वाजसातममङ्गिरस्वद्धवामहे । tam u tvā vājasātamam aṅgirasvad dhavāmahe | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[7?]8-3 as read [?])

"— in Ṛk sentences such as these, calling to mind Aṅgiras, we too ask in the same way: the request is, 'hear our prayer too'. In the same way in the Upaniṣads also Aṅgiras is a seer who knew the truth of the Self, and there is a story that he taught Śaunaka the knowledge of fire (agnividyā):"

शौनको ह वै महाशालोऽङ्गिरसं विधिवदुपसन्नः पप्रच्छ । कस्मिन्नु भगवो विज्ञाते सर्वमिदं विज्ञातं भवतीति ॥ śaunako ha vai mahāśālo 'ṅgirasaṃ vidhivad upasannaḥ papraccha | kasmin nu bhagavo vijñāte sarvam idaṃ vijñātaṃ bhavatīti ‖ (Muṇḍakopaniṣad 1-1-3 as read [?])

"— but who this human person Aṅgiras is will be explained later.

Second: it is the name of a line of seers. That the seer Aṅgiras, who was born in the very first Agni, and that lineage grew from him, is also hinted at in the Ṛksaṃhitā:"

त्वमग्ने प्रथमो अङ्गिरा ऋषिर्देवो देवानामभवः शिवः सखा । tvam agne prathamo aṅgirā ṛṣir devo devānām abhavaḥ śivaḥ sakhā | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-31-1 as read [?])

"This story is also described in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa."

original p. 189

येऽङ्गिरा आसंस्तेऽङ्गिरसोऽभवन् । ye 'ṅgirā āsaṃs te 'ṅgiraso 'bhavan | (Ai. Brā. 3-3[4?] as read [?])

"In the same way, in some other places the story is told, in the Ṛksaṃhitā and in the Brāhmaṇas, that the seers called Aṅgirases sought Agni who was hidden in a cave, found him, and gained him."

त्वामग्ने अङ्गिरसो गुहा हितमन्वविन्दञ्छिश्रियाणं वनेवने । tvām agne aṅgiraso guhā hitam anvavindañ chiśriyāṇaṃ vane-vane | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-11-6 as read [?])

"— so in the Ṛgveda; and"

समिद्भिर्हैतमङ्गिरस इन्धत । samidbhir haitam aṅgirasa indhata | (Śat. Brā. 1-4-1-[3?]5 as read [?])

"— in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa too it is described how the Aṅgirases obtained Agni and how they worshipped him. In the same way —"

अङ्गिरसो नः पितरो नवग्वा अथर्वाणो भृगवः सोम्यासः । aṅgiraso naḥ pitaro navagvā atharvāṇo bhṛgavaḥ somyāsaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-14-6 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these also the worshipful Aṅgirases are praised.

Here, since we need to know what relation Indra has with the Aṅgirases, how it grew, and how this epithet aṅgirobhiḥ aṅgirastamaḥ arises for Indra, that matter is briefly told with examples from the Śruti. In former times the seven seers named Aṅgirases went to seek the cows hidden in the cave of a mountain; and, meditating then on Indra with devotion, [it is described in the Ṛksaṃhitā how] Indra became their deity of worship:" Gloss, editorial and tentative and only in outline: "The wise seven seers pierced the firm [places], they impelled [it] forward with the mind; they found the whole path of the Law; knowing it, he entered with homage. When Saramā found the cleft of the rock, she made the great ancient way her own; she led the way of the syllables, first knowing, she went toward the sound. The wisest came, wishing friendship; the rock gave up its embryo for the good-doer. The mortal won it with the youths, [wishing for] the sacrifice, and then he became Aṅgiras, honouring at once."

वीळौ सतीरभि धीरा अतृन्दन्प्राचाहिन्वन्मनसा सप्त विप्राः । विश्वामविन्दन्पथ्यामृतस्य प्रजानन्नित्ता नमसा विवेश । विदद्यदी सरमा रुग्णमद्रेर्महि पाथः पूर्व्यं सध्र्यक्कः । अग्रं नयत्सुपद्यक्षराणामच्छा रवं प्रथमा जानती गात् । अगच्छदु विप्रतमः सखीयन्नसूदयत्सुकृते गर्भमद्रिः । ससान मर्यो युवभिर्मखस्यन्नथाभवदङ्गिराः सद्यो अर्चन् । vīḷau satīr abhi dhīrā atṛndan prācāhinvan manasā sapta viprāḥ | viśvām avindan pathyām ṛtasya prajānann ittā namasā viveśa | vidad yadī saramā rugṇam adrer mahi pāthaḥ pūrvyaṃ sadhryak kaḥ | agraṃ nayat supady akṣarāṇām acchā ravaṃ prathamā jānatī gāt | agacchad u vipratamaḥ sakhīyann asūdayat sukṛte garbham adriḥ | sasāna maryo yuvabhir makhasyann athābhavad aṅgirāḥ sadyo arcan | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-31-3 to 6 as read [?]; the print divides the lines somewhat differently, and the second and third lines are clotted in places [?])

"In the story thus described, Indra went to develop friendship with the Aṅgirases; then their friendship grew; and afterwards Indra too, becoming the chief among the Aṅgirases, when fighting" the sentence continues on p. 190

original p. 190

Special Topics of Rik 100.4, continued from p. 189 (Kannada)

"[…Indra too, becoming the chief among the Aṅgirases, when fighting] split the mountain, the cows and the waters were released: so it is described in the form of a story, that Indra stood foremost, most worthy of reverence among all the Aṅgirases. Therefore the expression aṅgirobhiḥ aṅgirastamaḥ is fitting.

Ṛgmibhiḥ ṛgmī — arcanīyebhyo 'pi arcanīyo bhavati: 'he is worshipful even among the worshipful': the sense is, the most excellent worshipful one among all those who are worthy of worship."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.4) grammar pages, pp. 190–191, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?]

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: aṅgirobhiḥ (aṅganti gacchantīti aṅgirasaḥ; the roots agi, ragi, lagi in the sense of going; the Uṇādi affix asun, fixed by the rule aṅgirā apsarāḥ [Uṇ. Sū. 4-[?]-[?] as read, ?]; the word aṅgiras; before bhis, s → ru → u with guṇa; since the affix is nit, acute on the first syllable; the instrumental in the sense of the ablative in this mantra); aṅgirastamaḥ (atiśayena aṅgirāḥ; tamap by atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau [Pā. Sū. 5-3-55 as read]; being pit, unaccented); bhūt (luṅ in the sense of the present in the Veda by chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ [Pā. Sū. 3-4-6 as read]; loss of the i of tip by itaś ca [Pā. Sū. 3-4-100 as read]; luk of sic by gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ [Pā. Sū. 2-4-77 as read]; the aṭ does not come, by bahulaṃ chandasy māṅyoge 'pi [Pā. Sū. 6-4-75 as read]; nighāta); vṛṣā (root vṛṣu secane; the Uṇādi kanin; acute on the first syllable, the affix being nit); ṛgmibhiḥ (root ṛc stutau; kvip by the class sampadādibhyaḥ [vārttika, as read [Pā. 3-3-108, ?]]; the form ṛc; mini in the possessive sense; c → k by coḥ kuḥ [Pā. Sū. 8-2-30 as read] since the word has pada status; g by jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte [Pā. Sū. 8-2-39 as read]; ṛgmin; final acute by the affix; instrumental); gātubhiḥ (root gā stutau; tu in the passive by kamimanijani… [Uṇ. Sū. 1-73 as read, ?]; final acute by the affix).

The grammar of Rik 100.4 concludes: jyeṣṭhaḥ (atiśayena praśastaḥ jyeṣṭhaḥ; iṣṭhan after the word praśasya by atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau; the substitution jya for praśasya by jya ca [Pā. Sū. 5-3-61 as read]; if loss of the final were to arise, it does not, since prakṛtyaikāc [Pā. Sū. 6-4-163 as read] keeps the stem; guṇa; acute on the first syllable, the affix being nit). Rik 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 100.5)

स सूनुभिर्न रुद्रेभिर्ऋभ्वा नृषाह्ये सासह्वाँ अमित्रान् । सनीळेभिः श्रवस्यानि तूर्वन्मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विन्द्र ऊती ॥ ५ ॥

sa sūnubhir na rudrebhir ṛbhvā nṛṣāhye sāsahvāṃ amitrān | sanīḷebhiḥ śravasyāni tūrvan marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ‖ 5 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 100.5)

सः । सूनुऽभिः । न । रुद्रेभिः । ऋभ्वा । नृऽसह्ये । ससह्वान् [?] । अमित्रान् । सऽनीळेभिः । श्रवस्यानि । तूर्वन् । मरुत्वान् । नः । भवतु । इन्द्रः । ऊती ॥ ५ ॥

saḥ | sūnu-bhiḥ | na | rudrebhiḥ | ṛbhvā | nṛ-sahye | sasahvān [?] | amitrān | sa-nīḷebhiḥ | śravasyāni | tūrvan | marutvān | naḥ | bhavatu | indraḥ | ūtī ‖ 5 ‖ The Pada's sasahvān is read with short a, against the Saṃhitā's sāsahvān; see the like doubt at 100.3 [?].

original p. 192

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.5) The print's srava is read as śrava [?].

सूनुभिर्न पुत्रैरिव रुद्रेभिः रुद्रपुत्रैर्मरुद्भिर्युक्तः ऋभ्वा महान् एवंभूतः स इन्द्रो नृषाह्ये नृभिः पुरुषैः सोढव्ये संग्रामेऽमित्रान् शत्रून् सासह्वानभिभूतवान् । अपि च सनीळेभिः समाननिलयैर्मरुद्भिः सह श्रवस्यानि श्रव इत्यन्ननाम । तद्धेतुभूतान्युदकानि तूर्वन् मेघात्प्रच्यावयन् मरुत्वानिन्द्रोऽस्माकं रक्षणाय भवतु ॥ sūnubhir na putrair iva rudrebhiḥ rudraputrair marudbhir yuktaḥ ṛbhvā mahān evaṃbhūtaḥ sa indro nṛṣāhye nṛbhiḥ puruṣaiḥ soḍhavye saṃgrāme 'mitrān śatrūn sāsahvān abhibhūtavān | api ca sanīḷebhiḥ samānanilayair marudbhiḥ saha śravasyāni srava ity anna­nāma | taddhetubhūtāny udakāni tūrvan meghāt pracyāvayan marutvān indro 'smākaṃ rakṣaṇāya bhavatu ‖

"As if with sons, rudrebhiḥ — with the Maruts, the sons of Rudra — joined, ṛbhvā — great: such an Indra, in the battle (nṛṣāhye) that is to be endured by men, overcame (sāsahvān) the enemies, the foes. And also, with the Maruts who dwell in the same abode (sanīḷebhiḥ), śravasyāni — śrava is a name of food; the waters that are the cause of it — tūrvan — making them fall from the cloud: such an Indra, with the Maruts — may he be for our protection."

Bhāṣya's grammatical tail (characterized, partly transcribed) Characterized: the form nṛṣāhye (ṣah 'to endure' with yat by śakisahoś ca [Pā. Sū. 3-1-99, as read [?]]; lengthening of the a of the root in the Saṃhitā, 'as seen in others also'; acute on the first syllable by yato 'nāvaḥ, together with the accent of the last member of a compound ending in a kṛt); sāsahvān (root ṣah 'to overcome', kvasu for liṭ; Vedic lengthening of the reduplicative syllable); amitrān (na + mitra; acute on the second member by nañ jaramaramitramṛtāḥ); sanīḷebhiḥ (sa for samāna by samānasya chandasi).

नृषाह्ये । षह मर्षणे । शकिसहोश्च । पा. ३-१-९९ [?] । इति कर्मणि यत् । अन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति संहितायां धात्वकारस्य दीर्घत्वम् । यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । सासह्वान् । षह अभिभवे । लिटः क्वसुः । आभ्यासदीर्घत्वं छान्दसम् । अमित्रान् । मित्राण्येषु न सन्तीत्यमित्राः । नञो जरमरमित्रमृताः इत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । सनीळेभिः । समानं नीळं येषां ते सनीळाः । समानस्य छन्दसीति सभावः ॥ nṛṣāhye | ṣaha marṣaṇe | śakisahoś ca | Pā. 3-1-99 [?] | iti karmaṇi yat | anyeṣām api dṛśyata iti saṃhitāyāṃ dhātvakārasya dīrghatvam | yato 'nāva ity ādyudāttatve kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | sāsahvān | ṣaha abhibhave | liṭaḥ kvasuḥ | ābhyāsadīrghatvaṃ chāndasam | amitrān | mitrāṇy eṣu na santīty amitrāḥ | nañ jaramaramitramṛtāḥ ity uttarapadādyudāttatvam | sanīḷebhiḥ | samānaṃ nīḷaṃ yeṣāṃ te sanīḷāḥ | samānasya chandasīti sabhāvaḥ ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"sūnubhir na — (his own) as if together with sons; rudrebhiḥ — with the Maruts, sons of Rudra; ṛbhvā — the great one; saḥ — Indra; nṛṣāhye — in the battle that is to be faced by men; amitrān — the enemies; sasahvān — he who overcame [them]; (and) sanīḷebhiḥ — together with the Maruts who dwell in the same abode with him; śravasyāni — the waters that are the root cause of food; tūrvan — causing [them] to pour down from the clouds; marutvān — joined with the Maruts; indraḥ — Indra; naḥ — our; ūtī — for protection; bhavatu — may [he] be."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"The great Indra, joined with the Maruts, the sons of Rudra, as if with his own sons, with pride, overcame his enemies in the battle that is to be faced by men, and protected his devotees, men. And, making fall from the clouds the waters that are the root cause of food, together with the Maruts who dwell with him in his own abode — may that Indra, together with the Maruts, be the one who brings about our protection."

English Translation (as printed)

Mighty with the Rudras, as if with his sons, victorious in battle over his enemies, and sending down with his co-dwellers (the waters which are productive of) food ; Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.

original p. 193

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.5 (Kannada)

"Rudrebhiḥ — rudraputrair marudbhiḥ: with the Maruts who are the sons of Rudra. That the Maruts are the sons of Rudra is well known from the Śruti."

रुद्रो यद्वो मरुतो रुक्मवक्षसो वृषाजनि पृश्न्याः शुक्र ऊधनि । rudro yad vo maruto rukmavakṣaso vṛṣājani pṛśnyāḥ śukra ūdhani | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-34-2 as read [?])

"— as said in this Ṛk, the story that the Maruts were born to Rudra as sons, in Pṛśni, is well known; so, whenever they are addressed, this epithet is used most often. In explaining this Ṛk, Sāyaṇācārya tells another story as well:"

पृश्निर्नानावर्णा इयं भूमिः पुरा गोरूपधरासीत् । तस्यां महेशो वृषो भूत्वा मरुत उत्पादयामासेत्याचक्षते ॥ pṛśnir nānāvarṇā iyaṃ bhūmiḥ purā gorūpadharāsīt | tasyāṃ maheśo vṛṣo bhūtvā maruta utpādayām āsety ācakṣate ‖ (Sāyaṇa's commentary on Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-34-2)

"— that this many-coloured earth formerly took the form of a cow, and Maheśa [Rudra], becoming a bull, begot the Maruts in her: so Sāyaṇa has shown the relation of father and sons between Rudra and the Maruts. And the story told in the Ṛk 2-34-2 above is also told in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā; so he has cited the sentence from there:"

पृश्न्यै वै पयसो मरुतो जाताः । pṛśnyai vai payaso maruto jātāḥ | (Tai. Saṃ. 2-2-11-4 as read [?])

"— and for this reason in many places the Maruts are addressed as Rudra's sons. For example —" Glosses, editorial and tentative: "Who adorn themselves like women [or: like steeds], the sons of Rudra, the skilful, on their way"; "This word is spoken for the father of the Maruts, sweeter than the sweet, a [word] that strengthens Rudra: and give us, O immortal, mortals' food; be gracious to ourselves, our child, our offspring".

प्र ये शुम्भन्ते जनयो न सप्तयो यामन्रुद्रस्य सूनवः सुदंससः । pra ye śumbhante janayo na saptayo yāman rudrasya sūnavaḥ sudaṃsasaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-8[5?]-1 as read [?])

इदं पित्रे मरुतामुच्यते वचः स्वादोः स्वादीयो रुद्राय वर्धनम् । रास्वा च नो अमृत मर्तभोजनं त्मने तोकाय तनयाय मृळ ॥ idaṃ pitre marutām ucyate vacaḥ svādoḥ svādīyo rudrāya vardhanam | rāsvā ca no amṛta martabhojanaṃ tmane tokāya tanayāya mṛḷa ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-114-6 as read [?])

"In Ṛks such as these, and in the Ṛks 1-1[4?]7-9 and 2-3[3?]-1 [as read [?]] and in many other places, the Maruts bear the epithet 'sons of Rudra'. In explaining the Ṛk 1-114-6 quoted above, Sāyaṇa has told yet another story:"

रुद्रस्य च मरुतां पितृपुत्रत्वेनैवमाख्यायते । पुरा कदाचिदिन्द्रोऽसुरान् जिगाय । तदानीं दितिरसुरमाता इन्द्रहननसमर्थं पुत्रं कामय- rudrasya ca marutāṃ pitṛputratvenaivam ākhyāyate | purā kadācid indro 'surān jigāya | tadānīṃ ditir asuramātā indrahananasamarthaṃ putraṃ kāmaya- (Sāyaṇa on Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-114-6; continues on the next page)

original p. 194

Special Topics of Rik 100.5, continued from p. 193 (Kannada, with Sāyaṇa's Sanskrit) Reading note: āruadan above stands for the print's āruden, i.e. arudan 'they wept' [?]; the words garbhaikadeśāyor and keveme are clotted in print.

[…कामय]मानातपसा [read: कामयमाना तपसा] भर्तुः सकाशाद्गर्भं लेभे । इमं वृत्तान्तमवगच्छन्निन्द्रो वज्रहस्तः सन् सूक्ष्मरूपो भूत्वा तस्या उदरं प्रविश्य तं गर्भं सप्तधा बिभेद । पुनरप्येकैकं सप्तखण्डमकरोत् । ते सर्वे गर्भैकदेशायोर्निर्गत्य [?] आरुदन् । एतस्मिन्नवसरे लीलार्थं गच्छन्तौ पार्वतीपरमेश्वरौ इमान् ददृशतुः । महेशं प्रति पार्वती एवमुवाच । इमे मांसखण्डा यथा प्रत्येकं पुत्राः सम्पद्येरन्नेवं त्वया कार्यं मयि चेत्प्रीतिरस्तीति । स च महेश्वरस्तान् समानरूपान् समानवयसः समानालंकारान् पुत्रान् कृत्वा गौर्यै प्रददौ केवेमे [?] पुत्राः सन्तीति । अतः सर्वेषु मारुतेषु सूक्तेषु मरुतो रुद्रपुत्रा इति स्तूयन्ते । रौद्रेषु च मरुतां पिता रुद्र इति । […kāmaya]mānā tapasā bhartuḥ sakāśād garbhaṃ lebhe | imaṃ vṛttāntam avagacchann indro vajrahastaḥ san sūkṣmarūpo bhūtvā tasyā udaraṃ praviśya taṃ garbhaṃ saptadhā bibheda | punar apy ekaikaṃ saptakhaṇḍam akarot | te sarve garbhaikadeśāyor [?] nirgatya āruadan | etasminn avasare līlārthaṃ gacchantau pārvatīparameśvarau imān dadṛśatuḥ | maheśaṃ prati pārvatī evam uvāca | ime māṃsakhaṇḍā yathā pratyekaṃ putrāḥ sampadyerann evaṃ tvayā kāryaṃ mayi cet prītir astīti | sa ca maheśvaras tān samānarūpān samānavayasaḥ samānālaṃkārān putrān kṛtvā gauryai pradadau keveme [?] putrāḥ santīti | ataḥ sarveṣu māruteṣu sūkteṣu maruto rudraputrā iti stūyante | raudreṣu ca marutāṃ pitā rudra iti | (Sāyaṇa's commentary on Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-114-6)

"Once in former times Indra conquered the Asuras. Then Diti, the mother of the Asuras, wishing to obtain a son able to kill Indra, performed austerities and, by the favour of her husband, conceived. Indra, learning of this, took the thunderbolt in his hand, became of subtle form, entered her womb, and split the embryo into seven parts; and again he made each one into seven pieces. They all came out from one part of the womb and wept. At that time Pārvatī and Parameśvara, who were going about in sport, saw them; and Pārvatī, moved with compassion, begged Maheśvara to make all of them into children. Then Īśvara made them all of one form, of one age, with the same ornaments, as sons, and gave them to her, saying 'these are your sons'. Therefore in all the Marut-sūktas the Maruts are praised as sons of Rudra, and in the Rudra-sūktas Rudra is spoken of as father of the Maruts: so Sāyaṇa tells this story.

Sūnubhir na — 'as if together with his own sons': so the love between Indra and the Maruts is suggested. The nature of the established companionship between Indra and the Maruts was explained in detail in the explanation of the first Ṛk of this sūkta.

Ṛbhvā — for the word ṛbhvan the Nirukta-author, explaining Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-120-6 (Ni. 11-31 as read [?]), says 'urubhūtam mahattvāt svarūpavat' [as read, ?] — 'one who has the nature of vastness'; Sāyaṇa too gives the meaning mahān, 'great': the sense is, the great Indra. This epithet has also been used where the sense 'shining exceedingly' is to be given. For example —"

original p. 195

दक्षं महे पाययते हिरण्ययं रथमावृत्या हरियोगमृभ्वसम् । dakṣaṃ mahe pāyayate hiraṇyayaṃ rathaṃ āvṛtyā hariyogam ṛbhvasam | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-56-1 as read [?])

"— in contexts such as these, for the word ṛbhvasam the sense is urubhāsamānam, 'shining greatly, exceedingly'. In sum, the meaning is 'the great one'.

Nṛṣāhye — puruṣaiḥ soḍhavye saṃgrāme: in the battle that is to be endured by men; that is, in a battle that shows the power to withstand the onsets of enemies, by men.

Sanīḷebhiḥ — since gayaḥ, kṛdaraḥ, garta and the like are read among the twenty-two names of house (Ni. 3-[?]3 as read [?]), the word nīḷa means 'house'. Since the Maruts always dwell together, the sense is, 'those who have one abode'. This epithet is generally used when the Maruts are addressed. For example —"

कया शुभा सवयसः सनीळाः समान्या मरुतः सं मिमिक्षुः । kayā śubhā savayasaḥ sanīḷāḥ samānyā marutaḥ saṃ mimikṣuḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-165-1 as read [?])

क ईं व्यक्ता नरः सनीळा रुद्रस्य मर्या अधा स्वश्वाः । ka īṃ vyaktā naraḥ sanīḷā rudrasya maryā adhā svaśvāḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-3[3?]-1 as read [?])

"— in all such Ṛks the dwelling of the Maruts in one abode is described by 'sanīḷāḥ'. Sanīḷebhiḥ means 'with the Maruts who dwell in one abode'.

Śravasyāni — śrava is a name for food [as the print's srava ity anna nāma is read, ?]; taddhetubhūtāny udakāni: the waters that are the cause of food and are of the form of rain.

Tūrvan — meghāt pracyāvayan: making [the waters] pour from the cloud."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.5) grammar pages, pp. 195–196, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?]

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: rudrebhiḥ (rudra + bhis; the substitution ais does not come, by bahulaṃ chandasi [Pā. Sū. 7-1-10 as read]; e by bahuvacane jhaly et [Pā. Sū. 7-3-103 as read]; s → ru → visarga); nṛṣāhye (root saha marṣaṇe; ṣ for the initial s by dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-1-64 as read]; yat in the passive by śakisahoś ca [Pā. Sū. 3-1-99 as read]; lengthening of the root's a in the Saṃhitā by anyeṣām api dṛśyate [Pā. Sū. 6-3-137 as read]; nṛbhiḥ sāhyaḥ nṛṣāhyaḥ; the acute on the first syllable that yato 'nāvaḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-1-213 as read] would give is replaced by the accent of the last member of a kṛt-ended compound with a kāraka first member, by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt [Pā. Sū. 6-2-139 as read]; locative singular).

original p. 196

The grammar of Rik 100.5 continues: sāsahvān (root ṣah abhibhave; kvasu for liṭ by kvasuś ca [Pā. Sū. 3-2-107 as read]; doubling of the root; ādihalśeṣa; Vedic lengthening of the reduplicative syllable; acute on the affix; before su lengthening of the penult by atvasantasya [Pā. Sū. 6-4-14 as read]; num because the affix is ugit, by ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ [Pā. Sū. 7-1-70 as read]; the loss of the final consonant of the cluster is treated as not having happened, so n is not lost); amitrān (mitrāṇi eṣu na santi; the acute on the second member by nañ jaramaramitramṛtāḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-2-116 as read]); sanīḷebhiḥ (samānaṃ nīḷaṃ yeṣāṃ te sanīḷāḥ; sa for samāna by samānasya chandasy amūrdhaprabhṛtyudarkeṣu [Pā. Sū. 6-3-84 as read]; ais does not arise, by bahulaṃ chandasi; e); tūrvan (root turvī hiṃsārthe, bhvādi; śatṛ in the sense of the present; the penult lengthened because it ends in r; śap; the single substitute a by ato guṇe [Pā. Sū. 6-1-97 as read]; the lasārvadhātuka accent being the low one after a root with a-initial upadeśa, by tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam [Pā. Sū. 6-1-186 as read], the root keeps its own accent; num before the nominative su since the affix is ugit, and, as before, the loss of t is treated as not having happened so that n is not lost; the form tūrvan). The Rik is closed with ‖ 5 ‖ and a rule of dashes.

Rik 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 100.6)

स मन्युमीः समदनस्य कर्तास्माकेभिर्नृभिः सूर्यं सनत् । अस्मिन्नहन्सत्पतिः पुरुहूतो मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विन्द्र ऊती ॥ ६ ॥

sa manyumīḥ samadanasya kartāsmākebhir nṛbhiḥ sūryaṃ sanat | asminn ahan satpatiḥ puruhūto marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ‖ 6 ‖

original p. 197

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 100.6)

सः । मन्युऽमीः । सऽमदनस्य । कर्ता । अस्माकेभिः । नृऽभिः । सूर्यम् । सनत् । अस्मिन् । अहन् । सत्ऽपतिः । पुरुऽहूतः । मरुत्वान् । नः । भवतु । इन्द्रः । ऊती ॥ ६ ॥

saḥ | manyu-mīḥ | sa-madanasya | kartā | asmākebhiḥ | nṛ-bhiḥ | sūryam | sanat | asmin | ahan | sat-patiḥ | puru-hūtaḥ | marutvān | naḥ | bhavatu | indraḥ | ūtī ‖ 6 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.6)

शत्रुभिरपहृतासु गोषु तैः सह युद्धार्थं विनिर्गता ऋज्राश्वादयोऽनेन सूक्तेनेन्द्रमस्तुवन् । स इन्द्रो मन्युमीर्मन्योः कोपस्य निर्माता [?] । यद्वा । अभिमन्यमानस्य शत्रोर्हिंसकः । अपि च समदनस्य संग्रामस्य कर्ता । सत्पतिः सतां पालयिता । पुरुहूतो बहुभिर्यजमानैराहूतः । एवंगुणविशिष्टः स अस्मिन्नहन् अस्मिन् दिनेऽस्माकेभिरस्मदीयैर्नृभिः पुरुषैः सूर्यं सूर्यप्रकाशं सनत् सम्भक्तं करोतु । शत्रुपुरुषैस्तु वृष्टिनिरोधकमन्धकारं संयोजयतु । स च मरुत्वानिन्द्रोऽस्माकं रक्षणाय भवतु ॥ śatrubhir apahṛtāsu goṣu taiḥ saha yuddhārthaṃ vinirgatā ṛjrāśvādayo 'nena sūktenendram astuvan | sa indro manyumīr manyoḥ kopasya nirmātā [?] | yadvā | abhimanyamānasya śatror hiṃsakaḥ | api ca samadanasya saṃgrāmasya kartā | satpatiḥ satāṃ pālayitā | puruhūto bahubhir yajamānair āhūtaḥ | evaṃguṇaviśiṣṭaḥ sa asminn ahan asmin dine 'smākebhir asmadīyair nṛbhiḥ puruṣaiḥ sūryaṃ sūryaprakāśaṃ sanat sambhaktaṃ karotu | śatrupuruṣais tu vṛṣṭinirodhakam andhakāraṃ saṃyojayatu | sa ca marutvān indro 'smākaṃ rakṣaṇāya bhavatu ‖

"When their cows had been carried off by enemies, Ṛjrāśva and the others, having set out to fight those [enemies], praised Indra with this sūkta. That Indra is manyumīḥ — the one who brings about [or: measures out] wrath; or, the destroyer of an enemy who is behaving with arrogance (abhimanyamāna). And he is the maker (kartā) of samadana, of battle; satpatiḥ — the protector of the good; puruhūtaḥ — called by many sacrificers. Being endowed with such qualities, asminn ahan — this day — may he make sūryam, the light of the sun, to be shared (sanat) by our men (asmākebhiḥ nṛbhiḥ); but may he join the enemy men to the darkness that holds back rain [print's wording, as read]. And may that Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, be for our protection."

Bhāṣya's grammatical tail (characterized, partly transcribed) Characterized: the stem manyumī ('one who destroys wrath/the arrogant', root mī 'to injure', with kvip); samadana (saha mādyanty asmin, 'where they rejoice together', = battle; root mad 'to rejoice' with lyuṭ in the locus; sa for saha by sahasya saḥ saṃjñāyām [Pā. Sū. 6-3-78, as read [?]]); asmākebhiḥ (the substitute asmāka for asmad with the aṇ affix, and the non-substitution of ais; a short illustrative Ṛgveda citation, clotted in the print); sanat (root van/ṣaṇ 'to share', leṭ with aḍāgama); ahan (the locative's ending dropped by supāṃ suluk…); satpatiḥ (the first member keeps its accent by patyāvaiśvarye).

मन्युमीः । मन्युं मिनातीति मन्युमीः । मीञ् हिंसायाम् । क्विप् । समदनस्य । सह माद्यन्त्यस्मिन्निति समदनः संग्रामः । मदी हर्षे । अधिकरणे ल्युट् । सहस्य सः संज्ञायाम् । पा. ६-३-७८ [?] । इति सभावः । अस्माकेभिः । तस्मिन्नणि च युष्माकास्माकौ [?] … अस्मच्छब्दस्यास्माकादेशः । संज्ञापूर्वकस्य विधेरनित्यत्वादैस्यैष्यभावः [?] । बहुलं छन्दसीति भिस ऐसभावः । [Rik-citation, clotted; Ṛ. 1-82-3 as read [?]] इत्युदाहृतः । सनत् । वन षण सम्भक्तौ । लेट्यडागमः । अहन् । सुपां सुलुगिति सप्तम्या लुक् । सत्पतिः । पत्यावैश्वर्ये इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥ manyumīḥ | manyuṃ mināti iti manyumīḥ | mīñ hiṃsāyām | kvip | samadanasya | saha mādyanty asminn iti samadanaḥ saṃgrāmaḥ | madī harṣe | adhikaraṇe lyuṭ | sahasya saḥ saṃjñāyām | Pā. 6-3-78 [?] | iti sabhāvaḥ | asmākebhiḥ | tasminn aṇi ca yuṣmākāsmākau [?] … asmacchabdasyāsmākādeśaḥ | saṃjñāpūrvakasya vidher anityatvād aisyaiṣyabhāvaḥ [?] | bahulaṃ chandasīti bhisa aisabhāvaḥ | [clotted citation] ity udāhṛtaḥ | sanat | vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau | leṭy aḍāgamaḥ | ahan | supāṃ suluk iti saptamyā luk | satpatiḥ | patyāvaiśvarye iti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada) begun at the foot of p. 197; continues on p. 198

"manyumīḥ — one who makes anger manifest, or one who destroys the cruel enemy; samadanasya — of battle; kartā — the maker; satpatiḥ — the protector of the good; puruhūtaḥ — one called (for help) by many sacrificers; saḥ — that Indra; asmin ahan — on this day; asmākebhiḥ nṛbhiḥ — with the men connected with us; sūryam — the sun's"

original p. 198

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha of Rik 100.6, concluded from p. 197 (Kannada)

"[sūryam —] the light [of the sun]; sanat — may he join [it] (may he give us light and make darkness for the enemies' share); marutvān — together with the Maruts; indraḥ — Indra; naḥ — our; ūtī — for protection; bhavatu — may he be."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"May Indra — who makes his fierce anger manifest and destroys his enemies, who is the maker of battle, the protector of the good, the one called for help by many sacrificers — on this day give the light of the sun to all who are with us, and make darkness for the share of our enemies; and, together with the Maruts, be for our protection."

English Translation (as printed)

May he, the repressor of (hostile) wrath, the author of war, the protector of the good, the invoked of many, share with our people on this day the (light of the) sun : may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.6 (Kannada)

"Manyumīḥ —"

मन्युर्मन्यतेर्दीप्तिकर्मणः क्रोधकर्मणो वधकर्मणो वा । manyur manyater dīptikarmaṇaḥ krodhakarmaṇo vadhakarmaṇo vā | (Ni. 10-29 as read [?])

"— from the root man, the word manyu acquires the meanings 'to shine', 'to be angry', or 'to kill'. [Sāyaṇa gives for] manyumīḥ: 'manoḥ kopasya nirmātā, abhimanyamānasya śatror hiṃsakaḥ': 'one who makes anger manifest, or one who destroys an enemy who is in a rage'. Skandasvāmin says:"

अत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते । प्रजापतेः पुत्रो मन्युर्नाम । तं प्रजापतिः सेनापत्ये नियुक्तवान् । तेन सहेन्द्रो निजघान इति । atrétihāsam ācakṣate | prajāpateḥ putro manyur nāma | taṃ prajāpatiḥ senāpatye niyuktavān | tena sahendro nijaghāna iti | (Skandasvāmin, as read)

"— [that is: here they tell the tale: the son of Prajāpati, named Manyu; Prajāpati appointed him as commander; with his help Indra slew the foes.] Thus he tells the story, and explains manyumīḥ as 'one who killed with the help of Manyu'. [The Śruti itself shows that] Manyu, who is the son of Prajāpati, stands in a most close relation to Indra; the story of Manyu, how he was changed into Rudra, is told in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa:"

प्रजापतेर्विस्रस्ताद्देवता उदक्रामन्त्स्मैक एव [?] देवो नाजहान्मन्युरेव सोऽस्मिन्नन्तर्वर्तितोऽतिष्ठत्सोऽरोदीत्तस्य यान्यश्रूणि प्रास्कन्दंस्तान्यस्मिन्नो [?] प्रत्यतिष्ठत् [?] स एव शतशीर्षा रुद्रः समभवत् सहस्राक्षः शतेषुधिः । prajāpater visrastād devatā udakrāman smaika eva [?] devo nājahān manyur eva so 'smin antarvartito 'tiṣṭhat so 'rodīt tasya yāny aśrūṇi prāskandaṃs tāny asminno [?] pratyatiṣṭhat [?] sa eva śataśīrṣā rudraḥ samabhavat sahasrākṣaḥ śateṣudhiḥ | (Śat. Brā. 9-1-1-6 as read [?]; several words clotted in print [?])

original p. 199

"When Prajāpati had become weak, all the other deities abandoned him; only the deity named Manyu did not leave him but stayed with him, close beside him. Then Prajāpati wept; and when the tears fell on Manyu, he became Rudra with a hundred heads, a thousand eyes and a hundred quivers: so the story goes. By this it is known that Manyu is bold and valorous in battle. (But it does not say that he is a son of Prajāpati.) The close relation between this deity called Manyu and Indra is known from a sentence of the Bṛhaddevatā —"

इन्द्राश्रयस्तु पर्जन्यो रुद्रो वायुर्बृहस्पतिः । वरुणः कश्च मृत्युश्च देवश्च ब्रह्मणस्पतिः ॥ मन्युश्च विश्वकर्मा च मित्रः क्षेत्रपतिर्यमः । indrāśrayas tu parjanyo rudro vāyur bṛhaspatiḥ | varuṇaḥ kaś ca mṛtyuś ca devaś ca brahmaṇaspatiḥ ‖ manyuś ca viśvakarmā ca mitraḥ kṣetrapatir yamaḥ | (Bṛ. De. 8-93–95 as read [?])

"— so the Bṛhaddevatā says that Manyu and the other deities [listed] are indrāśraya, 'resting in Indra'. Quoting this Ṛk-saṃhitā sentence [sic, as printed], [the Nirukta-author] has followed the sentence of the Nirukta-author (Ni. 10-29 as read [?]) that gives the derivation of the word manyu. The Nirukta-author, citing the Ṛk"

त्वया मन्यो सरथमारुजन्तो हर्षमाणासो धृषिता मरुत्वः । तिग्मेषव आयुधा संशिशाना अभि प्र यन्तु नरो अग्निरूपाः ॥ tvayā manyo sarathām ārujanto harṣamāṇāso dhṛṣitā marutvaḥ | tigmeṣava āyudhā saṃśiśānā abhi pra yantu naro agnirūpāḥ ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-84-1 as read [?])

"— has shown that Indra and the other deities conquered their enemies with the help of Manyu. In the present context also manyumīḥ means 'one who destroyed enemies with Manyu's help'.

Samadanasya — since raṇaḥ, vivāk, vikhādaḥ and the like are read among the [forty-six, as read, ?] names of battle (Ni. 2-[?] as read [?]), the meaning is 'of battle'. When the Nirukta-author derives the word samat, citing the Ṛk"

चित्रो यदभ्राट् श्वेतो [print: छ्वेतो] न विक्षु रथो न रुक्मी त्वेषः समत्सु । citro yad abhrāṭ śveto [print: chveto] na vikṣu ratho na rukmī tveṣaḥ samatsu | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-66-6 as read [?])

"— he has said that the word samat has the meaning 'battle'. The word samadana is a synonym of the word samat. Because Indra, even at his birth, manifested the aspects of the war-deity, and afterwards fought and destroyed all the Asuras, he is praised as the maker of battle."

original p. 200

"Sūryaṃ sanat" —

सूर्यस्य हि यागादिकर्मनिवृत्तिः फलम् । अस्मदीयैः ऋत्विग्भिः सह देवतात्मत्वमापन्नः इन्द्रः सूर्योदयफलभूतमस्मदीयं योगं निर्वर्तयत्वित्यर्थः । sūryasya hi yāgādikarmanivṛttiḥ phalam | asmadīyaiḥ ṛtvigbhiḥ saha devatātmatvam āpannaḥ indraḥ sūryodayaphalabhūtam asmadīyaṃ yogaṃ nirvartayatv ity arthaḥ | (as printed, a short Sanskrit gloss; read as given [?])

"— the completion of the sacrificial acts, the yāga and the rest, is indeed the fruit of the [rising of the] sun. [The sense is:] may Indra, who has attained the nature of a deity together with our priests, bring about for us that sacrifice which has the sunrise as its fruit. For the performance of the yāga and the other acts is the result of the sun's rising, and so, for the completion of those rites, the prayer is that Indra give us the light of the sun and bring our rites to completion with all their parts."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.6) grammar pages, pp. 200–201, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?]

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: manyumīḥ (manyuṃ mināti; root mīñ hiṃsāyām; kvip by kvip ca [Pā. Sū. 3-2-76 as read]; since the first member is a kāraka, the accent of the last member by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt [Pā. Sū. 6-2-139 as read]; nominative singular); samadanasya (saha mādyanty asmin iti samadanaḥ saṃgrāmaḥ; root madī harṣe; lyuṭ in the locus; ana for yu by yuvoranākau [Pā. Sū. 7-1-1 as read]; sa for saha by sahasya saḥ saṃjñāyām [Pā. Sū. 6-3-78 as read]; the syllable before the affix is acute because the affix is lit, by liti [Pā. Sū. 6-1-193 as read]; genitive); kartā (root ḍukṛñ karaṇe; tṛc in the agent; final acute by citaḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-1-163 as read]); asmākebhiḥ (asmākaṃ sambandhinaḥ asmākāḥ; aṇ in the sense of 'connected with'; asmāka for asmad by tasmin aṇi ca yuṣmākāsmākau [Pā. Sū. 4-3-2 as read]; the vṛddhi that aṇ would cause does not arise, since a rule that depends on a name is not invariable [saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ, Paribhāṣā 93 as read]; asmāka + bhis: ais does not come, by bahulaṃ chandasi [Pā. Sū. 7-1-10 as read]; the accent rule for this is stated at the place prāsmākāsaś ca sūrayaḥ [Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-97-3 as read [?]]); sanat (root vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau; leṭ, third person singular, tip; loss of the final i by itaś ca lopaḥ [Pā. Sū. 3-4-97 as read]; aṭ by leṭo 'ḍāṭau [Pā. Sū. 3-4-94 as read]; nighāta); ahan (the locative ending dropped by supāṃ suluk… [Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 as read]).

original p. 201

The grammar of Rik 100.6 concludes: satpatiḥ (satāṃ patiḥ; though the acute on the last syllable might be expected for the compound, the accent of the first member comes by patyāvaiśvarye [Pā. Sū. 6-2-18 as read]); puruhūtaḥ (purubhiḥ hūtaḥ; root hu dānādanayoḥ [as read]; kta; acute on the last syllable by the affix; in the compound, as the first member is a kāraka, the accent of the last member by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt). The Rik is closed with ‖ 6 ‖ and a printed ornament.

Rik 7

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 100.7)

तमूतयो रणयञ्छूरसातौ तं क्षेमस्य क्षितयः कृण्वत त्राम् । स विश्वस्य करुणस्येश एको मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विन्द्र ऊती ॥ ७ ॥

tam ūtayo raṇayañ chūrasātau taṃ kṣemasya kṣitayaḥ kṛṇvata trām | sa viśvasya karuṇasyeśa eko marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ‖ 7 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 100.7)

तम् । ऊतयः । रणयन् । शूरऽसातौ । तम् । क्षेमस्य । क्षितयः । कृण्वत । त्राम् । सः । विश्वस्य । करुणस्य । ईशे । एकः । मरुत्वान् । नः । भवतु । इन्द्रः । ऊती ॥ ७ ॥

tam | ūtayaḥ | raṇayan | śūra-sātau | tam | kṣemasya | kṣitayaḥ | kṛṇvata | trām | saḥ | viśvasya | karuṇasya | īśe | ekaḥ | marutvān | naḥ | bhavatu | indraḥ | ūtī ‖ 7 ‖

original p. 202

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.7)

तमिन्द्रं शूरसातौ शूरैर्वीरपुरुषैः सम्भजनीये संग्रामे ऊतयो गन्तारो मरुतो रणयन् । रमयन्ति । यद्वा प्रहर भगवो जहि वीरयस्वेत्येवंरूपं शब्दमिन्द्रमुद्दिश्य कुर्वन्ति । अपि च क्षितयो मनुष्यास्तमिन्द्रं क्षेमस्य रक्षणीयस्य सर्वस्य धनस्य त्रां त्रातारं रक्षितारं कृण्वत । कुर्वन्ति । देवतान्तरादस्य कोऽतिशय इति चेदुच्यते । स इन्द्रो विश्वस्य सर्वस्य करुणस्याभिमतफलनिष्पादनरूपस्य कर्मण एकोऽसहाय एवेशे । ईष्टे । अन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥ tam indraṃ śūrasātau śūrair vīrapuruṣaiḥ sambhajanīye saṃgrāme ūtayo gantāro maruto raṇayan | ramayanti | yadvā prahara bhagavo jahi vīrayasvety evaṃrūpaṃ śabdam indram uddiśya kurvanti | api ca kṣitayo manuṣyās tam indraṃ kṣemasya rakṣaṇīyasya sarvasya dhanasya trāṃ trātāraṃ rakṣitāraṃ kṛṇvata | kurvanti | devatāntarād asya ko 'tiśaya iti ced ucyate | sa indro viśvasya sarvasya karuṇasyābhimataphalaniṣpādanarūpasya karmaṇa eko 'sahāya eveśe | īṣṭe | anyat pūrvavat ‖

"Him, Indra, in the śūrasātau — in the battle in which heroic men take part — the Maruts, who come as helpers (ūtayaḥ, 'those who go'), raṇayan — delight; or they utter, addressing Indra, cries of the kind 'strike, Lord! kill! show your valour!'. And the people, kṣitayaḥ — men — make that Indra trām — the protector, the guardian — of kṣemasya, of all wealth that is to be preserved. If it be asked what excellence he has over another deity, it is answered: that Indra viśvasya karuṇasya — of all work, which consists in bringing about the fruit that is wished for — alone, without a helper, is lord (īśe, 'he rules'). The rest is as before."

Bhāṣya's grammatical tail (characterized, partly transcribed) Characterized: the stem ūti from the root av 'to go', with ktin in the agent by kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam, the augment iṭ barred, and ūṭ for the v and the penultimate syllable by jvaratvara…, the accent fixed by ūtiyūtijūti…; or with ktic; raṇayan (root ram with the causative ṇic, the Vedic laṅ in the present sense; or from the root raṇ 'to sound'); trām (root trai 'to protect', with kvip, which applies even without a prefix by the word ca drawing in dṛśi); karuṇa (root ḍukṛñ with unan by an Uṇādi rule [Uṇ. Sū. 3-53, as read, ?]); īśe (root īś 'to rule', loss of t by lopas ta ātmanepadeṣu). Several rule-names are clotted and marked [?].

ऊतयः । अवतेर्गत्यर्थात् कृत्यल्युटो बहुलमिति कर्तरि क्तिन् । श्र्युकः किति [?] इति [rule-name clotted] इट्प्रतिषेधः । ज्वरत्वरेत्यादिना वकारस्योपधायाश्च ऊट् । ऊतियूतीत्यादिना क्तिन उदात्तत्वम् । यद्वा । कर्तरि क्तिच् । रणयन् । रमतेर्हेतुमण्णिजन्तात् वर्तमाने छान्दसो लङ् । अन्त्यैकारश्छान्दसः [?] । यद्वा । रण शब्दार्थः । अस्माण्णिजन्तात्पूर्ववल्लङ् । त्राम् । त्रैङ् पालने । त्रायत इति त्राः । क्विप् चेति चशब्देन दृशिग्रहणानुकर्षणान्निरुपसदादपि क्विप् । करुणस्य । दुकृञ् करणे । क्याप्त्रादारिभ्य उनन् [?] । उ. ३-५३ [?] । इति भावे उनन् । व्यत्ययेन प्रत्ययोदात्तत्वम् । ईशे । ईश ऐश्वर्ये । लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेष्विति तलोपः ॥ ūtayaḥ | avater gatyarthāt kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam iti kartari ktin | śryukaḥ kiti [?] iti [rule-name clotted] iṭpratiṣedhaḥ | jvaratvarety ādinā vakārasyopadhāyāś ca ūṭ | ūtiyūtīty ādinā ktina udāttatvam | yadvā | kartari ktic | raṇayan | ramater hetumaṇ ṇijantāt vartamāne chāndaso laṅ | antyaikāraś chāndasaḥ [?] | yadvā | raṇa śabdārthaḥ | asmāṇ ṇijantāt pūrvavat laṅ | trām | traiṅ pālane | trāyata iti trāḥ | kvip ceti caśabdena dṛśigrahaṇānukarṣaṇān nirupasadād api kvip | karuṇasya | dukṛñ karaṇe | kyāptrādāribhya unan [?] | U. 3-53 [?] | iti bhāve unan | vyatyayena pratyayodāttatvam | īśe | īśa aiśvarye | lopas ta ātmanepadeṣv iti talopaḥ ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"taṃ — that Indra; śūrasātau — at the time of battle fought with heroes; ūtayaḥ — the Maruts who go about for help; raṇayan — [they] rejoice, with sounds that suggest victory; kṣitayaḥ — men; taṃ — that Indra; kṣemasya — of their wealth that is to be protected; trām — as the protector; kṛṇvata — have made [him]; saḥ — that Indra; viśvasya karuṇasya — (of the rites that bring about the desired objects) of all rites; ekaḥ — he alone; īśe — is lord; marutvān — together with the Maruts; indraḥ — Indra; naḥ — our; ūtī — for protection; bhavatu — may he be."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"At the time of fighting with heroes, the Maruts, who go along with that Indra for his help, make sounds that suggest victory and rejoice. Men make that Indra the protector of their wealth. That Indra alone is the lord of all the rites that bring about the desired objects. May such an Indra, together with the Maruts, be our protector."

original p. 203

English Translation (as printed)

Him, his allies, the Maruts, animate in battle ; him, men regard as the preserver of their property ; he alone presides over every act of worship : may Indra, associated with the Maruts be our protection.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.7 (Kannada)

"Śūrasātau — śūrair vīrapuruṣaiḥ sambhajanīye saṃgrāme: in a battle in which heroic men take part; that is, a battle that heroic men enter into with eagerness.

Ūtayaḥ — the Maruts, who have come to help.

Raṇayan — ramayanti: they delight, they cause delight; or they make a sound that suggests exultation. On the basis of the root meaning 'delightful', the word raṇa is also a synonym for battle. Even there, the idea that, when Indra and the Maruts, helping one another, enter the battlefield together, it must be delightful, is shown by the Ṛk"

मरुत्वाँ इन्द्र वृषभो रणाय पिबा सोममनुष्वधं मदाय । marutvāṃ indra vṛṣabho raṇāya pibā somam anuṣvadhaṃ madāya | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-47-1 as read [?])

"— and for the word raṇāya in this Ṛk, [Sāyaṇa] has given ramaṇīyāya saṃgrāmāya, 'for the delightful battle': an apt meaning for the word. That the Maruts, whether in the sacrificial house or in the field of battle, make their delightful sounds is described in many places. For example —" Glosses, editorial and tentative: "Rejoice, O Maruts, with the altar-offerings; set down [your] wrath, unyoke the horses"; "Here, at the rite, O Maruts, the blameless, bright, purifying ones rejoice".

रराणता मरुतो वेद्याभिर्नि हेळो धत्त वि मुचध्वमश्वान् । rarāṇatā maruto vedyābhir ni heḷo dhatta vi mucadhvam aśvān | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-171-1 as read [?])

कृते चिदत्र मरुतो रणन्तानवद्यासः शुचयः पावकाः । kṛte cid atra maruto raṇantānavadyāsaḥ śucayaḥ pāvakāḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. [5?]-52-3 as read [?])

"— in many Ṛks like these the Maruts are described as showing their joy, in the sacrificial house, by their delightful sound. In the same way —" Gloss, editorial and tentative: "The Maruts, the playful, played all around Indra, who had come to slay Vṛtra, honouring him; so, indeed, they play around the one who is about to slay this evil, the hating rival".

मरुतो ह वै क्रीडिनो वृत्रं हनिष्यन्तमिन्द्रमागतं तमभितः परिचिक्रीडुर्मर्हयन्तस्तथो एवैतं पाप्मानं द्विषन्तं भ्रातृव्यं हनिष्यन्तमभितः परिक्रीडन्ते । maruto ha vai krīḍino vṛtraṃ haniṣyantam indram āgataṃ tam abhitaḥ paricikrīḍur marhayantas tatho evaitaṃ pāpmānaṃ dviṣantaṃ bhrātṛvyaṃ haniṣyantam abhitaḥ parikrīḍante | (Śat. Brā. 2-5-3-10 as read [?])

original p. 204

"— so, at the time of the slaying of Vṛtra, the Maruts, being Indra's companions, showed their joy and played; and in the same way it is described that they do so in the sacrificial house. This kind of raṇana ('sounding in joy') is natural to the Maruts, and so the same is described here.

Kṣitayaḥ — manuṣyāḥ: since naraḥ and the rest are read among the twenty-five [as read, ?] names of man, the sense is 'men' (Ni. 2-[2?] as read [?])."

अग्निर्नेता भग इव क्षितीनां दैवीनां देव ऋतुपा ऋतावा । agnir netā bhaga iva kṣitīnāṃ daivīnāṃ deva ṛtupā ṛtāvā | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-20-4 as read [?])

"— in such places, to show the difference between men and the subjects connected with the gods, by the word kṣiti it is suggested that the subjects of the earth are men.

Karuṇasya — since apaḥ, apnaḥ, daṃsaḥ and the like are read among the twenty-six [as read, ?] names of action (Ni. 2-1 as read [?]), the sense is 'of action'. Since Indra is the lord in all actions, protection of the action is asked of him; since, at every step, obstacles come to the action from the Asuras and the like, and by destroying those Asuras he is himself the chief protector in carrying the action through."

इन्द्रो वै यज्ञस्य देवता । indro vai yajñasya devatā | (Śat. Brā. 1-4-1-[3?]2 as read [?])

इन्द्राय विमृधेऽनुनिर्वपति सेन्द्रो मे यज्ञोऽसदिति सर्वो वै यज्ञ इन्द्रस्यैव । indrāya vimṛdhe 'nunirvapati sendro me yajño 'sad iti sarvo vai yajña indrasyaiva | (Śat. Brā. 11-1-3-4 as read [?])

"— in many places such as these Indra is praised as the chief lord of the sacrifice. Not only by the destruction of the Asuras: since the rain, so essential to the sacrifice, must be obtained by Indra's favour, Indra is the chief lord of the sacrifice. Skandasvāmin explains this point: 'sarvakarmaṇāṃ vṛṣṭinibandhanatvāt vṛṣṭeś ca kevalendrāyattatvāt' [as read, ?] — since rain is the basis of all rites, and rain depends on Indra alone, [the carrying out of] all rites must come by rain, and since Indra himself is the one who makes rain, he alone is lord of the rites."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.7) grammar pages, pp. 204–205, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?]

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: ūtayaḥ (a ktin-ending noun fixed by nipātana, with its accent, by ūtiyūtijūti… [Pā. Sū. 3-3-97 as read]; the root av rakṣaṇe, used here in the sense of going; ktin in the agent by bahulam under kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam [Pā. Sū. 3-3-113 as read]; the prohibition of iṭ [a rule beginning śri-…, as read, Pā. Sū. 7-2-[9?]]; the root's v and its penultimate vowel become ūṭ, by jvaratvarasrivyavimavām upadhāyāś ca [Pā. Sū. 6-4-20 as read], giving ūti; or ktic in the agent by ktic ktau ca saṃjñāyām [Pā. Sū. 3-3-174 as read], with the advantage that no appeal to nipātana is needed; acute on the last syllable because the affix is cit; nominative plural).

original p. 205

The grammar of Rik 100.7 continues: raṇayan (root ramu krīḍāyām; the causative sense shown, ṇic by hetumati ca [Pā. Sū. 3-1-26 as read]; as the form ends in ṇic, it is called mit and its penult shortened by miṭāṃ hrasvaḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-4-92 as read]; the Vedic laṅ in the present sense by chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ [Pā. Sū. 3-4-6 as read]; third person plural, jhi replaced by anta [ending]; loss of the i by itaś ca [Pā. Sū. 3-4-100 as read]; śap the vikaraṇa; guṇa of ṇic and the ay-substitution; loss of the final t of the ending by saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ [Pā. Sū. 8-2-23 as read]; no aṭ, by bahulaṃ chandasy māṅyoge 'pi [Pā. Sū. 6-4-75 as read]; the ṇ for the m of the root is Vedic; or the root raṇa śabdārthe with ṇic and laṅ as before; nighāta accent); śūrasātau (śūraiḥ sātiḥ, in it; the first member keeps its accent in the compound with a third-case first member by tṛtīyā karmaṇi [Pā. Sū. 6-2-48 as read]; locative singular); kṣitayaḥ (root kṣi nivāsagatyoḥ; ktic by ktic ktau ca saṃjñāyām [Pā. Sū. 3-3-174 as read]; acute on the last syllable by citaḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-1-163 as read]; nominative plural); kṛṇvata (root kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca; Vedic laṅ in the present sense; third person plural, jhi; the ātādeśa by ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ [Pā. Sū. 7-1-5 as read]; the vikaraṇa u by dhinvikṛṇvyor a [Pā. Sū. 3-1-80 as read]; a-ending of the root; loss of the a by ato lopaḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-4-48 as read]; yaṇ for the u; nighāta; no aṭ, by bahulaṃ chandasi); trām (root traiṅ pālane; trāyata iti trāḥ; kvip by kvip ca [Pā. Sū. 3-2-76 as read], which applies even to a root without a prefix, the word ca drawing in the sense of dṛśi-; complete loss of the kvip; the root keeps its accent; ā for e by ādeca upadeśe 'śiti [Pā. Sū. 6-1-45 as read], the print breaking off here).

original p. 206

The grammar of Rik 100.7 concludes: trām (ā for e by ādeca upadeśe 'śiti [Pā. Sū. 6-1-45 as read]; accusative singular); karuṇasya (root ḍukṛñ karaṇe; the affix unan in the sense of the action by kyavṛtyādāribhya unan [Uṇ. Sū. 3-53, read in print as 3-[?]3, ?]; guṇa of the root vowel because of the affix; raparatva by uraṇ raparaḥ [Pā. Sū. 1-1-51 as read]; the ṇ of the affix by āṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi [Pā. Sū. 8-4-2 as read]; the first-syllable acute that nit gives is made to stand by vyatyayo bahulam [Pā. Sū. 3-1-85 as read], in the print's words, 'if another accent were attained'); īśe (root īśa aiśvarye, adādi; laṭ, third person singular, ta; e by ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere [Pā. Sū. 3-4-79 as read]; loss of the t of the ending in the Veda by lopas ta ātmanepadeṣu [Pā. Sū. 7-1-41 as read]; the form īśe; nighāta accent because it follows a non-verb). The Rik is closed with ‖ 7 ‖ and a rule of dashes.

Rik 8

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 100.8)

तमप्सन्त शवस उत्सवेषु नरो नरमवसे तं धनाय । सो अन्धे चित्तमसि ज्योतिर्विदन्मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विन्द्र ऊती ॥ ८ ॥

tam apsanta śavasa utsaveṣu naro naram avase taṃ dhanāya | so andhe cit tamasi jyotir vidan marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ‖ 8 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 100.8)

तम् । अप्सन्त । शवसः । उत्ऽसवेषु । नरः । नरम् । अवसे । तम् । धनाय । [the Pada continues on p. 207]

original p. 207

सः । अन्धे । चित् । तमसि । ज्योतिः । विदत् । मरुत्वान् । नः । भवतु । इन्द्रः । ऊती ॥ ८ ॥

tam | apsanta | śavasaḥ | ut-saveṣu | naraḥ | naram | avase | tam | dhanāya | saḥ | andhe | cit | tamasi | jyotiḥ | vidat | marutvān | naḥ | bhavatu | indraḥ | ūtī ‖ 8 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.8)

नरो नेतारः स्तोतारः शवसो बलस्य सम्बन्धिष्वुत्सवेषु संग्रामेषु नरं जयस्य नेतारं तमिन्द्रमप्सन्त । आप्नुवन्ति । किमर्थम् । अवसे । अन्नार्थं रक्षणार्थं वा । तथा धनाय धनार्थं च तमिन्द्रं प्राप्नुवन्ति । यस्मात्स इन्द्रस्तमसि दृष्टिप्रतिबन्धकेऽन्धे चित् आध्यानरहिते [?] चित्तव्यामोहकरेऽपि संग्रामे ज्योतिर्विजयलक्षणं प्रकाशं विदत् । लम्भयति । तस्मात्तमेव प्राप्नुवन्तीत्यर्थः । अप्सन्त । आप्ऌ व्याप्तौ । लङि व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदम् । व्यत्ययेन क्नप्रत्ययः [?] । व्यत्ययेन धातोर्[?]त्वम् [?] । विदत् । विद्ऌ लाभे । छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिट इति वर्तमाने छान्दसो लुङ् । ऌदित्त्वाच्चेरङादेशः [?] । बहुलं छन्दस्यमाङ्योगेऽपीत्यडभावः ॥ naro netāraḥ stotāraḥ śavaso balasya sambandhiṣv utsaveṣu saṃgrāmeṣu naraṃ jayasya netāraṃ tam indram apsanta | āpnuvanti | kimartham | avase | annārthaṃ rakṣaṇārthaṃ vā | tathā dhanāya dhanārthaṃ ca tam indraṃ prāpnuvanti | yasmāt sa indras tamasi dṛṣṭipratibandhake 'ndhe cit ādhyānarahite [?] cittavyāmohakare 'pi saṃgrāme jyotir vijayalakṣaṇaṃ prakāśaṃ vidat | lambhayati | tasmāt tam eva prāpnuvantīty arthaḥ | apsanta | āpḷ vyāptau | laṅi vyatyayenātmanepadam | vyatyayena knapratyayaḥ [?] | vyatyayena dhātor[?]tvam [?] | vidat | vidḷ lābhe | chandasi luṅlaṅliṭa iti vartamāne chāndaso luṅ | ḷdittvāc ceraṅādeśaḥ [?] | bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pīty aḍabhāvaḥ ‖

"The men (naraḥ) — the leaders, the praisers — in the utsavas (battles) of śavas, of strength, apsanta — approach, obtain — that Indra, the man (naram), the leader to victory. For what? Avase — for food, or for protection. And likewise for wealth (dhanāya) they come to that Indra. Because that Indra, in the darkness (tamasi) that obstructs sight, in the blind (andhe cit) — even in a battle that is without clear thought, that causes confusion of mind — obtains [for them] jyotiḥ, the light that has the character of victory, he makes [them] attain: therefore they come to him alone — that is the sense." The grammatical tail is characterized: the root āp 'to attain' with the middle voice in the laṅ by vyatyaya, and two further vyatyaya-changes marked [?]; vidat from the root vid 'to obtain', with the Vedic luṅ in the present sense, and no augment aṭ by bahulaṃ chandasi. Several words are clotted and marked [?].

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"saḥ — Indra; tamasi — in the one that causes pitch darkness; andhe cit — and the one that causes mental confusion, [even in] a (dreadful) battle too; jyotiḥ — light in the form of victory; vidat — he causes [them] to obtain; naraḥ — the devotee-subjects; śavasaḥ — who must show valour; utsaveṣu — in battles; naram — the one who brings victory; tam — that Indra; apsanta — approach (take refuge in); avase — for food or for protection; dhanāya — for wealth also; tam — [that] Indra (they take refuge in); marutvān — together with the Maruts; indraḥ — Indra; naḥ — our; ūtī — for protection; bhavatu — may he be."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"Indra, even in the dreadful battle that causes pitch darkness and mental confusion, gives the light that has the form of victory. The subjects who are his devotees approach that Indra who brings victory in battles that call for valour. And for food or for protection, and for wealth too, they take refuge in him. May Indra, together with the Maruts, be our protector."

original p. 208

English Translation (as printed)

To him, a leader (to victory) his worshippers apply in contests of strength for protection and for wealth, as he grants them the light (of conquest) in the bewildering darkness (of battle) : may Indra, associated with the Maruts be our protection.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.8 (Kannada)

"Two kinds of obstruction, which could not be withstood by the human sacrificers, were created by the Asuras at every step. The first was, by concealing the light of the world, to cause pitch darkness; the second was, by waging deceitful war, to cause confusion of mind in them. The chief thing was that these two came about. In such contexts, in order to help his devotees, Indra, standing straight in front of these deceivers, destroyed them by deceiving them with his own power of illusion, and, by spreading light, benefited the world; and that valorous deed is here described, with a suggestion of gratitude.

Andhe cit — citravyāmohakare 'pi saṃgrāme: even in a battle that causes confusion of mind; jyotir vidat — he grants the light of victory. As the Asuras' power of illusion is extremely strong, it is natural that any warrior, however brave, should be confused. In such contexts it is described, most fittingly, that Indra destroyed those Asuras and also deceived them beyond their own deceit."

अहोहानम् [?] अप आशयानं प्र मायाभिर्मायिनं सक्षदिन्द्रः [?] । ahohānam [?] apa āśayānaṃ pra māyābhir māyinaṃ sakṣad indraḥ [?] | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-30-6 as read [?]; the first word clotted in print, not completed from memory)

"— having overcome Vṛtra, who obstructs the deities and who is exceedingly deceitful, with his own power of illusion; and, when he struck, one fighter after another rose from his body, showing the fury of those who stand against Indra: the context too, in which it is described that even at such hard occasions Indra easily destroyed them all, uprooting them —"

त्यस्य चिन्महतो निर्मृगस्य वधर्जघान तविषीभिरिन्द्रः । य एक इदप्रतिर्मन्यमान आदस्मादन्यो अजनिष्ट तव्यान् ॥ tyasya cin mahato nirmṛgasya vadhar jaghāna taviṣībhir indraḥ | ya eka id apratir manyamāna ād asmād anyo ajaniṣṭa tavyān ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-32-3 as read [?])

निर्जघानायुधं शक्रो वृत्रेण क्षिप्तमोजसा । वृत्रस्य गात्रादन्यो यः प्रादुर्भूतो महासुरः ॥ nirjaghānāyudhaṃ śakro vṛtreṇa kṣiptam ojasā | vṛtrasya gātrād anyo yaḥ prādurbhūto mahāsuraḥ ‖

original p. 209

वृत्रं पूर्वं निहत्येन्द्रो द्वितीयं शुष्णसंज्ञकम् [?] । पुनर्जघानेन्द्र इति पुराभिः कीर्त्येते ऋषिः [?] ॥ vṛtraṃ pūrvaṃ nihatyendro dvitīyaṃ śuṣṇasaṃjñakam [?] | punar jaghānendra iti purābhiḥ kīrtyete ṛṣiḥ [?] ‖

Gloss, editorial and tentative, the print being doubtful: "Mighty Indra struck down the weapon thrown by Vṛtra with his power; [and] the other great Asura who appeared from Vṛtra's body; after first killing Vṛtra, Indra again struck down the second one, named Śuṣṇa" — so it is told.

"— in commenting on the above Ṛk, Sāyaṇa has given these verses by way of introduction (upodghāta). In the same way, when it is said that Indra released the sun that the Asuras were holding fast, and gave light to the worlds which had been covered by darkness —

Tamasi jyotiḥ vidat — even in battles that cause pitch darkness, Indra obtained, for them, the light in the form of victory: so it is said. And in the same way in other places —" Glosses, editorial and tentative: "Indra, winning the heavenly light, bringing forth the days, conquered the battles with the eager ones; he made the banner of the days shine for man; he found the light for the great battle"; "Then, O Indra, you struck down the illusions of Svarbhānu that were working below the sky; Atri found the sun hidden in darkness with the fourth prayer".

यः सूर्यं य उषसं जजान यो अपां नेता स जनास इन्द्रः । yaḥ sūryaṃ ya uṣasaṃ jajāna yo apāṃ netā sa janāsa indraḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-12-7 as read [?])

इन्द्रः स्वर्षा जनयन्नहानि जिगायोशिग्भिः पृतना अभिष्टिः । प्रारोचयन्मनवे केतुमह्नामविन्दज्ज्योतिर्बृहते रणाय ॥ indraḥ svarṣā janayann ahāni jigāyośigbhiḥ pṛtanā abhiṣṭiḥ | prārocayan manave ketum ahnām avindaj jyotir bṛhate raṇāya ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-34-4 as read [?])

स्वर्भानोरध यदिन्द्र माया अवो दिवो वर्तमाना अवाहन् । गूळ्हं सूर्यं तमसापव्रतेन तुरीयेण ब्रह्मणाविन्ददत्रिः ॥ svarbhānor adha yad indra māyā avo divo vartamānā avāhan | gūḷhaṃ sūryaṃ tamasāpavratena turīyeṇa brahmaṇāvindad atriḥ ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-40-6 as read [?])

"— the brilliance of the sun, which had been concealed by Asuras and others, Indra released, and gave light to all the worlds, earth, mid-air and the rest: so his greatness is praised.

Utsaveṣu — saṃgrāmeṣu, 'in battles'; balavatām utsavabhūteṣu saṃgrāmeṣu: in battles that are festivals for the strong. For the strong, battle itself is a source of enthusiasm: so it is counted as an utsava. Skandasvāmin gives one sense for utsaveṣu in this way, and another with abhiṣaveṣu. Explaining the second meaning, he says:"

अथवा उत्सवेष्वित्युच्छब्द अभीत्येतस्य स्थाने । बलस्य सम्बन्धिष्वभिषवेषु । बलेन येषु यज्ञेष्वभिषूयन्ते सोमस्तेष्वित्यर्थः । athavā utsaveṣv ity ucchabda abhīty etasya sthāne | balasya sambandhiṣv abhiṣaveṣu | balena yeṣu yajñeṣv abhiṣūyante somas teṣv ity arthaḥ | (Skandasvāmin, as read)

"— in the word utsaveṣu, the syllable ut is in the place of abhi: 'in the pressings (abhiṣava) connected with strength'; the sacrifices in which Soma is pressed with strength: that is the sense."

Rik 9

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 100.9)

स सव्येन यमति व्राधतश्चित्स दक्षिणे सङ्गृभीता कृतानि । स कीरिणा चित्सनिता धनानि मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विन्द्र ऊती ॥ ९ ॥

sa savyena yamati vrādhataś cit sa dakṣiṇe saṃgṛbhītā kṛtāni | sa kīriṇā cit sanitā dhanāni marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ‖ 9 ‖
