॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 100.9)

सः । सव्येन । यमति । व्राधतः । चित् । सः । दक्षिणे । सम्ऽगृभीता । कृतानि । सः । कीरिणा । चित् । सनिता । धनानि । मरुत्वान् । नः । भवतु । इन्द्रः । ऊती ॥ ९ ॥

saḥ | savyena | yamati | vrādhataḥ | cit | saḥ | dakṣiṇe | saṃ-gṛbhītā | kṛtāni | saḥ | kīriṇā | cit | sanitā | dhanāni | marutvān | naḥ | bhavatu | indraḥ | ūtī ‖ 9 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.9) The print's śatroṇ api stands for śatrūn api [?]. The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read: the causative of yam 'to restrain' with shortening of the penult by mitāṃ hrasvaḥ, loss of ṇi before an ārdhadhātuka; vrādhat (root vradh 'to grow', with the affix ati and the Uṇādi augment ām, acute on the first syllable as belonging to the class vṛṣādi); saṃgṛbhītā (from grah, with the dropping of the vikaraṇa, the samprasāraṇa of r and the change of h to bh, and the lengthening by dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ); sanitā (root ṣaṇu 'to give', with tṛn in the sense of habit); and the prohibition of the genitive by na lokāvyaya… in dhanāni. The words marked [?] are clotted.

स इन्द्रः सव्येन वामहस्तेनैकहस्तेन व्राधतश्चित् हिंसतो महतः शत्रोनपि यमति । नियमयति । तथा स इन्द्रो दक्षिणे दक्षिणपार्श्वस्थेन हस्तेनैकेन यजमानैः कृतानि हवींषि संगृभीता । संगृह्णाति । अपि च स इन्द्रः कीरिणा चित् कीर्तयित्रा स्तोत्रा स्तुतः सन् धनानि सनिता प्रदानशीलो भवति । हविष्मदात्रादामिव स्तोत्रादामपि धनं प्रयच्छतीत्यर्थः । शिष्टं स्पष्टम् ॥ यमति । यमु उपरमे । णिच्चेमन्तः शत्संनित्वे [?] मितां ह्रस्व इति ह्रस्वत्वम् । छन्दस्युभयथेति शप आर्धधातुकत्वाणेरनिटीति णिलोपः । व्राधतः । व्रधु वृद्धौ । अस्मादतिप्रत्ययः । औणादिक आमागमश्च । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । सङ्गृभीता । ग्रह उपादाने । लिटि [?] बहुलं छन्दसीति विकरणस्य लुक् । लिङः सलोप इति सलोपः [?] । ग्रहिज्यादिना सम्प्रसारणम् । हृग्रहोर्भ इति भत्वम् । द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङ इति दीर्घः । सनिता । षणु दाने । ताच्छीलिकस्तृन् । धनानि । न लोकाव्ययेति षष्ठीप्रतिषेधः ॥ sa indraḥ savyena vāmahastenaikahastena vrādhataś cit hiṃsato mahataḥ śatroṇ api yamati | niyamayati | tathā sa indro dakṣiṇe dakṣiṇapārśvasthena hastenaikena yajamānaiḥ kṛtāni havīṃṣi saṃgṛbhītā | saṃgṛhṇāti | api ca sa indraḥ kīriṇā cit kīrtayitrā stotrā stutaḥ san dhanāni sanitā pradānaśīlo bhavati | haviṣmadātrād āmiva stotrād āmapi dhanaṃ prayacchatīty arthaḥ | śiṣṭaṃ spaṣṭam ‖ yamati | yamu uparame | ṇicce mantaḥ śatsaṃnitve [?] mitāṃ hrasva iti hrasvatvam | chandasy ubhayatheti śapa ārdhadhātukatvāṇ ṇer aniṭīti ṇilopaḥ | vrādhataḥ | vradhu vṛddhau | asmād atipratyayaḥ | auṇādika āmāgamaś ca | vṛṣāditvād ādyudāttatvam | saṅgṛbhītā | graha upādāne | liṭi [?] bahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇasya luk | liṅaḥ salopa iti salopaḥ [?] | grahijyādinā samprasāraṇam | hṛgrahor bha iti bhatvam | dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti dīrghaḥ | sanitā | ṣaṇu dāne | tācchīlikas tṛn | dhanāni | na lokāvyayeti ṣaṣṭhīpratiṣedhaḥ ‖

"That Indra, with his savyena — left — hand, with that single hand, restrains (yamati, 'holds in check') even a mighty enemy who is harming (vrādhataḥ cit). And likewise that Indra, with one hand, the one on the right side (dakṣiṇe), saṃgṛbhītā — receives — the oblations made by the sacrificers. And also, when praised by the praiser (kīriṇā cit, 'by one who proclaims'), that Indra is sanitā — disposed to give — dhanāni, wealth: he gives wealth even to the praiser, as to a sacrificer who has oblations. The rest is clear."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada) begun at the foot of p. 211; continues on p. 212

"saḥ — that Indra; savyena — with the left hand; vrādhataś cit — even [an enemy] who is able to do harm, if he is a powerful one; yamati — [he] stops, holds back; saḥ — that same Indra; dakṣiṇe — with the right [hand]; kṛtāni — [havis] offered by the sacrificers —"

original p. 212

"— saṃgṛbhītā — accepts; (and) saḥ — Indra; kīriṇā cit — by the praiser, the devotee, praised; dhanāni — wealth; sanitā — becomes the giver; marutvān — together with the Maruts; indraḥ — Indra; naḥ — our; ūtī — for protection; bhavatu — may he be."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"However strong the enemy who does harm, Indra stops him with his left hand alone. And with his right hand he accepts the oblations offered by the sacrificers. When he is praised by the devotee, he gives wealth to him. May such an Indra, together with the Maruts, be our protector."

English Translation (as printed)

With his left hand he restrains the malignant, with his right he receives the (sacrificial) offerings ; he is the giver of riches, (when propitiated) by one who celebrates his praise : may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.9 (Kannada)

तमूतयो रणयञ्छूरसातौ तं क्षेमस्य क्षितयः कृण्वत त्राम् । स विश्वस्य करुणस्येश एको मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विन्द्र ऊती ॥ tam ūtayo raṇayañ chūrasātau taṃ kṣemasya kṣitayaḥ kṛṇvata trām | sa viśvasya karuṇasyeśa eko marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-100-7 as read — this is Rik 7 of the present sūkta, cited by the author)

"— as described in the preceding Ṛk, in the same way the greatness of Indra, who is at one and the same time the deity of war and the deity of sacrifice, is praised here as well. With one hand Indra can stop an enemy, however strong; with the other hand he accepts the oblations offered at the sacrifices; thereafter he gives wealth freely to his devotees: thus the manifold powers of Indra are described.

Vrādhataś cit — 'vrādhan' is read among the names of mahat' — mahato 'pi śatrūn [Sāyaṇa]: as the bhāṣya-author says, vrādhan is read among the names of 'great'. In general the word mahat is used in the sense 'worshipful', 'honoured'. But since the epithet vrādhan is used mostly with reference to enemies, it comes to mean 'one with exceedingly great power'. It is unusual that this epithet should be applied to deities."

original p. 213

इमे ये ते सु वायो बाह्वोजसोऽन्तर्नदी ते पतयन्त्युक्षणो महि व्राधन्त उक्षणः । ime ye te su vāyo bāhvojaso 'ntar nadī te patayanty ukṣaṇo mahi vrādhanta ukṣaṇaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-134-4 as read [?])

"— here the word vrādhantaḥ, as an adjective of the bulls of Vāyu, in mahi vrādhante means atiprabhūtaṃ vardhamānāḥ, 'growing in great abundance'. And —"

स चन्द्रो विप्र मर्त्यो महो व्राधन्तमो दिवि । sa candro vipra martyo maho vrādhantamo divi | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1[4?]0-3 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk it is an epithet that praises the greatness of the man who worships Agni. Vrādhantamaḥ — pravṛddhatamaḥ | itaradevānām api śreṣṭhaḥ: 'the most grown; the best even among other deities': that is, extremely excellent. Thus, apart from a couple of Ṛks, in all other places it is used as a synonym of 'enemy'."

स व्राधतो नहुषो दंसुजूतः शर्धस्तरो नरां गूर्तश्रवाः । sa vrādhato nahuṣo daṃsujūtaḥ śardhastaro narāṃ gūrtaśravāḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1[1?]3-10 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk, hiṃsakān vā mahato 'pi: 'oppressors, however very strong', is the meaning. And —"

शत्रूयन्तो अभि ये नस्ततस्रे महि व्राधन्त ओगणास इन्द्र । śatrūyanto abhi ye nas tatasre mahi vrādhanta ogaṇāsa indra | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[6?]9-[1?]2 as read [?])

"— in this, vrādhantaḥ = asmān bādhamānāḥ: 'those who afflict us greatly'. So in some other places likewise, the word is used in the sense of an enemy who is extremely powerful, hard to stop and harming; and so, in the present Ṛk too, the sense is: however great the strength of the enemy, he is able to stop him, even in his left hand [alone].

Kīriṇā — kīrtayitrā stotrā: by the praiser, the devotee. Since rebhaḥ, jaritā, kāruḥ and the like are read among the [names] of the praiser (stotṛ) (Ni. 3-1[6?] as read [?]), kīri means 'praiser'. [Another word:] sūrayaḥ kīrayo rudrāḥ [as printed, ?]."

यो रातहव्योऽवृकाय धायसे कीरेश्चिन्मन्त्रं मनसा वनोषि तम् । yo rātahavyo 'vṛkāya dhāyase kīreś cin mantraṃ manasā vanoṣi tam | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-3[1?]-13 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk, for the words kīreḥ cit Sāyaṇa gives 'stotuḥ eva' — 'of the praiser' [as printed stutikāra, ?]; Skandasvāmin too says the same, but [he adds:] yo dāridryāt na yajate [as read, ?]" the sentence continues on the next page

original p. 214

Special Topics of Rik 100.9, concluded from p. 213 (Kannada)

"[Skandasvāmin says] stotraiva [as read, ?], and gives also a sense that suggests poverty. Oldenberg, the English commentator, supporting this same sense, has rendered it, 'Thou acceptest in thy mind the hymn even of the poor' English as printed in the Kannada text. Though the word kīri does not literally mean 'poor', it may be that the praisers who had not the means for performing sacrifices were mostly poor, and that this prayer, which suggests poverty, was therefore made. In the present Ṛk, too, the sense is that Indra, praised by the praiser, gives him wealth and the like; so Indra is praised."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.9) grammar pages, pp. 214–215, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?]

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: yamati (root yamu uparame; since the causative sense is shown, ṇic by hetumati ca [Pā. Sū. 3-1-26 as read]; vṛddhi of the penult by ata upadhāyāḥ [Pā. Sū. 7-2-116 as read]; the root is called mit by the rule janījṛṣknasurañjo 'mantāś ca [as read], since it ends in m; shortening of the penult by mitāṃ hrasvaḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-4-92 as read]; the śap of the laṭ counting as ārdhadhātuka as well by chandasy ubhayathā [Pā. Sū. 6-4-117 as read]; loss of ṇi by ṇer aniṭi [Pā. Sū. 6-4-51 as read]; nighāta accent); vrādhataḥ (root vradhu vṛddhau; the Uṇādi affix ati and the augment ām after the root's last vowel by midaco 'ntyāt paraḥ [Pā. Sū. 1-1-47 as read]; yaṇ; acute on the first syllable by vṛṣādīnāṃ ca [Pā. Sū. 6-1-203 as read]; the case is printed as 'accusative plural', as read); saṃgṛbhītā (root graha upādāne; the third person singular ending in the liṅ-like form; loss of the vikaraṇa by bahulaṃ chandasi; suṭ by suṭ tithoḥ [Pā. Sū. 3-4-107 as read]; sīyuṭ by liṅaḥ sīyuṭ [Pā. Sū. 3-4-102 as read]; loss of the s by liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya [Pā. Sū. 7-2-79 as read]; loss of y by lopo vyor vali [Pā. Sū. 6-1-66 as read]; the affix being treated as ṅit, no guṇa; samprasāraṇa by grahijyāvayi… [Pā. Sū. 6-1-16 as read]; the form gṛhīta; bh for h by hṛgrahor bhaś chandasi [vārttika]; lengthening by dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-3-135 as read]; nighāta).

original p. 215

The grammar of Rik 100.9 concludes: kṛtāni (root ḍukṛñ karaṇe; kta in the passive by niṣṭhā [Pā. Sū. 3-2-102 as read]; acute on the last syllable by the affix; accusative plural); sanitā (root ṣaṇu dāne; s for ṣ by dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-1-64 as read]; tṛn in the sense of habit by tācchīlyārthe [Pā. Sū. 3-2-135 as read]; iṭ by ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ [Pā. Sū. 7-2-35 as read]; the word sanitṛ, as its affix is nit, is acute on the first syllable; nominative singular); dhanāni (in dhanāni sanitā the genitive would be expected by kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti [Pā. Sū. 2-3-65 as read], but, since a word ending in the present-time tṛn is joined, it is prevented by na lokāvyaya… [Pā. Sū. 2-3-69 as read]). The Rik is closed with ‖ 9 ‖ and a rule of dashes.

Rik 10

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 100.10)

स ग्रामेभिः सनिता स रथेभिर्विदे विश्वाभिः कृष्टिभिर्न्वद्य । स पौंस्येभिरभिभूरशस्तीर्मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विन्द्र ऊती ॥ १० ॥

sa grāmebhiḥ sanitā sa rathebhir vide viśvābhiḥ kṛṣṭibhir nv adya | sa pauṃsyebhir abhibhūr aśastīr marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ‖ 10 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 100.10)

सः । ग्रामेभिः । सनिता । सः । रथेभिः । विदे । विश्वाभिः । कृष्टिऽभिः । नु । अद्य । [the Pada continues on p. 216]

original p. 216

सः । पौंस्येभिः । अभिऽभूः । अशस्तीः । मरुत्वान् । नः । भवतु । इन्द्रः । ऊती ॥ १० ॥

saḥ | grāmebhiḥ | sanitā | saḥ | rathebhiḥ | vide | viśvābhiḥ | kṛṣṭi-bhiḥ | nu | adya | saḥ | pauṃsyebhiḥ | abhi-bhūḥ | aśastīḥ | marutvān | naḥ | bhavatu | indraḥ | ūtī ‖ 10 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.10)

स इन्द्रो ग्रामेभिर्मरुत्संघैः सह सनिता फलानां प्रदाता भवति । स चाद्यास्मिन्नहनि नु क्षिप्रं विश्वाभिः कृष्टिभिः सर्वैर्मनुष्यै रथेभिरिन्द्रसम्बन्धिभी रथैः कारणभूतैर्विदे । विज्ञायते । अपि च स इन्द्रः पौंस्येभिः स्वकीयैर्बलैरशस्तीरशंसनीयान् शत्रूनभिभूः । अभिभवन् वर्तते [?] । मरुत्वान्स इन्द्रोऽस्माकं रक्षणाय भवतु ॥ ग्रामेभिः । बहुलं छन्दसीति भिस ऐसभावः । ग्रामादीनां च । फि. २-१४ [?] । इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । विदे । विद ज्ञाने । कर्मणि लट् । बहुलं छन्दसीति विकरणस्य लुक् । लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेष्विति तलोपः ॥ sa indro grāmebhir marutsaṃghaiḥ saha sanitā phalānāṃ pradātā bhavati | sa cādyāsminn ahani nu kṣipraṃ viśvābhiḥ kṛṣṭibhiḥ sarvair manuṣyai rathebhir indrasambandhibhī rathaiḥ kāraṇabhūtair vide | vijñāyate | api ca sa indraḥ pauṃsyebhiḥ svakīyair balair aśastīr aśaṃsanīyān śatrūn abhibhūḥ | abhibhavan vartate [?] | marutvān sa indro 'smākaṃ rakṣaṇāya bhavatu ‖ grāmebhiḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti bhisa aisabhāvaḥ | grāmādīnāṃ ca | Phi. 2-14 [?] | ity ādyudāttatvam | vide | vida jñāne | karmaṇi laṭ | bahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇasya luk | lopas ta ātmanepadeṣv iti talopaḥ ‖

"That Indra, with the grāmas — the Maruts' bands — is sanitā, the giver of fruits. And he, adya — today, nu — quickly, by viśvābhiḥ kṛṣṭibhiḥ — all men — is known (vide) by rathebhiḥ, his chariots, which are the means [of knowing him]. Also that Indra, by his own pauṃsya — strengths — is the conqueror (abhibhūḥ) of aśastīḥ — the unpraiseworthy enemies; [he lives] overcoming [them] [?]. May that Indra, with the Maruts, be for our protection." The grammatical tail is characterized: the instrumental plural grāmebhiḥ with bhis and no ais, and the acute on the first syllable by grāmādīnāṃ ca [Phiṭ-sūtra 2-14, as read [?]]; vide (root vid 'to know', the present passive, the vikaraṇa dropped, and the loss of the t of the ending).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"saḥ — that Indra; grāmebhiḥ — together with his companions the Maruts; sanitā — becomes the giver, a benefactor; saḥ — he; adya — today; nu — in haste, quickly; viśvābhiḥ kṛṣṭibhiḥ — by all men; rathebhiḥ — (with his) chariots (as one mounted on his chariot); vide — is recognized; saḥ — that Indra; pauṃsyebhiḥ — by his [own] strengths; aśastīḥ — the unworthy enemies; abhibhūḥ — he overcomes; marutvān — together with the Maruts; indraḥ — Indra; naḥ — our; ūtī — for protection; bhavatu — may he be."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"Indra, together with his companions the Maruts, is exceedingly beneficent to all as the giver of wealth. All men, too, recognize Indra today as the rider of his chariot. By his prowess that Indra overcomes the enemies who are unworthy. May that Indra, together with the Maruts, be our protector."

English Translation (as printed)

He, along with his attendants, in [sic] a benefactor ; he is quickly recognized by all men to-day, through his chariots ; by his manly energies he is victor over unruly (adversaries) : may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.

original p. 217

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.10 (Kannada)

"Grāmebhiḥ — marutsaṃghaiḥ, 'with the bands of Maruts': 'come together with the groups of the Maruts' — here [Sāyaṇa] has given grāma the sense of saṃgha, 'band'. This word, besides the established meaning 'village' — in which it is used in many Ṛks, such as 1-44-10; 1-1[?]4-1; 10-90-8 [as read [?]] — is used in many places also in the sense of 'band', saṃgha."

यदङ्ग त्वा भरताः संतरेयुर्गव्यन्ग्राम इषित इन्द्रजूतः । yad aṅga tvā bharatāḥ saṃtareyur gavyan grāma iṣita indrajūtaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-33-11 as read [?])

नियुत्वन्तो ग्रामजितो यथा नरोऽर्यमणो न मरुतः कबन्धिनः । niyutvanto grāmajito yathā naro 'ryamaṇo na marutaḥ kabandhinaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-54-8 as read [?])

"— here grāmajitaḥ means 'saṃghātmakasya padārthasya vikleṣayitāraḥ', those who separate a thing that consists of a band, that is, who split apart things joined together; and in the same way —"

अपश्यं ग्रामं वहमानमारादचक्रया स्वधया वर्तमानम् । apaśyaṃ grāmaṃ vahamānam ārād acakrayā svadhayā vartamānam | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-27-19 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these also the sense is 'band'. In the present Ṛk, too, grāmebhiḥ means 'together with the Maruts, who are in the form of a band'.

Rathebhiḥ vide — [he] is known along with his chariots. Because he is the rider of a chariot that moves in the mid-air with exceeding speed, that is furnished with thousands of supports [as read, ?], and that draws all to itself, the sense is that, as soon as they know the distinctive quality of his chariot, they recognize him."

आ यस्मिन्हस्ते नर्या मिमिक्षुरा रथे हिरण्यये रथेष्ठाः । आ रश्मयो गभस्त्योः स्थूरयोराध्वन्नश्वासो वृषणो युजानाः ॥ ā yasmin haste naryā mimikṣur ā rathe hiraṇyaye ratheṣṭhāḥ | ā raśmayo gabhastyoḥ sthūrayor ādhvann aśvāso vṛṣaṇo yujānāḥ ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-29-2 as read [?])

यस्ते रथो मनसो जवीयानेन्द्र तेन सोमपेयाय याहि । yas te ratho manaso javīyān endra tena somapeyāya yāhi | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-112-2 as read [?])

"— as described in many Ṛks like these, he is recognized by all as the rider of a chariot of great attraction.

Viśvābhiḥ kṛṣṭibhiḥ — the word kṛṣṭi means 'races of men'. Just as the Nirukta-author, for pañcakṛṣṭīḥ in the Ṛk 4-3[8?]-10, gives 'pañcajanān' (Ni. 10-31 as read [?]), including all human races in the meaning, so here also the sense is 'by all men'. (The word pañcajana —"

original p. 218

Special Topics of Rik 100.10, continued from p. 217 (Kannada)

"[The word pañcajana] — what the five groups suggested by that word are will be told later, in the explanation of the [thirteenth, as read, ?] Ṛk of this same sūkta). Thus Sāyaṇa's explanation is that Indra is recognized by all men as the rider of a chariot. Skandasvāmin has explained giving a different sense:"

ग्रामेभिः रथेभिरिति द्वितीयार्थे तृतीया । स ग्रामान् सनिता दाता । स एव रथान् । इत्येवमहं विदे जानामि । grāmebhiḥ rathebhir iti dvitīyārthe tṛtīyā | sa grāmān sanitā dātā | sa eva rathān | ity evam ahaṃ vide jānāmi | (Skandasvāmin, as read)

"— [that is: in grāmebhiḥ rathebhiḥ the third case stands in the sense of the second; 'he is the giver of villages, and of chariots; thus I know']. These two words grāmebhiḥ, rathebhiḥ are in the third case, but they must be given the sense of the second case: 'I know that Indra gives villages and chariots.' If it is explained thus, the word grāma does not have the sense of 'band', but only 'village'. But in this context Sāyaṇa's explanation appears the more fitting.

Pauṃsyebhiḥ — the word pauṃsya is read among the names of strength and among the names of battle (Ni. 2-[9?] as read [?]); here it means 'by strengths'.

Aśastīḥ — aśasaḥ, aśastīḥ: these are words that are synonyms of 'enemy':"

शंसन्ति स्तुवन्तीति शसः स्तोतारः । ते न भवन्तीत्यशसः नृशंसाः [?] । śaṃsanti stuvantīti śasaḥ stotāraḥ | te na bhavantīty aśasaḥ nṛśaṃsāḥ [?] |

"— those who praise are śasaḥ, praisers; those who are not such are aśasaḥ, [cruel to men, as read [?]]: enemies who have fallen away from [sacrificial] rites. They may be Asuras, or they may be men fallen away from rites. Such unworthy enemies Indra abhibhūḥ — overcomes."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.10) grammar pages, pp. 218–219, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?]

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: grāmebhiḥ (the word grāma, instrumental plural, bhis following; ais does not arise by bahulaṃ chandasi [Pā. Sū. 7-1-10 as read]; e by bahuvacane jhaly et [Pā. Sū. 7-3-103 as read]; s → ru → visarga; acute on the first syllable by grāmādīnāṃ ca [Phiṭ-sūtra 2-[?]4 as read, ?]; likewise rathebhiḥ); vide (root vida jñāne; laṭ in the passive, third person singular, ta; the vikaraṇa dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi; e for the ṭi of the ending by ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere [Pā. Sū. 3-4-79 as read]; loss of the t of the ending by lopas ta ātmanepadeṣu [Pā. Sū. 7-1-41 as read]; since it stands at the beginning of the pāda no nighāta; final acute by the affix); kṛṣṭibhiḥ (root kṛṣa vilekhane; ktic by ktic ktau ca saṃjñāyām [Pā. Sū. 3-3-174 as read]; acute on the last syllable by citaḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-1-163 as read]; ṭ for the affix's t by the ṣṭutva rule; instrumental plural); pauṃsyebhiḥ (as before, no ais; e).

original p. 219

The grammar of Rik 100.10 concludes: aśastīḥ (root śaṃsu stutau; ktin in the passive, in the feminine, by striyāṃ ktin [Pā. Sū. 3-3-94 as read]; because the affix is kit, the nasal of the penult is lost by aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti [Pā. Sū. 6-4-24 as read]; the form śastiḥ; na śastiḥ aśastiḥ, a negative tatpuruṣa; the accent of the first member kept, as it is an indeclinable, by tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā… [Pā. Sū. 6-2-2 as read]; accusative plural); abhibhūḥ (abhi bhavati iti abhibhūḥ; kvip by kvip ca; the accent of the last member by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt [Pā. Sū. 6-2-139 as read]). The Rik is closed with ‖ 10 ‖ and a printed ornament.

Rik 11

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 100.11)

स जामिभिर्यत्समजाति मीळ्हेऽजामिभिर्वा पुरुहूत एवैः । अपां तोकस्य तनयस्य जेषे मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विन्द्र ऊती ॥ ११ ॥

sa jāmibhir yat samajāti mīḷhe 'jāmibhir vā puruhūta evaiḥ | apāṃ tokasya tanayasya jeṣe marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ‖ 11 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 100.11)

सः । जामिऽभिः । यत् । सम्ऽअजाति । मीळ्हे । अजामिऽभिः । वा । पुरुऽहूतः । एवैः । अपाम् । तोकस्य । तनयस्य । जेषे । मरुत्वान् । नः । भवतु । इन्द्रः । ऊती ॥ ११ ॥

saḥ | jāmi-bhiḥ | yat | sam-ajāti | mīḷhe | ajāmi-bhiḥ | vā | puru-hūtaḥ | evaiḥ | apām | tokasya | tanayasya | jeṣe | marutvān | naḥ | bhavatu | indraḥ | ūtī ‖ 11 ‖

original p. 220

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.11)

पुरुहूतो बहुभिर्यजमानैराहूतः स इन्द्रो मीळ्हे संग्रामे । मीळ्हमिति धननाम । तद्धेतुत्वात्संग्रामोऽपि मीळ्हशब्देनोच्यते । जामिभिर्बन्धुभिरजामिभिर्वा बान्धवरहितैर्वा एवैर्मरुद्भिः सह युद्धार्थं यद्यदा समजाति सङ्गच्छते । तेषामुभयविधानामपां [?] इन्द्रं प्राप्नुवतां पुरुषाणां तोकस्य पुत्रस्य तनयस्य च तत्पुत्रस्य च जेषे जयप्राप्तये स इन्द्रो भवति । किमु वक्तव्यमस्माकं स्तोतृत्वमानां जयो भवतीति । अन्यत्स्पष्टम् ॥ समजाति । अज गतिक्षेपणयोः । लेट्यडागमः । जेषे । जि जये । औणादिकः सप्रत्ययः । चतुर्थ्यर्थे सप्तमी । यद्वा । जेषृ [?] गतौ । क्विप् चेति क्विप् । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् ॥ puruhūto bahubhir yajamānair āhūtaḥ sa indro mīḷhe saṃgrāme | mīḷham iti dhananāma | taddhetutvāt saṃgrāmo 'pi mīḷhaśabdenocyate | jāmibhir bandhubhir ajāmibhir vā bāndhavarahitair vā evair marudbhiḥ saha yuddhārthaṃ yadyadā samajāti saṅgacchate | teṣām ubhayavidhānām apāṃ [?] indraṃ prāpnuvatāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ tokasya putrasya tanayasya ca tatputrasya ca jeṣe jayaprāptaye sa indro bhavati | kimu vaktavyam asmākaṃ stotṛtvamānāṃ jayo bhavatīti | anyat spaṣṭam ‖ samajāti | aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ | leṭy aḍāgamaḥ | jeṣe | ji jaye | auṇādikaḥ sapratyayaḥ | caturthyarthe saptamī | yadvā | jeṣṛ [?] gatau | kvip ceti kvip | sāv ekāca iti vibhakter udāttatvam ‖

"Puruhūtaḥ — called by many sacrificers, that Indra, in mīḷhe — in battle. Mīḷha is a name of wealth; because battle is the cause of it, battle too is called by the word mīḷha. Jāmibhiḥ — with kinsmen, or ajāmibhiḥ — with those without kinsmen, together with the Maruts, 'who go' (evaiḥ), whenever he goes forth (samajāti) for battle: for the people of both kinds who have reached Indra, for their son (tokasya), their grandson (tanayasya) and their son's son, for the winning of victory (jeṣe) that Indra becomes [the means]. What need to say, then, that victory is for us who are praisers! The rest is clear." The grammatical tail is characterized: the form samajāti from the root aja 'to drive, to cast' with the leṭ and aḍāgama; jeṣe from ji 'to conquer' with an Uṇādi affix, a locative used for the dative; or from a root jeṣṛ [?] 'to go', with kvip; accent on the ending by sāv ekāca. The word apām at the head of the bhāṣya's list is read as printed [?].

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"puruhūtaḥ — Indra, who is called by many sacrificers; saḥ — Indra; mīḷhe — in the battle (that is the root cause of wealth); jāmibhiḥ — with kinsmen, be it; ajāmibhiḥ vā — or with those who are not kinsmen; evaiḥ — (those who go to battle) with the Maruts; yat — whenever; samajāti — [he] joins [them]; apām — [all] those who join [him] and obtain [his] protection; tokasya — to their sons; tanayasya — and to their grandsons; jeṣe — he becomes the giver of victory; marutvān — together with the Maruts; indraḥ — Indra; naḥ — our; ūtī — for protection; bhavatu — may he be."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"Indra, who is called by many sacrificers for help, in the battle that is the root cause of wealth, whenever he joins his kinsmen, or those who are not his kinsmen, together with the Maruts who go to battle, then, to those who gain Indra's protection, and to their sons and grandsons, he becomes the giver of victory. May Indra, together with the Maruts, be our protector."

English Translation (as printed)

Invoked by many, he goes to battle with his kinsmen, or with (followers) not of his kindred ; he secures the (triumph) of those who trust in him, and of their sons and grandsons : may Indra associated with the Maruts, be our protection.

original p. 221

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.11 (Kannada)

"The idea that, for those who gain Indra's protection, victory in battle is assured, whether they are kinsmen or not, is plainly shown in this Ṛk.

Mīḷhe — since raṇaḥ, vivāk and the like are read among the [forty-six, as read, ?] names of battle (Ni. 2-[?] as read [?]), the sense is 'in battle'."

बाधसे जनान्वृषभेव मन्युना घृषौ मीळ्ह ऋचीषमः । bādhase janān vṛṣabheva manyunā ghṛṣau mīḷha ṛcīṣamaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-46-4 as read [?])

असर्जि कलशाँ अभि मीळ्हे सप्तिर्न वाजयुः । asarji kalaśāṃ abhi mīḷhe saptir na vājayuḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-106-13 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these, as the word mīḷhe has the sense 'in battle', so here too the sense is 'in battle'. According to the classification in the Nirukta this word comes to have the meaning 'battle' directly. Even so, Sāyaṇa has given an explanation showing the sense that has come down by tradition: 'mīḷham iti dhananāma | taddhetutvāt saṃgrāmo 'pi mīḷhaśabdenocyate' — he has said that, mīḷha being a name of wealth, since battle is the cause of wealth the word is also used for battle. In the Nirukta this word is included in both lists, the names of wealth and the names of battle (Ni. 2-[?] as read [?]).

Jāmibhiḥ —"

जामीरन्येऽस्यां जनयन्ति जामुपत्वम् [?] । जमतीर्वा स्यान्निगमनप्रायाः भवति [?] । jāmīr anye 'syāṃ janayanti jāmupatvam [?] | jamatīr vā syān nigamanaprāyāḥ bhavati [?] | (Ni. 3-6 as read [?]; clotted in the print)

"— with the idea 'others cause offspring to be born in her', and from the root jan, which gives the sense 'to be born', the title jāmi is derived in one way; or, with the idea 'she who goes to her husband's house', and from the root jam, which gives the sense 'to go', the title jāmi is derived in another way. By both explanations, it is known from the Nirukta-author's derivation that the word jāmi means 'sister' (sahodari). Supporting this meaning —"

न जामये तान्वो रिक्थमारैक्चकार गर्भं सनितुर्निधानम् । na jāmaye tānvo rikthām āraik cakāra garbhaṃ sanitur nidhānam | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-31-2 as read [?]; the print's tānvo rikthamāraik followed as printed)

"— quoting this Ṛk [the Nirukta-author] explains jāmi as 'sister'. In the same way —" Glosses, editorial and tentative: "He does not leave the [father's] inheritance to a sister…; the embryo, the deposit of the giver"; "O Uṣas, sister of Bhaga, kin of Varuṇa, O truthful one, speak first!".

भगस्य स्वसा वरुणस्य जामिरुषः सूनृते प्रथमा जरस्व । bhagasya svasā varuṇasya jāmir uṣaḥ sūnṛte prathamā jarasva | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-123-5 as read [?])

original p. 222

Special Topics of Rik 100.11, continued from p. 221 (Kannada)

"In Ṛks like these also the word jāmi has just the sense 'sister'. But in the present Ṛk the sense of jāmi is more extended: it means 'kinsmen'. Jāmibhiḥ, ajāmibhir vā — with kinsmen, or with those who are not kinsmen: that is the sense. In the same way in many other Ṛks too this extended meaning is seen. For example —"

जामिः सिन्धूनां भ्रातेव स्वस्रामिभ्यान्न राजा वनान्यत्ति । jāmiḥ sindhūnāṃ bhrāteva svasrām ibhyān na rājā vanāny atti | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-65-[2/4?] as read [?])

कस्ते जामिर्जनानामग्ने को दाश्वध्वरः । kas te jāmir janānām agne ko dāśvadhvaraḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[2?]3-3 as read [?])

"— in these Ṛks too the sense is 'kinsmen', as in this Ṛk. Besides the above two senses, the word jāmi is also used as a synonym of 'fingers'. For example —" Glosses, editorial and tentative: "Like a brother of the rivers, like [a king consuming forest] of the sisters"; "Who is your kinsman among men, O Agni, who has done the sacrifice for you?"; "This bull, roaring, held by the ten fingers"; "The shoot, adorned with barley, held by men, is joined by the fingers; the head is guarded".

एष वृषा कनिक्रददशभिर्जामिभिर्यतः । eṣa vṛṣā kanikradad daśabhir jāmibhir yataḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-[3?]9-4 as read [?])

अंशुर्यवेन पिपिशे यतो नृभिः सं जामिभिर्नसते रक्षते शिरः । aṃśur yavena pipiśe yato nṛbhiḥ saṃ jāmibhir nasate rakṣate śiraḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-68-4 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these, for the word jāmi the meaning is 'fingers'.

Evyaiḥ — yuddhārthaṃ gacchadbhiḥ marudbhiḥ saha: with the Maruts who go to battle. The special character of the word evyaiḥ as used of the Maruts was told in the explanation of the third Ṛk of this sūkta [as read, ?].

Yat evyaiḥ samajāti — 'whenever he joins with the Maruts who go for battle': it is said so because, in battle, when the Maruts help Indra, victory is unfailing; hence victory comes easily to all who gain Indra's protection: that is the sense."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.11) grammar pages, pp. 222–223, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?]

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: samajāti (the preverb sam; root aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ; leṭ, third person singular, tip; aṭ by leṭo 'ḍāṭau [Pā. Sū. 3-4-94 as read]; the form ajāti; because the relative yat is related to it earlier, the nighāta accent is prevented by yadvṛttān nityam [Pā. Sū. 8-1-66 as read]; since tip is pit it is unaccented, and the root's accent remains; since the finite verb retains an acute, the preverb sam gets the nighāta accent by the rule beginning tiṅ ca… [Pā. Sū. 8-1-71 as read]); evyaiḥ (root iṇ gatau; van by iṇśīṅbhyāṃ van [Uṇ. Sū. 1-150 as read]; guṇa by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ [Pā. Sū. 7-3-84 as read]; acute on the first syllable, the affix being nit; instrumental plural).

original p. 223

The grammar of Rik 100.11 concludes: apām (the word ap is always feminine and plural; genitive plural; the ending acute by ūḍidaṃpadādi [Pā. Sū. 6-1-171 as read]); jeṣe (root ji jaye; the Uṇādi affix sa; guṇa because of the affix; ṣ for s by ādeśapratyayayoḥ [Pā. Sū. 8-3-59 as read], the i being the cause; a locative in the sense of the dative, 'since the kārakas arise as the speaker intends'; or from the root jeṣṛ gatau [as read, ?] with kvip by kvip ca, with total loss, the form jyeṣ; dative singular, with the ending ṅe standing as e; acute on the ending by sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-1-168 as read]). The Rik is closed with ‖ 11 ‖ and a rule of dashes.

Rik 12

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 100.12)

स वज्रभृद्दस्युहा भीम उग्रः सहस्रचेताः शतनीथ ऋभ्वा । चम्रीषो न शवसा पाञ्चजन्यो मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विन्द्र ऊती ॥ १२ ॥

sa vajrabhṛd dasyuhā bhīma ugraḥ sahasracetāḥ śatanītha ṛbhvā | camrīṣo na śavasā pāñcajanyo marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ‖ 12 ‖

original p. 224

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 100.12)

सः । वज्रऽभृत् । दस्युऽहा । भीमः । उग्रः । सहस्रऽचेताः । शतऽनीथः । ऋभ्वा । चम्रीषः । न । शवसा । पाञ्चऽजन्यः । मरुत्वान् । नः । भवतु । इन्द्रः । ऊती ॥ १२ ॥

saḥ | vajra-bhṛt | dasyu-hā | bhīmaḥ | ugraḥ | sahasra-cetāḥ | śata-nīthaḥ | ṛbhvā | camrīṣaḥ | na | śavasā | pāñca-janyaḥ | marutvān | naḥ | bhavatu | indraḥ | ūtī ‖ 12 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.12)

स इन्द्रो वज्रभृत् अन्यैर्भर्तुमशक्यस्य वज्रस्य भर्ता । दस्युहा दस्यूनामुपक्षपयितॄणामसुराणां हन्ता । भीमः सर्वेषां भयहेतुः उग्र उद्गूर्णतेजाः सहस्रचेता बहुविधज्ञानः । सर्वज्ञ इत्यर्थः । शतनीथो बहुस्तुतिर्बहुविधप्रापको वा ऋभ्वा उरु भासमानो महान् चम्रीषो न चम्रा चमसे रसात्मनावस्थितः सोम इव शवसा बलेन पाञ्चजन्यः । गन्धर्वा अप्सरसो देवा असुरा रक्षांसि पञ्च जनाः । निषादपञ्चमाश्चत्वारो वर्णा वा । तेषु रक्षकत्वेन भवः । एवंभूतः स मरुत्वानिन्द्रो नोऽस्माकं रक्षणाय भवतु ॥ दस्युहा । बहुलं छन्दसीति हन्तेः क्विप् । भीमः । ञिभी भये । भीमादयोऽपादाने । पा. ३-४-७४ । इत्यपादाने भियः षुग्भा उ. १-१४४ [?] । इति मक् । शतनीथः । नीञ् प्रापणे । हनिकुषिनीरमिकाशिभ्यः क्थन् । उ. २-२ [?] । इति क्थन्प्रत्ययः । चम्रीषः । ईष गतौ । चम्रामीषति गच्छतीति चम्रीषः । इगुपधलक्षणः कप्रत्ययः । वर्णव्यापत्त्या रेफो दीर्घश्च । यद्वा चमेरौणादिक ईषन्प्रत्ययः । पूर्ववद्रेफः । पाञ्चजन्यः । भवार्थे बहिर्देवपञ्चजनेभ्यश्चेति वक्तव्यम् । का. ४-३-५८-१ [?] । इति ञ्यप्रत्ययः । ञित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥ sa indro vajrabhṛt anyair bhartum aśakyasya vajrasya bhartā | dasyuhā dasyūnām upakṣapayitṝṇām asurāṇāṃ hantā | bhīmaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhayahetuḥ ugra udgūrṇatejāḥ sahasracetā bahuvidhajñānaḥ | sarvajña ity arthaḥ | śatanītho bahustutir bahuvidhaprāpako vā ṛbhvā uru bhāsamāno mahān camrīṣo na camrā camase rasātmanāvasthitaḥ soma iva śavasā balena pāñcajanyaḥ | gandharvā apsaraso devā asurā rakṣāṃsi pañca janāḥ | niṣādapañcamāś catvāro varṇā vā | teṣu rakṣakatvena bhavaḥ | evaṃbhūtaḥ sa marutvān indro no 'smākaṃ rakṣaṇāya bhavatu ‖ dasyuhā | bahulaṃ chandasīti hanteḥ kvip | bhīmaḥ | ñibhī bhaye | bhīmādayo 'pādāne | Pā. 3-4-74 | ity apādāne bhiyaḥ ṣugbhā U. 1-144 [?] | iti mak | śatanīthaḥ | nīñ prāpaṇe | hanikuṣinīramikāśibhyaḥ kthan | U. 2-2 [?] | iti kthanpratyayaḥ | camrīṣaḥ | īṣa gatau | camrām īṣati gacchatīti camrīṣaḥ | igupadhalakṣaṇaḥ kapratyayaḥ | varṇavyāpattyā repho dīrghaś ca | yadvā camer auṇādika īṣanpratyayaḥ | pūrvavad rephaḥ | pāñcajanyaḥ | bhavārthe bahirdevapañcajanebhyaś ceti vaktavyam | Kā. 4-3-58-1 [?] | iti ñyapratyayaḥ | ñittvād ādyudāttatvam ‖

"That Indra is vajrabhṛt — the bearer of the thunderbolt which others cannot bear. Dasyuhā — the slayer of the Dasyus, the Asuras who cause destruction. Bhīmaḥ — the cause of fear to all; ugraḥ — of upraised splendour; sahasracetāḥ — of manifold knowledge, that is, all-knowing; śatanīthaḥ — much praised, or one who bestows many kinds of things; ṛbhvā — shining widely, great; camrīṣo na — like Soma that is present in the cup (camasa) as juice; śavasā — with strength; pāñcajanyaḥ — the five peoples: Gandharvas, Apsarases, gods, Asuras and Rākṣasas; or the four castes with the Niṣāda as the fifth: he is the protector among them. Such an Indra, accompanied by the Maruts — may he be for our protection." The grammatical tail is characterized: the forms dasyuhā, bhīmaḥ (mak from bhī by an Uṇādi rule), śatanīthaḥ (kthan by hanikuṣinīramikāśibhyaḥ), camrīṣaḥ (root īṣ 'to go', with ka by igupadha…, with letter-interchange; or an Uṇādi īṣan from cam) and pāñcajanyaḥ (ñya by a Kāśikā statement on bahirdevapañcajanebhyaś ca). The Pāṇini and Uṇādi numerals and some clotted words are read as given [?].

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"saḥ — that Indra; vajrabhṛt — the bearer of the thunderbolt weapon (which cannot be borne by others); dasyuhā — the destroyer of the Rākṣasas who have the form of robbers; bhīmaḥ — the fearful; ugraḥ — the one with fierce splendour; sahasracetāḥ — the one with manifold knowledge (the all-knowing); śatanīthaḥ — the one who is praised in many ways, or the one who makes many kinds of things be obtained; ṛbhvā —" continues on p. 225

original p. 225

"[ṛbhvā —] the one of great splendour; camrīṣo na — like the Soma-juice that is in the cup (camasa); śavasā — with strength; pāñcajanyaḥ — the one who is the protector of the five groups beginning with the Gandharvas, or of the four castes together with the Niṣāda; marutvān — together with the Maruts; indraḥ — Indra; naḥ — our; ūtī — for protection; bhavatu — may he be."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"That Indra holds the exceedingly mighty thunderbolt weapon; is the destroyer of the Rākṣasas who have the form of robbers; is the terrifying one, of fierce splendour; of manifold knowledge; one who accepts many kinds of praise; highly powerful; and, with strength of exceeding excellence like the Soma in the cup, is the protector of all the gods and Asuras, from the Gandharvas on, and also of the people of the five classes beginning with the Brāhmaṇas. May such an Indra, together with the Maruts, be our protector."

English Translation (as printed)

He is the wielder of the thunderbolt, the slayer of robbers, fearful and fierce, knowing many things, much eulogized, and mighty, and, like the Soma juice, inspiring the five classes of beings with vigour : may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.12 (Kannada)

"In this Ṛk two kinds of power of Indra are described together. The first is the power that is terrifying, of fierce splendour, and that destroys the Dasyus; the second is the power that is highly splendid and that protects the pāñcajanyas. Because of this incomparable greatness Indra is praised by the epithets sahasracetāḥ, śatanīthaḥ, ṛbhvā and the like. This twofold power — terrifying toward the wicked and protecting toward the good, and spreading knowledge by dispelling darkness — is described in the Śrutis, Smṛtis and the rest, in all contexts, in words and ideas suited to those contexts. That this twofold greatness and brilliance becomes manifest in Indra alone is described in many parts of the Ṛksaṃhitā; in this Ṛk, too, that point is set out.

Dasyuhā — the destroyer of the dasyu. Dasyu means the Asuras, Piśācas and the like, who cause decay. From the word deva, which in that sense has [the senses] expansive, illuminating, giving (Ni. 7-15 as read [?]), whatever sense appears — the opposite of all of that: destructive, blind [—"

original p. 226

Special Topics of Rik 100.12, continued from p. 225 (Kannada)

"[…the opposite of all of that: destructive, blind,] causing darkness, and violent — such senses the word dasyu shows. [The Nirukta:] dasyur dasyateḥ kṣayārthād upadasyanty asmin rasāḥ upadāsayati karmāṇi (Ni. 7-23 as read [?]) [as read, doubtful [?]]: from the root das (upakṣaye), which gives the sense 'to cause to waste away', the dasyu is known as one who makes the groups of cows and the like dry up and who destroys the sacrificial acts and the like. Vṛtra and the other Asuras all belong to this group of dasyus. Those who stop the flow of the waters and conceal the light — by their deeds Indra destroyed them, made the waters flow, and spread the light. Therefore Indra is praised in many places as dasyuhā. The word dasyu is used in many places as a synonym of the Asuras, but in some places this word is also used of men who are without rites (karmahīna). For example —"

त्वं ह नु त्यददमायो दस्यूँरेकः कृष्टीरवनोरार्याय । tvaṃ ha nu tyad adamāyo dasyūm̐r ekaḥ kṛṣṭīr avanor āryāya | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-18-3 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these, dasyūn means 'people without rites'. Because Indra killed both such enemies, Vṛtra and the like, and the dasyus who are without rites, Indra has the epithet dasyuhā."

कुवित्सस्य प्र हि व्रजं गोमन्तं दस्युहा गमत् । kuvit sasya pra hi vrajaṃ gomantaṃ dasyuhā gamat | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-45-24 as read [?])

अनु त्वा रोदसी उभे क्रक्षमाणमकृपेताम् । इन्द्र यद्दस्युहाभवः ॥ anu tvā rodasī ubhe krakṣamāṇam akṛpetām | indra yad dasyuhābhavaḥ ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-86-11 as read [?])

दस्युहनं पूर्भिदमिन्द्र सत्यमस्मभ्यं चित्रं वृषणं रयिं दाः । dasyuhanaṃ pūrbhidam indra satyam asmabhyaṃ citraṃ vṛṣaṇaṃ rayiṃ dāḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-47-4 as read [?])

"— in many Ṛks like these, Indra's power, and the protection of the world that came from the slaying of the dasyus, are made known.

Bhīmaḥ, ugraḥ — since Indra, as soon as he was born, took on the form of the war-deity and showed his incomparable valour, the description that the earth and the sky, with the mountains and the rest, trembled shows the greatness of Indra."

अस्येदु भिया गिरयश्च दृळ्हा द्यावा च भूमा जनुषस्तुजेते । asyed u bhiyā girayaś ca dṛḷhā dyāvā ca bhūmā januṣas tujete | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-61-14 as read [?]; the same Ṛk as quoted on p. 170)

तव त्विषो जनिमन्रेजत द्यौरेजद्भूमिर्भियसा स्वस्य मन्योः । tava tviṣo janiman rejata dyaur ejad bhūmir bhiyasā svasya manyoḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-17-2 as read [?])

original p. 227

क्रन्दद्विश्वानि भुवनानि वज्रिन् द्यावा रेजेते पृथिवी च भीषा । krandad viśvāni bhuvanāni vajrin dyāvā rejete pṛthivī ca bhīṣā | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-4[?]-1[?] as read [?])

"— Ṛks like these describe Indra's terrifying nature and his fierceness.

Sahasracetāḥ — bahuvidhajñānaḥ, sarvajña ity arthaḥ: 'one of manifold knowledge', that is, one who knows everything."

त्वं विश्वस्य जगतश्चक्षुरिन्द्रासि चक्षुषः । tvaṃ viśvasya jagataś cakṣur indrāsi cakṣuṣaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-103-1[?] as read [?])

"— as described in Ṛks like these, since Indra alone is the eye of the whole world, he is praised as all-knowing.

Śatanīthaḥ — bahustutir bahuvidhaprāpako vā: one who is praised in many ways, or one who obtains many kinds of desired things.

Ṛbhvā — uru bhāsamānaḥ mahān vā: shining exceedingly, or great.

Pāñcajanyaḥ — gandharvā apsaraso devā asurā rakṣāṃsi pañca janāḥ | niṣādapañcamāś catvāro varṇā vā: Gandharvas, Apsarases, gods, Asuras and Rākṣasas — five groups; or the four castes with the Niṣādas, the hunter tribe, as the fifth: so Sāyaṇa explains. In this classification there are differences of view. The Nirukta-author, saying that it is not his own view, tells only the views of others:"

पञ्चजनाः (मम होत्रं जुषध्वम्) गन्धर्वाः पितरो देवा असुरा रक्षांसीत्येके । चत्वारो वर्णा निषादः पञ्चम इत्यौपमन्यवः । pañca janāḥ (mama hotraṃ juṣadhvam) gandharvāḥ pitaro devā asurā rakṣāṃsīty eke | catvāro varṇā niṣādaḥ pañcama ity aupamanyavaḥ | (Ni. 3-8 as read [?])

"— 'the Gandharvas, Pitṛs, gods, Asuras and Rākṣasas are the five peoples,' say some; 'the four castes, with the Niṣāda as fifth,' say Aupamanyava and the others: [the Nirukta-author] has told only the views of others.

In former times all the gods, addressing Agni, prayed that the oblation offered for them in the sacrifice be accepted and shared with all; and Agni agreed to that:"

तदद्य वाचः प्रथमं मसीय येनासुराँ अभि देवा असाम । ऊर्जाद उत यज्ञियासः पञ्च जना मम होत्रं जुषध्वम् ॥ tad adya vācaḥ prathamaṃ masīya yenāsurāṃ abhi devā asāma | ūrjāda uta yajñiyāsaḥ pañca janā mama hotraṃ juṣadhvam ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-53-4 as read [?])

original p. 228

"[This question — whether] the five peoples (pañcajana) too should enjoy this oblation — was answered in this sentence; and the author of the Bṛhaddevatā quoted it and discussed who the pañcajanas are, showing the differences of opinion:"

प्रत्युवाचाथ तान्नग्निर्विश्वेदेवा यदोचत माम् । तत्करिष्ये जुषन्तां तु होत्रं पञ्चजना मम ॥ pratyuvācātha tān agnir viśvedevā yad ocata mām | tat kariṣye juṣantāṃ tu hotraṃ pañcajanā mama ‖ (Bṛ. De. 7-66 as read [?])

"— in this verse Agni told the answer to the gods, and afterwards explained the word pañcajana:"

शालामुख्यः प्रणीतश्च पुत्रो गृहपतेश्च यः । उत्तरो दक्षिणश्चाग्निरेते पञ्चजनाः स्मृताः ॥ śālāmukhyaḥ praṇītaś ca putro gṛhapateś ca yaḥ | uttaro dakṣiṇaś cāgnir ete pañcajanāḥ smṛtāḥ ‖ (Bṛ. De. 7-62 as read [?])

"— that is: the fire at the entrance part of the hall, the Āhavanīya fire that is carried forward, the Gārhapatya fire, which is the son of the sacrificer, and the southern and northern fires: these five kinds of fires are held to be the five classes — a usage that is traditional; this is one view. Besides —"

मनुष्याः पितरो देवा गन्धर्वोरगराक्षसाः । गन्धर्वाः पितरो देवा असुरा यक्षराक्षसाः ॥ manuṣyāḥ pitaro devā gandharvoragarākṣasāḥ | gandharvāḥ pitaro devā asurā yakṣarākṣasāḥ ‖ (Bṛ. De. 7-6[8?] as read [?])

"By the first view, the serpents (uraga) and the Rākṣasas make up one group; by the second, the Yakṣas and the Rākṣasas make up one group."

यास्कौपमन्यवावेतानाहतुः पञ्च वै जनान् । निषादपञ्चमान् वर्णान् मन्यते शाकटायनः ॥ yāskaupamanyavāv etān āhatuḥ pañca vai janān | niṣādapañcamān varṇān manyate śākaṭāyanaḥ ‖ (Bṛ. De. 7-69 as read [?])

"The view of Yāska [is stated] first, says the author of the Bṛhaddevatā in this sentence. [Yāska] did not make his own view clear in the Nirukta beyond telling the views of others; probably he too accepted that."

ऋत्विजो यजमानं च शाकपूणिस्तु मन्यते । ṛtvijo yajamānaṃ ca śākapūṇis tu manyate | (Bṛ. De. 7-70 as read [?])

"The view of Śākapūṇi: the four priests beginning with the Hotṛ, together with the sacrificer, make five groups."

original p. 229

चक्षुः श्रोत्रं [print: श्रोतं] मनो वाक् च प्राणश्चेत्यात्मवादिनः । गन्धर्वाप्सरसो देवा मनुष्याः पितरस्तथा ॥ सर्पाश्च ब्राह्मणे चैव श्रूयन्ते ह्यैतरेयिके । cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ [print: śrotaṃ] mano vāk ca prāṇaś cety ātmavādinaḥ | gandharvāpsaraso devā manuṣyāḥ pitaras tathā ‖ sarpāś ca brāhmaṇe caiva śrūyante hy aitareyike | (Bṛ. De. 7-7[?] as read [?]; and Ai. Brā. 3-[?]1-5 as read [?])

"Eye, ear, mind, speech and breath: these five are the pañcajanas, hold the ātmavādins [those who speak of the Self, the adhyātma view]; the Gandharvas and the rest are set out in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (Ai. Brā. 3-[?]1-5 as read [?]). 'Let such pañcajanas too enjoy the oblation': Agni gave this answer to the gods; and in the explanation of the Bṛhaddevatā too differences of opinion were pointed out in this way.

In this Ṛk in question, where Indra is the protector of the pāñcajanyas, Indra's greatness is described. Since all the worlds are included in Indra's protection, the word pāñcajanya will fit all the opinions given above."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.12) grammar pages, begun on p. 229, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?]

Grammar page, noted briefly. It treats: vajrabhṛt (vajraṃ bibharti iti vajrabhṛt; root ḍubhṛñ bharaṇe; kvip when the word vajra is the first member; the augment tuk after the short vowel of a root before a pit kṛt affix by hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk [Pā. Sū. 6-1-71 as read]; the form vajrabhṛt; the accent of the last member by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt [Pā. Sū. 6-2-139 as read]); dasyuhā (root han hiṃsāgatyoḥ [as read, ?], adādi; kvip by bahulaṃ chandasi; the word dasyuhan; since the first member is a kāraka, the accent of the last member); bhīmaḥ (root ñibhī bhaye; bibheti asmāt iti bhīmaḥ; bhīmādayo 'pādāne [Pā. Sū. 3-4-74 as read], in the sense of the ablative; bhiyaḥ ṣuk vā [Uṇ. Sū. 1-[1?]43 as read, ?]; mak after the root; as the affix is kit, no guṇa of the root vowel; final acute by the affix); sahasracetāḥ (sahasrāṇi cetāṃsi yasya saḥ; in the bahuvrīhi, the first member keeps its accent by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam [Pā. Sū. 6-2-1 as read]; nominative singular).

original p. 230

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 100.12, concluded (grammar page, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])

Grammar page, noted briefly. The grammar of Rik 100.12 concludes: śatanīthaḥ (root nīñ prāpaṇe; kthan by hanikuṣinīramikāśibhyaḥ kthan [Uṇ. Sū. 2-[?]4 as read, ?]; as the affix is kit, no guṇa of the root vowel; śata and the root-word together, as before, in a bahuvrīhi; the accent of the first member); camrīṣaḥ (root īṣa gatau; camrām īṣati gacchatīti camrīṣaḥ; since the root stands as the last member, ka by igupadhajñāprīkiraḥ kaḥ [Pā. Sū. 3-1-135 as read]; in the Veda, by letter-interchange, r comes in and the vowel is lengthened; the form camrīṣa; since the first member is a kāraka, the accent of the last member by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt [Pā. Sū. 6-2-139 as read]; or from the root camu adane with the Uṇādi īṣan, r coming in as before, and the final acute by vyatyaya); pāñcajanyaḥ (in the sense 'born among the five peoples', ñya by the statement bahirdevapañcajanebhyaś ca vaktavyam [Kāśikā 4-3-58, vārttika 1, as read [?]]; vṛddhi by taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ; loss of the final a by yasyeti ca [Pā. Sū. 6-4-148 as read]; as the affix is ñit, acute on the first syllable by ñnityādir nityam). The Rik is closed with ‖ 12 ‖ and a printed ornament.

Rik 13

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 100.13)

तस्य वज्रः क्रन्दति स्मत्स्वर्षा [as printed] दिवो न त्वेषो रवथः शिमीवान् । तं सचन्ते सनयस्तं धनानि मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विन्द्र ऊती ॥ १३ ॥

tasya vajraḥ krandati smat svarṣā [as printed] divo na tveṣo ravathaḥ śimīvān | taṃ sacante sanayas taṃ dhanāni marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ‖ 13 ‖

original p. 231

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 100.13)

तस्य । वज्रः । क्रन्दति । स्मत् । स्वःऽसाः [as read, ?] । दिवः । न । त्वेषः । रवथः । शिमीऽवान् । तम् । सचन्ते । सनयः । तम् । धनानि । मरुत्वान् । नः । भवतु । इन्द्रः । ऊती ॥ १३ ॥

tasya | vajraḥ | krandati | smat | svaḥ-sāḥ [as read, ?] | divaḥ | na | tveṣaḥ | ravathaḥ | śimī-vān | tam | sacante | sanayaḥ | tam | dhanāni | marutvān | naḥ | bhavatu | indraḥ | ūtī ‖ 13 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.13)

तस्येन्द्रस्य वज्रः कुलिशः स्मत् भृशं क्रन्दति । शत्रूनाक्रन्दयति । रोदयतीत्यर्थः । य इन्द्रः स्वर्षाः शोभनस्योदकस्य दाता दिवो न दिवः सम्बन्धी सूर्य इव त्वेषो दीप्तः रवथः शब्दस्य गर्जनलक्षणस्य कर्ता शिमीवान् । शिमीति कर्मनाम । लोकानुग्राहकेण कर्मणा युक्तस्तमिन्द्रं सनयो धनस्य दानानि सचन्ते । सेवन्ते । तथा तं धनानि च सेवन्ते । स मरुत्वानिन्द्रो नोऽस्माकं रक्षणाय भवतु ॥ क्रन्दति । कदि क्रदि क्लदि आह्वाने रोदने च । छन्दस्युभयथेति शप आर्धधातुकत्वाण्णेरनिटीति णिलोपः । स्वर्षाः । सुपूर्वात् [?] । सुष्ठु ऋच्छतीति स्वः उदकम् । तत् सनोतीति स्वर्षाः । षणु दाने । जनसनखनक्रमगमो विट् । विड्वनोरनुनासिकस्यात् इत्यात्वम् । सनोतेरनः । पा. ८-३-१०८ [?] । इति षत्वम् । त्वेषः । त्विष दीप्तौ । पचाद्यच् । रवथः । रु शब्दे । शीङ्क्षसिरुगमिवञ्चिजीविप्राणिभ्योऽथः [?] । उ. ३-१०३ [?] । इत्यथप्रत्ययः । गुणावादेशौ । सनयः । सनोतेर्भावे औणादिक इप्रत्ययः ॥ tasyendrasya vajraḥ kuliśaḥ smat bhṛśaṃ krandati | śatrūn ākrandayati | rodayatīty arthaḥ | ya indraḥ svarṣāḥ śobhanasyodakasya dātā divo na divaḥ sambandhī sūrya iva tveṣo dīptaḥ ravathaḥ śabdasya garjanalakṣaṇasya kartā śimīvān | śimīti karmanāma | lokānugrāhakeṇa karmaṇā yuktas tam indraṃ sanayo dhanasya dānāni sacante | sevante | tathā taṃ dhanāni ca sevante | sa marutvān indro no 'smākaṃ rakṣaṇāya bhavatu ‖ krandati | kadi kradi kladi āhvāne rodane ca | chandasy ubhayatheti śapa ārdhadhātukatvāṇ ṇer aniṭīti ṇilopaḥ | svarṣāḥ | supūrvāt [?] | suṣṭhu ṛcchatīti svaḥ udakam | tat sanotīti svarṣāḥ | ṣaṇu dāne | janasanakhanakramagamo viṭ | viḍvanor anunāsikasyāt ity ātvam | sanoter anaḥ | Pā. 8-3-108 [?] | iti ṣatvam | tveṣaḥ | tviṣa dīptau | pacādyac | ravathaḥ | ru śabde | śīṅkṣasirugamivañcijīviprāṇibhyo 'thaḥ [?] | U. 3-103 [?] | ity athapratyayaḥ | guṇāvādeśau | sanayaḥ | sanoter bhāve auṇādika ipratyayaḥ ‖

"The thunderbolt (kuliśa) of that Indra smat — greatly — krandati: makes the enemies cry out, that is, makes them weep. That Indra, who is svarṣāḥ — the giver of good water — divo na — like the sun that belongs to heaven, tveṣaḥ — shining — ravathaḥ — maker of a sound that has the character of thunder — śimīvān — śimī is a name of action; he is joined to action that helps the world: sanayaḥ, the gifts of wealth, sacante — attend, follow him; and likewise dhanāni, riches, attend him. May that Indra, with the Maruts, be for our protection." The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read: the stem svarṣā (from svar 'water' [as read] and san 'to give', with viṭ by janasanakhanakramagamo viṭ, ā for the nasal, and ṣ by a rule given in the print as Pā. Sū. 8-3-108 [?]); tveṣa (from tviṣ 'to shine' with ac of the pacādi class); ravatha (from ru 'to sound', with the Uṇādi atha [Uṇ. Sū. 3-103, as read, ?], with guṇa and av-substitution); sanaya (from san with an Uṇādi i in the sense of the action). The Uṇādi sūtra's list of roots is clotted [?].

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"tasya — of that Indra; vajraḥ — the thunderbolt weapon; smat — greatly; krandati — (makes the enemies) weep, makes them wail; (yaḥ — that Indra, who is) svarṣāḥ — the giver of excellent waters; divo na — like the sun that shines in the world of heaven; tveṣaḥ — shining; ravathaḥ — the one who makes a roaring sound; śimīvān — (the cause of benefit to the world) endowed with action; tam — that Indra; sanayaḥ — liberal gifts; sacante — attend; tam — him; dhanāni — wealth also (attends); marutvān — together with the Maruts; indraḥ — Indra; naḥ — our; ūtī — for protection; bhavatu — may he be."

original p. 232

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"Indra's thunderbolt weapon makes the enemies weep copiously. That Indra, the giver of waters, who shines like the sun in the world of heaven, makes a roaring sound, and who is endowed with the action that is the cause of benefit to the world — such an Indra is served by wealth and liberal gifts. May such an Indra, together with the Maruts, be our protector."

English Translation (as printed)

His thunderbolt draws cries (from his enemies), he is the sender of good waters, brilliant as (the luminary) of heaven, the thunderer, the promoter of beneficent acts, upon him do donations and riches attend : may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.13 (Kannada)

"Vajraḥ —"

वज्रः कस्मात् । व्रजयतीति सतः । vajraḥ kasmāt | vrajayatīti sataḥ | (Ni. [?] as read [?])

"— since it separates the vital breaths from living creatures and drives them forth, it is called vajra. It has the power to kill the extremely strong Asuras. The greatness of the thunderbolt weapon, and how Indra obtained it, are described here and there in various ways."

अस्मा इदु त्वष्टा तक्षद्वज्रं स्वपस्तमं स्वर्यं रणाय । asmā id u tvaṣṭā takṣad vajraṃ svapastamaṃ svaryaṃ raṇāya | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-32-2 as read [?])

अनवस्ते रथमश्वाय तक्षन्त्वष्टा वज्रं पुरुहूत द्युमन्तम् । anavas te ratham aśvāya takṣan tvaṣṭā vajraṃ puruhūta dyumantam | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-31-4 as read [?])

"— in many Ṛks like these it is told that Tvaṣṭṛ prepared for Indra the shining thunderbolt weapon. Besides —"

यं ते काव्य उशना मन्दिनं दाद्वृत्रहणं पार्यं ततक्ष वज्रम् । yaṃ te kāvya uśanā mandinaṃ dād vṛtrahaṇaṃ pāryaṃ tataksa vajram | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-121-12 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these it is said that it was made by Kāvya Uśanas."

समुद्रे अन्तः शयत उद्ना वज्रो अभीवृतः । भरन्त्यस्मै संयतः पुरःप्रस्रवणा बलिम् ॥ samudre antaḥ śayata udnā vajro abhīvṛtaḥ | bharanty asmai saṃyataḥ puraḥprasravaṇā balim ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-100-9 as read [?])

original p. 233

"— in this and similar places the nature and the power of the thunderbolt weapon are described. [This weapon] lies in the sea, covered with water, and hidden; and with the [Maruts and] friends, the enemies in the field of battle give up their very lives as an offering to it: so the power of the thunderbolt weapon is told. With such a weapon Indra destroyed all the Rākṣasas; and before killing them he made them smat krandati — cry out copiously, so that they were overcome. The word smat is generally explained by Sāyaṇa in many places as having the senses 'beautiful, auspicious, praiseworthy'; in some places he has shown it as a synonym of saha, 'together with'. Here he explains it as bhṛśam, 'greatly'."

अस्मिन्निन्द्र वृजने सर्ववीराः स्मत्सूरिभिस्तव शर्मन्स्याम । asminn indra vṛjane sarvavīrāḥ smat sūribhis tava śarman syāma | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-91-13 as read [?])

सिषक्तु माता महीरसा नः स्मत्सूरिभिर्ऋजुहस्त ऋजुवनिः । siṣaktu mātā mahī rasā naḥ smat sūribhir ṛjuhasta ṛjuvaniḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-41-15 as read [?])

"— in these Ṛks, and likewise in [the Ṛks 3-4?-?; 1-1?-?; 2-?-?; 8-?-? and others, numerals as read [?]], for the word smat used there, he has given the sense suprasasta — 'very praiseworthy' — or śobhana, 'beautiful'. And —"

उत न ईं मरुतो वृद्धसेनाः स्मद्रोदसी समनसः सदन्तु । uta na īṃ maruto vṛddhasenāḥ smad rodasī samanasaḥ sadantu | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-186-9 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these, [he has given] also the sense saha, 'together'; and for the word smat used in the Ṛk 1-23-6 [as read [?]] — 'smacchabdo nityaśabdasamānārthaḥ | nityam ūḍhasā yuktāḥ' [as read, ?] — he has given the sense nitya, 'always'.

In the present Ṛk, as in the Ṛk 3-4-9 [as read [?]], he has explained 'saha, bhṛśam, atiprabhūtam' — 'greatly, exceedingly': the sense is that he made the enemies wail exceedingly.

Svarṣāḥ — śobhanasya udakasya dātā: the giver of good water; one who gives waters of excellent quality.

Śimīvān — 'śimīti karmanāma | śamayater vā śaknoter vā' (Ni. 2-[?]5 as read [?]): 'from the root śam, which gives the sense of toiling, exerting oneself, or from the root śak, which gives the sense of being able': the word is thus derived and means 'action' —"

आपान्तमन्युस्तृपलप्रभर्मा धुनिः शिमीवाञ्छरुमाँ ऋजीषी । āpāntamanyus tṛpalaprabharmā dhuniḥ śimīvāñ charumāṃ ṛjīṣī | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-99-3 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these, as the sense comes, here too it means 'endowed with action'. By such actions as the killing of Vṛtra, by actions of the form of sending rain, and because he is joined to other actions that are means of protecting the world, the epithet śimīvān is fitting for Indra."

original p. 234

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.13) grammar pages, pp. 234–235, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?]

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: krandati (root kadi kradi kladi āhvāne rodane ca; since the causative sense is shown, ṇic by hetumati ca [Pā. Sū. 3-1-26 as read]; since the root is idit, the augment num by idito num dhātoḥ [Pā. Sū. 7-1-58 as read]; krand gets the name of a root by sanādyantā dhātavaḥ [Pā. Sū. 3-1-32 as read]; laṭ, third person singular, tip; śap; the śap counting as ārdhadhātuka in the Veda by chandasy ubhayathā [Pā. Sū. 3-4-117 as read], loss of ṇi by ṇer aniṭi [Pā. Sū. 6-4-51 as read]; the form krandati; nighāta accent); svarṣāḥ (root ṛ gatau; with su as the preceding member, viṭ [viC] by anyeṣām api dṛśyate [Pā. Sū. 3-2-75 as read], with total loss of the affix; suṣṭhu ṛcchati gacchatīti svar udakam — 'water' [as read, 'that which goes well']; svar sanotīti svarṣāḥ, root ṣaṇu dāne; viṭ by janasanakhanakramagamo viṭ [Pā. Sū. 3-2-67 as read]; s for the initial ṣ by dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-1-64 as read]; ā for the nasal of the root by viḍvanor anunāsikasyāt [Pā. Sū. 6-4-41 as read]; the ṣ of svarṣā by sanoter anaḥ [Pā. Sū. 8-3-108 as read]; the word ends in ā; the accent of the last member by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt [Pā. Sū. 6-2-139 as read]); divaḥ (ūḍidaṃpadādi [Pā. Sū. 6-1-171 as read]); tveṣaḥ (root tviṣa dīptau; since it belongs to the pacādi class, ac by nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ [Pā. Sū. 3-1-134 as read]; guṇa of the penult because of the affix; acute on the last syllable by the affix); ravathaḥ (root ru śabde; atha by śīṅśapiruguminañcijīviprāṇibhyo 'thaḥ [Uṇ. Sū. 3-[?]3 as read, ?]; guṇa by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ [Pā. Sū. 7-3-84 as read]; av-substitution; the form ravatha; the accent of the affix makes the word acute on the middle syllable); sacante (root ṣac sevane secane ca [print: paca, as read, ?], bhvādi; laṭ, third person plural; nighāta).

original p. 235

The grammar of Rik 100.13 concludes: sanayaḥ (root ṣaṇu dāne; s for the initial ṣ by dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ; the Uṇādi affix i in the sense of the action; the form sani; nominative plural; by the accent of the affix, sanayaḥ is acute on the middle syllable). The Rik is closed with ‖ 13 ‖ and a rule of dashes.

Rik 14

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 100.14)

यस्याजस्रं शवसा मानमुक्थं परिभुजद्रोदसी विश्वतः सीम् । स पारिषत्क्रतुभिर्मन्दसानो मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विन्द्र ऊती ॥ १४ ॥

yasyājasraṃ śavasā mānam ukthaṃ paribhujad rodasī viśvataḥ sīm | sa pāriṣat kratubhir mandasāno marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ‖ 14 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 100.14)

यस्य । अजस्रम् । शवसा । मानम् । उक्थम् । परिऽभुजत् । रोदसी इति । विश्वतः । सीम् । सः । पारिषत् । क्रतुऽभिः । मन्दसानः । मरुत्वान् । नः । भवतु । इन्द्रः । ऊती ॥ १४ ॥

yasya | ajasram | śavasā | mānam | ukthaṃ | pari-bhujat | rodasī iti | viśvataḥ | sīm | saḥ | pāriṣat | kratu-bhiḥ | mandasānaḥ | marutvān | naḥ | bhavatu | indraḥ | ūtī ‖ 14 ‖

original p. 236

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.14)

यस्येन्द्रस्योक्थं प्रशस्यं शवसा मानं बलेन सर्वस्य परिच्छेदकं सर्वेषां बलस्योपमानभूतं वा रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ विश्वतः सीं सर्वत उभयतः सर्वतोऽजस्रमनवरतं परिभुजत् परितो भुनक्ति । पालयति स इन्द्रः क्रतुभिरस्माभिः कृतैर्यागैर्मन्दसानो मोदमानः सन् पारिषत् अस्मान् दुरितात्पारयतु । उक्थं वच परिभाषणे । पात्र्यतुदिवचीत्यादिना [?] कर्मणि थक् । वचिस्वपीत्यादिना सम्प्रसारणम् । परिभुजत् । भुज पालनाभ्यवहारयोः । लेट्यडागमः । व्यत्ययेन शः । पारिषत् । पार तीर कर्मसमाप्तौ । लेट्यडागमः । सिब्बहुलं लेटीति सिप् । तस्यार्धधातुकत्वादिट् । व्यत्ययेन णिलोपः । मन्दसानः । मदि स्तुतिमोदमदस्वप्नकान्तिगतिषु । ऋञ्जिवृधिमन्दिसहिभ्यः कित् । उ. २-८२ [?] । इत्यसानच् प्रत्ययः ॥ yasyendrasyokthaṃ praśasyaṃ śavasā mānaṃ balena sarvasya paricchedakaṃ sarveṣāṃ balasyopamānabhūtaṃ vā rodasī dyāvāpṛthivyau viśvataḥ sīṃ sarvata ubhayataḥ sarvato 'jasram anavarataṃ paribhujat parito bhunakti | pālayati sa indraḥ kratubhir asmābhiḥ kṛtair yāgair mandasāno modamānaḥ san pāriṣat asmān duritāt pārayatu | ukthaṃ vaca paribhāṣaṇe | pātryatudivacīty ādinā [?] karmaṇi thak | vacisvapīty ādinā samprasāraṇam | paribhujat | bhuja pālanābhyavahārayoḥ | leṭy aḍāgamaḥ | vyatyayena śaḥ | pāriṣat | pāra tīra karmasamāptau | leṭy aḍāgamaḥ | sib bahulaṃ leṭīti sip | tasyārdhadhātukatvād iṭ | vyatyayena ṇilopaḥ | mandasānaḥ | madi stutimodamadasvapnakāntigatiṣu | ṛñjivṛdhimandisahibhyaḥ kit | U. 2-82 [?] | ity asānac pratyayaḥ ‖

"Of which Indra the uktha — the praiseworthy — mānam: with strength (śavasā), the measure of all, or the one that serves as the standard of comparison for the strength of all; [the two worlds] rodasī, heaven and earth, viśvataḥ sīm — on all sides, in both [directions], everywhere — ajasram — without cease — paribhujat — he cherishes all around, protects: that Indra, mandasānaḥ — rejoicing, delighted — by the kratus, the sacrifices performed by us — may he pāriṣat, carry us across sin." The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read: the stem uktha (root vac 'to speak', with thak in the passive, and samprasāraṇa of the v); paribhujat (root bhuj 'to protect, to enjoy', with the leṭ and aḍāgama, and śa by vyatyaya); pāriṣat (root pāra/tīra 'to finish an act', with the leṭ, sip by sib bahulaṃ leṭi, iṭ because of the ārdhadhātuka status, loss of ṇi by vyatyaya); mandasāna (root madi, with kit affix asānac by an Uṇādi rule [Uṇ. Sū. 2-82, as read, ?]). The opening Pāṇini rule-names are clotted and marked [?].

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"śavasā — by strength; yasya — of which Indra; ukthaṃ — the praiseworthy; mānaṃ — the measure (or the standard for the strength of others); rodasī — heaven and earth; viśvataḥ sīm — in all regions; ajasram — always; paribhujat — he protects completely; saḥ — that Indra; kratubhiḥ — by the sacrifices (performed by us); mandasānaḥ — made glad; pāriṣat — may he make [us] free from sin; marutvān — together with the Maruts; indraḥ — Indra; naḥ — our; ūtī — for protection; bhavatu — may he be."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"The praiseworthy strength of Indra surpasses the strength of all others in the world, is the standard and the model for them all, and always protects completely all the regions of heaven and earth. May Indra, who has such strength, made glad by the sacrifices we perform, make us free from sin. May that Indra, together with the Maruts, be our protector."

English Translation (as printed)

May he, of whom the excellent measure (of all things), through strength, eternally and everywhere cherishes heaven and earth, propitiated by our acts, convey us beyond (evil) : may Iudra [sic], associated with the Maruts, be our protection.

original p. 237

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.14 (Kannada)

"No one can surpass Indra's strength in earth or in sky, either. His strength surpasses all the strength of earth and sky, and is the standard for all strengths. Therefore two points that show the greatness of Indra are explained: that he is extremely praiseworthy, and that, by such divine power, Indra protects earth and sky both. First: his power is praiseworthy, and is the measure for everyone. The excellence of that power can be known from the descriptions in the Saṃhitā."

नहि नु यादधीमसीन्द्रं [print: …योदधी…, ?] को वीर्या परः । तस्मिन्नृम्णमुत क्रतुं देवा ओजांसि सं दधुरर्चन्ननु स्वराज्यम् ॥ nahi nu yādadhīmasīndraṃ [print: …yodadhī…, ?] ko vīryā paraḥ | tasminn nṛmṇam uta kratuṃ devā ojāṃsi saṃ dadhur arcann anu svarājyam ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-80-15 as read [?])

"— who can know Indra, who is all-pervading, who dwells in places so deep that men cannot know them, and who is endowed with such ability? Because of this heroism, all the gods made Indra their leader for the performance of heroic deeds and for becoming a support for strength."

नि षु सीद गणपते गणेषु त्वामाहुर्विप्रतमं कवीनाम् । ni ṣu sīda gaṇapate gaṇeṣu tvām āhur vipratamaṃ kavīnām | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-112-9 as read [?])

"— he is counted as the most excellent poet among all the poets, who are intelligent and of transcendent mind.

Thus, not only in bodily power but in the power of the Self also, Indra is the model for all: in hundreds of places such greatness of his is described in this way. That such an Indra, incomparable in valour and in wisdom, is the lord of the whole universe and its protector — this second point, set out in this Ṛk, can be seen in many places."

एको विश्वस्य भुवनस्य राजा स योधया च क्षयया च जनान् । eko viśvasya bhuvanasya rājā sa yodhayā ca kṣayayā ca janān | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-46-2 as read [?])

"— for the whole universe, Indra alone is the lord, the one able. Therefore —" Gloss, editorial and tentative, the second quotation: "Whose great might, of double strength, upheld the two worlds, the mountains, the plains, the waters, [and] the heaven, by his manliness".

यस्य द्विबर्हसो बृहत्सहो दाधार रोदसी । गिरीँरज्राँ अपः स्वर्वृषत्वना । yasya dvibarhaso bṛhat saho dādhāra rodasī | girīm̐r ajrām̐ apaḥ svar vṛṣatvanā | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-1[?]3-2 as read [?])

original p. 238

Special Topics of Rik 100.14, continued from p. 237 (Kannada)

"[…the Ṛk 8-13-2 says that] Indra upheld heaven and earth both by his power, and, having established them, made them firm and secure [as read, ?]. In this way, because Indra's power, his sovereignty and his work of protection are unmatched —"

नहि न्वस्य प्रतिमानमस्त्यन्तर्जातेषूत ये जनित्वाः । nahi nv asya pratimānam asty antar jāteṣūta ye janitvāḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-18-4 as read [?]; as quoted on p. 171)

"— [the Ṛk] declares that none, whether among those who have been born or among those who will be born hereafter, can be compared with Indra. These two points alone are set out, in the present Ṛk, as śavasā yasya ukthaṃ mānaṃ rodasī viśvataḥ sīm ajasraṃ paribhujat.

Mandasānaḥ — modamānaḥ, 'rejoicing': mandater tṛptikarmaṇaḥ [as read] (Ni. 2-[3?]5 as read [?]); the word is derived from the root mand, which means 'to attain satisfaction'. Kratubhiḥ mandasānaḥ: be satisfied by our sacrifices and the like, and, having obtained that satisfaction, [free] us —

Pāriṣat — duritāt pārayatu: 'make us pass over sin', is Sāyaṇa's explanation.

Skandasvāmin has made another construction:"

स पारिषत् — पृ पालनपूरणयोः । पूरयत्यस्मान् । क्रतुभिः प्रज्ञाभिः । अत्यन्तप्रज्ञान् अस्मान् करोतीत्यर्थः । मन्दसानः । मन्दतिरर्चतिकर्मा । स्तूयमानोऽस्माभिः । sa pāriṣat — pṛ pālanapūraṇayoḥ | pūrayaty asmān | kratubhiḥ prajñābhiḥ | atyantaprajñān asmān karotīty arthaḥ | mandasānaḥ | mandatir arcatikarmā | stūyamāno 'smābhiḥ | (Skandasvāmin, as read)

"— [that is: pāriṣat is from the root pṛ, 'to protect, to fill': 'he fills us'; kratubhiḥ — with intelligences, the sense is 'he makes us of exceeding intelligence'; mandasānaḥ: the root mand is a verb of 'honouring'; he who is praised by us]. Since mand is read among the [forty-four, as read, ?] names of the arcati-verbs [?], mandasānaḥ means 'Indra, who is praised by us'. Skandasvāmin explains that the intention is that such an Indra may give us full wisdom. Here Sāyaṇa's meaning appears the more suitable."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.14) grammar pages, pp. 238–239, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?]

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: mānam (root māṅ māne; lyuṭ in the sense of the action; ana for yu by yuvoranākau [Pā. Sū. 7-1-1 as read]; the syllable before the affix acute by liti [Pā. Sū. 6-1-193 as read]); uktham (root vaca paribhāṣaṇe; thak in the passive by a rule beginning pātṛtudi… [as read [?]]; since the affix is kit, samprasāraṇa by vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti [Pā. Sū. 6-1-15 as read]; the single substitute by samprasāraṇāc ca [Pā. Sū. 6-1-108 as read]; k for c by coḥ kuḥ [Pā. Sū. 8-2-30 as read]; final acute by the affix; accusative singular).

original p. 239

The grammar of Rik 100.14 continues: paribhujat (root bhuja pālanābhyavahārayoḥ, with the preverb pari; leṭ, third person singular, tip; loss of the i by itaś ca lopaḥ [Pā. Sū. 3-4-97 as read]; aṭ by leṭo 'ḍāṭau [Pā. Sū. 3-4-94 as read]; the śa-vikaraṇa in place of śap by vyatyayo bahulam [Pā. Sū. 3-1-85 as read]; since the relative yasya has been mentioned earlier, the nighāta is prevented by yadvṛttān nityam [Pā. Sū. 8-1-66 as read], and the accent of the root remains; the preverb pari receives the nighāta by tiṅ codāttavati [Pā. Sū. 8-1-71 as read]); viśvataḥ (in the sense of 'from all', tasil by pañcamyās tasil [Pā. Sū. 5-3-7 as read]; the preceding syllable acute by liti [Pā. Sū. 6-1-193 as read]); pāriṣat (root pāra tīra karmaparisamāptau; leṭ, tip; loss of i; aṭ; sip by sib bahulaṃ leṭi [Pā. Sū. 3-1-34 as read]; ārdhadhātukaṃ śeṣaḥ [Pā. Sū. 3-4-114 as read] gives it ārdhadhātuka status and iṭ by ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ [Pā. Sū. 7-2-35 as read]; the root belongs to the curādi class and so takes ṇic in its own sense; though the iṭ-initial affix follows, by vyatyaya the ṇic is dropped; the form pāriṣat; nighāta); mandasānaḥ (root madi stutimodamadasvapnakāntigatiṣu; asānac by ṛñjivṛdhimandisahibhyaḥ kit [Uṇ. Sū. 2-[?]4 as read, ?]; num by idito num dhātoḥ; the form mandasāna; final acute, the affix being cit, by citaḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-1-163 as read]). The Rik is closed with ‖ 14 ‖ and a rule of dashes.

na | yasya | devāḥ | devatā | na | martāḥ | āpaḥ | cana | śavasaḥ | antam | āpuḥ | saḥ | pra-rikvā | tvakṣasā | kṣmaḥ | divaḥ | ca | marutvān | naḥ | bhavatu | indraḥ | ūtī ‖ 15 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.15)

देवता देवस्य दानादिगुणयुक्तस्य यस्येन्द्रस्य शवसो बलस्यान्तमवसानं देवा वस्वादयो देवगणा नापुः । नाप्नुवन् । तथा मर्ता मनुष्या आपश्च नापोऽपि न प्राप्नुवन् । स तादृश इन्द्रस्त्वक्षसा शत्रूणां तनूकर्त्रात्मीयेन बलेन क्ष्मः पृथिव्या दिवश्च स्वर्गस्य च प्ररिक्वा प्रकर्षेण रेचको भवति । लोकद्वयोदपस्य [?] बलमतिरिच्यत इत्यर्थः । मरुद्भिर्युक्तः स इन्द्रोऽस्माकमूतये रक्षणाय भवतु ॥ देवता । देव इव देवता । देवात्मकेति स्वार्थे तल् । सुपां सुलुगिति षष्ठ्या लुक् । मर्ताः । मृङ् प्राणत्यागे । असिहसीत्यादिना तन्प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । प्ररिक्वा । रिचिर् विरेचने । अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्त इति क्वनिप् । आन्त्यैकारश्छान्दसः [?] । त्वक्षसा । तक्षू त्वक्षू तनूकरणे । असुन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । क्ष्मः । क्ष्मेति पृथिवीनाम । [the rest of the tail is on p. 241 and is clotted] devatā devasya dānādiguṇayuktasya yasyendrasya śavaso balasyāntam avasānaṃ devā vasvādayo devagaṇā nāpuḥ | nāpnuvan | tathā martā manuṣyā āpaś ca nāpo 'pi na prāpnuvan | sa tādṛśa indras tvakṣasā śatrūṇāṃ tanūkartrātmīyena balena kṣmaḥ pṛthivyā divaś ca svargasya ca prarikvā prakarṣeṇa recako bhavati | lokadvayodapasya [?] balam atiricyata ity arthaḥ | marudbhir yuktaḥ sa indro 'smākam ūtaye rakṣaṇāya bhavatu ‖ devatā | deva iva devatā | devātmaketi svārthe tal | supāṃ suluk iti ṣaṣṭhyā luk | martāḥ | mṛṅ prāṇatyāge | asihasītyādinā tanpratyayaḥ | nittvād ādyudāttatvam | prarikvā | ricir virecane | anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti kvanip | āntyaikāraś chāndasaḥ [?] | tvakṣasā | takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe | asun | nittvād ādyudāttatvam | kṣmaḥ | kṣmeti pṛthivīnāma |

"Of Indra, the deity, endowed with such qualities as generosity, of whose śavas — of whose strength — the antam, the limit, the gods, the groups of gods, the Vasus and the rest, did not reach; and likewise mortals, men, and the waters [as the print has it, āpaś ca nāpo 'pi, ?] have not attained it: such an Indra, by his tvakṣas — his own strength that makes his enemies weak — prarikvā — greatly surpasses — kṣmaḥ — the earth — and divaḥ — the heaven; the sense is that his strength exceeds [that of] both worlds. May that Indra, joined with the Maruts, be for our protection." The remaining part of the bhāṣya's grammatical tail, at the head of this page, deals with kṣmaḥ (the word kṣmā, 'earth', with the dropping of the final ā before the ending of the accusative/genitive plural by the rule of bha-status, or from a root kṣmāyī vidhūnane with kvip by kvip ca; loss of the end of the affix before a consonant-initial ending; asmāt …) and the accent of the ending by udāttanivṛttisvareṇa. The text here is crowded and clotted, and only this outline is given [?].

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"devatā — [Indra,] endowed with qualities such as generosity, of the nature of a deity; yasya — of which Indra; śavasaḥ — of the strength; antam — the limit; devāḥ — the gods; na āpuḥ — have not reached (nor obtained); martāḥ — men; āpaś cana — and the water-deities too; na — have not reached; saḥ — that Indra; tvakṣasā — by the strength that makes [enemies] weak; kṣmaḥ — of the earth; divaḥ ca — and of heaven; prarikvā — becomes the excellent illuminator, surpasses; marutvān — together with the Maruts; indraḥ — Indra; naḥ — our; ūtī — for protection; bhavatu — may he be."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"The power of Indra, who is of the nature of a deity, endowed with such qualities as generosity, exceeds that of all others in the world. Neither gods, nor men, nor the water-deities could reach its limit. That Indra, by his enemy-destroying and majestic power, makes the earth and the heavenly world both shine together. May such an Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, be our protector."

English Translation (as printed)

Nor gods, nor men, nor waters, have reached the limit of the strength of that beneficent (divinity), for he surpasses both earth and heaven by his foe-consuming (might) : may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.15 (Kannada)

"In the previous Ṛk, [the author] described that Indra's power and sovereignty are the standard for the whole universe; in this Ṛk he explains that his power surpasses the power of earth and sky, and the power of gods and men, and that none in the universe could attain to that power. This point is described in many places in the Ṛksaṃhitā."

"In Ṛks like these, Indra's greatness surpassed earth and sky both. Neither earth nor heaven could hold this greatness. By descriptions such as 'Indra's influence expanded exceedingly, pervaded all, and grew beyond the universe', it is declared that his influence grew to such a degree that it could not be attained even by the gods — [as in the vow-like declaration]:"

सत्यमित्तन्न त्वावाँ अन्यो अस्तीन्द्र देवो न मर्त्यो ज्यायान् । satyam it tan na tvāvām̐ anyo astīndra devo na martyo jyāyān | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-30-4 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these Indra's greatness is described. Just as in these descriptions, so in the present Ṛk also:

yasya śavasaḥ antaṃ devāḥ na āpuḥ — the gods could not approach the limit of that Indra's valour;

martāḥ āpaś ca na — men and the water-deities could not approach it either; and

kṣmaḥ divaś ca prarikvā — he became the illuminator of earth and sky: thus the greatness of the extremely great Indra is praised.

Tvakṣasā — since ojaḥ, pājaḥ and the like are read among the [thirty-eight, as read, ?] names of strength, tvakṣaḥ means 'strength'; tvakṣasā means 'by strength'.

Prarikvā — prakarṣeṇa recako bhavati | lokadvayād apy asya balam atiricyata ity arthaḥ: 'he becomes the one who greatly surpasses; the sense is that his strength exceeds even the two worlds'; by his own strength he makes earth and sky both shine; that is, with his strength he exceeds the two worlds." Note: the bhāṣya's clause printed on p. 240 and read there as lokadvayodapasya [?] is, on this repeat on p. 242, read as lokadvayād apy asya, 'than even the two worlds, his [strength]'; the earlier reading was a misreading.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.15)

Grammar page, noted briefly. It treats: devatā (deva eva devatā; tal in the sense of the thing itself by devāt tal [Pā. Sū. 5-4-27 as read]; feminine by talantaṃ striyām [as read]; the sixth-case ending dropped by supāṃ suluk… [Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 as read]); martāḥ (root mṛṅ prāṇatyāge; tan by asihasi… [Uṇ. Sū.]; guṇa of the root vowel because of the affix; raparatva by uraṇ raparaḥ [Pā. Sū. 1-1-51 as read]; the form marta; acute on the first syllable, the affix being nit, by ñnityādir nityam); āpuḥ (root āp-ḷ vyāptau; liṭ, third person plural; since the relative is related to it, the nighāta is prevented by yadvṛttān nityam [Pā. Sū. 8-1-66 as read]; acute on the last syllable by the affix); prarikvā (root ricir virecane; kvanip by anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante [Pā. Sū. 3-2-75 as read]; preverb pra; rikvan; k for c in the Vedic manner; since vanip is pit, unaccented, the root's accent remains; nominative singular); tvakṣasā (root takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe; asun by sarvadhātubhya asun [Uṇ. Sū. 4-[?]3 as read, ?]; the word tvakṣas; acute on the first syllable by ñnityādir nityam; instrumental singular); kṣmaḥ (kṣmā is a name of the earth; by the splitting of the rule ato dhātoḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-4-140 as read], the desired result is reached: when the stem ending in ā has bha-status, before jas, the ā is dropped; or from the root kṣmāyī vidhūnane with kvip by kvip ca [Pā. Sū. 3-2-76 as read]; loss of v by verapṛktasya [Pā. Sū. 6-1-67 as read] and of y by lopo vyor vali [Pā. Sū. 6-1-66 as read]; the form kṣmā, a stem by kṛttaddhitasamāsāś ca [Pā. Sū. 1-2-46 as read]; the loss of the final ā is natural; since the ending is unaccented, the ending is acute by anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-1-161 as read]). The Rik is closed with ‖ 15 ‖.

"Rohit — red-coloured; śyāvā — dark-coloured: that is, [the horse-line] having both kinds of colour on the two flanks. Sumadaṃśuḥ — sumat, of its own nature, tall; and Yāska has said: sumat svayam ity arthaḥ (Ni. 6-22 as read [?]). Very long-limbed. Lalāmīḥ — marked with a spot, or furnished with the ornaments of horses. Dyukṣā — having its dwelling in the sky, the world of heaven. For rāye — for the wealth, for the sake of giving wealth — of the royal sage named Ṛjrāśva, the line [of horses], bibhratī — carrying on the yoke-places, the carrying places connected with the yoke (dhūrṣu), the chariot (ratha) that is joined with vṛṣaṇvantam — Indra, the sprinkler, — mandrā — the line of horses, which gladdens all, ciketa — is known, nāhuṣīṣu — among the sons of Nahuṣa, men, vikṣu — in the peoples connected with them, in the form of armies. The sense is that Indra, joined to such a line of horses, appears in battles as a helper." The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read: lalāmī (possessive ī after lalāma), dyukṣā (root kṣi 'to dwell, to go', with an Uṇādi ḍa), ṛjrāśva (ṛjra a nipātana form with ra), vṛṣaṇvant (augment nuṭ before matup), ciketa (root kit 'to know', with the Vedic liṭ in the present sense, in the passive, and tip by vyatyaya). Numerals and one clotted clause are marked [?].
