॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"rohit — red-coloured too; śyāvā — dark-coloured too; sumadaṃśuḥ — having long limbs; lalāmīḥ — having beautiful ornaments; dyukṣāḥ — dwelling in the heavenly world; ṛjrāśvasya — to the king named Ṛjrāśva; rāye — for wealth (for giving); vṛṣaṇvantaṃ — joined with Indra, the sprinkler of desired objects; rathaṃ — the chariot; dhūrṣu — on the yokes; bibhratī — carrying; mandrā — [the line of horses] that gladdens all; nāhuṣīṣu — [among] the people; vikṣu — in the subjects who have the form of armies; ciketa — is recognized."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"The line of horses of Indra's chariot — red and dark on its two sides, long-limbed, with beautiful ornaments, dwelling in the world of heaven — carries on its yokes the chariot that has been called, with Indra, to give wealth to the king named Ṛjrāśva; and all the armies belonging to men recognize that line of horses, which gladdens all."

English Translation (as printed)

The red and black coursers, long-limbed, well-caparisoned, and celestial and harnessed, well-pleased, to the yoke of the chariot in which the showerer of benefits is conveyed, for the enrichment of Rijraswa [sic], and is recognized amongst human hosts.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.16 (Kannada)

"Sumadaṃśuḥ — here there are two words, sumat and aṃśuḥ. As the Nirukta-author has explained:"

सुमत् स्वयमित्यर्थः । sumat svayam ity arthaḥ | (Ni. 6-22 as read [?])

"— he has given the word sumat the sense svayam, 'of itself'. Here, too, in sumadaṃśuḥ, sumat means svayam, that is, svataḥ prāṃśuḥ, 'tall of its own nature' the passage continues on the next page

original p. 246

Special Topics of Rik 100.16, continued from p. 245 (Kannada)

"[sumadaṃśuḥ — 'tall of its own nature'; and] atidīrghāvayavā, 'having very long limbs': [Sāyaṇa] has explained it by quoting a Nirukta sentence, since in the whole this is the intended sense: 'having exceedingly long limbs'.

Earlier, in explaining the [thirteenth, as read, ?] Ṛk of this same sūkta, it was shown that Sāyaṇa gave different meanings, in different contexts, to the word smat used there; and it was suggested that the word smat is a synonym of the words kalyāṇa, śobhana or bhadra. In the same way it cannot be wrong to say that the word sumat too is a synonym of the words kalyāṇa, śobhana or bhadra. Just as in sumadaṃśuḥ, many other words such as sumadrathaḥ and sumadgaṇaḥ are found in use; so, if we see in what way Sāyaṇa explains the words used in the Ṛksaṃhitā —"

अथा मन्दस्व जुजुषाणो अन्धसस्त्वष्टर्देवेभिर्जनिभिः सुमद्गणः । athā mandasva jujuṣāṇo andhasas tvaṣṭar devebhir janibhiḥ sumadgaṇaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-36-3 as read [?])

"— in the Ṛk he has given, for the word sumadgaṇaḥ, the meaning śobhanagaṇaḥ ('of splendid retinue'). The sense: the word sumat is a synonym of śobhana."

विभावा देवः सुरणः परि क्षितीरग्निर्बभूव शवसा सुमद्रथः । vibhāvā devaḥ suraṇaḥ pari kṣitīr agnir babhūva śavasā sumadrathaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-3-8 as read [?])

"— here sumadrathaḥ means śobhanarathaḥ, 'of splendid chariot'. Moreover —"

आ ते [?] वचोयुजा हरी गृभ्णे सुमद्रथा [?] । ā te [?] vacoyujā harī gṛbhṇe sumadrathā [?] | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-43-29 as read [?]; clotted in the print, not completed from memory)

"— in this Ṛk, too, [Sāyaṇa] has explained kalyāṇarathau. In the same way, for the word sumadaṃśuḥ occurring in the present Ṛk also, the sense could be 'having a splendid aṃśu', that is, splendid brilliance, or 'having a splendid bridle'. (samadaṃśu [as printed] — 'Together with reins or harness': Monier Williams, Sanskrit-English Dictionary.) English in the original.

Skandasvāmin also —"

सुमच्छब्दोऽत्र स्मच्छब्देन समानार्थः प्रशस्तवचनः । अंशुशब्दो रश्मिवचनः । प्रशस्तरश्मिः । sumacchabdo 'tra smacchabdena samānārthaḥ praśastavacanaḥ | aṃśuśabdo raśmivacanaḥ | praśastaraśmiḥ | (Skandasvāmin, as read)

"— [that is: 'the word sumat here is of the same meaning as the word smat, a word of praise; the word aṃśu means ray; so 'of excellent ray'']. 'Just as for the word smat, so for the word sumat too the sense is "praiseworthy".' Aṃśu means 'bridle': so he explains that [the horse-line] is 'one having an excellent bridle'.

Dyukṣā — divi dyuloke kṛtanivāsā: one that has made her dwelling in the heavenly world: that dwells in the world of heaven."

original p. 247

"Ṛjrāśvasya — etannāmakasya rājarṣeḥ: of the royal sage named Ṛjrāśva; or — by the mention of Ṛjrāśva, [his brothers] all five Vārṣāgiras are indicated [as read, the print's Sanskrit clotted [?]]. Ṛjrāśva is the son of Vṛṣāgira. Ambarīṣa and the others are his brothers; their names are told in the next Ṛk. These too are the seers of this sūkta. A story describing a charming occasion in the life of Ṛjrāśva is told in the Ṛksaṃhitā itself:"

शतं मेषान्वृक्ये चक्षदानमृज्राश्वं तं पिताऽन्धं चकार । तस्मा अक्षी नासत्या विचक्ष आधत्तं दस्रा भिषजावनर्वन् ॥ śataṃ meṣān vṛkye cakṣadānam ṛjrāśvaṃ taṃ pitā 'ndhaṃ cakāra | tasmā akṣī nāsatyā vicakṣa ādhattaṃ dasrā bhiṣajāv anarvan ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-16 as read [?])

"Once Ṛjrāśva killed a hundred sheep [print: young goats] for a she-wolf and gave them to her; for that his father was angry and cursed him: 'let him not see!' At once the son became blind. Then, by the favour of the Aśvins, the divine physicians, his sight came to him. Thus, to Ṛjrāśva, who had become worthy of the favour of the gods, Indra too appeared in person and gave abundant wealth. This is the sense of the Ṛk: that, when Indra, to give wealth to Ṛjrāśva, harnessed his most excellent horses and came in his chariot, all men recognized Indra.

Nāhuṣīṣu — since manuṣyāḥ, naraḥ and the like are read among the twenty-five [as read, ?] names of man (Ni. 2-2 as read [?]), nahuṣa means 'man', and nāhuṣa means 'belonging to men'.

Vikṣu — Skandasvāmin explains it as manuṣyajātiṣu, 'among the races of men', and Sāyaṇa as senārūpāsu prajāsu, 'among the subjects who have the form of armies'. They recognized Indra, who came to help in battle. Here, in nāhuṣīṣu vikṣu, either [it may be taken]: 'among men, among the subjects who have the form of armies' — one sense, taking nahuṣa as the word for man; or, [Skandasvāmin:] nahuṣanāmno vā rājñaḥ svabhūtāsu vikṣu manuṣyajātiṣu brāhmaṇādikāsu — 'among the subjects, the races of men, the Brāhmaṇas and the rest, belonging to a king named Nahuṣa' — another sense. Sāyaṇa has given only one sense here. These same words nāhuṣīṣu vikṣu occur in the eighth maṇḍala —"

उत त्यदाश्वश्व्यं यदिन्द्र नाहुषीष्वा । अग्रे विक्षु प्रदीदयत् ॥ uta tyad āśvaśvyaṃ yad indra nāhuṣīṣv ā | agre vikṣu pradīdayat ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-6-24 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk, for the words nāhuṣīṣu vikṣu [Sāyaṇa gave:] nahuṣā iti manuṣyanāma tatsambandhinīṣu vikṣu | yadvā | nāhuṣo nāma kaścid rājā | tadīyāsu vikṣu | prajāsu | — 'for nahuṣa is a name for man; among the subjects connected with them; or, there was a king named Nahuṣa; among the subjects belonging to him' — two kinds of" the sentence continues on p. 248

original p. 248

"[— two kinds of] sense. A story about the king named Nahuṣa is also subtly hinted in the Ṛksaṃhitā itself:"

एका चेतत्सरस्वती नदीनां शुचिर्यती गिरिभ्य आ समुद्रात् । रायश्चेतन्ती भुवनस्य भूरेर्घृतं पयो दुदुहे नाहुषाय ॥ ekā cetat sarasvatī nadīnāṃ śucir yatī giribhya ā samudrāt | rāyaś cetantī bhuvanasya bhūrer ghṛtaṃ payo duduhe nāhuṣāya ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-95-2 as read [?])

"The king named Nahuṣa, wishing to perform a sacrifice for a thousand years, entreated the river Sarasvatī; she, being pleased, gave him milk and ghee enough for a thousand years: with this introduction Sāyaṇa explains this Ṛk. The story hinted in this Ṛk is told, at somewhat greater length, in the Bṛhaddevatā:"

राजा वर्षसहस्राय दीक्षिष्यन्नाहुषः पुरा । चचारैकरथेनेमां ब्रुवन् सर्वाः समुद्रगाः ॥ rājā varṣasahasrāya dīkṣiṣyan nāhuṣaḥ purā | cacāraikarathenemāṃ bruvan sarvāḥ samudragāḥ ‖ (Bṛ. De. 6-20 as read [?])

"— the king named Nahuṣa, wishing to take the initiation and perform a sacrifice for a thousand years, travelled round this earth in one chariot, addressing all the rivers that flow to the sea thus:"

यक्ष्ये वहत भागान्मे द्वन्द्वशो वाथ वैकशः । प्रत्यूचुस्तं नृपं नद्यः स्वल्पवीर्याः कथं वयम् ॥ वहेम भागान् स्वर्वाँस्ते [as printed; read sarvāṃs te?] सत्रे वार्षसहस्रके । सरस्वतीं प्रपद्यस्व सा ते वक्ष्यति नाहुष ॥ yakṣye vahata bhāgān me dvandvaśo vātha vaikaśaḥ | pratyūcus taṃ nṛpaṃ nadyaḥ svalpavīryāḥ kathaṃ vayam ‖ vahema bhāgān svarvāṃs te [as printed] satre vārṣasahasrake | sarasvatīṃ prapadyasva sā te vakṣyati nāhuṣa ‖ (Bṛ. De. 6-21 and 22 as read [?])

"— 'I shall sacrifice; carry my portions, two at a time or one by one.' The rivers answered that king: 'We have little strength; how could we carry all your portions in a sacrifice of a thousand years? Resort to Sarasvatī; she will carry them for you, O Nāhuṣa.'"

तथेत्युक्त्वा जगामाशु आपगां स सरस्वतीम् । सा चैनं प्रतिजग्राह दुदुहे च पयो घृतम् ॥ tathety uktvā jagāmāśu āpagāṃ sa sarasvatīm | sā cainaṃ pratijagrāha duduhe ca payo ghṛtam ‖ (Bṛ. De. 6-23 as read [?])

"— and so, saying 'So be it', he quickly went to the river Sarasvatī; she received him and gave milk and ghee, as he had wished. Thus, since the story of the king named Nahuṣa is famous in the Ṛksaṃhitā itself, the meaning in the present Ṛk may also be taken as Skandasvāmin has explained it."

original p. 249

"Mandrā — sarveṣām āhlādakarī aśvapaṅktiḥ: the line of horses that gladdens all: the sense is that, since the chariot's horses naturally draw [all eyes], and since, in this very setting, they come bringing Indra, who gives wealth and other desired objects, they are exceedingly gladdening."

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.17)

हे इन्द्र वृष्णे कामानां वर्षित्रे ते तव तृप्त्यादेतदुक्थं स्तोत्रं राधः संराधकं तृप्तिहेतुं वार्षागिरा वृषागिरो राज्ञः पुत्रा ऋज्राश्वादयोऽभि गृणन्ति । अभिमुखेन वदन्ति । वार्षागिरा इत्येतद्विवृणोति । ऋज्राश्वश्चैतन्नामा राजर्षिः पृष्टिभिः पार्श्वस्थैरन्यैर्ऋषिभिः सहेन्द्रमस्तौत् । के ते पार्श्वस्थाः । अम्बरीषादयश्चत्वारो राजर्षयः ॥ वार्षागिराः । तस्यापत्यम् । पा. ४-१-९३ [?] । इत्यण्प्रत्ययः । गृणन्ति । गृ शब्दे । प्वादीनां ह्रस्व इति ह्रस्वत्वम् । राधः । राध साध संसिद्धौ । राध्नोति सम्यद्धो भवत्यनेनेति राधः । करणेऽसुन् । ऋज्राश्वः । ऋज्रा गतिमन्तोऽश्वा यस्य स तथोक्तः । अम्बरीषः । अबि शब्दे । औणादिक ईषन्प्रत्ययः । उ. ४-२९ [?] । सहदेवः । देवैः सह वर्तत इति सहदेवः । वोपसर्जनस्येति विकल्पेन सभावाभावः [?] । भयमानः । ञिभी भये । अस्माद् अन्तर्भावितण्यर्थाद् व्यत्ययेन शानच् । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपः श्लौ [?] रभावः । अदुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वर एव शिष्यते । सुराधाः । राध इति धननाम । शोभनं राधो यस्य । सोर्मनसी अलोमोषसी इत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥ he indra vṛṣṇe kāmānāṃ varṣitre te tava tṛptyād etad uktham stotraṃ rādhaḥ saṃrādhakaṃ tṛptihetuṃ vārṣāgirā vṛṣāgiro rājñaḥ putrā ṛjrāśvādayo 'bhi gṛṇanti | abhimukhena vadanti | vārṣāgirā ity etad vivṛṇoti | ṛjrāśvaś caitannāmā rājarṣiḥ pṛṣṭibhiḥ pārśvasthair anyair ṛṣibhiḥ sahendram astaut | ke te pārśvasthāḥ | ambarīṣādayaś catvāro rājarṣayaḥ ‖ vārṣāgirāḥ | tasyāpatyam | Pā. 4-1-93 [?] | ity aṇpratyayaḥ | gṛṇanti | gṛ śabde | pvādīnāṃ hrasva iti hrasvatvam | rādhaḥ | rādha sādha saṃsiddhau | rādhnoti samyaddho bhavaty aneneti rādhaḥ | karaṇe 'sun | ṛjrāśvaḥ | ṛjrā gatimanto 'śvā yasya sa tathoktaḥ | ambarīṣaḥ | abi śabde | auṇādika īṣanpratyayaḥ | U. 4-29 [?] | sahadevaḥ | devaiḥ saha vartata iti sahadevaḥ | vopasarjanasyeti vikalpena sabhāvābhāvaḥ [?] | bhayamānaḥ | ñibhī bhaye | asmād antarbhāvitaṇyarthād vyatyayena śānac | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapaḥ ślau [?] rabhāvaḥ | adupadeśāl lasārvadhātukānudāttatve dhātusvara eva śiṣyate | surādhāḥ | rādha iti dhananāma | śobhanaṃ rādho yasya | sormanasī alomoṣasī ity uttarapadādyudāttatvam ‖

"O Indra, vṛṣṇe — you who rain down desires — te, for your satisfaction, this praise (uktha), rādhaḥ — that fulfils, that is the cause of satisfaction — the vārṣāgirāḥ, the sons of King Vṛṣāgira, Ṛjrāśva and the others, abhi gṛṇanti — speak facing [you]. [The commentator] explains vārṣāgirāḥ: the royal sage named Ṛjrāśva, with pṛṣṭibhiḥ — the other seers who stand at his sides — praised Indra. Who are those who stand at his sides? The four royal sages beginning with Ambarīṣa." The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read: vārṣāgira (aṇ in the sense of 'offspring of him', [Pā. Sū. 4-1-93, as read [?]]); gṛṇanti (root gṛ 'to sound', with shortening by pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ); rādhas (root rādh 'to succeed', 'that by which one is made perfect', with asun as instrument); ṛjrāśva (he whose horses are swift); ambarīṣa (root abi 'to sound', with the Uṇādi īṣan [Uṇ. Sū. 4-29, as read, ?]); sahadeva ('who is with the gods', with an optional sa-substitution by vopasarjanasya [as read [?]]); bhayamāna (root ñibhī 'to fear', with a causative sense included, and śānac by vyatyaya); surādhas (rādhas is a name of wealth; 'of excellent wealth'; the accent of the last member by sormanasī alomoṣasī). Clotted rule-names are marked [?].

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"vṛṣṇe — [to you] who shower the desired objects; indra — O Indra; te — your; tyat — the well-known; etat uktham — this praise; rādhaḥ — [for the satisfaction of you] who are endowed with the best wealth, for your satisfaction; vārṣāgirāḥ — the sons of the king named Vṛṣāgira; ṛjrāśvaḥ — the royal sage named Ṛjrāśva; pṛṣṭibhiḥ — with (his) companions at his side; ambarīṣaḥ — Ambarīṣa; sahadevaḥ — Sahadeva; bhayamānaḥ — Bhayamāna; surādhāḥ — and Surādhas; abhi gṛṇanti — stand facing [you] and recite."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Indra, giver of desired objects! The sons of the king Vṛṣāgira, the royal sage Ṛjrāśva, together with Ambarīṣa, Sahadeva, Bhayamāna and Surādhas, who are with him, stand before you and recite to you this well-known praise."

English Translation (as printed)

Indra, showerer (of benefits) the Varshagiras, Rijraswa and his companions Ambarisha, Sahadeva, Bhayamana and Surdhas [sic], address to you this propitiatory praise.

original p. 252

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.17 (Kannada)

"Uktham — stotram: in the explanation [Sāyaṇa] has given only the general meaning, 'hymn of praise'. But since it says 'tyat te uktham' — 'that uktha addressed to you, the well-known' — it is suggested that this uktha is one that is directed to Indra and that is also the one recited from earlier times, in the times of sacrifice. This uktha that is directed to Indra has an extraordinary distinction.

The nature of the uktha, its greatness, its connection with the śastra, the uktha and the sāman, and the subtle differences between them, and also the order in which the Hotṛ and his assistant priests are to recite it at the time of the Soma-pressing — all this was set out in detail in the previous part [of this edition].

Here, because the greatness of Indra is praised through the uktha, the power of the uktha, and through it the greatness of Indra, is subtly shown, with a former story connected with it. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa there is a story that the power of the uktha was extremely great; that the Asuras took refuge in it and so their power also grew; and that then Indra came, was praised, and drove them out."

ते वा असुरा मैत्रावरुणस्योक्थमश्रयन्त सोऽब्रवीदिन्द्रः कश्चाहं चेमानितोऽसुरान्नोत्स्यवहा [?] इत्यहं चेत्यब्रवीद्वरुणस्तस्मादैन्द्रावरुणं मैत्रावरुणस्तृतीयसवने शंसतीन्द्रश्च हि तान् वरुणश्च ततो नुदेताम् ॥ te vā asurā maitrāvaruṇasyokthamaśrayanta so 'bravīd indraḥ kaś cāhaṃ cemān ito 'surān notsyavahā [?] ity ahaṃ cety abravīd varuṇas tasmād aindrāvaruṇaṃ maitrāvaruṇas tṛtīyasavane śaṃsatīndraś ca hi tān varuṇaś ca tato nudetām ‖ (Ai. Brā., as printed; the numeral on p. 253 [?])

"The Asuras took refuge in the uktha of the Maitrāvaruṇa. Then Indra said, 'Who will help me to drive these Asuras out of this uktha?' When he asked, Varuṇa said that he would help him. At that time the Maitrāvaruṇa, the assistant priest to the Hotṛ, at the third Soma-pressing, reciting the sūkta that begins with the Ṛk"

इन्द्रावरुणा युवमध्वराय नो विशे जनाय महि शर्म यच्छतम् । indrāvaruṇā yuvam adhvarāya no viśe janāya mahi śarma yacchatam | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-68-1 as read [?])

"— praised Indra and Varuṇa. Then Indra and Varuṇa drove those Asuras out by means of the Maitrāvaruṇa śastra."

ते वै ततोऽपहता असुरा ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिन उक्थमश्रयन्त सोऽब्रवीदिन्द्रः कश्चाहं चेमानितोऽसुरान्नोत्स्यवहा [?] इत्यहं चेत्यब्रवीद्बृहस्पतिस्तस्मादैन्द्राबार्हस्पत्यं ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी तृतीयसवने शंसतीन्द्रश्च हि तान् बृहस्पतिश्च ततो नुदेताम् ॥ te vai tato 'pahatā asurā brāhmaṇācchaṃsina ukthamaśrayanta so 'bravīd indraḥ kaś cāhaṃ cemān ito 'surān notsyavahā [?] ity ahaṃ cety abravīd bṛhaspatis tasmād aindrābārhaspatyaṃ brāhmaṇācchaṃsī tṛtīyasavane śaṃsatīndraś ca hi tān bṛhaspatiś ca tato nudetām ‖

"The Asuras driven out from there took refuge in the uktha of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin."

original p. 253

"Then Indra rose, and asked who would help him to drive these Asuras out from there; and Bṛhaspati rose and said that he would help. Then the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, at the time of the third pressing,"

उदेप्रुतो न वयो रक्षमाणा वावदतो अभ्रियस्येव घोषाः । udeprato na vayo rakṣamāṇā vāvadato abhriyasyeva ghoṣāḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-68-1 as read [?]; the first word is printed as udeprato, read as given [?])

"— reciting the sūkta that begins with this Ṛk, praised Indra and Bṛhaspati; and then Indra and Bṛhaspati drove the Asuras out from there."

ते वै ततोऽपहता असुरा अच्छावाकस्योक्थमश्रयन्त सोऽब्रवीदिन्द्रः कश्चाहं चेमानितोऽसुरान्नोत्स्यवहा [?] इत्यहं चेत्यब्रवीद्विष्णुस्तस्मादैन्द्रावैष्णवमच्छावाकस्तृतीयसवने शंसतीन्द्रश्च हि तान् विष्णुश्च ततो नुदेताम् ॥ te vai tato 'pahatā asurā acchāvākasyokthamaśrayanta so 'bravīd indraḥ kaś cāhaṃ cemān ito 'surān notsyavahā [?] ity ahaṃ cety abravīd viṣṇus tasmād aindrāvaiṣṇavam acchāvākas tṛtīyasavane śaṃsatīndraś ca hi tān viṣṇuś ca tato nudetām ‖ (Ai. Brā. 1[3?]-6 as read [?])

"The Asuras driven out from the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin's uktha took refuge in the uktha of the Acchāvāka. Then Indra rose and asked who among them would help him to drive these [Asuras] out from there. Then Viṣṇu said that he would help. At that time the Acchāvāka,"

सं वां कर्मणा समिषा हिनोमीन्द्राविष्णू अपसस्पारे अस्य । saṃ vāṃ karmaṇā samiṣā hinomīndrāviṣṇū apasaspāre asya | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-69-1 as read [?])

"— reciting the sūkta that begins with this Ṛk, praised Indra and Viṣṇu. Then they drove the Asuras out from there also: so the story is told in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa ([1?]3-6 as read [?]). From this the power of the uktha, and the greatness of Indra, are known. Tat tye uktham means 'this uktha of such influence'.

For this reason, in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa also —"

इन्द्रो वै यज्ञस्य देवता तस्मादाहेन्द्राय त्वेति बृहद्वते वयस्वत इति वीर्यवत इत्येवैतदाह यदाह बृहद्वते वयस्वत इत्युक्थाख्यं गृह्णामीत्युक्थेभ्यो ह्येनं गृह्णाति । indro vai yajñasya devatā tasmād āhendrāya tveti bṛhadvate vayasvata iti vīryavata ity evaitad āha yad āha bṛhadvate vayasvata ity ukthākhyaṃ gṛhṇāmīty ukthebhyo hy enaṃ gṛhṇāti | (Śat. Brā. 4-2-3-10 as read [?])

"Indra alone is the deity of all the sacrifice; therefore, 'to Indra, [the one] with bṛhat, with vayas' — 'one endowed with valour' — as is said, 'I take up the [cup] named uktha': thus it is said, and thereby he takes him [Indra] up from [or: by means of] the ukthas." Gloss, editorial and tentative; the print's Sanskrit is cited in part [?]. "Indra alone is the deity of the sacrifice. Therefore the uktha — which is the cause of Indra's valour and of his satisfaction, endowed with [the qualities of] bṛhat and power — and through it Indra himself, are praised."

original p. 254

Special Topics of Rik 100.17, continued from p. 253 (Kannada)

"[…just as the power of the uktha was described at the time of sacrificial acts, so, in the time of teaching spiritual knowledge too, the greatness of this uktha, which has the form of a hymn, is praised. In the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad —"

उक्थं प्राणो वा उक्थं प्राणो हीदं सर्वमुत्थापयत्यद [?]स्मादुक्थविद्वीरस्तिष्ठत्युक्थस्य सायुज्यं सलोकतां जयति य एवं वेद । uktham prāṇo vā uktham prāṇo hīdaṃ sarvam utthāpayaty ada[?] smād ukthavid vīras tiṣṭhaty ukthasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda | (Bṛ. Up. 5-13-1 as read [?]; the print's words utthāpayety adrā… are clotted and read as given [?])

उक्थं तथोपासनान्तरम् । उक्थं शस्त्रम् । तद्धि प्रधानं महाव्रते क्रतौ । uktham tathopāsanāntaram | uktham śastram | tad dhi pradhānaṃ mahāvrate katau [sic: kratau] | (Śāṅkara-bhāṣya, as printed)

"— in the sacrifice that has the form of the Mahāvrata, the uktha, the chief śastra, is itself the breath (prāṇa). From it, indeed, the rising up (utthāna) comes about. Therefore the son who has the knowledge of the uktha is born [in this world], and obtains equality with it and equal esteem: so the greatness of the uktha is told.

Ṛjrāśvaḥ — the story of Ṛjrāśva was told in the explanation of the previous Ṛk.

Ambarīṣaḥ — the name of Ambarīṣa appears to occur only in this one place; his name is not as famous in the Vedas as it is in the Purāṇas.

Sahadevaḥ — Sahadeva's story is told in many places: in the Ṛksaṃhitā, in the Ṛk 4-15-7 [as read [?]], in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (2-4-3-4 as read [?]), and in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa also, the matter of Sahadeva is told.

Pṛṣṭibhiḥ — pārśvasthaiḥ anyair ṛṣibhiḥ: together with the other royal sages, Ambarīṣa and the others, who are with him.

It is said in the Anukramaṇikā: 'sa yo vṛṣaikonā vārṣāgirā ṛjrāśvāmbarīṣasahadevabhayamānasurādhasaḥ': the Vṛṣāgira sons, Ṛjrāśva and the others, received the vision of this sūkta, of nineteen Ṛks beginning with sa yo vṛṣā; and in the Ārṣānukramaṇikā also:"

सूक्तं स यो वृषेत्येतत्पञ्च वार्षागिरा विदुः । नियुक्ता नामधेयैः स्वरैरपि चैतत्त्यदित्यृचि ॥ sūktaṃ sa yo vṛṣety etat pañca vārṣāgirā viduḥ | niyuktā nāmadheyaiḥ svarair api caitat tyad ity ṛci ‖ (Ārṣānukramaṇī, as printed here [clear on this page; the reading caitat tyad ity ṛci settles the clotted words caitat… noted in the introduction to Sūkta 100 on p. 165])

"— so these five seers received the vision of this sūkta."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.17) grammar pages, pp. 254–256, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?]

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They begin with uktham — 'explained at the fourteenth mantra' [as printed; i.e. at Rik 100.14].

original p. 255

The grammar of Rik 100.17 continues: vārṣāgirāḥ (vṛṣāgiraḥ apatyaṃ pumān vārṣāgiraḥ; aṇ after vṛṣāgira in the sense of 'son' by tasyāpatyam [Pā. Sū. 4-1-92 as read]; since the affix is ñit, acute on the first syllable; vṛddhi by taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ [Pā. Sū. 7-2-117 as read]; raparatva by uraṇ raparaḥ; the form vārṣāgira; nominative plural); gṛṇanti (root gṝ śabde, kryādi; since it belongs to the pvādi class, shortening by pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ [Pā. Sū. 7-3-80 as read]; laṭ, third person plural, jhi → anta; śnā by kryādibhyaḥ śnā [Pā. Sū. 3-1-81 as read]; since the affix is treated as ṅit, loss of the ā of śnā by śnābhyastayor ātaḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-4-112 as read]; ṇ because of the preceding ṛ; nighāta); rādhaḥ (root rādha sādha saṃsiddhau; rādhnoti samyaddho bhavaty aneneti rādhaḥ; asun, in the instrumental sense, the Uṇādi affix that goes with all roots; the word rādhas; acute on the first syllable by ñnityādir nityam); ṛjrāśvaḥ (ṛjrāḥ gatimantaḥ aśvāḥ yasya saḥ; in the bahuvrīhi the first member keeps its accent); ambarīṣaḥ (root abi śabde; the Uṇādi īṣan [Uṇ. Sū. 4-[?]4 as read, ?]; num by idito num dhātoḥ; r in the Vedic manner; the accent of the affix stays by vyatyaya); sahadevaḥ (devaiḥ saha vartate; sa for saha optionally by vopasarjanasya [Pā. Sū. 6-3-82 as read], and here it does not apply; the accent of the first member in the bahuvrīhi); bhayamānaḥ (root ñibhī bhaye; since the causative sense is included, the root has the causative meaning; śānac in the sense of the present by vyatyayo bahulam; ślu does not replace śap by bahulaṃ chandasi; guṇa of the root vowel because of śap; ay-substitution; muk to a vowel-ending stem by āne muk [Pā. Sū. 7-2-82 as read]; bhayamāna; since the root has a-ending upadeśa, the lasārvadhātuka affix āna is unaccented by tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam [Pā. Sū. 6-1-186 as read]; the root's own accent remains).

original p. 256

The grammar of Rik 100.17 concludes: surādhāḥ (rādhaḥ is a name of wealth; śobhanaṃ rādhaḥ yasya saḥ; the accent of the last member by sormanasī alomoṣasī [Pā. Sū. 6-2-117 as read]). The Rik is closed with ‖ 17 ‖ and a rule of dashes.

Rik 18

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 100.18)

दस्यूञ्छिम्यूँश्च पुरुहूत एवैर्हत्वा पृथिव्यां शर्वा नि बर्हीत् । सनत्क्षेत्रं सखिभिः श्वित्न्येभिः सनत्सूर्यं सनदपः सुवज्रः ॥ १८ ॥

dasyūñ chimyūm̐ś ca puruhūta evair hatvā pṛthivyāṃ śarvā ni barhīt | sanat kṣetraṃ sakhibhiḥ śvitnyebhiḥ sanat sūryaṃ sanad apaḥ suvajraḥ ‖ 18 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 100.18)

दस्यून् । शिम्यून् । च । पुरुऽहूतः । एवैः । हत्वा । पृथिव्याम् । शर्वा । नि । बर्हीत् । सनत् । क्षेत्रम् । सखिऽभिः । श्वित्न्येभिः । सनत् । सूर्यम् । सनत् । अपः । सुऽवज्रः ॥ १८ ॥

dasyūn | śimyūn | ca | puru-hūtaḥ | evaiḥ | hatvā | pṛthivyām | śarvā | ni | barhīt | sanat | kṣetram | sakhi-bhiḥ | śvitnyebhiḥ | sanat | sūryam | sanat | apaḥ | su-vajraḥ ‖ 18 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.18)

पुरुहूतो बहुभिर्यजमानैराहूत इन्द्र एवैर्गमनशीलैर्मरुद्भिर्युक्तः सन् पृथिव्यां भूमौ वर्तमानान् दस्यून् उपक्षपयितॄन् [?] राक्षसान् शिम्यूंश्च शमयितॄन् [?] … शमयित्वा [?] स्व- puruhūto bahubhir yajamānair āhūta indra evair gamanaśīlair marudbhir yuktaḥ san pṛthivyāṃ bhūmau vartamānān dasyūn upakṣapayitṝn [?] rākṣasān śimyūṃś ca śamayitṝn [?] … śamayitvā [?] sva- (the line breaks off at the foot of p. 256)

original p. 257

[…]धकारिणो [?] राक्षसादींश्च हत्वा प्रहृत्य तदनन्तरं शर्वा हिंसकेन वज्रेण नि बर्हीत् । अवधीत् । निबर्हयति वधकर्मा । एवं शत्रून्निरस्य श्वित्न्येभिः श्वेतवर्णैरलङ्कारेण दीप्ताङ्गैः सखिभिर्मित्रभूतैर्मरुद्भिः सह क्षेत्रं शत्रूणां स्वभूतं भूमिं सनत् । समभाश्रित् [?] । तथा वृत्रेण तिरोहितं सूर्यं तस्य वृत्रस्य हननेन सनत् । अभजत प्राप्तवानित्यर्थः । तथा सुवज्रः शोभनवज्रयुक्त इन्द्रो वृत्रेण निरुद्धा अपो वृष्ट्युदकानि सनत् । समभजत ॥ […]dhakāriṇo [?] rākṣasādīṃś ca hatvā prahṛtya tadanantaraṃ śarvā hiṃsakena vajreṇa ni barhīt | avadhīt | nibarhayati vadhakarmā | evaṃ śatrūn nirasya śvitnyebhiḥ śvetavarṇair alaṅkāreṇa dīptāṅgaiḥ sakhibhir mitrabhūtair marudbhiḥ saha kṣetraṃ śatrūṇāṃ svabhūtaṃ bhūmiṃ sanat | samabhāśrit [?] | tathā vṛtreṇa tirohitaṃ sūryaṃ tasya vṛtrasya hananena sanat | abhajata prāptavān ity arthaḥ | tathā suvajraḥ śobhanavajrayukta indro vṛtreṇa niruddhā apo vṛṣṭyudakāni sanat | samabhajata ‖

"…and, having killed the Rākṣasas and the rest [who are the destroyers?], having struck, thereafter śarvā — with the weapon that does harm, the thunderbolt — ni barhīt: he killed. [Nibarhayati is a word meaning 'to kill'.] Having thus driven off the enemies, together with sakhibhiḥ, the friends, the Maruts, śvitnyebhiḥ — white-coloured, with limbs shining with ornaments — he sanat [divided, took] the kṣetra, the land that belonged to the enemies. So also, the sun hidden by Vṛtra he sanat — obtained, shared — by the slaying of that Vṛtra. And likewise Indra, suvajraḥ, endowed with the splendid thunderbolt, sanat — released — the waters, the rain-waters, shut in by Vṛtra." The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read: the stem dasyu (root dasu 'to waste', Uṇādi yu) and śimyu (root śam 'to quiet', Uṇādi yu, 'one who quiets, suppresses everything: a Rākṣasa and the like'); śarvā (root śṛ 'to injure', with vanip by anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante, and ḍā for the third-case ending by supāṃ suluk…); sanat (root van/ṣaṇ 'to share', with leṭ and aḍāgama and, by bahulaṃ chandasi, no augment); śvitnya (root śvit 'to be white', with an Uṇādi nak, 'worthy of white colour'); suvajra (accent on the last member by ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi). The Uṇādi numerals and the words marked [?] are clotted.

दस्यून् । दसु उपक्षये । यजिमनिशुन्धिदसिजनिभ्यो युः । उ. ३-[२?]० [?] । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । शिम्यून् । शमु उपशमे । शमयति सर्वं तिरस्करोतीति राक्षसादिः शिम्युः । औणादिको युप्रत्ययः । वर्णव्यापत्त्या [?] ह्रस्वत्वम् [?] । शर्वा । शृ हिंसायाम् । अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्त इति वनिप् । सुपां सुलुगिति तृतीयाया डादेशः । सनत् । वन षण सम्भक्तौ । लेट्यडागमः । बहुलं छन्दस्यमाङ्योगेऽपीत्यडभावः । श्वित्न्येभिः । श्विता वर्णे । औणादिको नक्प्रत्ययः । श्वित्नं शुक्लवर्णमर्हन्तीति श्वित्न्याः । छन्दसि ञेति यः [?] । सुवज्रः । आद्युदात्तं द्व्यच्छन्दसीत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥ dasyūn | dasu upakṣaye | yajimaniśundhidasijanibhyo yuḥ | U. 3-[2?]0 [?] | vṛṣāditvād ādyudāttatvam | śimyūn | śamu upaśame | śamayati sarvaṃ tiraskarotīti rākṣasādiḥ śimyuḥ | auṇādiko yupratyayaḥ | varṇavyāpattyā [?] hrasvatvam [?] | śarvā | śṛ hiṃsāyām | anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti vanip | supāṃ suluk iti tṛtīyāyā ḍādeśaḥ | sanat | vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau | leṭy aḍāgamaḥ | bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pīty aḍabhāvaḥ | śvitnyebhiḥ | śvitā varṇe | auṇādiko nakpratyayaḥ | śvitnaṃ śuklavarṇam arhantīti śvitnyāḥ | chandasi ñeti yaḥ [?] | suvajraḥ | ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasīty uttarapadādyudāttatvam ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"puruhūtaḥ — Indra, who is called by many; evaiḥ — together with the moving Maruts; pṛthivyām — on the earth; dasyūn — the enemies who do harm (the Dasyus); śimyūn ca — and the Rākṣasas who kill; hatvā — having struck; śarvā — with the thunderbolt weapon that does harm; ni barhīt — he killed [afterwards]; śvitnyebhiḥ — with limbs shining with white ornaments; sakhibhiḥ — with the Maruts who are his friends; kṣetram — the fields (of the enemies); sanat — he divided; sūryam — the sun (that was hidden by Vṛtra); sanat — he released; suvajraḥ — Indra, he of the splendid thunderbolt; apaḥ — the rain-waters; sanat — he released and made flow."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"Indra, called by many for help, together with the roving Maruts, killed with the thunderbolt all the harmful Dasyus who were on the earth, and the Rākṣasas who do harm. And with his friends the Maruts, bright with white ornaments, he divided the fields of the enemies. He released the sun that Vṛtra had hidden. And Indra, with the splendid thunderbolt, released and made flow the rain-waters."

English Translation (as printed)

Indra, who is invoked by many, attended by the moving (Maruts), having attacked the Dasyus and the Simyus, slew them with his thunderbolt ; (the translation continues on p. 258)

original p. 258

English Translation of Rik 100.18, concluded from p. 257 (as printed)

the thunderer then divided the fields with his white-complexioned friends, and rescued the sun and set free the water.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.18 (Kannada)

"Puruhūtaḥ — bahubhir yajamānair āhūtaḥ: Indra, who is called by many sacrificers.

Evyaiḥ — formed from the root iṇ, which has the sense of going, the form eva results. When it is said, 'one whose nature is to go or to move, and in that, to move swiftly', this epithet has been used in many places, chiefly as an epithet of the Maruts; and how this epithet shows the distinguishing character of the Maruts has been explained in the special topics of the second Ṛk of this very sūkta. Here also evyaiḥ means gamanaśīlair marudbhiḥ, 'with the Maruts of moving nature'. Since the word is used in contexts that show the sense of movement — as a synonym of 'praise (stotra)', as a synonym of 'horse (aśva)', as a synonym of 'sacrifice (kratu)' — the sense of the word must be given according to each context. For example —"

सनाद्दिवं परि भूमा विरूपे पुनर्भुवा युवती स्वेभिरेवैः । sanād divaṃ pari bhūmā virūpe punarbhuvā yuvatī svebhir evaiḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-62-8 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk 'evaiḥ' means 'gamanaiḥ', 'by [their] movements': it shows, as a general adverb, the eternal going of Night and Dawn."

भजन्त विश्वे देवत्वं नाम ऋतं सपन्तो अमृतमेवैः । bhajanta viśve devatvaṃ nāma ṛtaṃ sapanto amṛtam evaiḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-68-4 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk, for the word evaiḥ, [Sāyaṇa] has given 'tvāṃ gantṛbhiḥ stotṛbhiḥ' [as printed, ?] — a synonym of 'praisers' (stotṛ)."

उप वामवः शरणं गमेयं शूरो नाज्म पतयद्भिरेवैः । upa vāmavaḥ śaraṇaṃ gameyaṃ śūro nājma patayadbhir evaiḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-158-3 as read [?]; the first words clotted in print [?])

"— in this Ṛk, evaiḥ = aśvaiḥ, a synonym of horses."

स सूर्य प्रति पुरो न उद्गा एभिः स्तोमेभिरेतशेभिरेवैः । sa sūrya prati puro na udgā ebhiḥ stomebhir etaśebhir evaiḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-19-3 as read [?])

"— here, for evaiḥ, Sāyaṇa has explained aśvaiḥ, yet there he has shown a doubtful mind [about it]. Here, since it is natural as a qualifier of stomebhiḥ"

original p. 259

"[— since it is natural as a qualifier of stomebhiḥ, it is] a synonym of stotra, 'praise'. Only in the present Ṛk, however, evaiḥ means 'with the Maruts, who are always of a moving nature, the friends of Indra'.

Dasyūn — it was said earlier, in the special topics of the twelfth Ṛk of this sūkta, that for the word dasyu the senses 'Rākṣasas who cause decay' and 'men without rites' arise as separate meanings. Here [Sāyaṇa] gives upakṣapayitṝn śatrūn, 'enemies who cause decay': that is the sense.

Śimyūṃś ca — śamayitṝn, vadhakāriṇaḥ rākṣasān ca [as printed]: 'the Rākṣasas who kill' — so a difference is shown between the two kinds of harmers, dasyu and śimyu. Though the general meaning of both is 'enemies', a subtle difference is stated here. As it is derived from the root śim, which gives the sense of power [śakti], the sense is 'enemies endowed with the power to harm'. Indra is entreated to destroy both kinds of harmers. As this word is used here, so —"

शर्धन्तं शिम्युमुचथस्य नव्यः शासं सिन्धूनामकृणोदशस्तीः । śardhantaṃ śimyum ucathasya navyaḥ śāsaṃ sindhūnām akṛṇod aśastīḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-19-[3/5?] as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk also it is used in the sense of bādhamāna, 'oppressing'.

Śarvā — śṛṇāti śatrūn aneneti śaruḥ vajraḥ: 'with which one harms and destroys enemies', the thunderbolt is named śaru; śarvā means 'with the thunderbolt weapon'. Though in general śaru need not mean the thunderbolt weapon alone, there is no rule."

यः शश्वतो मह्येनो दधानानमन्यमानाञ्छर्वा जघान । yaḥ śaśvato mahy eno dadhānān amanyamānāñ charvā jaghāna | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-12-10 as read [?])

युवं ताँ इन्द्रावरुणावमित्रान् हतं पराचः शर्वा विषूचः । yuvaṃ tām̐ indrāvaruṇāv amitrān hataṃ parācaḥ śarvā viṣūcaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-68-3 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these, since it is a weapon connected with Indra, śaru means the thunderbolt weapon. But —"

आरे सा वः सुदानवो मरुत ऋञ्जती शरुः । āre sā vaḥ sudānavo maruta ṛñjatī śaruḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-172-3 as read [?])

"— in places like this, since it is connected with the Maruts and the other deities, the meaning is only 'a weapon that harms enemies'."

original p. 260

"Śvitnyebhiḥ — śvetavarṇair alaṅkāreṇa dīptāṅgaiḥ: 'with limbs shining with white ornaments': with the Maruts whose limbs shine with bright ornaments.

Together with such friendly Maruts, Indra released the sun from the enemy who had concealed it, and made the light spread. By sending rain he made the waters flow for the world."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.18) grammar pages, pp. 260–261, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?]

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: dasyūn (root dasu upakṣaye; yu by yajimaniśundhidasijanibhyo yuḥ [Uṇ. Sū. 3-[2?]00 as read, ?]; the form dasyu; the accent of the affix would be expected, but by vṛṣādīnāṃ ca [Pā. Sū. 6-1-203 as read] the first syllable is acute; accusative plural); śimyūn (root śamu upaśame; śamayati sarvaṃ tiraskaroti iti rākṣasādiḥ śimyuḥ; the affix yun, established in the Uṇādi; i for the a of the root in the Veda by letter-interchange; acute on the first syllable, the affix being nit, by ñnityādir nityam [Pā. Sū. 6-1-197 as read]; accusative plural); hatvā (root han hiṃsāgatyoḥ; ktvā by samānakartṛkayoḥ pūrvakāle ktvā [Pā. Sū. 3-4-21 as read]; since kit, loss of the nasal by anudāttopadeśavanatitanotyādīnām anunāsikalopo jhali kṅiti [Pā. Sū. 6-4-37 as read]); pṛthivyām (udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt [Pā. Sū. 6-1-174 as read]); śarvā (root śṝ hiṃsāyām; vanip by anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante [Pā. Sū. 3-2-75 as read]; guṇa of the root vowel because of the affix; the word śarvan; before the instrumental ending, ḍā by supāṃ suluk… [Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 as read]; since ḍit, loss of the ṭi part (an) of the stem; śarvā; since vanip is pit, the root's accent remains); sanat (root vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau; leṭ, third person singular, tip; loss of the i by itaś ca; śap; s for the initial ṣ by dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ; no aṭ by bahulaṃ chandasy māṅyoge 'pi [Pā. Sū. 6-4-75 as read]; since it is at the beginning of the pāda, no nighāta; since śap is pit, unaccented, the root's accent remains).

original p. 261

The grammar of Rik 100.18 concludes: śvitnyebhiḥ (root śvitā varṇe; the Uṇādi affix nak; since kit, no guṇa of the penult; the form śvitna; śvitnaṃ śuklavarṇam arhantīti śvitnyāḥ; ya in the sense of 'worthy of' in the Veda by arhārthe chandasi ca [Pā. Sū. 5-1-67 as read]; loss of the a by yasyeti ca [Pā. Sū. 6-4-148 as read]; the form śvitnya; bhis follows, and ais does not arise by bahulaṃ chandasi [Pā. Sū. 7-1-10 as read]; e by bahuvacane jhaly et [Pā. Sū. 7-3-103 as read]); suvajraḥ (śobhanaḥ vajraḥ yasya saḥ; the accent on su would be expected [susvara], but, since the last member has two syllables [ac], the last member keeps its acute on the first syllable by ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi [Pā. Sū. 6-2-119 as read]; nominative singular). The Rik is closed with ‖ 18 ‖ and a printed ornament.

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 100.19)

विश्वाहेन्द्रो अधिवक्ता नो अस्त्वपरिह्वृताः सनुयाम वाजम् । तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहन्तामदितिः सिन्धुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥ १९ ॥

viśvāhendro adhivaktā no astv aparihvṛtāḥ sanuyāma vājam | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ‖ 19 ‖

विश्वाहा । इन्द्रः । अधिऽवक्ता । नः । अस्तु । अपरिऽह्वृताः । सनुयाम । वाजम् । [the Pada continues on p. 262]

तत् । नः । मित्रः । वरुणः । मामहन्ताम् । अदितिः । सिन्धुः । पृथिवी । उत । द्यौः ॥ १९ ॥

viśvāhā | indraḥ | adhi-vaktā | naḥ | astu | aparī-hvṛtāḥ | sanuyāma | vājam | tat | naḥ | mitraḥ | varuṇaḥ | māmahantām | aditiḥ | sindhuḥ | pṛthivī | uta | dyauḥ ‖ 19 ‖ the Pada's aparihvṛtāḥ is divided in the print as apari-hvṛtāḥ

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.19)

विश्वाहा सर्वकालं नोऽस्माकमिन्द्रोऽधिवक्तास्तु । अधिवचनं पक्षपातेन वचनम् । यथोक्तम् । ब्राह्मणायाधिब्रूयात् । तै. सं. २-५-११-४ [?] । इति । सर्वदास्माकमिन्द्रः पक्षपातवचनयुक्तो भवतु । वयं चापरिह्वृता अकुटिलगतयः सन्तो वाजं हविर्लक्षणमन्नं सनुयाम । सम्भजामहे । यदनेन सूक्तेनास्माभिः प्रार्थितं तन्मित्रादयो मामहन्ताम् । पूजितं कुर्वन्तु ॥ विश्वाहा । विश्वान्यहानि विश्वाहानि । अत्यन्तसंयोगे द्वितीया । शेश्छन्दसि बहुलमिति शेर्लोपः । उपधादीर्घत्वम् । नलोपः । मरुद्वृधादित्वात्पूर्वपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । अपरिह्वृताः । ह्वृ कौटिल्ये । निष्ठायामपरिह्वृताश्च [?] । पा. ७-२-३२ [?] । इति निपातनात् ह्वृभावाभावः [?] । अव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । सनुयाम । षणु दाने । लिङि तनादित्वादुप्रत्ययः । वन षण सम्भक्ताविति अस्माद्वा व्यत्ययेनोप्रत्ययः ॥ viśvāhā sarvakālaṃ no 'smākam indro 'dhivaktāstu | adhivacanaṃ pakṣapātena vacanam | yathoktam | brāhmaṇāyādhibrūyāt | Tai. Saṃ. 2-5-11-4 [?] | iti | sarvadāsmākam indraḥ pakṣapātavacanayukto bhavatu | vayaṃ cāparihvṛtā akuṭilagatayaḥ santo vājaṃ havirlakṣaṇam annaṃ sanuyāma | sambhajāmahe | yad anena sūktenāsmābhiḥ prārthitaṃ tan mitrādayo māmahantām | pūjitaṃ kurvantu ‖ viśvāhā | viśvāny ahāni viśvāhāni | atyantasaṃyoge dvitīyā | śeś chandasi bahulam iti śerlopaḥ | upadhādīrghatvam | nalopaḥ | marudvṛdhāditvāt pūrvapadāntodāttatvam | aparihvṛtāḥ | hvṛ kauṭilye | niṣṭhāyām aparihvṛtāś ca [?] | Pā. 7-2-32 [?] | iti nipātanāt hvṛbhāvābhāvaḥ [?] | avyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | sanuyāma | ṣaṇu dāne | liṅi tanāditvād upratyayaḥ | vana ṣaṇa sambhaktāv iti asmād vā vyatyayenopratyayaḥ ‖

"Viśvāhā — at all times, may Indra be for us an adhivaktā: adhivacana is speech with partiality [in favour]. As it is said, 'brāhmaṇāyādhibrūyāt' [may he speak for the Brāhmaṇa] (Tai. Saṃ. 2-5-11-4 as read [?]). May Indra always be endowed with speech of partisanship for us; and we, aparihvṛtāḥ — going on paths that are not crooked — vājam, food that has the nature of an oblation, sanuyāma — may we enjoy. What we have prayed for by this sūkta, may Mitra and the rest māmahantām — honour, make it honoured (that is, fulfil it)." The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read: viśvāhā ('all days', the second case in the sense of continuous connection, loss of śi by śeś chandasi bahulam, lengthening of the penult, loss of n, accent of the first member as of the marudvṛdhādi class); aparihvṛtāḥ (root hvṛ 'to be crooked', with the niṣṭhā affix, the form fixed by a nipātana rule [Pā. Sū. 7-2-32, as read [?]], with the accent of an indeclinable first member); sanuyāma (root ṣaṇu 'to give', with u as in the tanādi class in the liṅ; or from vana/ṣaṇa sambhaktau with u by vyatyaya). The Pāṇini numerals and the words marked [?] are clotted.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"viśvāhā — at all times; naḥ — for us; indraḥ — Indra; adhivaktā — the one who speaks words of partisanship; astu — may he be (and we also); aparihvṛtāḥ — leaving the crooked path (staying on the straight path); vājam — (abundant) food; sanuyāma — may we enjoy; naḥ — our; tat — that prayed-for desired object; mitraḥ — Mitra; varuṇaḥ — and Varuṇa; aditiḥ — Aditi; sindhuḥ — the deity presiding over the sea; pṛthivī — the earth; uta — and; dyauḥ — the heavenly world also; māmahantām — may they guard."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"May Indra be, at all times, one who speaks words of partisanship for us. And may we also, staying always on the straight path, enjoy abundant food. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, the deity of the sea, the earth and the heavenly world guard that desired object which we have prayed for."

original p. 263

English Translation (as printed)

May Indra be daily our vindicator, and may we, with undiverted course, enjoy (abundant) food ; and may Mitra, Varuna, Aditi,—ocean, earth, and heaven, preserve it to us.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.19 (Kannada)

"Adhivaktā — adhivacanaṃ pakṣapātena vacanam: 'speaking with partisanship': that is, '[Indra] as one who speaks with pride [or favour]': it asks for Indra's partisanship. But if Indra's partisanship and favour are to be gained, they can be gained only by those who stand on the straight path, that is, those who are not crooked: so the adjective aparihvṛtāḥ shows [the need for] purity of conduct.

Aparihvṛtāḥ — akuṭilagatayaḥ santaḥ: 'those who have left the crooked path, that is, who stand on the straight path'. Or, as Skandasvāmin explains, 'sāmarthyād ahiṃsārthaḥ | āhiṃsitāḥ kenacit' [as printed]: 'unharmed by anyone'; since the pressure of enemies is exceedingly strong, even though food and the like be given by Indra, enemies may carry it off; so the prayer may be: 'may we be unharmed by the enemies'. Sāyaṇa too, for this word in other places, has given both these two meanings. For example —" Glosses, editorial and tentative: "He who has come with friendship to his friends, unobstructed, like a courser"; "The joint-sovereigns, the good increasers, who came to the sacrifice, unobstructed, established their dwelling in heaven".

आ यो विवाय सख्या सखिभ्योऽपरिह्वृतो अत्यो न सप्तिः । ā yo vivāya sakhyā sakhibhyo 'parihvṛto atyo na saptiḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-6-3 as read [?])

सम्राजो ये सुवृधो यज्ञमाययुरपरिह्वृता दधिरे दिवि क्षयम् । samrājo ye suvṛdho yajñam āyayur aparihvṛtā dadhire divi kṣayam | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-63-5 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these, for the word aparihvṛte used there, 'kenacid asya ahiṃsitāḥ': Sāyaṇa too has given the meaning 'unharmed by anyone'. In the same way the meaning may be taken in this Ṛk also.

Vājaṃ sanuyāma — may we enjoy food; the prayer to Indra is that he make us enjoy food without harm.

Tan no mitro varuṇaḥ — this prayer, a prayer to many deities at the end of the sūkta, shows, in the form of a conclusion (udarka), the style of the seer Kutsa's works: so it was said earlier in the explanation of the last Ṛk of the ninety-fourth sūkta [as read, ?]. Even though this style is seen in the works of other seers, the distinction of Kutsa's style"

original p. 264

"[— the distinction of Kutsa's style is] not in the works of Bharadvāja and the other seers: this matter too was told earlier, quoting a sentence of the Bṛhaddevatā (Bṛ. De. 3-13 as read [?])."

Sūkta 101 — "pra mandine"

ನೂರೊಂದನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು — nūrondaneya sūktavu, "the hundred-and-first Sūkta" Kannada heading

Sāyaṇa's introduction to Sūkta 101 (Sanskrit in Kannada script; doubtful places [?]): Sense, mine, from the Kannada that follows: "The eighth sūkta, of eleven Ṛks, beginning pra mandine, is the seer-composition of Kutsa Āṅgirasa; the four beginning with the eighth are Triṣṭubh, the remaining seven Jagatī; the deity is Indra. So the Anukramaṇī: 'pra mandine — eleven; Kutsa; four Triṣṭubh at the end; the first [Ṛk] is a garbhasrāviṇī [a Ṛk for the miscarriage?], upaniṣad.' On the ninth day of the Daśarātra this sūkta is used in the Marutvatīya [śastra]; set down in the Sūtra in the section called Viśvajit: pra mandine, imā u tvā — the Marutvatīya."

प्र मन्दिन इत्येकादशर्चमष्टमं सूक्तमाङ्गिरसस्य कुत्सस्यार्षम् । अष्टम्याद्याश्चतस्रस्त्रिष्टुभः शिष्टाः सप्त जगत्यः । इन्द्रो देवता । तथा चानुक्रान्तम् । प्र मन्दिन एकादश कुत्सश्चतुस्त्रिष्टुबन्तमाद्या गर्भस्राविण्युपनिषत् ॥ दशरात्रस्य नवमेऽहनि मरुत्वतीय एतत्सूक्तम् । विश्वजित इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । प्र मन्दिन इमा उ त्वेति मरुत्वतीयम् । आ. ८-[७?] [?] । इति ॥ pra mandina ity ekādaśarcam aṣṭamaṃ sūktam āṅgirasasya kutsasyārṣam | aṣṭamyādyāś catasras triṣṭubhaḥ śiṣṭāḥ sapta jagatyaḥ | indro devatā | tathā cānukrāntam | pra mandina ekādaśa kutsaś catustriṣṭubantam ādyā garbhasrāviṇy upaniṣat ‖ daśarātrasya navame 'hani marutvatīya etat sūktam | viśvajita iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | pra mandina imā u tveti marutvatīyam | Ā. 8-[7?] [?] | iti ‖

Anuvāda (Kannada): "Pra mandine — this sūkta is the eighth sūkta in the fifteenth anuvāka. It has eleven Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Kutsa, the son of Aṅgiras. Four Ṛks, from the eighth, are in the Triṣṭubh metre; the remaining seven Ṛks are in the Jagatī metre. Indra is the deity. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said 'pra mandina ekādaśa kutsaś catustriṣṭubantam ādyā garbhasrāviṇy upaniṣat'. On the ninth day of the sacrifice called Daśarātra this sūkta is applied for the Marutvatīya mantras: it is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section called Viśvajit, by the aphorism pra mandina imā u tveti marutvatīyam (Ā. 8-[7?])." A rule of dashes follows.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 101.1)

हे ऋत्विजः । मन्दिने स्तुतिमते स्तोतव्यायेन्द्राय पितुमत् हविर्लक्षणेनान्नेनोपेतं वचः स्तुतिलक्षणं वचनं प्रार्चत । प्रकर्षेणोच्चारयत । य इन्द्र ऋजिश्वनैतन्नाम्ना राज्ञा सख्या सहितः सन् कृष्णगर्भाः । वर्षितारं वज्रदक्षिणं वज्रयुक्तेन दक्षिणहस्तेनोपेतं तं मरुत्वन्तमिन्द्रं सख्याय सख्युः कर्मणे हवामहे । आह्वयामहे ॥ मन्दिने । मदि स्तुतिमोदमदस्वप्नकान्तिगतिषु । औणादिक इनिप्रत्ययः । उक्तं च यास्केन । । अवस्यवः । अवेरौणादिको भावेऽसुन् । अव इच्छतीति [?] अवस्यति । सुप आत्मनः क्यच् । क्यच्छन्दसीत्युप्रत्ययः [?] । वृषणम् । वा षपूर्वस्य निगमे इति विकल्पनादुपधादीर्घाभावः । सख्याय । सख्युः कर्म सख्यम् । yapratyayaḥ | havāmahe | hveño laṭi bahulaṃ chandasīti samprasāraṇam ‖

"O priests! To Indra, who is mandine — who has [the quality of] praise, who is to be praised — offer, prārcata, with great force, the vacaḥ, the speech which has the character of praise, pitumat, accompanied with food that has the character of an oblation. That Indra who, with his friend the king named Ṛjiśvan, nirahan — killed — kṛṣṇagarbhāḥ: there was an Asura named Kṛṣṇa; his wives, in whom the embryos placed by him were — [Indra] killed them. The sense is that, having killed the Asura Kṛṣṇa, he killed also his pregnant wives, in order that no other offspring should arise [from them] [?]. We, avasyavaḥ, who wish for protection, havāmahe — call — for the sake of friendship, that vṛṣaṇam — the sprinkler of desires — vajradakṣiṇam — he who has the thunderbolt in the right hand — Indra, accompanied by the Maruts." The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read: mandin (root mad with the Uṇādi ini; Yāska's statement: mandī mandateḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ [Ni. 4-31, as read, ?]); pitumat (the acute on matup after a stem with shortened and nuṭ-augmented …); kṛṣṇagarbhāḥ (a compound with the accent on the last syllable of the first member by parādiś chandasi bahulam); avasyu (root av with the Uṇādi asun, the denominative kyac, and u by kyac chandasi, [as read, ?]); vṛṣaṇam (no lengthening of the penult, by an optional rule); sakhyāya (ya by sakhyur yaḥ); havāmahe (root hve with samprasāraṇa by bahulaṃ chandasi). Several words are clotted and marked [?].

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"mandine — (O priests,) to Indra, who is worthy of praise; pitumat — accompanied by food in the form of oblation; vacaḥ — words in the form of a hymn; pra arcata — recite exceedingly; yaḥ — which Indra; ṛjiśvanā — together with the king named Ṛjiśvan [his friend]; kṛṣṇagarbhāḥ — the pregnant wives of the Asura named Kṛṣṇa; nirahan — killed; avasyavaḥ — we who wish for protection; vṛṣaṇam — the one who showers desired objects; vajradakṣiṇam — the one who holds the thunderbolt weapon in his right hand; marutvantam — [the one] who is together with the Maruts; sakhyāya — to make friendship (with us); havāmahe — we call."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O priests, praise, with words of hymn together with oblations, Indra, who is to be delighted by hymns. That Indra, together with his friend the king named Ṛjiśvan, killed the Asura named Kṛṣṇa, and also killed his pregnant wives, and so made it that there should be no Asura progeny. We too, desiring protection, call to us, to be our friend, that Indra who showers desired objects, holds the thunderbolt in his right hand, and is together with the Maruts."

original p. 268

English Translation (as printed)

Offer adoration with oblations to him who is delighted (with praise), who, with Rijis'wan, destroyed the pregnant wives of Krishna : desirous of protection, we invoke, to become our friend, him, who is the showerer (of benefits), who holds the thunderbolt in his right hand, attended by the Maruts.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 101.1 (Kannada)

"To show, by the example of the king named Ṛjiśvan, that victory and happiness are sure to come to those who obtain Indra's friendship, the Ṛk prays to Indra, desiring such friendship and also protection.

Mandine — mandī mandateḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ (Ni. 4-[3?]1 as read [?]): derived from the root mand, which gives the sense of praising, [the word means] one who is worthy of praise: it shows honour. Mandine means 'to Indra, who is worthy of reverence, who is worthy of praise'.

Showing the derivation of the word mandine in the manner given above, the Nirukta-author quoted this very Ṛk (Ni. 4-3[1?]):"

प्रार्चत मन्दिने पितुमद्वचः । prārcata mandine pitumad vacaḥ | (Ni. 4-3[1?] as read [?])

"— 'to Indra, who is worthy of praise, offer and honour him with words of praise accompanied by food', is the sense.

Pitumat — since andhaḥ, vājaḥ and the like are read among the twenty-eight [as read, ?] names of food (Ni. 2-7 as read [?]), the word pitu means 'food'. Here the intention is 'together with food in the form of oblations'."

पितुरित्यन्ननाम पातेर्वा पिबतेर्वा प्यायतेर्वा । pitur ity annanāma pāter vā pibater vā pyāyater vā | (Ni. 9-[2?]4 as read [?])

"— from the root pā, which gives the sense 'to protect', or from the root pyai, which gives the sense 'to grow, to fatten': the word pitu is formed and may be a synonym of food: such is the Nirukta-author's derivation. Later, in order to state the right meaning, [the Nirukta-author] again uses this word, in —"

पितुं नु स्तोषं महो धर्माणं तविषीम् । pitum nu stoṣaṃ maho dharmāṇaṃ taviṣīm | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-187-1 as read [?])

original p. 269

"— quoting this Ṛk, he has shown the meaning of the word pitu: 'I praise the food, which bears power and is the nourisher'. In the same way, in the present Ṛk also, for the word pitu the meaning is 'food in the form of an oblation'.

Ṛjiśvanā kṛṣṇagarbhāḥ nirahan — together with his friend, the king named Ṛjiśvan: the idea that Indra killed the Asura named Kṛṣṇa is suggested here, as is the friendship between Indra and Ṛjiśvan. The matter of the king Ṛjiśvan was told in the special topics of the explanations of the [first-maṇḍala sūktas 53 and 5[1?]], as read [?]. This king's name occurs in the Ṛksaṃhitā in many places. Besides the Ṛks 1-53-8 [as read] and 1-5[?]-[?] explained earlier —"

त्वं पिप्रुं मृगयं शूशुवांसमृजिश्वने वैदथिनाय रन्धीः । tvaṃ pipruṃ mṛgayaṃ śūśuvāṃsam ṛjiśvane vaidathināya randhīḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-16-13 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk it is said that Indra destroyed the Asuras Pipru, Mṛgaya and the rest, and helped the king named Ṛjiśvan, son of Vidathin. Likewise —"

आ त्वामृजिश्वा सख्याय चक्रे पचन्पक्तीरपिबः सोममस्य । ā tvām ṛjiśvā sakhyāya cakre pacan paktīr apibaḥ somam asya | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-29-11 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk too Indra's and Ṛjiśvan's friendship is praised. But in the Ṛk 1-[?]-[?] Sāyaṇa has explained Ṛjiśvan as a king, and in 5-29-11 as a seer. Joining the two —"

सुदामन्नद्रेक्णो अप्रमृष्यमृजिश्वने दात्रं दाशुषे दाः । sudāmann adrekṇo apramṛṣyam ṛjiśvane dātraṃ dāśuṣe dāḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-20-2 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk he says 'royal sage' [rājarṣi] [taking both together]. So, in the Ṛks 6-49-10; 10-1[?]-3 and others, too, Ṛjiśvan's name, and his friendship with Indra and the other deities, are described.

Kṛṣṇagarbhāḥ — kṛṣṇo nāmāsuraḥ | sa garbhabhūto 'ntargato yāsāṃ senānāṃ tāḥ kṛṣṇagarbhāḥ | kṛṣṇasahitā ity arthaḥ [as printed, in this context]: 'the Asura named Kṛṣṇa; the armies in whom he had gone as [if] the embryo — those are kṛṣṇagarbhāḥ; that is: together with Kṛṣṇa'. [That is to say: the armies] into which the Asura Kṛṣṇa had entered, giving strength and encouragement to that army, and himself fighting — that army: one meaning. Further —"

अथवा वृष्टिलक्षणा आपः कृष्णगर्भाः कृष्णवर्णस्य मेघस्य गर्भभूतत्वात् । ताः निरहन् । ऋजिश्वना ऋजुगामिना वज्रेण । athavā vṛṣṭilakṣaṇā āpaḥ kṛṣṇagarbhāḥ kṛṣṇavarṇasya meghasya garbhabhūtatvāt | tāḥ nirahan | ṛjiśvanā ṛjugāminā vajreṇa | (Skandasvāmin, as read)

"— [that is: 'or, the waters, which have the character of rain, are kṛṣṇagarbhāḥ because they are the embryo of the black-coloured cloud; those he released (nirahan) with Ṛjiśvan, the straight-going thunderbolt']. Skandasvāmin gives another sense: that the waters in the form of rain, being in the black clouds, [Indra] split the clouds with the straight-travelling thunderbolt and sent down the rain. Sāyaṇa" the sentence continues on the next page

"[Sāyaṇa] explains that Indra killed the Asura named Kṛṣṇa, and also killed his pregnant wives, and so uprooted the Asura family itself."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 101.1) grammar pages, pp. 270–271, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?]

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: mandine (root madi stutimodamadasvapnakāntigatiṣu; num by idito num dhātoḥ [Pā. Sū. 7-1-58 as read]; the Uṇādi affix ini; the word mandin; the i of the affix acute; dative singular; Yāska says the same: mandī mandateḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ [Ni. 4-[3?]1 as read]); pitumat (pituḥ asya asti; matup by hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup [Pā. Sū. 6-1-176 as read]; in the Veda, since a short vowel precedes, matup is acute); arcata (root arca pūjāyām; loṭ, second person plural; since the ṅit-ness is wanting, ta by tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ [Pā. Sū. 3-4-101 as read]; nighāta accent); vacaḥ (root vaca paribhāṣaṇe; asun, the affix attached to all roots; vacas; the first syllable acute, the affix being nit; accusative singular); kṛṣṇagarbhāḥ (kṛṣṇena niṣiktāḥ garbhāḥ yāsu tāḥ; the last syllable of the first member acute by parādiś chandasi bahulam [Pā. Sū. 6-2-199 as read]); ahan (root han hiṃsāgatyoḥ; laṅ, third person singular; since the relative yaḥ is related to it, no nighāta; since the augment aṭ is acute, the word is acute on the first syllable); avasyavaḥ (root ava rakṣaṇe; the Uṇādi asun, which goes with all roots; the word avas; avaḥ ātmanaḥ icchati — in the sense 'wishes for protection for himself', kyac by supa ātmanaḥ kyac [Pā. Sū. 3-1-8 as read]; the word gets the name of a root by sanādyantā dhātavaḥ [Pā. Sū. 3-1-32 as read]; u by kyāc chandasi [Pā. Sū. 3-2-170 as read]; loss of a by ato lopaḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-4-48 as read]; the word avasyu; the final acute by the affix; jas, guṇa by jasi ca [Pā. Sū. 7-3-109 as read], av-substitution; avasyavaḥ).

original p. 271

The grammar of Rik 101.1 concludes: vṛṣaṇam (root vṛṣu secane; the Uṇādi kanin; in the accusative singular the lengthening of the penult, which might be expected, does not come here, since by vā ṣapūrvasya nigame [Pā. Sū. 6-4-9 as read] it is optional); sakhyāya (sakhyuḥ karma sakhyam; ya after sakhi by sakhyur yaḥ [Pā. Sū. 4-1-[?]4 as read, ?]; loss of the i by yasyeti ca [Pā. Sū. 6-4-148 as read]; final acute by the affix; dative singular); havāmahe (root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; laṭ, first person plural, mahiṅ; e for the ṭi by ṭita ātmanepadānām ṭere [Pā. Sū. 3-4-79 as read]; samprasāraṇa by bahulaṃ chandasi; the single substitute by samprasāraṇāc ca [Pā. Sū. 6-1-108 as read]; śap; guṇa of a because of it; av-substitution; lengthening by ato dīrgho yañi [Pā. Sū. 7-3-101 as read] before the mahiṅ beginning with m, giving the form havāmahe; nighāta accent). The Rik is closed with ‖ 1 ‖ and a rule of dashes.

यो व्यंसं जाहृषाणेन मन्युना यः शम्बरं यो अहन्पिप्रुमव्रतम् । इन्द्रो यः शुष्णमशुषं न्यावृणङ्मरुत्वन्तं सख्याय हवामहे ॥ २ ॥

yo vyaṃsaṃ jāhṛṣāṇena manyunā yaḥ śambaraṃ yo ahan pipruṃ avratam | indro yaḥ śuṣṇam aśuṣaṃ ny āvṛṇaṅ marutvantaṃ sakhyāya havāmahe ‖ 2 ‖

यः । विऽअंसम् । जहृषाणेन [?] । मन्युना । यः । शम्बरम् । यः । अहन् । पिप्रुम् । अव्रतम् । इन्द्रः । यः । शुष्णम् । अशुषम् । नि । अवृणक् । मरुत्वन्तम् । सख्याय । हवामहे ॥ २ ॥

yaḥ | vi-aṃsam | jahṛṣāṇena [?] | manyunā | yaḥ | śambaram | yaḥ | ahan | pipruṃ | avratam | indraḥ | yaḥ | śuṣṇam | aśuṣam | ni | avṛṇak | marutvantam | sakhyāya | havāmahe ‖ 2 ‖ the print's Saṃhitā has jāhṛṣāṇena, the Pada jahṛṣāṇena [?]

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 101.2) The print's sakhyāyopyayāmahe is read as sakhyāya hvayāmahe [?].

य इन्द्रो जहृषाणेन प्रवृद्धेन मन्युना क्रोधेन व्यंसं विगतभुजं वृत्रमहन् । अवधीत् । अपि च य इन्द्रः शम्बरमेतन्नामानमसुरं चावधीत् । तथाव्रतं व्रतस्य यागादेः कर्मणो विरोधिनं पिप्रुमेतन्नामानमसुरं च य इन्द्रोऽवधीत् । किंच य इन्द्रोऽशुषं शोषकरहितं शुष्णं सर्वस्य जगतः शोषकमेतन्नामानमसुरं न्यवृणक् । न्यवर्जयत् । समूलं हतवानित्यर्थः । तं मरुत्वन्तमिन्द्रं सख्यायोप्ययामहे । व्यंसम् । विगतोंऽसो यस्मात् । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । यणि उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः इति परस्यानुदात्तस्य स्वरितत्वम् । जहृषाणेन । हृष तुष्टौ । अत्र वृद्ध्यर्थः । छन्दसि लिट् । लिटः कानज्वेति तस्य कानजादेशः । अन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति संहितायामभ्यासस्य दीर्घत्वम् । चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तत्वम् । अशुषम् । शुष शोषणे । इगुपधलक्षणः कः । शुषाः शोषका न सन्त्यस्येत्यशुषः । परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलमित्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । अवृणक् । वृजी वर्जने । रौधादिकः ॥ ya indro jahṛṣāṇena pravṛddhena manyunā krodhena vyaṃsaṃ vigatabhujaṃ vṛtram ahan | avadhīt | api ca ya indraḥ śambaram etannāmānam asuraṃ cāvadhīt | tathāvrataṃ vratasya yāgāder karmaṇo virodhinaṃ pipruṃ etannāmānam asuraṃ ca ya indro 'vadhīt | kiṃ ca ya indro 'śuṣaṃ śoṣakarahitaṃ śuṣṇaṃ sarvasya jagataḥ śoṣakam etannāmānam asuraṃ ny avṛṇak | nyavarjayat | samūlaṃ hatavān ity arthaḥ | taṃ marutvantam indraṃ sakhyāyopyayāmahe [read: hvayāmahe] | vyaṃsam | vigato 'ṃso yasmāt | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | yaṇi udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ iti parasyānudāttasya svaritatvam | jahṛṣāṇena | hṛṣa tuṣṭau | atra vṛddhyarthaḥ | chandasi liṭ | liṭaḥ kānaj veti tasya kānajādeśaḥ | anyeṣām api dṛśyata iti saṃhitāyām abhyāsasya dīrghatvam | cittvād antodāttatvam | aśuṣam | śuṣa śoṣaṇe | igupadhalakṣaṇaḥ kaḥ | śuṣāḥ śoṣakā na santy asyety aśuṣaḥ | parādiś chandasi bahulam ity uttarapadādyudāttatvam | avṛṇak | vṛjī varjane | raudhādikaḥ ‖

"That Indra who, in swelling wrath (jahṛṣāṇena manyunā), killed Vṛtra, who was vyaṃsa — bereft of arms (shoulders); and also killed the Asura named Śambara; and likewise killed the Asura named Pipru, who was avrata, hostile to the rite, the sacrificial act and the like; and further, who ny avṛṇak — cut off, destroyed utterly — the Asura named Śuṣṇa, aśuṣa, who was without the dryness [? i.e. who could not be dried up], the withering of the whole world: him, Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, we call to be our friend." The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read: vyaṃsa (a bahuvrīhi with the accent of its first member); jahṛṣāṇa (root hṛṣ 'to be glad', with the Vedic liṭ and kānac, with lengthening of the reduplicative syllable, final acute because the affix is cit); aśuṣa (root śuṣ 'to dry', with ka by igupadha…, 'one for whom there are no witherers' [as read], accent of the last member); avṛṇak (root vṛj 'to avoid', of the rudhādi class).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"yaḥ — which Indra; jahṛṣāṇena — [with] growing; manyunā — wrath; vyaṃsam — Vṛtra, who was deprived of arms; ahan — killed; yaḥ — which Indra; śambaram — the Rākṣasa named Śambara; (so killed;) yaḥ — which Indra; avratam — the one who is hostile to rites such as sacrifices; pipruṃ — the Asura named Pipru; (killed besides;) yaḥ indraḥ — which Indra; aśuṣam — [him whom others] could not kill or wither; śuṣṇam — [one who withers up the world,] the Asura named Śuṣṇa; ni avṛṇak — uprooted completely;" continues on p. 273

original p. 273

"[marutvantam —] that Indra, together with the Maruts; sakhyāya — to make friendship (with us); havāmahe — we call."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"That Indra who killed Vṛtra, bereft of arms, in wrath growing to the highest degree; and who killed the Rākṣasa named Śambara, and the Asura named Pipru, who was hostile to rites such as sacrifice; and who uprooted completely the Asura named Śuṣṇa, who could not be held back by others, and who had the power to hold back all the world — such an Indra, together with the Maruts, we call to make friendship and to help us."

English Translation (as printed)

We invoke to be our friend, Indra, who is attended by the Maruts ; he who, with increasing wrath, slew the mutilated Vritra, and Sambara, and unrighteous Pipru, and who extirpated the unabsorbable S'ushna.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 101.2 (Kannada)

"In explaining the sense of this Ṛk, there are differences in some places between Sāyaṇa's bhāṣya and Skandasvāmin's bhāṣya.

Jahṛṣāṇena manyunā vyaṃsam ahan — to this sentence Sāyaṇa has given the explanation: 'pravṛddhena krodhena vigatabhujaṃ vṛtram avadhīt': 'by a growing anger he killed Vṛtra, who was bereft of arms'.

Skandasvāmin explained, taking vyaṃsa as the name of a certain Rākṣasa, [thus:]"

जहृषाणेन आत्मार्थं हृष्यता मन्युना मन्युनाम्ना प्रजापतिपुत्रेण सह अहन् । jahṛṣāṇena ātmārthaṃ hṛṣyatā manyunā manyunāmnā prajāpatiputreṇa saha ahan | (Skandasvāmin, as read)

"— [that is: 'with the Manyu — the son of Prajāpati, named Manyu — who was rejoicing for his own sake, he killed']: so, joined with Manyu, who showed the greatest delight and who was the son of Prajāpati, he killed the Asura named Vyaṃsa — one sense; or:"

अथवा मन्युरिति क्रोधनाम । आत्मार्थं हृष्यता क्रोधेन । प्रविवेकसता [?] क्रोधेन इत्यर्थः । athavā manyur iti krodhanāma | ātmārthaṃ hṛṣyatā krodhena | praviveka-satā [?] krodhena ity arthaḥ |

"— [that is: 'or manyu is a name of anger; with anger that rejoices for its own sake'] — 'by the anger that grew exceedingly' is another sense that he has given. According to this second explanation, vyaṃsa is a name, a proper noun, and manyu has only the sense of 'anger' [and not the person]. But here Skandasvāmin's construction and meaning appear to have no support; Sāyaṇa's explanation is the natural one: the word vyaṃsa, which means 'one whose arms have gone', is used in many Ṛks, and is an adjective of Vṛtra and of other Asuras."

original p. 274

Special Topics of Rik 101.2, continued from p. 273 (Kannada)

अहन्वृत्रं वृत्रतरं व्यंसमिन्द्रो वज्रेण महता वधेन । ahan vṛtraṃ vṛtrataraṃ vyaṃsam indro vajreṇa mahatā vadhena | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-32-5 as read [?])

अहन्निहिमभिनद्रौहिणं व्यस्यंसं मघवा शचीभिः । ahann ihim abhinad rauhiṇaṃ vy aṃsaṃ maghavā śacībhiḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-103-2 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these, 'one who has lost his shoulders' is an adjective of Vṛtra. And further —"

अध्वर्यवो यः स्वश्नं जघान यः शुष्णमशुषं यो व्यंसम् । adhvaryavo yaḥ svaśnaṃ jaghāna yaḥ śuṣṇam aśuṣaṃ yo vyaṃsam | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-14-5 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk it is an adjective of Śuṣṇa, 'one who has lost his shoulders'. Thus vyaṃsa is in the sense of 'deprived of arms'; apart from this, it is not seen used anywhere as a proper name.

Śambaram (ahan) — Indra's [killing of] the enemy Śambara is told in the Ṛks 1-[?]-[?], 1-5[?]-[?], 1-1[?]-[?], 1-130-[?], 1-1[?]-[?], 1-1[?]-[?]. In general, his name is found mostly alongside the Asuras Śuṣṇa, Pipru and Varcin."

अव गिरेर्दासं शम्बरं हन्प्रावो दिवोदासं चित्राभिरूतिभिः । ava girer dāsaṃ śambaraṃ han prāvo divodāsaṃ citrābhir ūtibhiḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-26-5 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk he is called a dāsa."

दिवोदासाय नवतिं च नवेन्द्रः पुरो व्यैरच्छम्बरस्य । divodāsāya navatiṃ ca navendraḥ puro vy airac chambarasya | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-19-6 as read [?])

अध्वर्यवो यः शतं शम्बरस्य पुरो बिभेदाश्मनेव पूर्वीः । adhvaryavo yaḥ śataṃ śambarasya puro bibhedāśmaneva pūrvīḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-14-6 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these, Divodāsa is both a devoted friend of Indra and a natural enemy of Śambara. It is described that Indra, for the sake of that king named Divodāsa, laid waste the ninety-nine, a hundred — that is, innumerable — fortresses of Śambara, and made his sovereignty his own [Divodāsa's]. In the same way —"

अतिथिग्वाय शम्बरं गिरेरुग्रो अवाभरत् । atithigvāya śambaraṃ girer ugro avābharat | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-130-7 as read [?])

उत दासं कौलितरं बृहतः पर्वतादधि । अवाहन्निन्द्र शम्बरम् ॥ uta dāsaṃ kaulitaraṃ bṛhataḥ parvatād adhi | avāhann indra śambaram ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-30-14 as read [?])

original p. 275

अव गिरेर्दासं शम्बरं हन्प्रावो दिवोदासं चित्राभिरूतिभिः ॥ ava girer dāsaṃ śambaraṃ han prāvo divodāsaṃ citrābhir ūtibhiḥ ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-26-5 as read [?]; the same Ṛk as quoted on p. 274)

"— from Ṛks like these it is understood that Indra, having thrown Śambara down from the mountain where he lay hidden, destroyed him and gave his own protection to both Atithigva and Divodāsa, who were exceedingly oppressed by him. Likewise in many other places the slaying of Śambara is told.

Avrataṃ pipruṃ — like Śambara, Pipru too is said in many Ṛks to have been overcome by Indra. As Divodāsa and Atithigva fought a war with Śambara, so Indra fought with Pipru for the sake of Ṛjiśvan; Pipru is spoken of in the Ṛks 4-1[6?]-1[3?], 5-[2?]9-11, 6-20-[?], 8-4[?]-1[?], 10-[?]-[?], 10-1[?]-[?] and others."

वि पिप्रोरहिमायस्य दृळ्हाः पुरो वज्रिञ्छवसा न दर्दः । vi pipror ahimāyasya dṛḷhāḥ puro vajriñ chavasā na dardaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-20-7 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these, that Indra destroyed the strong fortresses and the like of Pipru; and —"

यः स्वबिन्दुमर्णनिं पिप्रुं दासमहीशुनम् । yaḥ svabinduṃ arṇaniṃ pipruṃ dāsam ahīśunam | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-3[?]-[?] as read [?]; the first word clotted in print, not completed from memory)

"— in Ṛks like these Pipru is said to belong to the group of dāsas; and in many other places likewise his form and his power are described. Some have expressed doubt whether Pipru was an Asura or a man without rites:

'It is uncertain whether he was a demon, according to Roth's view, which is favoured by the use of the word Asura, or a human foe, as Ludwig, Oldenberg and Hillebrandt believe.' English in the original.

(Vide Vedic Index of Names and Subjects by Keith and Macdonell, Vol. I, p. 532.)

But the bhāṣya-author has called him an Asura.

Aśuṣaṃ śuṣṇaṃ — [Indra killed] Śuṣṇa, who could not be killed: that is, no one other than Indra could kill him. The Asura named Śuṣṇa dried up all the waters, and, though he was extremely powerful, he was at last killed by Indra. Apart from Vṛtra, this is the foe most harmful [to the world], the Asura who caused drought. After his slaying the earth became full of the abundance of crops and full of fruit."

"So, in many places the description of the deformed form of Śuṣṇa shows his terrifying shape."

न्यविध्यदिलीबिशस्य दृळ्हा वि शृङ्गिणमभिनच्छुष्णमिन्द्रः । nyavidhyad ilībiśasya dṛḷhā vi śṛṅgiṇam abhinac chuṣṇam indraḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-33-12 as read [?])

तत्त्वा याचामहे ऽवः शुष्णं यद्धन्नमानुषम् । tat tvā yācāmahe 'vaḥ śuṣṇaṃ yad dhann amānuṣam | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-22-[?] as read [?])

"— this was Indra's effort to uproot the very race of such a drier-up, Śuṣṇa."

उतो नु चिद्य ओजसा शुष्णस्याण्डानि भेदति । जेषत्स्वर्वतीरपो नभन्तामन्यके समे ॥ uto nu cid ya ojasā śuṣṇasyāṇḍāni bhedati | jeṣat svarvatīr apo nabhantām anyake same ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-40-10 as read [?])

उतो चिद्य ओहत अण्डा शुष्णस्य भेदत्यजैः स्वर्वतीरपो नभन्तामन्यके समे । uto cid ya ohata aṇḍā śuṣṇasya bhedaty ajaiḥ svarvatīr apo nabhantām anyake same | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-40-11 as read [?]; the print repeats this line with small differences, probably for the second half-verse, and it is given as printed [?])

"— in Ṛks like these, Indra's effort to destroy the very offspring of Śuṣṇa is described.

[A further point:] the slaying of Śuṣṇa was something extremely dear and desired by Kutsa Ārjuneya, Indra's friend; so —"

त्वं सत्य इन्द्र धृष्णुरेतान्त्वमृभुक्षा नर्यस्त्वं षाट् । त्वं शुष्णं वृजने पृक्ष आणौ यूने कुत्साय द्युमते सचाहन् ॥ tvaṃ satya indra dhṛṣṇur etān tvam ṛbhukṣā naryas tvaṃ ṣāṭ | tvaṃ śuṣṇaṃ vṛjane pṛkṣa āṇau yūne kutsāya dyumate sacāhan ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-63-3 as read [?])

"— and in the Ṛks 8-1-[?]; 6-3[?]-3; 2-1[?]-[?] and others the slaying of Śuṣṇa is described.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 101.2) grammar pages, pp. 276–277, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?]

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: vyaṃsam (vigataḥ aṃśaḥ yasmāt saḥ vyaṃsaḥ; in the bahuvrīhi the first member keeps its accent by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam [Pā. Sū. 6-2-1 as read]; the i of vi is acute; since yaṇ takes its place, the unaccented a following it receives the svarita by udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritaḥ [Pā. Sū. 8-2-4 as read]).

original p. 277

The grammar of Rik 101.2 concludes: jahṛṣāṇena (root hṛṣa tuṣṭau, which has several senses, here used in the sense of vṛddhi; liṭ by chandasi liṭ [Pā. Sū. 3-2-105 as read], though liṭ is generally expected; for it kānac by liṭaḥ kānac vā [Pā. Sū. 3-2-106 as read]; doubling of the root; halādiśeṣa in the reduplicative; ur at by ur at [Pā. Sū. 7-4-66 as read]; since raparatva comes, again halādiśeṣa; since the affix is kit, no guṇa of the penult of the root; ṇ for the n of the affix by āṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi [Pā. Sū. 8-4-2 as read], on account of the ṣ; the form jahṛṣāṇa; lengthening of the reduplicative in the Saṃhitā by anyeṣām api dṛśyate [Pā. Sū. 6-3-137 as read]; since kānac is cit, final acute by citaḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-1-163 as read]; instrumental singular); manyunā (root manu avabodhane; the Uṇādi yu; final acute by the affix; instrumental); ahan (root han hiṃsāgatyoḥ, adādi; laṅ, third person singular; because yaḥ is related to it, no nighāta by yadvṛttān nityam [Pā. Sū. 8-1-66 as read]; since the augment aṭ is acute, the word is acute on the first syllable); aśuṣam (root śuṣa śoṣaṇe; ka by igupadhajñāprīkiraḥ kaḥ [Pā. Sū. 3-1-135 as read]; since kit, no guṇa of the penult; śuṣāḥ śoṣakāḥ na santy asya iti aśuṣaḥ; the accent of the second member by parādiś chandasi bahulam [Pā. Sū. 6-1-199 as read]; accusative singular); avṛṇak (root vṛjī varjane, rudhādi; laṅ, third person singular, tip; loss of the i by itaś ca [Pā. Sū. 3-4-100 as read]; śnam by rudhādibhyaḥ śnam [Pā. Sū. 3-1-78 as read]; num and its m-augment after the last vowel by midaco 'ntyāt paraḥ [Pā. Sū. 1-1-47 as read]; loss of t by halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisyapṛktaṃ hal [Pā. Sū. 6-1-68 as read]; k for j by coḥ kuḥ [Pā. Sū. 8-2-30 as read]; since a ṛ precedes it, ṇ for the n of the vikaraṇa; since the relative yaḥ is related to it, no nighāta, and since the augment aṭ is acute, the word is acute on the first syllable).
