Rik 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 101.3)

यस्य द्यावापृथिवी पौंस्यं महद्यस्य व्रते वरुणो यस्य सूर्यः । यस्येन्द्रस्य सिन्धवः सश्चति व्रतं मरुत्वन्तं सख्याय हवामहे ॥ ३ ॥

yasya dyāvāpṛthivī pauṃsyaṃ mahad yasya vrate varuṇo yasya sūryaḥ | yasyendrasya sindhavaḥ saścati vrataṃ marutvantaṃ sakhyāya havāmahe ‖ 3 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 101.3)

यस्य । द्यावापृथिवी इति । पौंस्यम् । महत् । यस्य । व्रते । वरुणः । यस्य । सूर्यः । यस्य । इन्द्रस्य । सिन्धवः । सश्चति । व्रतम् । मरुत्वन्तम् । सख्याय । हवामहे ॥ ३ ॥

yasya | dyāvāpṛthivī iti | pauṃsyam | mahat | yasya | vrate | varuṇaḥ | yasya | sūryaḥ | yasya | indrasya | sindhavaḥ | saścati | vratam | marutvantam | sakhyāya | havāmahe ‖ 3 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 101.3)

यस्येन्द्रस्य महद्विपुलं पौंस्यं बलं द्यावापृथिवी द्यावापृथिव्योरनुवर्तते । यस्य चेन्द्रस्य व्रते नियमरूपे कर्मणि वरुणो वर्तते । वरुणोऽपीन्द्रस्य नियमनं नातिक्रामतीत्यर्थः । अपि च सूर्योऽपि यस्येन्द्रस्य व्रते वर्तते । तथा यस्येन्द्रस्य व्रतं कर्म सिन्धवो नद्यः सश्चति । वचनव्यत्ययः । गच्छन्ति । सश्चतिर्गतिकर्मा । इन्द्रेणानुशिष्टाः प्रवहन्तीत्यर्थः । तं मरुत्वन्तमिन्द्रं सख्यायाह्वयामहे ॥ द्यावापृथिवी । द्यौश्च पृथिवी च द्यावापृथिव्यौ । दिवो द्यावेति द्यावादेशः । स चाद्युदात्तो निपातितः । पृथिवीशब्दो जातिष्प्रत्ययान्तोऽन्तोदात्तः । देवताद्वन्द्वे चेत्युभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । वा छन्दसीति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः ॥ yasyendrasya mahad vipulaṃ pauṃsyaṃ balaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī dyāvāpṛthivyor anuvartate | yasya cendrasya vrate niyamarūpe karmaṇi varuṇo vartate | varuṇo 'pīndrasya niyamanaṃ nātikrāmatīty arthaḥ | api ca sūryo 'pi yasyendrasya vrate vartate | tathā yasyendrasya vrataṃ karma sindhavo nadyaḥ saścati | vacanavyatyayaḥ | gacchanti | saścatir gatikarmā | indreṇānuśiṣṭāḥ pravahantīty arthaḥ | taṃ marutvantam indraṃ sakhyāyāhvayāmahe ‖ dyāvāpṛthivī | dyauś ca pṛthivī ca dyāvāpṛthivyau | divo dyāveti dyāvādeśaḥ | sa cādyudātto nipātitaḥ | pṛthivīśabdo jāṣpratyayānto 'ntodāttaḥ | devatādvandve cety ubhayapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | vā chandasīti pūrvasavarṇadīrghaḥ ‖

"Of that Indra whose great, abundant manly strength is followed by heaven and earth, and in whose vrata — in the work that has the form of a [fixed] rule — Varuṇa stays: the sense is that even Varuṇa does not go beyond Indra's regulation. And also the sun stays in the vrata of that Indra. And likewise the rivers, the streams, saścati [plural, by exchange of number] — go, in the work of that Indra: saścati is a verb of going. The sense is that, instructed by Indra, they flow on. Him, that Indra with the Maruts, we call to be our friend." The grammatical tail is characterized: dyāvāpṛthivī (a dvandva of dyu and pṛthivī, with dyāvā for div by divo dyāvā, the accent on the first syllable by nipātana; the second member ends in ṅīṣ/jāṣ, acute on the last; the accent of both members stays by devatādvandve ca, and the long vowel is of the same class by vā chandasi).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada) begins on p. 279

original p. 279

"yasya — of which Indra; mahat — exceeding; pauṃsyam — the strength; dyāvāpṛthivī — [that has pervaded] heaven and earth, both; yasya — of which Indra; vrate — in the command, which has the form of work; varuṇaḥ — Varuṇa (who stands firm, intent on the work to be done), and; sūryaḥ — the sun too; yasya — of which Indra; (who stand intent on the work to be done in obedience to the command;) yasya indrasya — of which Indra; vratam — the work of command; sindhavaḥ — the rivers too; saścati — go on carrying out (they flow); marutvantam — Indra, thus together with the Maruts; sakhyāya — to make friendship (with us); havāmahe — we call."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"Indra whose exceeding strength has pervaded heaven and earth both; in whose command Varuṇa and the sun stand firm, intent on the work to be done; and in whose commanded work the rivers too flow — such an Indra, together with the Maruts, we call to make friendship with us."

English Translation (as printed)

We invoke to become our friend, Indra who is attended by the Maruts ; whose great power (pervades) heaven and earth, in whose service Varuna and Surya are steadfast, and whose command the rivers obey.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 101.3 (Kannada)

आवासृजन्त जिव्रयो न देवा भुवः सम्राळिन्द्र सत्ययोनिः । āvāsṛjanta jivrayo na devā bhuvaḥ samrāḷ indra satyayoniḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-19-3 as read [?]; as quoted on p. 171)

एवा वस्व इन्द्रः सत्यः सम्राड्ढन्ता वृत्रं वरिवः पूरवे कः । evā vasva indraḥ satyaḥ samrāḍ dhantā vṛtraṃ varivaḥ pūrave kaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-21-10 as read [?]; as quoted on p. 171)

"— since in many places like these Indra is praised as the lord of the whole universe, all the affairs of the universe are carried out as Indra commands. For that very reason Varuṇa, the sun and all the rivers carry out their duty under Indra's command alone. And Indra's strength has pervaded heaven and earth both, and surpassed them —"

उताभये पुरुहूत श्रवोभिरेको दृळ्हमवदो वृत्रहा सन् । इमे चिदिन्द्र रोदसी अपारे यत्संगृभ्णा मघवन्काशिरित्ते ॥ utābhaye puruhūta śravobhir eko dṛḷham avado vṛtrahā san | ime cid indra rodasī apāre yat saṃgṛbhṇā maghavan kāśir it te ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-30-5 as read [?]; the first line is given as read, the second is clotted in places [?])

original p. 280

"— so, since he has pervaded both heaven and earth, which are difficult to measure and have extensive expanse, and shown his own strength, in this Ṛk also it is described that yasya mahat pauṃsyaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī (saścati). It is because he has such strength and sovereignty that Varuṇa and the others are obedient to his commands."

विश्वे ते इन्द्र वीर्यं देवा अनु क्रतुं ददुः । viśve te indra vīryaṃ devā anu kratuṃ daduḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-6-3 as read [?])

"— that all the gods yield to Indra's valour and prowess; and —"

यदा सूर्यममुं दिवि शुक्रं ज्योतिरधारयः । आदित्ते विश्वा भुवनानि येमिरे ॥ yadā sūryam amuṃ divi śukraṃ jyotir adhārayaḥ | ād it te viśvā bhuvanāni yemire ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-12-30 as read [?])

"— in many places it is praised that, when Indra established the shining sun in the mid-air, all the worlds became subject to him. The same points are described here.

Vratam — here vrata means 'work'. The rain-like and sacrifice-like works, and the other works as well, are carried out by Indra's command.

Saścati — vartate. Since ayate, saścati and the like are read among the twenty-two [as read, ?] names of verbs of going (Ni. 2-[?] as read [?]), saścati means 'goes'; that is, 'carries out'."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 101.3) grammar pages, pp. 280–281, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?]

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: dyāvāpṛthivī (dyauś ca pṛthivī ca dyāvāpṛthivyau; in the compound, dyāvā for div by divo dyāvā [Pā. Sū. 6-3-29 as read]; this substitute is fixed by nipātana as acute on the first syllable; the word pṛthivī, ending in the affix ṅīṣ, is acute on the last; then in the compound the accent of both members is retained by devatādvandve ca [Pā. Sū. 6-2-141 as read]; to it, the dual ending following, the single substitute of the previous homogeneous long vowel comes by vā chandasi [Pā. Sū. 6-1-106 as read]); pauṃsyam (puṃsaḥ bhāvaḥ pauṃsyam; ṣyañ; as it is ñit, vṛddhi by taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ; acute on the first syllable by ñnityādir nityam [Pā. Sū. 6-1-197 as read]); sūryaḥ (sarati ākāśe iti sūryaḥ; root sṛ gatau; kyap-ending form fixed by nipātana in rājasūyasūrya… [Pā. Sū. 3-1-114 as read]; since the affix is pit, unaccented, the root's accent remains).

original p. 281

The grammar of Rik 101.3 concludes: sindhavaḥ (root syandū prasravaṇe; uṇ by an Uṇādi rule [Uṇ. Sū. 1-[?]1 as read, ?], with samprasāraṇa of the root and dh for d, by skandeḥ samprasāraṇaṃ dhaś ca; the form sindhu; in the nominative plural jas, guṇa by jasi ca, av-substitution); saścati (root saśca gatau; laṭ, third person plural; the singular tip by vyatyayo bahulam [Pā. Sū. 3-1-85 as read]; śap; because of the relative [yasya], no nighāta; since śap and tip are pit, unaccented, the root's accent remains). The Rik is closed with ‖ 3 ‖ and a rule of dashes.

Rik 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 101.4)

यो अश्वानां यो गवां गोपतिर्वशी य आरितः कर्मणिकर्मणि स्थिरः । वीळोश्चिदिन्द्रो यो असुन्वतो वधो मरुत्वन्तं सख्याय हवामहे ॥ ४ ॥

yo aśvānāṃ yo gavāṃ gopatir vaśī ya āritaḥ karmaṇi-karmaṇi sthiraḥ | vīḷoś cid indro yo asunvato vadho marutvantaṃ sakhyāya havāmahe ‖ 4 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 101.4)

यः । अश्वानाम् । यः । गवाम् । गोऽपतिः । वशी । यः । आरितः । कर्मणिऽकर्मणि । स्थिरः । वीळोः । चित् । इन्द्रः । यः । असुन्वतः । वधः । मरुत्वन्तम् । सख्याय । हवामहे ॥ ४ ॥

yaḥ | aśvānām | yaḥ | gavām | go-patiḥ | vaśī | yaḥ | āritaḥ | karmaṇi-karmaṇi | sthiraḥ | vīḷoḥ | cit | indraḥ | yaḥ | asunvataḥ | vadhaḥ | marutvantam | sakhyāya | havāmahe ‖ 4 ‖

original p. 282

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 101.4)

यः इन्द्रोऽश्वानामीशानानां पतिरधिपतिः । तथा य इन्द्रो गोपतिः । न केवलमेकस्या गोः किन्तु सर्वासामित्याह गवामिति । सर्वासां गवामधिपतिर्भवति । वशी अपराधीनः स्वतन्त्र इत्यर्थः । अपि च य इन्द्रः कर्मणि कर्मणि सर्वेषु कर्मसु स्थिरो नैश्चल्येनावतिष्ठमान आरितः स्तुतिभिः प्रत्यृतः प्राप्तो भवति । आरितः प्रत्यृतः स्तोमानिति निरुक्तम् । नि. ५-[३?]२ [?] । यश्चेन्द्रोऽसुन्वतः सुन्वतां योगानुष्ठात्रॄणां विरोधिनो वीळोश्चित् दृढस्यापि शत्रोर्वधो हन्ता तं मरुत्वन्तमिन्द्रं सख्यायोप्ययामहे ॥ गवाम् । न गोश्वन्साववर्णे । पा. ६-१-[१८?]२ [?] । इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वस्य प्रतिषेधः । गोपतिः । पत्यावैश्वर्य इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । आरितः । ऋ गतौ । अस्माण्ण्यन्तात्क्तः । आगमानुशासनस्यानित्यत्वात्पुगागमाभावः । यद्वा । सूचिसूत्रिमूत्र्यृत्यर्तिभ्यश्च [?] । पा. ३-२-[?] । इति विहितस्य यजो यजोऽचि [?] चेत्यत्र चकारेण बहुलग्रहणानुकर्षणादन्येमित्रके लुकि प्रत्ययलक्षणेन सन्यजोरिति …(the line is clotted) … ऋ इत्येतस्य द्विर्वचने उरदत्वहलादिशेषयोः सतो रुग्रिकौ च लुकीति रुक् । ततो निष्ठायां छान्दस इडागमः । ऋकारस्य यणादेशः रो रीत्यभ्यासरेफलोपः । द्र्लोपे पूर्वस्य दीर्घोऽणः इति दीर्घत्वम् । वधः । कृत्यल्युटो बहुलमिति बहुलवचनाद्धनश्च वध इति कर्तर्यप् वधादेशश्च । स चान्तः । अतो लोपे उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण प्रत्ययस्योदात्तत्वम् ॥ ya indro 'śvānām īśānānāṃ patir adhipatiḥ | tathā ya indro gopatiḥ | na kevalam ekasyā goḥ kintu sarvāsām ity āha gavām iti | sarvāsāṃ gavām adhipatir bhavati | vaśī aparādhīnaḥ svatantra ity arthaḥ | api ca ya indraḥ karmaṇi karmaṇi sarveṣu karmasu sthiro naiścalyenāvatiṣṭhamāna āritaḥ stutibhiḥ pratyṛtaḥ prāpto bhavati | āritaḥ pratyṛtaḥ stomān iti niruktam | Ni. 5-[3?]2 [?] | yaś cendro 'sunvataḥ sunvatāṃ yogānuṣṭhātṝṇāṃ virodhino vīḷoś cit dṛḍhasyāpi śatror vadho hantā taṃ marutvantam indraṃ sakhyāyopyayāmahe ‖ gavām | na gośvansāvavarṇe | Pā. 6-1-[18?]2 [?] | iti vibhakter udāttatvasya pratiṣedhaḥ | gopatiḥ | patyāvaiśvarya iti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | āritaḥ | ṛ gatau | asmāṇ ṇyantāt ktaḥ | āgamānuśāsanasyānityatvāt pugāgamābhāvaḥ | yadvā | sūcisūtrimūtryṛtyartibhyaś ca [?] | … [the middle is clotted] … vadhaḥ | kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam iti bahulavacanād dhanaś ca vadha iti kartary ap vadhādeśaś ca | sa cāntaḥ | ato lope udāttanivṛttisvareṇa pratyayasyodāttatvam ‖

"That Indra who is the lord, the sovereign, of the horses, the ruling ones. And that Indra is the lord of the cows (gopati): not of a single cow only, but of all; so he says, gavām — he is the sovereign of all cows. Vaśī — not subordinate to another: independent. And that Indra, in each and every work (karmaṇi karmaṇi), sthiraḥ — standing without moving — āritaḥ, pratyṛtaḥ — reached, attained, by praises. [The Nirukta:] āritaḥ pratyṛtaḥ stomān [as read (Ni. 5-[3?]2 [?])]. And that Indra who is the destroyer (vadhaḥ) of the enemy of those who perform sacrifices, the asunvat, the one who presses no Soma, even though he is strong (vīḷoḥ cit) — him, the Indra with the Maruts, we call to be our friend." The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read: gavām (the genitive plural; the prohibition of the acute on the ending by na gośvansāvavarṇe… [Pā. Sū. 6-1-[18?]2, as read [?]]); gopati (the accent of the first member by patyāvaiśvarye); arita (root ṛ 'to go', with the causative ṇic and kta, no puk because the rules of augment-teaching are not invariable; or from ṛ with yaj …; the middle is clotted and not reproduced [?]); vadha (the affix ap in the agent with the substitute vadha for han). The sūtra numerals are small and doubtful.

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"yaḥ — which Indra; aśvānām — of horses; adhipatiḥ — the sovereign; yaḥ — which Indra; gavām — of all cows; gopatiḥ — the protector of the cows, and; vaśī — independent (not subordinate to another); yaḥ — which Indra; karmaṇi karmaṇi — in every sacrificial act; sthiraḥ — standing firm; āritaḥ — praised by the praisers, or brought near (reached by all); yaḥ indraḥ — which Indra; asunvataḥ — those who hate the performers of sacrifices; vīḷoḥ cit — even a powerful enemy; vadhaḥ — is the killer; marutvantam — together with the Maruts, that Indra; sakhyāya — to make friendship (with us); havāmahe — we call."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"Which Indra is the sovereign of all horses and cows; who is independent; who stands firm in every sacrificial act and is praised by the praisers; and who, even if the enemy is mighty, slays him who is without sacrifice and who hates those who sacrifice; that Indra, together with the Maruts, we call to make friendship with us."

original p. 283

English Translation (as printed)

Who is the lord over all horses and cattle, who is independent, who, propitiated by praise, is constant in every act, and who is the slayer of the obstinate abstainer from libations : we invoke to become our friend, Indra, attended by the Maruts.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 101.4 (Kannada)

"Gavāṃ gopatiḥ — na kevalam ekasyā goḥ kintu sarvāsām ity āha gavām iti | sarvāsāṃ gavām adhipatir bhavati: [Sāyaṇa] has explained that, since he is the sovereign of all cows, the repetition in gavāṃ gopatiḥ [go… gavām] is [only apparent]. But Skandasvāmin:"

गोशब्दोऽत्राप्शब्दवचनः सोमवचनो वा स्तुतिवचनो वा स्तोत्रवचनो वा । पतिशब्दोऽप्यधिपतिवचनः पालयितृवचनो वा । अपां वा सोमस्य वा स्तुतीनां वा स्तोत्र्याणां वा अधिपतिः पालयिता वेत्यर्थः । gośabdo 'tra apśabdavacanaḥ somavacano vā stutivacano vā stotravacano vā | patiśabdo 'py adhipativacanaḥ pālayitṛvacano vā | apāṃ vā somasya vā stutīnāṃ vā stotryāṇāṃ vā adhipatiḥ pālayitā vety arthaḥ | (Skandasvāmin, as read)

"— [that is: here the word go is a word for water, or for Soma, or for praise, or for praisers; and the word pati is a word for lord or protector: the sense is 'lord or protector of the waters, or of Soma, or of the praises, or of the praisers']. For the word go here, any meaning may be given among waters, Soma, praise or praiser: he explains that it means 'lord of water, or of Soma, or of praise, or of praiser'.

Vaśī — Skandasvāmin has made the construction yaś cāśvānāṃ gavāṃ ca vaśī and given it the meaning that he rules the horses and cows; and for the word gopati he has given the above meaning. But Sāyaṇa gives for the word vaśī the sense aparādhīnaḥ svatantraḥ, 'independent'."

यस्य ते नू चिदादिशं न मिनन्ति स्वराज्यम् । न देवो नाध्रिगुर्जनः ॥ yasya te nū cid ādiśaṃ na minanti svarājyam | na devo nādhrigur janaḥ ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]3-11 as read [?])

त्वमिन्द्राभिभूरसि त्वं सूर्यमरोचयः । विश्वकर्मा विश्वदेवो महाँ असि ॥ tvam indrābhibhūr asi tvaṃ sūryam arocayaḥ | viśvakarmā viśvadevo mahām̐ asi ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-98-2 as read [?])

original p. 284

"— since in such Ṛks Indra alone is the one who commands the whole universe, it is he who is independent. As is said in the third Ṛk of this very sūkta —"

यस्य द्यावापृथिवी पौंस्यं महद्यस्य व्रते वरुणो यस्य सूर्यः । यस्येन्द्रस्य सिन्धवः सश्चति व्रतं मरुत्वन्तं सख्याय हवामहे ॥ yasya dyāvāpṛthivī pauṃsyaṃ mahad yasya vrate varuṇo yasya sūryaḥ | yasyendrasya sindhavaḥ saścati vrataṃ marutvantaṃ sakhyāya havāmahe ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-101-3 as read [?]; Rik 3 of the present sūkta)

"— Varuṇa, the sun and all the rivers follow the command of that Indra, and all affairs of the universe go on subject to him. Everything is subject to him; he is subject to nothing. He is truly independent.

Āritaḥ — āgata ity arthaḥ | punaḥ punaḥ sarvayajñeṣv āgatas san ā yajñaparisamāpter aviśālī: [Skandasvāmin:] 'he who, having come again and again to all sacrifices, remains till the completion of the sacrifice, unmoving' — that is, he who stands in place at every step of the sacrifice until the sacrifice is completed: Skandasvāmin's explanation. Sāyaṇa, quoting the Nirukta sentence āritaḥ pratyṛtaḥ stomān (Ni. 5-[3?]2 as read [?]), says stutibhiḥ pratyṛtaḥ prāpto bhavati — 'he is attained by praises'. This meaning is the more fitting. In the same way —"

वृतंचयः सहुरिर्विक्ष्वारित इन्द्रस्य वोचं प्र कृतानि वीर्या । vṛtaṃcayaḥ sahurir vikṣv ārita indrasya vocaṃ pra kṛtāni vīryā | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1[?]-3 as read [?]; the first word clotted in print [?])

"— in this Ṛk too, for the word āritaḥ used there, the sense is pālakatvena prāpitaḥ, 'brought near as protector': he was brought near as a protector; the sense is that he came together with all.

Asunvataḥ — one who does not press the Soma juice, and does not do sacrifices and the like; or one who hates the performers of sacrifices.

Vīḷoś cit — vīḷayatiś ca prīḷayatiś ca saṃstambhakarmaṇau (Ni. 5-[?]) — the Nirukta-author says that the words vīḷa and prīḷa are used in the sense of 'hard' or 'firm', and has quoted the Ṛk"

तद्देवानां देवतमाय कर्त्वमश्रथ्नन्दृळ्हाववदन्त वीळिता । tad devānāṃ devatamāya kartvam aśrathnan dṛḷhāv avadanta vīḷitā | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-31-[?] as read [?])

"— there, for the word vīḷitā, the sense dṛḍhīkṛtā is shown; so here also vīḷoḥ means dṛḍhasya, 'of the firm, hard': in the enemy sense it is construed 'extremely hard, or firm'. 'However strong the enemy may be, however hard, he destroys him,' is the sense. And for the full sense of the word vīḷa and the fitting context of its use, also —"

original p. 285

अग्ने वीळो वीळित वीळयस्व मा यामादस्माद्देव जीहिपो नः । agne vīḷo vīḷita vīḷayasva mā yāmād asmād deva jīhipo naḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]2-[?] as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk it may be seen.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 101.4) grammar pages, pp. 285–[286], noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?]

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: gavām (the word go; genitive plural; the acute on the ending, which sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-1-168 as read] would give, is prevented by na gośvansāvavarṇarāḍaṅkukrukṣuk… [Pā. Sū. 6-1-182 as read]); gopatiḥ (gavāṃ patiḥ gopatiḥ; the accent of the first member by patyāvaiśvarye [Pā. Sū. 6-2-18 as read]); vaśī (vaśaḥ asyāsti iti vaśī; in the possessive sense ini by ata iniṭhanau [Pā. Sū. 5-2-115 as read]; acute on the affix); āritaḥ (root ṛ gatau; the causative ṇic and kta in the sense of the passive by niṣṭhā [Pā. Sū. 3-2-102 as read]; though puk would be expected by arttihrīvlī… [Pā. Sū. 7-3-36 as read] after the ṇic ending, the augment does not come, by the statement āgamānuśāsanam anityam; vṛddhi of the root because of ṇic; raparatva; iṭ for the affix by ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ; or by the statement sūcisūtrimūtryaṭyartibhyaś ca [vārttika, Pā. 3-2-[?]3 as read, ?] the affix yaj, which is lost by yajo yaji ca [Pā. Sū. 2-4-[?]4 as read, ?]; by pratyayalope pratyayalakṣaṇam [Pā. Sū. 1-1-62 as read] the ṅit-like effect remains; doubling of the root by sanyaṅoḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-1-9 as read]; in the reduplicative a by ur at [Pā. Sū. 7-4-66 as read]; halādiśeṣa; ruk by rurikau ca luki [Pā. Sū. 7-4-[?]1 as read]; iṭ for the affix ta in the Veda; yaṇ for the ṛ; with ar + r + ita, loss of the former r by ro ri [Pā. Sū. 8-3-14 as read]; since the r is lost, lengthening of the preceding vowel by ḍhralope pūrvasya dīrgho 'ṇaḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-3-111 as read]; final acute by the affix); karmaṇi karmaṇi (doubling by nityavīpsayoḥ [Pā. Sū. 8-1-4 as read]); asunvataḥ (root ṣuñ abhiṣave; śatṛ in the sense of the present; śnu; the form sunvat; na sunvan asunvan; in the negative tatpuruṣa the accent of the first member kept by tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā… [Pā. Sū. 6-2-2 as read]).

original p. 286

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 101.4, concluded (grammar page, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])

Grammar page, noted briefly. The grammar of Rik 101.4 concludes: vadhaḥ (by the word bahulam in kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam [Pā. Sū. 3-3-113 as read] and by hanaś ca vadhaḥ [Pā. Sū. 3-3-76 as read], the affix ap in the agent; by its connection, the substitute vadha for the root han; this ends in a; loss of the a by ato lopaḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-4-48 as read]; since the affix ap is unaccented, and the loss of the acute a is made, the affix is made acute by anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-1-161 as read]). The Rik is closed with ‖ 4 ‖ and a rule of dashes.

Rik 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 101.5)

यो विश्वस्य जगतः प्राणतस्पतिर्यो ब्रह्मणे प्रथमो गा अविन्दत् । इन्द्रो यो दस्यूँरधराँ अवातिरन्मरुत्वन्तं सख्याय हवामहे ॥ ५ ॥

yo viśvasya jagataḥ prāṇatas patir yo brahmaṇe prathamo gā avindat | indro yo dasyūm̐r adharām̐ avātiran marutvantaṃ sakhyāya havāmahe ‖ 5 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 101.5)

यः । विश्वस्य । जगतः । प्राणतः । पतिः । यः । ब्रह्मणे । प्रथमः । गाः । अविन्दत् । इन्द्रः । यः । दस्यून् । अधरान् । अवऽअतिरत् । मरुत्वन्तम् । सख्याय । हवामहे ॥ ५ ॥

yaḥ | viśvasya | jagataḥ | prāṇataḥ | patiḥ | yaḥ | brahmaṇe | prathamaḥ | gāḥ | avindat | indraḥ | yaḥ | dasyūn | adharān | ava-atirat | marutvantam | sakhyāya | havāmahe ‖ 5 ‖

original p. 287

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 101.5)

य इन्द्रो विश्वस्य जगतो गच्छतः प्राणतः प्रश्वसतः प्राणिजातस्य पतिः स्वामी । यश्च ब्रह्मणे ब्राह्मणजातिभ्योऽङ्गिरोभ्यः प्रथमोऽन्येभ्यो देवेभ्यः पूर्वभावी सन् पणिभिरपहृता गा अविन्दत् । अलभत । अन्येभ्यो देवेभ्यः पूर्वमेव तैरसुरैर्युद्ध्वा गाः स्वयमलभतेत्यर्थः । अपि च य इन्द्रो दस्यून् उपक्षपयित्न्नसुरानधरान्निकृष्टान् स्तृत्वा [?] अवातिरत् अवधीत् । अवतिरतिर्वधकर्मा । तं मरुत्वन्तमिन्द्रं सख्यायोप्ययामहे ॥ जगतः । गम्ऌ सृप्ऌ गतौ । वर्तमाने पृषद्बृहन्महज्जगच्छतृवच्च । उ. २-८४ [?] । इत्यतिप्रत्ययान्तो निपातितो जगच्छब्द आद्युदात्तः । प्राणतः । श्वस प्राणने अन च । अस्माल्लटः शतृ । अदादित्वाच्छपो लुक् । शतुरनुम इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । षष्ठ्याः पतिपुत्रेति विसर्जनीयस्य सत्वम् ॥ ya indro viśvasya jagato gacchataḥ prāṇataḥ praśvasataḥ prāṇijātasya patiḥ svāmī | yaś ca brahmaṇe brāhmaṇajātibhyo 'ṅgirobhyaḥ prathamo 'nyebhyo devebhyaḥ pūrvabhāvī san paṇibhir apahṛtā gā avindat | alabhata | anyebhyo devebhyaḥ pūrvam eva tair asurair yuddhvā gāḥ svayam alabhatety arthaḥ | api ca ya indro dasyūn upakṣapayitṝn asurān adharān nikṛṣṭān stṛtvā [?] avātirat avadhīt | avatiratir vadhakarmā | taṃ marutvantam indraṃ sakhyāyopyayāmahe ‖ jagataḥ | gamḷ sṛpḷ gatau | vartamāne pṛṣadbṛhanmahajjagacchatṛvac ca | U. 2-84 [?] | ity atipratyayānto nipātito jagacchabda ādyudāttaḥ | prāṇataḥ | śvasa prāṇane ana ca | asmāl laṭaḥ śatṛ | adāditvāc chapo luk | śatur anuma iti vibhakter udāttatvam | ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputreti visarjanīyasya satvam ‖

"That Indra who is the pati, the lord, the master, of the whole world — of all that moves, breathes, draws breath: of the whole race of living beings. And who brahmaṇe — for the Brāhmaṇa race, the Aṅgirases — being first (prathamaḥ), prior to the other gods, avindat — found, obtained — the cows that had been carried off by the Paṇis; that is, before the other gods, himself fought those Asuras and got back the cows. And that Indra who avātirat — killed — the Dasyus, the Asuras who cause destruction, adharān, the lowly, [having laid them low] [?]. Avatirati is a verb meaning 'to kill'. Him, the Indra with the Maruts, we call to be our friend." The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read: jagat ('that which moves'; root gam/sṛp with the Uṇādi ati fixed by nipātana like pṛṣat, bṛhat, mahat and śatṛ [Uṇ. Sū. 2-84, as read, ?], acute on the first syllable); prāṇat (root śvas 'to breathe' with ana ca …, then laṭ → śatṛ, luk of śap, acute on the ending by śatur anumo nadyajādī; visarga → s by ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputra…).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"yaḥ — which Indra; viśvasya — of the whole; jagataḥ — of all moving beings; prāṇataḥ — of all creatures that breathe; patiḥ — the lord; yaḥ — which Indra; brahmaṇe — to the Aṅgirases of the Brāhmaṇa race; prathamaḥ — first (before the other gods); gāḥ — the cows (carried off by the Paṇis); avindat — obtained and gave; yaḥ indraḥ — which Indra; dasyūn — the Asuras who do harm; adharān — made low (humble); avātirat — killed (such); marutvantam — that Indra together with the Maruts; sakhyāya — to make friendship (with us); havāmahe — we call."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"Which Indra is lord of all moving and breathing creatures; who, being before the other gods, fought with the Paṇis and first obtained for the Aṅgirases the cows that had been carried off; and who humbled and killed the Asuras who have the form of Dasyus — such an Indra, together with the Maruts, we call to make friendship with us."

English Translation (as printed)

Who is the lord of all moving and breathing creatures, who first recovered the (stolen) cows for the Brahman and who slew the humbled Dasyus : we invoke to become our friend, Indra, attended by the Maruts.

original p. 288

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 101.5 (Kannada)

"Jagataḥ prāṇataḥ patiḥ — the lord or protector of all moving beings and of all those who draw breath."

इन्द्रो महा रोदसी पप्रथच्छव इन्द्रः सूर्यमरोचयत् । इन्द्रे ह विश्वा भुवनानि येमिर इन्द्रे सुवानास इन्दवः ॥ indro mahā rodasī paprathac chava indraḥ sūryam arocayat | indre ha viśvā bhuvanāni yemira indre suvānāsa indavaḥ ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-3-6 as read [?])

"— thus the all-pervading lordship of Indra is praised.

Brahmaṇe prathamaḥ gāḥ avindat — for the word brahmaṇe, Skandasvāmin gives brāhmaṇādīnāṃ caturṇām api varṇānām: 'he caused [the people of] the four castes, beginning with Brāhmaṇas, to get back the cows carried off by the Asuras'. But Sāyaṇa has given for the word brahmaṇe the sense aṅgirobhyaḥ, 'to the Aṅgirases'. This meaning also is fitting. For Indra's relation with the Aṅgirases is very close, and Indra's pride in the Aṅgirases is exceedingly great. This subject is told in the Ṛksaṃhitā itself —"

वीळौ सतीरभि धीरा अतृन्दन्प्राचाहिन्वन्मनसा सप्त विप्राः । विश्वामविन्दन्पथ्यामृतस्य प्रजानन्नित्ता नमसा विवेश ॥ विदद्यदी सरमा रुग्णमद्रेर्महि पाथः पूर्व्यं सध्र्यक्कः । अग्रं नयत्सुपद्यक्षराणामच्छा रवं प्रथमा जानती गात् ॥ अगच्छदु विप्रतमः सखीयन्नसूदयत्सुकृते गर्भमद्रिः । ससान मर्यो युवभिर्मखस्यन्नथाभवदङ्गिराः सद्यो अर्चन् ॥ vīḷau satīr abhi dhīrā atṛndan prācāhinvan manasā sapta viprāḥ | viśvām avindan pathyām ṛtasya prajānann it tā namasā viveśa ‖ vidad yadī saramā rugṇam adrer mahi pāthaḥ pūrvyaṃ sadhryak kaḥ | agraṃ nayat supady akṣarāṇām acchā ravaṃ prathamā jānatī gāt ‖ agacchad u vipratamaḥ sakhīyann asūdayat sukṛte garbham adriḥ | sasāna maryo yuvabhir makhasyann athābhavad aṅgirāḥ sadyo arcan ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-31-3 to 5 [print: 3-31-3 to 6, as read [?]]; the same passage as quoted on p. 189)

"In former times the cows of the Aṅgirases were carried off by the Asuras called Paṇis, who hid them in a secret place on a mountain. Then the Aṅgirases prayed to Indra that they might get those cows. Indra, to search for them, sent Saramā, the bitch of the gods." the passage continues on the next page

original p. 289

"[Saramā, going and] finding the cows, and telling Indra the place where they were, Indra went, brought the cows, and gave them to the Aṅgirases; and Indra became their worshipful deity: this tale is told in the Ṛks 10-108 [as read [?]]. In accordance with this, Sāyaṇa's meaning here is also right.

Yaḥ dasyūn adharān avātirat — the explanation of the word dasyu was given in the special topics of the twelfth Ṛk [as read, ?] of the previous sūkta [Sūkta 100]. The sense is that he overcame all the Asuras, humbling them.

Avātirat — dabhnoti, śṛṇāti and the like are read among the [thirty-three, as read, ?] names of 'killing' (Ni. 2-[?]0): hence avātirat means 'killed'."

विभिद्यस्य [?] वीर्यस्य पूरवः पुरो यदिन्द्र शारदीरवातिरः सासहानो अवातिरः । vibhid yasya [?] vīryasya pūravaḥ puro yad indra śāradīr avātiraḥ sāsahāno avātiraḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13[?]-[?] as read [?]; the first words clotted in print [?])

"— as said in this Ṛk, here too avātirat means 'destroyed'.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 101.5) grammar pages, pp. 289–[290], noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?]

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: jagataḥ (root gamḷ sṛpḷ gatau; ati fixed by nipātana among the words like pṛṣat, bṛhat, mahat, jagat by pṛṣadbṛhanmahajjagacchatṛvac ca [Uṇ. Sū. 2-[?]84 as read, ?]; the word jagat is acute on the first syllable); prāṇataḥ (root śvasa prāṇane, also ana; śatṛ in the sense of the present; preverb pra; with an + at, the luk of śap by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ [Pā. Sū. 2-4-72 as read]; pra + anat, the n of the root changed to ṇ by aniteḥ [Pā. Sū. 8-4-19 as read]; since num is wanting, the ending follows the śatṛ and the ending is acute by śaturanumo nadyajādī [Pā. Sū. 6-1-173 as read]; prāṇat + patiḥ: in the genitive the visarga becomes s by ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputra… [Pā. Sū. 8-3-53 as read]); gāḥ (the word go; accusative plural; the ā becomes the single substitute, by auto 'mśasoḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-1-93 as read]; s → ru → visarga); avindat (root vidḷ lābhe; laṅ, third person singular, tip; loss of the i by itaś ca; śa by tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ [Pā. Sū. 3-1-77 as read]; num by śemuc… ādīnām [Pā. Sū. 7-1-59 as read], after the last vowel of the root; the augment aṭ; the form avindat; the relative…) the grammar continues on the next page

original p. 290

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 101.5, concluded (grammar page, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])

Grammar page, noted briefly. The grammar of Rik 101.5 concludes: avindat (continued: yadvṛttānnityam [Pā. Sū. 8-1-66 as read] — since the relative is related to it, no nighāta; since the augment aṭ is acute, the word is acute on the first syllable); dasyūn (root dasu upakṣaye; yu by yajimaniśundhidasijanibhyo yuḥ [Uṇ. Sū. 3-[2?]00 as read, ?]; by its being in the vṛṣādi class, acute on the first syllable by vṛṣādīnāṃ ca [Pā. Sū. 6-1-[2?]03 as read]; accusative plural); adharān (ava with the lengthened a… adhara, with ru [i.e. r] by samāsapāde…, [Pā. Sū. 8-2-[?]9 as read], and the nasal inserted before it by ato 'ṭi nityam [Pā. Sū. 8-3-3 as read], the preceding being always nasalized); avātirat (the root tira, preceded by the preverb ava, is used in the sense of killing; laṅ, third person singular; since the relative is related to it, no nighāta; the augment aṭ being acute, the word is acute on the first syllable; since the verb is acute, the preverb [ava] receives the nighāta accent by tiṅ codāttavati [Pā. Sū. 8-1-71 as read]). The Rik is closed with ‖ 5 ‖ and a printed ornament.

Rik 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 101.6)

यः शूरेभिर्हव्यो यश्च भीरुभिर्यो धावद्भिर्ह्वयते यश्च जिग्युभिः । इन्द्रं यं विश्वा भुवनाभि संदधुर्मरुत्वन्तं सख्याय हवामहे ॥ ६ ॥

yaḥ śūrebhir havyo yaś ca bhīrubhir yo dhāvadbhir hvayate yaś ca jigyubhiḥ | indraṃ yaṃ viśvā bhuvanābhi saṃdadhur marutvantaṃ sakhyāya havāmahe ‖ 6 ‖

original p. 291

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 101.6)

यः । शूरेभिः । हव्यः । यः । च । भीरुऽभिः । यः । धावत्ऽभिः । ह्वयते । यः । च । जिग्युऽभिः । इन्द्रम् । यम् । विश्वा । भुवना । अभि । सम्ऽदधुः । मरुत्वन्तम् । सख्याय । हवामहे ॥ ६ ॥

yaḥ | śūrebhiḥ | havyaḥ | yaḥ | ca | bhīru-bhiḥ | yaḥ | dhāvat-bhiḥ | hvayate | yaḥ | ca | jigyu-bhiḥ | indram | yam | viśvā | bhuvanā | abhi | saṃ-dadhuḥ | marutvantam | sakhyāya | havāmahe ‖ 6 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 101.6)

य इन्द्रः शूरेभिः शौर्योपेतैः पुरुषैर्हव्यो योद्धुमाह्वातव्यः । यश्च भीरुभिर्भयशीलैः कातरैः पुरुषैः सहायार्थमाह्वातव्यः । अपि च य इन्द्रो धावद्भिः पराजयेन पलायमानैर्ह्वयते रक्षार्थमाहूयते । यश्च जिग्युभिः प्राप्तजयैराहूयते । यं चेन्द्रं विश्वा भुवना सर्वाणि भूतजातानि स्वेषु स्वेषु कार्येष्वभि संदधुः । अभिमुख्येन स्थापयन्ति । तं मरुत्वन्तमिन्द्रं सख्यायोप्ययामहे ॥ शूरेभिः । बहुलं छन्दसीति भिस ऐसभावः । हव्यः । ह्वयतेरचो यदिति यत् । ह्न इत्यनुवृत्तौ बहुलं छन्दसीति सम्प्रसारणम् । गुणे धातोस्तन्निमित्तस्यैव वेत्यक्वादेशः । भीरुभिः । भियः क्रुक्लुकनौ । उ. २-४१ [?] । इति क्रुप्रत्ययः । धावद्भिः । धावु गतौ । सर्तेर्वेगितायां शपि पाघ्रेत्यादिना धावादेशः । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । शतुश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वरः शिष्यते । जिग्युभिः । जि जये । लिटः क्वसुः । द्विर्वचने सन्यटोर्जेर्गिरित्यभ्यासादुत्तरस्य जकारस्य कुत्वम् । भस्य यस्यादित्वेन भत्वाद्वसोः सम्प्रसारणमिति सम्प्रसारणम् । छान्दसोऽन्त्यलोपः ॥ ya indraḥ śūrebhiḥ śauryopetaiḥ puruṣair havyo yoddhum āhvātavyaḥ | yaś ca bhīrubhir bhayaśīlaiḥ kātaraiḥ puruṣaiḥ sahāyārtham āhvātavyaḥ | api ca ya indro dhāvadbhiḥ parājayena palāyamānair hvayate rakṣārtham āhūyate | yaś ca jigyubhiḥ prāptajayair āhūyate | yaṃ cendraṃ viśvā bhuvanā sarvāṇi bhūtajātāni sveṣu sveṣu kāryeṣv abhi saṃdadhuḥ | abhimukhyena sthāpayanti | taṃ marutvantam indraṃ sakhyāyopyayāmahe ‖ śūrebhiḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti bhisa aisabhāvaḥ | havyaḥ | hvayater aco yad iti yat | hna ity anuvṛttau bahulaṃ chandasīti samprasāraṇam | guṇe dhātos tannimittasyaiva vety akvādeśaḥ [?] | bhīrubhiḥ | bhiyaḥ krukluknau | U. 2-41 [?] | iti krupratyayaḥ | dhāvadbhiḥ | dhāvu gatau | sarter vegitāyāṃ śapi pāghretyādinā dhāvādeśaḥ | śapaḥ pittvād anudāttatvam | śatuś ca lasārvadhātukasvareṇa dhātusvaraḥ śiṣyate | jigyubhiḥ | ji jaye | liṭaḥ kvasuḥ | dvirvacane sanyaṭor jer giḥ ity abhyāsād uttarasya jakārasya kutvam | bhasya yasyāditvena bhatvād vasoḥ samprasāraṇam iti samprasāraṇam | chāndaso 'ntyalopaḥ ‖

"That Indra who is to be called, for fighting, by heroes (śūrebhiḥ), men endowed with valour; and who is to be called for help by cowards (bhīrubhiḥ), men of fearful nature. And that Indra who is called for protection by those who run away (dhāvadbhiḥ), fleeing from defeat; and who is called by those who have won victory (jigyubhiḥ). And that Indra whom all the worlds, all beings, abhi saṃdadhuḥ — set before them, each in its own work. Him, the Indra with the Maruts, we call to be our friend." The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read: no ais in the instrumental plural by bahulaṃ chandasi; havya (root hve with yat and samprasāraṇa); bhīru (root bhī with kru by an Uṇādi rule [Uṇ. Sū. 2-41, as read, ?]); dhāvat (root dhāv 'to go', with the substitution dhāva for sṛ in the sense of speed); jigyu (root ji with kvasu in the liṭ, with kutva of the j after the reduplicative, and samprasāraṇa). Several words are clotted and marked [?].

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"yaḥ — which Indra; śūrebhiḥ — by men of valour; havyaḥ — is called (for help in battle); yaḥ ca — and which Indra; bhīrubhiḥ — by men of fearful nature (is called); yaḥ — who; dhāvadbhiḥ — by those who run from defeat; hvayate — is called (for protection); yaḥ ca — and which Indra; jigyubhiḥ — by those who have obtained victory (is called); yam indram — which Indra; viśvā bhuvanā — all beings; abhi saṃdadhuḥ — in their own work-times set facing themselves; marutvantam — that Indra together with the Maruts; sakhyāya — to make friendship (with us); havāmahe — we call."

original p. 292

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"Indra, whom the men of valour, the men of fearful nature, those who run from defeat, and those who have gained victory alike call, in the same way, for help and for protection; and whom all beings, each in its own time of work, keep before them — such an Indra, together with the Maruts, we call to make friendship with us."

English Translation (as printed)

Who is to be invoked by the brave and by the timid, by the vanquished and by victors, and whom all beings place before them (in their rites) : we invoke to become our friend, Indra, attended by the Maruts.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 101.6 (Kannada)

"Indra — brave heroes, fit to fight, call him to help them in battle; cowards, unable to fight, call him to give them suitable help; the afflicted call him that he give them protection; and those who have fought and won, to offer him their worship in joy: they each, in a different way, pray to Indra and call him. In this way, the prayer is that Indra, who has the power to give all kinds of help, may be our friend too. Because this manifold power of Indra and his universally facing wealth are well known in the world, the strong call upon him for help, and the weak for protection."

तदस्येदं पश्यता भूरि पुष्टं श्रदिन्द्रस्य धत्तन वीर्याय । tad asyedaṃ paśyatā bhūri puṣṭaṃ śrad indrasya dhattana vīryāya | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-103-5 as read [?])

वृक्षस्य नु ते पुरुहूत वया व्यूतयो रुरुहुरिन्द्र पूर्वीः । vṛkṣasya nu te puruhūta vayā vy ūtayo ruruhur indra pūrvīḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-24-1 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks such as these, Indra's valour is most nourishing, abundant and many-sided: therefore the protections that go with that valour are of many kinds. As the branches of a tree spread in many directions, so Indra's protections spread in many directions

original p. 293

"[— spread in many directions]. That Indra, with such a power of protection, [is called] not only as the friend of his devotees, but most dear, 'as a father cares for his devotees' — this too is well known in the world:"

सखा पिता पितृतमः पितॄणां कर्तेमु लोकमुशते वयोधाः । sakhā pitā pitṛtamaḥ pitṝṇāṃ kartemu lokam uśate vayodhāḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-17-17 [as read: 4-[?]2-[?]2] [?])

"— and as it is both respectful and powerful, and a helper:"

इन्द्र प्र णः पुरएतेव पश्य प्र नो नय प्रतरं वस्यो अच्छ । भवा सुपारो अतिपारयो नो भवा सुनीतिरुत वामनीतिः ॥ indra pra ṇaḥ puraeteva paśya pra no naya prataraṃ vasyo accha | bhavā supāro atipārayo no bhavā sunītir uta vāmanītiḥ ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-7 as read [?])

"— just as a guide is a protector for those who travel on the road, so, 'be a protector for us, protect us from dangers and give us happiness': since many such manifold prayers are found in many places, in this Ṛk too it is described that [Indra] is called śūrebhiḥ, bhīrubhiḥ, dhāvadbhiḥ, jigyubhiḥ.

Jigyubhiḥ — prāptajayaiḥ: they call, praying to Indra to offer worship also — those who have won victory.

Abhi saṃdadhuḥ — abhimukhyena sthāpayanti: 'they set [him] facing'; tasya tasya abhilaṣitasya dānārthaṃ dhyāyanti: [Skandasvāmin:] 'they meditate on him for the sake of giving each one's desired thing'. For the fulfilment of their respective particular wishes, they set Indra facing themselves, and offer meditation and worship; since each has his own desire, all beings worship Indra viśvā bhuvanā."

Sū. 3-1-97 as read]; samprasāraṇa of hve by hvaḥ samprasāraṇam [Pā. Sū. 6-1-32 as read], with the continuation of hvaḥ, also by bahulaṃ chandasi [Pā. Sū. 6-1-34 as read] here; the single substitute by samprasāraṇāc ca; hu + ya, guṇa of the u by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ [Pā. Sū. 7-3-84 as read]; since the ya is the cause, av…)

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 101.6, continued from p. 293 (grammar page, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])

Grammar page, noted briefly. The grammar of Rik 101.6 continues: havyaḥ (continued: by dhātos tannimittasyaiva [Pā. Rik 7

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 101.7)

रुद्राणामेति प्रदिशा विचक्षणो रुद्रेभिर्योषा तनुते पृथु ज्रयः । इन्द्रं मनीषा अभ्यर्चति श्रुतं मरुत्वन्तं सख्याय हवामहे ॥ ७ ॥

rudrāṇām eti pradiśā vicakṣaṇo rudrebhir yoṣā tanute pṛthu jrayaḥ | indraṃ manīṣā abhy arcati śrutaṃ marutvantaṃ sakhyāya havāmahe ‖ 7 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 101.7)

रुद्राणाम् । एति । प्रऽदिशा । विऽचक्षणः । रुद्रेभिः । योषा । तनुते । पृथु । ज्रयः । इन्द्रम् । मनीषा । अभि । अर्चति । श्रुतम् । मरुत्वन्तम् । सख्याय । हवामहे ॥ ७ ॥

rudrāṇām | eti | pra-diśā | vi-cakṣaṇaḥ | rudrebhiḥ | yoṣā | tanute | pṛthu | jrayaḥ | indram | manīṣā | abhi | arcati | śrutam | marutvantam | sakhyāya | havāmahe ‖ 7 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 101.7)

विचक्षणः सूर्यात्मना प्रकाशमान इन्द्रो रुद्राणां रुद्रपुत्राणामध्यात्मं प्राणरूपेण वर्तमानानां मरुतां । यद्वा । रोदयित्रृणां प्राणानां । प्राणा हि शरीरान्निर्गताः सन्तो बन्धुजनान्रोदयन्ति । प्रदिशा प्रदेशनेन मनुष्येभ्यः प्रदानेन सहैति । अन्तरिक्षे गच्छति । तथा चाम्नायते । योऽसौ तपन्नुदेति स सर्वेषां भूतानां प्राणानादायोदेतीति । तै. आ. १-[?]४-१ [?] इति । अपि च रुद्रेभिरधिभूतं वर्तमानैः रुद्रपुत्रैर्मरुद्भिर्योषा माध्यमिका वाक् पृथु विस्तीर्णं ज्रयो वेगं तनुते । विस्तारयति । प्रसङ्गादत्र मरुतां स्तुतिः । तैर्मरुद्भिः सह वर्तमानं श्रुतं प्रख्यातं सूर्यात्मानमिन्द्रं मनीषा स्तुतिलक्षणा वाक् अभ्यर्चति । अभिमुखेन स्तौति । तं मरुत्वन्तमिन्द्रं सख्यायाह्वयामहे ॥ प्रदिशा । दिश अतिसर्जने । सम्पदादिलक्षणो भावे क्विप् । ज्रयः । जि ज्रि अभिभवने । ज्रीयतेऽभिभूयतेऽनेनेति ज्रयो वेगः । करणेऽसुन् । मनीषा । ईषाक्षादित्वात्प्रकृतिभावः ॥ vicakṣaṇaḥ sūryātmanā prakāśamāna indro rudrāṇāṃ rudraputrāṇām adhyātmaṃ prāṇarūpeṇa vartamānānāṃ marutām | yadvā | rodayitṝṇāṃ prāṇānām | prāṇā hi śarīrān nirgatāḥ santo bandhujanān rodayanti | pradiśā pradeśanena manuṣyebhyaḥ pradānena sahaiti | antarikṣe gacchati | tathā cāmnāyate | yo 'sau tapann udeti sa sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ prāṇān ādāyodetīti | Tai. Ā. 1-[?]4-1 [?] iti | api ca rudrebhir adhibhūtaṃ vartamānaiḥ rudraputrair marudbhir yoṣā mādhyamikā vāk pṛthu vistīrṇaṃ jrayo vegaṃ tanute | vistārayati | prasaṅgād atra marutāṃ stutiḥ | tair marudbhiḥ saha vartamānaṃ śrutaṃ prakhyātaṃ sūryātmānam indraṃ manīṣā stutilakṣaṇā vāk abhy arcati | abhimukhena stauti | taṃ marutvantam indraṃ sakhyāyāhvayāmahe ‖ pradiśā | diśa atisarjane | sampadādilakṣaṇo bhāve kvip | jrayaḥ | ji jri abhibhavane | jrīyate 'bhibhūyate 'neneti jrayo vegaḥ | karaṇe 'sun | manīṣā | īṣākṣādittvāt prakṛtibhāvaḥ ‖

"Vicakṣaṇaḥ — Indra, shining in the form of the sun, goes together with the rudras, the sons of Rudra: the Maruts who are present within the individual (adhyātma) in the form of the vital breaths (prāṇa); or, with the breaths that make [people] weep (rodayitṝ): for, when the breaths leave the body, they make the kinsmen weep. Pradiśā — by indication, by giving to men: he goes with [that] to the mid-air. As the scripture says, 'The one who rises yonder, heating, rises taking up the breaths of all beings' (Tai. Ā. 1-[?]4-1 as read [?]). And rudrebhiḥ, with the sons of Rudra, the Maruts who are present in the cosmic [adhibhūta] sense, yoṣā, speech of the middle region, pṛthu — wide, jrayaḥ — speed — tanute: it spreads. Here, by occasion, the Maruts are praised. That Indra, who is famed, who has the form of the sun, accompanied by those Maruts — manīṣā, speech having the character of praise, abhy arcati — praises, facing him. Him, Indra with the Maruts, we call to be our friend." The grammatical tail is characterized: pradiśā (root diś 'to give out', with kvip as in the class of sampad); jraya (root ji/jri 'to overcome', 'that by which one is overcome': speed, with asun as instrument); manīṣā (no change of the stem, as of the class īṣākṣa…).

original p. 296

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"vicakṣaṇaḥ — (in the form of the sun) Indra who shines; rudrāṇām — (who are in the form of the breath in all living beings) the Maruts, the sons of Rudra, [or the breaths that cause weeping]; pradiśā — by causing [him] to join (all living beings); eti — [he] goes about in the mid-air; rudrebhiḥ — (in the form of breath) with the Maruts (by their help); yoṣā — the speech of men; pṛthu — widely; jrayam — and swiftly; tanute — spreads; śrutam — the famous; indram — Indra; manīṣā — speech having the form of praise; abhy arcati — praises facing [him]; marutvantam — that Indra, together with the Maruts; sakhyāya — to make friendship (with us); havāmahe — we call."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"Indra, who shines, goes about in the mid-air in the form of the sun, by giving the Maruts, who are in the form of breath, to all living beings. By the help of the Maruts, the speech of men spreads widely and swiftly. The speech that has the form of praise stands facing the famous Indra and praises him. That Indra, together with the Maruts, we call to make friendship with us."

English Translation (as printed)

The radiant Indra proceeds (along the firmament) with the manifestation of the Rudras : through the Rudras, speech spreads with more expansive celerity, and praise glorifies the renowned Indra ; him, attended by the Maruts, we invoke to be come [sic] our friend.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 101.7 (Kannada)

"Vicakṣaṇaḥ rudrāṇāṃ pradiśā eti — sūryātmanā prakāśamānaḥ indraḥ rudraputrāṇām adhyātmaṃ prāṇarūpeṇa vartamānānāṃ marutāṃ manuṣyebhyaḥ pradānena saha antarikṣe āgacchati: Indra, shining in the form of the sun, comes in the mid-air by giving to all living beings the Maruts, the sons of Rudra, who are in the form of breath — this is Sāyaṇa's explanation. Skandasvāmin:"

प्रदिशा इत्येतस्य आदेशेन वचनेन एति गच्छति अथवा रुद्र इति स्तोतृनाम स्तोतॄणाम् आदेशेन गच्छति । आयः स्तोतृगणानां प्रार्थनावाक्यम् इव अत्र अत्र गच्छति । pradiśā ity etasya ādeśena vacanena eti gacchati athavā rudra iti stotṛnāma stotṝṇām ādeśena gacchati | ayaḥ stotṛgaṇānāṃ prārthanāvākyam iva atra atra gacchati | (Skandasvāmin, as read; the last clause is clotted [?])

"— [that is: 'by pradiśā, by the order, the word; he goes; or rudra is a name of praisers; he goes at the order of the praisers']: as he explains, he goes everywhere as at the words of prayer of the praisers. If we look at the meaning of the previous Ṛk, since each one prays to Indra, Indra, who is the friend of all, must go [and answer] when he has accepted the prayer of each. And since the word rudra is read among the [names of the] stotṛ — rebhaḥ, jaritā, kāruḥ and the rest — twenty-three [as read, ?] — and since the sense of the previous Ṛk is here also, this meaning too is acceptable. But the explanation of rudra as Maruts is the natural one. And since Indra and the Maruts have constant companionship (see the first part [of this edition], p. 1[?]3-3), and since they have a close relation, the first meaning, that he goes about in the mid-air together with the Maruts as they wish, is right. How Indra, in the form of the sun, gives to all beings the vital breath in the form of wind will be discussed later.

Vicakṣaṇaḥ — paṇḍitaḥ says Skandasvāmin; sūryātmanā prakāśamānaḥ says Sāyaṇa. Since the word vicakṣaṇa has [the sense 'wise'] in all the Saṃhitā sentences, and since Sāyaṇa too, for this word in the remaining places, [has given] prājña, sarvajña —"

original p. 297

"— that is —"

त्वं नो गोपाः पथिकृद्विचक्षणस्तव व्रताय मतिभिर्जरामहे । tvaṃ no gopāḥ pathikṛd vicakṣaṇas tava vratāya matibhir jarāmahe | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]3-6 as read [?])

वैश्वानर तव धामान्या चके येभिः स्वर्विदभवो विचक्षण । vaiśvānara tava dhāmāny ā cake yebhiḥ svar vid abhavo vicakṣaṇa | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-10 as read [?])

प्र ते बभ्रू विचक्षण शंसामि गोषणो नपात् । pra te babhrū vicakṣaṇa śaṃsāmi goṣaṇo napāt | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-[?]2-[?]2 as read [?])

"— since in many Ṛks like these the word vicakṣaṇa is given the meaning prājña ('wise'), and since this meaning is accepted here too, the meaning given by Skandasvāmin is the right one.

Yoṣā — mādhyamikā vāk, says Sāyaṇa; and somāhutilakṣaṇā, says Skandasvāmin.

Jrayaḥ — since vartate, ayate and the like are read among the [twenty-two, as read, ?] names of verbs of movement, the word jraya means 'movement'. Here a swift movement is meant. To show the swiftness of movement, which has a distinguishing quality even among movements, the word jraya has been used in many places. For example —"

आधीवासं परि मातू रिहन्नहं तुविग्रेभिः सत्वभिर्याति वि ज्रयः । ādhīvāsaṃ pari mātū rihann aha tuvigrebhiḥ satvabhir yāti vi jrayaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-140-[?] as read [?])

"— here the speed with which the forest-fire spreads is described."

original p. 298

Special Topics of Rik 101.7, continued from p. 297 (Kannada)

प्रति भद्रा अदृक्षत गवां सर्गा न रश्मयः । ओषा अप्रा उरु ज्रयः । prati bhadrā adṛkṣata gavāṃ sargā na raśmayaḥ | oṣā aprā uru jrayaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-5[2?]-[?] as read [?])

"— in this [Ṛk], though the word jraya is given the meaning 'splendour' as of a great brightness, the intention is a splendour having the speed that destroys Rākṣasas and the like. In the same way here also the sense may be said to be 'swift going'.

Yoṣā pṛthu jrayaṃ tanute — [marudbhiḥ saha yajñaṃ prati gacchate indrasya] pipāsitā somāhutiḥ vistīrṇam asi vegaṃ vistārayatīty arthaḥ [as printed, partly clotted [?]]: 'the Soma-oblation, desired by Indra, spreads and goes with great speed': that is the intention — the Soma-oblation desired by Indra spreads widely, and goes extremely swiftly.

If the word yoṣā is explained as mādhyamikā vāk, 'the speech of the middle region', then here it is, by occasion, praise of the Maruts: this is Sāyaṇa's intention.

Manīṣā — speech in the form of praise."

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 101.7) grammar pages, pp. 298–299, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?]

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: eti (root iṇ gatau, adādi; laṭ, third person singular, tip; luk of śap by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ [Pā. Sū. 2-4-72 as read]; guṇa of the root's i, since tip is the cause; the form eti; since it stands at the beginning of the pāda no nighāta… [as printed: nighāta accent because ati… follows a non-verb]); pradiśā (root diśa atisarjane; kvip in the sense of the action by sampadādibhyaḥ kvip [vārttika, Pā. 3-3-[10?]8 as read]; total loss of the affix; the word diś; compounded with pra, the accent of the last member by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt [Pā. Sū. 6-2-139 as read]; instrumental singular); vicakṣaṇaḥ (root cakṣiṅ vyaktāyāṃ vāci; yuc by [a rule on agent and the like]; ana for yu by yuvoranākau [Pā. Sū. 7-1-1 as read]; ṇ by āṭkupvāṅ… [Pā. Sū. 8-4-2 as read]; final acute by citaḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-1-163 as read]; vi being a preverb, the accent of the last member as before); rudrebhiḥ (by bahulaṃ chandasi [Pā. Sū. 7-1-10 as read] the ais is optional, so does not come here; e [by bahuvacane jhaly et]); tanute (root tanu vistāre; laṭ, third person singular; nighāta).

original p. 299

The grammar of Rik 101.7 concludes: jrayaḥ (root ji jri abhibhave; jrīyate 'bhibhūyate 'neneti jrayaḥ vegaḥ; asun in the sense of the instrument; guṇa because of the affix; ay-substitution; the word jrayas; since the affix is nit, acute on the first syllable by ñnityādir nityam [Pā. Sū. 6-1-197 as read]); manīṣā + abhi (the lengthening of the same-class vowel would be expected here; but since īṣākṣa… is in the class, the stem remains unchanged in the Saṃhitā, by prakṛtibhāva). The Rik is closed with ‖ 7 ‖ and a rule of dashes.

Rik 8

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 101.8)

यद्वा मरुत्वः परमे सधस्थे यद्वावमे वृजने मादयासे । अत आ याह्यध्वरं नो अच्छा त्वाया हविश्चकृमा सत्यराधः ॥ ८ ॥

yad vā marutvaḥ parame sadhasthe yad vāvame vṛjane mādayāse | ata ā yāhy adhvaraṃ no acchā tvāyā haviś cakṛmā satyarādhaḥ ‖ 8 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 101.8)

यत् । वा । मरुत्वः । परमे । सधऽस्थे । यत् । वा । अवमे । वृजने । मादयासे । अतः । आ । याहि । अध्वरम् । नः । अच्छ । त्वाऽया । हविः । चकृम । सत्यऽराधः ॥ ८ ॥

yat | vā | marutvaḥ | parame | sadha-sthe | yat | vā | avame | vṛjane | mādayāse | ataḥ | ā | yāhi | adhvaram | naḥ | accha | tvā-yā | haviḥ | cakṛma | satya-rādhaḥ ‖ 8 ‖

original p. 300

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 101.8)

हे मरुत्वो मरुद्भिर्युक्तेन्द्र परमे उत्कृष्टे सधस्थे सहस्थाने गृहे यद्वा यदि वा मादयासे तृप्तो वर्तसे । यद्वा यदि वावमे अर्वाचीनेऽवृजने वृज्यते रिक्तीक्रियतेऽस्मिन्निमित्ति वृजनं गृहं तस्मिन्मादयासे । अतोऽस्माद्उभयविधात्स्थानान्नोऽस्माकमध्वरं यज्ञमच्छाभिमुख्येनायाहि । आगच्छ । हे सत्यराधः सत्यधन त्वाया त्वामात्मन इच्छन्तः हविश्चकृम । कृतवन्तः ॥ मरुत्वः । मतुवसोरुरिति सम्बुद्धौ नकारस्य रुत्वम् । सधस्थे । सुपि स्थ इति कप्रत्ययः । सध मादस्थयोश्छन्दसीति सहस्य सधादेशः । मादयासे । मद तृप्तियोगे । चुरादिराकृतिगणः [?] । लेट्यडागमः । त्वाया । त्वामात्मन इच्छन्ति । सुप आत्मनः क्यच् । प्रत्ययोत्तरपदयोश्चेति मपर्यन्तस्य त्वादेशः । व्यत्ययेन दकारस्यात्वम् । अ प्रत्ययादिति ककार[प्रत्ययः] । सुपां सुलुगिति तृतीयाया लुक् ॥ he marutvo marudbhir yuktendra parame utkṛṣṭe sadhasthe sahasthāne gṛhe yad vā yadi vā mādayāse tṛpto vartase | yad vā yadi vāvame arvācīne 'vṛjane vṛjyate riktīkriyate 'sminn iti vṛjanaṃ gṛhaṃ tasmin mādayāse | ato 'smād ubhayavidhāt sthānān no 'smākam adhvaraṃ yajñam acchābhimukhyenāyāhi | āgaccha | he satyarādhaḥ satyadhana tvāyā tvām ātmana icchantaḥ haviś cakṛma | kṛtavantaḥ ‖ marutvaḥ | matuvasor ur iti sambuddhau nakārasya rutvam | sadhasthe | supi stha iti kapratyayaḥ | sadha mādasthayoś chandasīti sahasya sadhādeśaḥ | mādayāse | mada tṛptiyoge | curādir ākṛtigaṇaḥ [?] | leṭy aḍāgamaḥ | tvāyā | tvām ātmana icchanti | supa ātmanaḥ kyac | pratyayottarapadayoś ceti mapayantasya tvādeśaḥ | vyatyayena dakārasyātvam | a pratyayād iti kakāra[pratyayaḥ] | supāṃ suluk iti tṛtīyāyā luk ‖

"O Marutvān, Indra joined with the Maruts! Whether you are mādayāse — satisfied, remain delighted — in the supreme, excellent sadhastha, the place where [gods] sit together, the house; or whether you are so in the lower, nearer vṛjana — vṛjyate, 'that in which one empties': the house — from either of these two kinds of place come, acchā — facing — to our sacrifice, adhvaram. Come. O satyarādhaḥ, one whose wealth is true! We, tvāyā — desiring you for ourselves — have made the oblation (cakṛma)." The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read: marutvaḥ (the vocative, with ru for the n by matuvasoḥ ru sambuddhau…); sadhastha (a ka affix after stha with a preceding member; the substitute sadha for saha by sadha mādasthayoś chandasi); mādayāse (the root mad in the sense of satisfaction, a curādi [open class?, as read [?]], the leṭ with aḍāgama); tvāyā (denominative kyac after 'you'; the substitution of tva for the stem up to m; the ā in place of the final d by vyatyaya; ka affix; the loss of the third-case ending by supāṃ suluk…). Some clauses are clotted and marked [?].

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"marutvaḥ — O Indra, together with the Maruts; parame — in the excellent (supreme); sadhasthe — place of residence, in the house; yat vā — or; avame — in the not-excellent; vṛjane — in the house; mādayāse — (while you remain) satisfied; yat vā — or; ataḥ — from those two kinds of residence; naḥ — our; adhvaram — (for) the sacrifice; acchā — facing; ā yāhi — be pleased to come; satyarādhaḥ — O giver of true wealth, Indra; tvāyā — desiring your coming; haviḥ — oblations; cakṛma — we have offered."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Indra, together with the Maruts! Whether you remain satisfied in a residence of the excellent kind or in one that is not excellent — from either of these two kinds of residence, be pleased to come to our sacrifice, facing us. O Indra, giver of true wealth, desiring your coming, we have offered you oblations."

English Translation (as printed)

Attended by the winds, giver of true wealth, whether you may be pleased (to dwell) in a stately mansion or in a lowly dwelling, come to our sacrifice : desirous of your presence we offer you oblations.

original p. 301

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 101.8 (Kannada)

"For Indra's favour, wealth is not the chief thing. Since devotion and faith are the chief, the prayer is made that Indra be gracious to the sacrifice of one who offers oblations with devotion, whether he is in an excellent house or not in an excellent house.

Sadhasthe — sahasthāne (Ni. 3-[?]1 as read [?]): since all [sit] together, it is a place common to others: gṛhe, 'in the house'. Skandasvāmin: saha tiṣṭhanty asmin devatāḥ sa sadhastho yajñaḥ — 'the one in which the gods stand together, that is sadhastha: the sacrifice' — he says that, since all the deities sit together, it is a sacrifice. Likewise, vṛjane — Sāyaṇa explains as 'house', and Skandasvāmin as varjite doṣaiḥ — 'the sacrifice that is free of faults'. Then the senses of parame and avame also differ. If it is explained as 'house': parame gṛhe, avame gṛhe, 'in an excellent house' and 'in a house that is not excellent'; if as 'sacrifice': parame yajñe, avame yajñe: 'those who take part in a sacrifice being carried out far away, and those who take part in a sacrifice being carried out near' — the intention is: 'come also to our sacrifice'.

Satyarādhāḥ — satyasādhanaḥ: one who gives true wealth to the sacrificers; the epithet satyarādhāḥ is given to Indra: 'one who has wealth in the form of truth, which gives it'."

स वृत्रहत्ये हव्यः स ईड्यः स सुष्टुत इन्द्रः सत्यराधाः । sa vṛtrahatye havyaḥ sa īḍyaḥ sa suṣṭuta indraḥ satyarādhāḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-24-2 as read [?])

तिरश्चिदर्यः सवना पुरूण्यांगूषेभिर्गृणानः सत्यराधाः । tiraś cid aryaḥ savanā purūṇy āṃgūṣebhir gṛṇānaḥ satyarādhāḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-3[?]-1 as read [?])

शंसेदुक्थं सुदानव उत द्युक्षं यथा नरः । चकृमा सत्यराधसे ॥ śaṃsed uktham sudānava uta dyukṣaṃ yathā naraḥ | cakṛmā satyarādhase ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-3[?]-[?] as read [?])

"— in all the Ṛks in which the epithet satyarādhas appears [except the Ṛk 5-40-2 (Ni. 5-[?]0)], it praises Indra, as an epithet, for his wealth and for his generosity.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 101.8) grammar page, begun at the foot of p. 301, noted briefly

Grammar page, noted briefly. It begins with marutvaḥ (marut asya asti iti marutvān; matup by tadasyāsty asmin… [Pā. Sū. 5-2-94 as read]; m → v by jhayaḥ [Pā. Sū. 8-2-10 as read]; in the vocative, ru for the n by matuvasor ru sambuddhau chandasi [Pā. Sū. 8-3-1 as read]; visarga) and continues on the next page.

original p. 302

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 101.8, continued from p. 301 (grammar page, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])

Grammar page, noted briefly. The grammar of Rik 101.8 continues: sadhasthe (root ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau; ka by supi sthaḥ [Pā. Sū. 3-2-4 as read], when the first member is a subanta; loss of the ā of the root by ato lopa iṭi ca [Pā. Sū. 6-4-64 as read]; the substitute sadha for saha by sadhamādasthayoś chandasi [Pā. Sū. 6-3-96 as read] before a form of the root sthā [and mad]; the form sadhastha; locative); vṛjane (root vṛjī varjane; lyuṭ in the sense of the locus; ana for yu by yuvoranākau [Pā. Sū. 7-1-1 as read]; no guṇa of the penult by the statement saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ; acute on the middle syllable by the affix); mādayāse (root mada tṛptiyoge, curādi; since the root has an anubandha ṅ-like marker [anudāttetva], it is regularly ātmanepada; ṇic in its own sense by satyāpapāśarūpavīṇātūlaślokasenālomatvacavarmavarṇacūrṇacurādibhyo ṇic [Pā. Sū. 3-1-25 as read]; guṇa/vṛddhi of the root's penult by ata upadhāyāḥ [Pā. Sū. 7-2-116 as read]; the ṇic-ended mādi, then leṭ, second person singular, thās by thāsaḥ se [Pā. Sū. 3-4-80 as read], aṭ by leṭo 'ḍāṭau [Pā. Sū. 3-4-94 as read]; śap; guṇa of the ṇic; ay-substitution; the form mādayāse; since the relative is related to it, no nighāta by yadvṛttānnityam [Pā. Sū. 8-1-66 as read]; by the accent of ṇic, the vowel after the d is acute); yāhi (root yā prāpaṇe; loṭ, second person singular; the preverb ā is unaccented because it stands before a verb); tvāyā (explained as 'wishes you for himself', kyac by supa ātmanaḥ kyac [Pā. Sū. 3-1-8 as read]; with yuṣmad + ya, by pratyayottarapadayoś ca [Pā. Sū. 7-2-98 as read], tva for the stem up to m; ā for the d by vyatyaya; the word, ending in kyac, takes the name of a root by sanādyantā dhātavaḥ; for it a by apratyayāt [Pā. Sū. 3-3-102 as read]; loss of the a; in the feminine ṭāp by ajādyatas ṭāp [Pā. Sū. 4-1-4 as read]; then, the third-case ending following, the loss of the ending by supāṃ suluk… [Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 as read]); satyarādhaḥ (satyaṃ rādhaḥ dhanaṃ yasya saḥ; the vocative with its accent: the nighāta by āmantritasya ca [Pā. Sū. 8-1-19 as read]). The Rik is closed with ‖ 8 ‖ and a printed ornament.

Rik 9

original p. 303

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 101.9)

त्वायेन्द्र सोमं सुषुमा सुदक्ष त्वाया हविश्चकृमा ब्रह्मवाहः । अधा नियुत्वः सगणो मरुद्भिरस्मिन्यज्ञे बर्हिषि मादयस्व ॥ ९ ॥

tvāyendra somaṃ suṣumā sudakṣa tvāyā haviś cakṛmā brahmavāhaḥ | adhā niyutvaḥ sagaṇo marudbhir asmin yajñe barhiṣi mādayasva ‖ 9 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 101.9)

त्वाऽया । इन्द्र । सोमम् । सुसुम । सुऽदक्ष । त्वाऽया । हविः । चकृम । ब्रह्मऽवाहः । अध । नियुत्वः । सऽगणः । मरुत्ऽभिः । अस्मिन् । यज्ञे । बर्हिषि । मादयस्व ॥ ९ ॥

tvā-yā | indra | somam | susuma | su-dakṣa | tvā-yā | haviḥ | cakṛma | brahma-vāhaḥ | adha | niyutvaḥ | sa-gaṇaḥ | marut-bhiḥ | asmin | yajñe | barhiṣi | mādayasva ‖ 9 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 101.9)

हे सुदक्ष शोभनबलेन्द्र त्वायो त्वत्कामनया सोमं सुषुम । अभिषुतवन्तो वयम् । हे ब्रह्मवाहो ब्रह्मणा मन्त्ररूपेण स्तोत्रेणोह्यमान प्राप्यमाणेन्द्र त्वाया त्वत्कामनयोहवनीये पुरोडाशलक्षणं हविश्चकृम । कृतवन्तः । हे नियुत्वः नियुतोऽश्वाः तद्वन्निन्द्र अधानन्तरं मरुद्भिः सप्तगणरूपैर्देवैः सगणो गणसहितः सन्नस्मिन्वर्तमाने यज्ञे बर्हिष्यास्तीर्णे दर्भ उपविश्य मादयस्व तृप्तो भव ॥ सुषुमा । षुञ् अभिषवे । लिटि क्रादिनियमप्राप्तस्येटोऽनित्यमागममुशासनमिति वचनादभावः ॥ he sudakṣa śobhanabalendra tvāyā tvatkāmanayā somaṃ suṣuma | abhiṣutavanto vayam | he brahmavāho brahmaṇā mantrarūpeṇa stotreṇohyamāna prāpyamāṇendra tvāyā tvatkāmanayohavanīye puroḍāśalakṣaṇaṃ haviś cakṛma | kṛtavantaḥ | he niyutvaḥ niyuto 'śvāḥ tadvann indra adhānantaraṃ marudbhiḥ saptagaṇarūpair devaiḥ sagaṇo gaṇasahitaḥ sann asmin vartamāne yajñe barhiṣy āstīrṇe darbha upaviśya mādayasva tṛpto bhava ‖ suṣumā | ṣuñ abhiṣave | liṭi krādiniyamaprāptasyeṭo 'nityam āgamam uśāsanam iti vacanād abhāvaḥ ‖

"O sudakṣa — you of excellent strength! Indra, tvāyā — desiring you — we have pressed (suṣuma) the Soma. O brahmavāhaḥ — you who are borne, brought, by the brahma, the praise in the form of a mantra; Indra! tvāyā — desiring you — we have made, on the āhavanīya [fire], the oblation, in the form of the puroḍāśa cake. O niyutvaḥ — you who have niyuts, horses, Indra: thereafter, sagaṇaḥ — accompanied by your band — with the Maruts, the gods who are in the form of seven groups, in this sacrifice now going on, seated on the barhis, the spread-out darbha grass, mādayasva — be satisfied." The grammatical tail is characterized: suṣumā (root ṣuñ 'to press', with the liṭ, and the absence of the augment iṭ, which the rule of kradi would give, by the statement that the augment's teaching is not invariable).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada) begun at the foot of p. 303; continues on p. 304

"sudakṣa — O Indra, of excellent strength; tvāyā — desiring (your help); somam — the Soma juice; suṣuma — we have pressed and offered; brahmavāhaḥ — O Indra, worthy to be attained by praise;"

original p. 304

"[brahmavāhaḥ — O Indra, worthy to be attained] by the means of praise; tvāyā — desiring your help; haviḥ — oblations; cakṛma — we have offered; niyutvaḥ — O Indra, who have horses; adha — therefore; marudbhiḥ — together with the Maruts; sagaṇaḥ — together with your retinue; asmin yajñe — in this sacrifice now being performed; barhiṣi — on the seats of darbha grass; mādayasva — sit and obtain satisfaction."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Indra, of excellent strength, desiring your help we have pressed and offered the Soma juice for you. O Indra, worthy to be approached by the means of praise, as one who loves praise, desiring your help we have offered you oblations. O Indra, who have horses yoked, together with the Maruts, in a company, sit on the darbha seats in this sacrifice now being performed and be satisfied."

English Translation (as printed)

Desirous of you, Indra, who are possessed of excellent strength, we pour forth to you libations : desirous of you, who are obtained by prayer, we offer you oblations ; therefore, do you, who are possessed of horses, sit down with pleasure upon the sacred grass, attended by the Maruts, at this sacrifice.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 101.9 (Kannada)

"Sudakṣa — śobhanabala: of excellent strength. In the address 'Indra, who have excellent strength', Indra's extraordinary strength is made known. In the Ṛk 15 of the previous sūkta [Sūkta 100]:"

न यस्य देवा देवता न मर्ता आपश्चन शवसो अन्तमापुः । स प्ररिक्वा त्वक्षसा क्ष्मो दिवश्च मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विन्द्र ऊती ॥ na yasya devā devatā na martā āpaś cana śavaso antam āpuḥ | sa prarikvā tvakṣasā kṣmo divaś ca marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-100-15; Rik 15 of Sūkta 100)

"— the description that neither the gods nor heaven and earth could come near your strength; and —"

विश्वे ते इन्द्र वीर्यं देवा अनु क्रतुं ददुः । viśve te indra vīryaṃ devā anu kratuṃ daduḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-6-3 as read [?]; as quoted on p. 280)

"— in Ṛks like these, all the gods praised and followed Indra's strength and valour; and so, in many other contexts, the praise of the greatness of Indra's prowess is understood; and this address sudakṣa here makes known that point."

original p. 305

"Brahmavāhaḥ — brahmaṇā mantrarūpeṇa stotreṇohyamāna prāpyamāṇendra: 'borne, attained, by praise in the form of a mantra': it shows the need for praise, in order to obtain Indra's favour, as one fit to be attained by praise. Although for the other deities too praise is essential, since they too must be pleased by praise, the epithet brahmavāha has been used in the sense of Indra alone."

इमा ब्रह्म ब्रह्मवाहः क्रियन्त आ बर्हिः सीद । imā brahma brahmavāhaḥ kriyanta ā barhiḥ sīda | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?] as read [?])

सुनोतेन पचत ब्रह्मवाहसे पुरुष्टुताय प्रतरं दधातन । sunotena pacata brahmavāhase puruṣṭutāya prataraṃ dadhātana | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-5[?]-1 as read [?])

सखायो ब्रह्मवाहसेऽर्चत प्र च गायत । sakhāyo brahmavāhase 'rcata pra ca gāyata | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-45-4 as read [?])

"— in these Ṛks, and so in 3-3[?]-?; 6-2[?]-?; 6-4[?]-? and many others, the word brahmavāha is an epithet of Indra alone.

Tvāyā — tvām ātmana icchati: [the sense] 'wishing you to be one who belongs to us' is a desire. This is a special formation. In all places where the sense tvatkāmanayā — 'out of desire for you' — occurs, this word is used; it is used in this sense in many Ṛks, such as 1-[?]-[?], 3-[?]-[?], 8-2-[?], 8-[?]-[?] and so on.

Niyutvaḥ — niyutaḥ aśvāḥ tadvann indra: niyut means horses: 'the one who has horses': an epithet of Indra. In general, this epithet is used chiefly of Vāyu, and in some places also of the deities Indra and Varuṇa. To show that niyut means 'Vāyu's horses', the Nirukta-author quotes the Ṛk"

विशामकोरुषसः पूर्वहूतौ वायुः पूषा स्वस्तये नियुत्वान् । viśām ko ruṣasaḥ pūrvahūtau vāyuḥ pūṣā svastaye niyutvān | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-34-3 as read [?]; the first words clotted in print [?])

"— and explains: niyutvān — niyuto 'syāśvāḥ [(Ni. 5-[?]2 as read [?])]: 'the niyuts are the horses of this Vāyu'. But the epithet niyutvān is used also of the deities Indra and Varuṇa."

अधा नियुत्व उभयस्य नः पिब शुचिं सोमं गवाशिरम् । adhā niyutva ubhayasya naḥ piba śuciṃ somaṃ gavāśiram | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-4[7?]-[?] as read [?]; the print's numeral is broken [?])

original p. 306

Special Topics of Rik 101.9, concluded from p. 305 (Kannada)

"— in Ṛks like these, it is only Vāyu's horses; and —"

आ वां रथो नियुत्वान्वक्षदवसेऽभि प्रयांसि सुधितानि वीतये । वायो हव्यानि वीतये ॥ ā vāṃ ratho niyutvān vakṣad avase 'bhi prayāṃsi sudhitāni vītaye | vāyo havyāni vītaye ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-135-[?] as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these the horses that carry the chariots belonging to both Indra and Vāyu are described.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 101.9) grammar page, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?]

Grammar page, noted briefly. It treats: tvāyā — explained in the previous mantra [Rik 101.8]; suṣuma (root ṣuñ abhiṣave; liṭ, first person plural; ma for the ending by parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatusus… [Pā. Sū. 3-4-82 as read]; doubling of the root; though by kṛsṛbhṛ… [Pā. Sū. 7-2-13 as read] the augment iṭ is ruled out [being restricted to those roots], properly iṭ should come here; but by the statement āgamaśāsanam anityam the augment iṭ does not come; ṣ for the s of the root by ādeśapratyayayoḥ [Pā. Sū. 8-3-59 as read]; since the verb is at the beginning of the pāda [as the print puts it], no nighāta because …); cakṛma (root ḍukṛñ karaṇe; liṭ, first person plural; since kryādi's rule applies, no augment iṭ; nighāta of the finite verb); niyutvaḥ (niyutaḥ aśvāḥ asya santi iti niyutvān; matup by tadasyāsty asmin [Pā. Sū. 5-2-94 as read]; m → v by jhayaḥ [Pā. Sū. 8-2-10 as read]; in the vocative, ru for the n by matuvasoru sambuddhau chandasi [Pā. Sū. 8-3-1 as read]; visarga); adhā (the word atha; dh for th by Vedic letter-interchange; the lengthening of the vowel in the Saṃhitā by dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-3-135 as read]); mādayasva (root mada tṛptiyoge, curādi; nityaṃ ātmanepade; loṭ, second person singular, thās, sa by thāsaḥ se; va by sevāsitasi… [Pā. Sū. 3-4-91 as read] — print: savābhyāṃ vāmau, i.e. sevābhyāṃ vāmau…, [Pā. Sū. 3-4-91 as read, ?]; śap; guṇa of ṇic; ay-substitution; since the verb has accent on the last syllable, nighāta). The Rik is closed with ‖ 9 ‖ and a rule of dashes.

मादयस्व हरिभिर्ये त इन्द्र वि ष्यस्व शिप्रे वि सृजस्व धेने । आ त्वा सुशिप्र हरयो वहन्तूशन्हव्यानि प्रति नो जुषस्व ॥ १० ॥

मादयस्व । हरिऽभिः । ये । ते । इन्द्र । वि । स्यस्व । शिप्रे इति । वि । सृजस्व । धेने इति । आ । त्वा । सुऽशिप्र । हरयः । वहन्तु । उशन् । हव्यानि । प्रति । नः । जुषस्व ॥ १० ॥

mādayasva | hari-bhiḥ | ye | te | indra | vi | ṣyasva | śipre iti | vi | sṛjasva | dhene iti | ā | tvā | su-śipra | harayaḥ | vahantu | uśan | havyāni | prati | naḥ | juṣasva ‖ 10 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 101.10)

हे इन्द्र हरिभिरश्वैः सह मादयस्व । तृप्तो भव । ये ते तव स्वभूतास्तदर्थं शिप्रे हनू संहते वि ष्यस्व । सोमपानार्थं विवृते कुरु । तथा धेने सास्नासाधनभूते जिह्वोपजिह्विके वि सृजस्व । सोमपानार्थं विश्लिष्टे कुरु । हे सुशिप्र शिप्रे हनू नासिके वा । शोभनशिप्रेन्द्र त्वा त्वां हरय उशा आ वहन्तु । अस्मदीयं यज्ञं प्रापयन्तु । त्वं जोषन् अस्माकं कामयमानो नोऽस्माकं हव्यानि हवींषि प्रति जुषस्व । प्रत्येकं सेवस्व । मोदासि [?] ॥ वि ष्यस्व । षो अन्तकर्मणि । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदम् । दिवादित्वात् श्यन् । ओतः श्यनि । पा. ७-३-७१ । इत्योकारलोपः । उपसर्गात्सुनोतीति षत्वम् ॥ he indra haribhir aśvaiḥ saha mādayasva | tṛpto bhava | ye te tava svabhūtās tadarthaṃ śipre hanū saṃhate vi ṣyasva | somapānārthaṃ vivṛte kuru | tathā dhene sāsnāsādhanabhūte jihvopajihvike vi sṛjasva | somapānārthaṃ viśliṣṭe kuru | he suśipra śipre hanū nāsike vā | śobhanaśipreṇdra tvā tvāṃ harayo 'śvā ā vahantu | asmadīyaṃ yajñaṃ prāpayantu | tvaṃ joṣan asmākaṃ kāmayamāno no 'smākaṃ havyāni havīṃṣi prati juṣasva | pratyekaṃ sevasva | modāsi [?] ‖ vi ṣyasva | ṣo antakarmaṇi | vyatyayenātmanepadam | divāditvāt śyan | oataḥ śyani | Pā. 7-3-71 | ity okāralopaḥ | upasargāt sunotīti ṣatvam ‖

"O Indra! mādayasva — be satisfied — together with the haribhiḥ, your steeds. Ye te — your own [horses, who are of your nature] — for them, vi ṣyasva — open wide your two jaws (śipre), which are joined: make them open for the drinking of Soma. And dhene — the tongue and the uvula, which serve as the means of swallowing — vi sṛjasva: set them wide apart, for the drinking of Soma. O suśipra — you of the beautiful jaws or nose! — may your horses (harayaḥ), uśan — desiring — bring you [here] to our sacrifice. You, joṣan, wishing us well, prati juṣasva — take, one by one, our oblations." The grammatical tail is characterized: vi ṣyasva (root ṣo 'to end', middle voice by vyatyaya; śyan of the divādi class; loss of o by oataḥ śyani [Pā. Sū. 7-3-71]; ṣ by upasargāt sunoti…).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada) begun at the foot of p. 307; continues on p. 308

"indra — O Indra; ye te — those [horses] which have attained your very nature; haribhiḥ — with those horses; mādayasva — be satisfied; śipre — [your] jaws —"

original p. 308

"[śipre — your jaws]; vi ṣyasva — [for the drinking of Soma] open well; dhene — the bells [the uvula and the like]; vi sṛjasva — set wide; suśipra — O Indra with beautiful jaws; tvā — you; harayaḥ — horses; ā vahantu — may they bring (facing our sacrifice) (and you also); uśan — [be] kindly disposed (with goodwill) to us; naḥ — our; havyāni — oblations; prati juṣasva — enjoy one by one."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Indra, be satisfied with your horses, who have attained your own nature. Open your jaws for the drinking of Soma. Set the bells wide open. O Indra of the beautiful jaws, may your horses bring you facing our sacrifice. And you also, being kindly disposed toward us, enjoy our oblations one by one and be satisfied."

English Translation (as printed)

Rejoice, Indra, with the steeds who are of your nature ; open your jaws, set wide your throat (to drink the Soma juice) ; let your horses bring you who have a handsome chin, (hither), and, benignant towards us, be pleased by our oblations.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 101.10 (Kannada)

"Suśipra —"

शिप्रे हनू नासिके वा । śipre hanū nāsike vā | (Ni. 6-1[?]2 as read [?])

"— since the Nirukta-author has said that the word śipra means either the jaws or the nose, Sāyaṇa too has said here that either of the two may be taken. Although the epithet suśipra, or śipre, is used of Indra, it is used also of other deities; and since the sense varies in each place, it must be understood in which senses the words śipra and suśipra are used in each place."

मत्स्वा सुशिप्र मन्दिभिः स्तोमेभिर्विश्वचर्षणे । matsvā suśipra mandibhiḥ stomebhir viśvacarṣaṇe | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-9-3 as read [?])

"— here, suśipra: he śobhanahano śobhananāsika vā: 'O one with beautiful jaws or beautiful nose' — since śipre hanū nāsike vā has been said by Yāska, the word śipra has two meanings, jaw or nose: so suśipra means 'one with beautiful jaws', or 'one with beautiful noses': thus Indra is addressed. In the same way, the meaning 'jaw' or 'nose' —"

original p. 309

शिप्रिन्वाजानां पते शचीवस्तव दंसना । śiprinn vājānāṃ pate śacīvas tava daṃsanā | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-30-2 as read [?])

श्रिये ऋष्व उपाकयोर्नि शिप्री हरिवान्दधे हस्तयोर्वज्रमायसम् । śriye ṛṣva upākayor ni śiprī harivān dadhe hastayor vajram āyasam | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-81-4 as read [?])

"— can be established in Ṛks like these too: śipravān means 'Indra'.

हिरण्यशिप्रा मरुतो दविध्वतः पृक्षं याथ पृषतीभिः समन्यवः । hiraṇyaśiprā maruto davidhvataḥ pṛkṣaṃ yātha pṛṣatībhiḥ samanyavaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-34-3 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk śipra means 'head-covering' (śirastrāṇa): 'having golden headgear': the epithet of the Maruts: 'having a helmet made of gold' the print's English: "Helmet". And —"

अग्निभ्राजसो विद्युतो गभस्त्योः शिप्राः शीर्षसु वितता हिरण्ययीः । agnibhrājaso vidyuto gabhastyoḥ śiprāḥ śīrṣasu vitatā hiraṇyayīḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-54-11 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk, for the word śipra, Sāyaṇa has given uṣṇīṣamayyaḥ, 'made of turbans', and the print adds 'Turban'.

In the whole, it appears that the word śipra may be explained also for the words śiprin and the like that are derived from this word, in the manner set out below. If this word is used in the dual, then the meaning is 'jaws', as in the Ṛks 1-100-10 [as read, i.e. Rik 10 of the present sūkta?], 3-3[?]-?, 5-36-2, 8-[?]-?, 10-[?]-[?], 10-1[?]-5 and the rest. Śiprin, then, as an epithet, is of Indra alone, 'one who has jaws or a nose'. In the Ṛks 1-3[?]-2, 1-[?]-1, 3-3[?]-10 and the like, it is an epithet of Indra: 'the one who has śipra'; and —"

पीवोअश्वाः शुचद्रथा हि भूताऽयःशिप्रा वाजिनः सुनिष्काः । pīvo-aśvāḥ śucadrathā hi bhūtāyaḥśiprā vājinaḥ suniṣkāḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-5[?]-2 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk ayaḥśiprāḥ is an epithet of the Ṛbhus. Here it may mean 'visors made of iron'; or, as Sāyaṇa explains, ayovat sārabhūtaśiprāḥ: 'those who have jaws as strong as iron'.

In the present Ṛk, in the address suśipra, 'Indra, with beautiful jaws or nose', Indra is addressed. The expression śipre vi ṣyasva means 'open the two jaws': the intention is 'open your jaws for the drinking of Soma'."

marutstotrasya vṛjanasya gopā vayam indreṇa sanuyāma vājam | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ‖ 11 ‖

मरुत्ऽस्तोत्रस्य । वृजनस्य । गोपाः । वयम् । इन्द्रेण । सनुयाम । वाजम् । तत् । नः । मित्रः । वरुणः । मामहन्ताम् । अदितिः । सिन्धुः । पृथिवी । उत । द्यौः ॥ ११ ॥

marut-stotrasya | vṛjanasya | gopāḥ | vayam | indreṇa | sanuyāma | vājam | tat | naḥ | mitraḥ | varuṇaḥ | māmahantām | aditiḥ | sindhuḥ | pṛthivī | uta | dyauḥ ‖ 11 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 101.11)

मरुत्स्तोत्रस्य । मरुद्भिः सह स्तोत्रं यस्य स मरुत्स्तोत्रः । तस्य वृजनस्य शत्रूणां क्षेप्तॄरिन्द्रस्य सम्बन्धिनो गोपा गोपायनीया रक्षणीया वयं तेनेन्द्रेण वाजमन्नं सनुयाम । लभेमहि । यदेतदस्माभिः प्रार्थितं नोऽस्मदीयं तन्मित्रादयो द्यावापृथिव्यौ च मामहन्ताम् । पूजितं कुर्वन्तु ॥ वृजनस्य । वृजी वर्जने । कैवृजिमन्दिनिधाभ्यः [?] कुरिति कुप्रत्ययः ॥ marutstotrasya | marudbhiḥ saha stotraṃ yasya sa marutstotraḥ | tasya vṛjanasya śatrūṇāṃ kṣeptṝr indrasya sambandhino gopā gopāyanīyā rakṣaṇīyā vayaṃ tenendreṇa vājam annaṃ sanuyāma | labhemahi | yad etad asmābhiḥ prārthitaṃ no 'smadīyaṃ tan mitrādayo dyāvāpṛthivyau ca māmahantām | pūjitaṃ kurvantu ‖ vṛjanasya | vṛjī varjane | kaivṛjimandinidhābhyaḥ [?] kur iti kupratyayaḥ ‖

"Marutstotrasya — one whose praise is together with the Maruts is marutstotra; of that Indra — vṛjanasya — who casts away the enemies [kṣeptṝ] — we, who are his to be protected (gopāḥ), by that Indra vājam — food — may we obtain (sanuyāma). What we have prayed for in this, our [prayer] — may Mitra and the rest, and heaven and earth, honour it: may they make it honoured." The grammatical tail is characterized: vṛjana (root vṛj 'to avoid', with an Uṇādi ku-affix; the list of roots is clotted [?]).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"marutstotrasya — [of him] who accepts praise together with the Maruts; vṛjanasya — of Indra, the destroyer of enemies; gopāḥ — who are fit for his protection; vayam — we; indreṇa — by that Indra; vājam — food; sanuyāma — may we obtain; naḥ — our; tat — (that prayed-for) food; mitraḥ — Mitra; varuṇaḥ — and Varuṇa; aditiḥ — Aditi; sindhuḥ — the deity presiding over the sea; pṛthivī — the earth; uta — and; dyauḥ — the heavenly world; māmahantām — may [they] make [it] honoured (and guard it)."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"We who are fit for the protection of Indra, who accepts praise together with the Maruts and who destroys enemies, may obtain food from that Indra. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, the deity presiding over the sea, the earth and the heavenly world guard that food which we have prayed for."

English Translation (as printed)

Protected by that destroyer of (foes), who is united in praise with the Maruts, we may receive sustenance from Indra ; and may Mitra, Varuna, Aditi,—ocean, and heaven, preserve it to us.

original p. 312

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 101.11 (Kannada)

"Marutstotrasya — marudbhiḥ saha stotraṃ yasya sa marutstotraḥ tasya: to Indra, who accepts praise together with the Maruts.

Vṛjanasya — śatrūṇāṃ kṣeptur indrasya: of Indra, who casts away and destroys the enemies; vṛjana means 'crooked', 'deceit' and 'power' (Ni. 2-9 as read [?]); here it means 'enemies who practise deceit': enemies who play false."

युक्ता मातासीद्धुरि दक्षिणाया अतिष्ठद्गर्भो वृजनीष्वन्तः । yuktā mātāsīd dhuri dakṣiṇāyā atiṣṭhad garbho vṛjanīṣv antaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-[?]9 as read [?])

"— here, [Sāyaṇa], explaining vṛjanīṣu as 'udakavatsu meghapaṅktiṣu', says: 'in the rows of clouds that have water': the sense is 'the rows of clouds that [hold] concealed [water]'.
