Sūkta 102 — "imāṃ te dhiyam"

ನೂರ ಎರಡನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು — nūra eraḍaneya sūktavu, "the hundred-and-second Sūkta" Kannada heading

Sāyaṇa's introduction to Sūkta 102 (Sanskrit in Kannada script; doubtful places [?]): Sense: "The ninth sūkta, of eleven Ṛks, beginning imāṃ te, is the seer-composition of Kutsa, addressed to Indra; the last [Ṛk] is Triṣṭubh, the remaining ten Jagatī. So the Anukramaṇī: 'imāṃ te; the last Triṣṭubh.' Its application is by the sign [i.e. by its fitness, not by a specific rule]."

इमां ते इत्येकादशर्चं नवमं सूक्तं कुत्सस्यार्षमैन्द्रम् । अन्त्या त्रिष्टुप् शिष्टा दश जगत्यः । तथा चानुक्रान्तम् । इमां ते ऽन्त्या त्रिष्टुबिति ॥ विनियोगो लैङ्गिकः ॥ imāṃ te ity ekādaśarcaṃ navamaṃ sūktaṃ kutsasyārṣam aindram | antyā triṣṭup śiṣṭā daśa jagatyaḥ | tathā cānukrāntam | imāṃ te 'ntyā triṣṭub iti ‖ viniyogo laiṅgikaḥ ‖

Anuvāda (Kannada): "Imāṃ te — this sūkta is the ninth sūkta in the fifteenth anuvāka. It has eleven Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Kutsa. The deity is Indra. The last Ṛk of this sūkta is in the Triṣṭubh metre; the remaining ten Ṛks are in the Jagatī metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said imāṃ te 'ntyā triṣṭub iti. Its application is laiṅgika." A printer's ornament follows.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 102.1)

हे इन्द्र महो महतस्ते तवेमामिदानीं क्रियमाणां महीं महतीमात्यन्तोत्कृष्टां धियं स्तुतिं प्रभरे । प्रकर्षेण सम्पादयामि । ते तव धिषणा त्वदीया बुद्धिरस्य मम स्तोतुः स्तोत्रे स्तुतौ यद्यस्मादानजे आक्ता संश्लिष्टासीत् । तस्मात्तव प्रियां स्तुतिं करोमीत्यर्थः । उत्तरार्धर्चः परोक्षकृतः । ससहिं शत्रूणामभिभवितारं पूर्वोक्तं तमिन्द्रं देवासः कर्मसु दीव्यन्त ऋत्विजः शवसा स्तुतिभिः कीर्तनबलेनानुमदन् । अनुक्रमेण हर्षं प्रापयन् । किमर्थम् । उत्सवे चोत्क्षेपणार्थमभिवृद्ध्यर्थं प्रसवे च धनानां वृष्ट्युदकानां वोत्पत्त्यर्थं च ॥ आनजे । अञ्जू व्यक्तिम्रक्षणकान्तिगतिषु । अस्मात्कर्मणि लिट् । ubhayatheti śapa ārdhadhātukatvāṇ ṇer aniṭīti ṇilopaḥ ‖

"O Indra! te — of you, mahaḥ — the great — I bring forth (pra bhare, 'I accomplish with force') this praise (dhiyam), now being made, mahīm — mighty, exceedingly excellent. Yat — because your dhiṣaṇā, your understanding, ānaje — has been attached, has been joined to, asya stotre — to this praise of me, the praiser, for that reason, the sense is, I make a praise dear to you. The latter half of the Ṛk is in the third person [parokṣakṛta]: tam indram — that Indra spoken of before, sasahim — the overcomer of enemies — the devāsaḥ, the priests who shine in the rites, śavasā — by their praises, by the strength of their proclaiming — anu amadan — made him glad one after another. For what purpose? For utsava — for lifting up, for increase — and for prasava — for the production of wealth or of rain-waters." The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read: ānaje (root añj 'to anoint, to shine, to go', in the Vedic liṭ passive; doubling; the ā of the reduplicative by ata ādeḥ; the augment nuṭ for a root with two consonants [Pā. Sū. 7-4-71 as read, ?]); utsave/prasave (root sū 'to impel', with ap; the locative of the purpose [Pā. Sū. 2-3-36, as read [?]]); sasahi (root ṣah with ki and the doubling as if liṭ, lengthened in the Saṃhitā by anyeṣām api dṛśyate); amadan (root mad with the causative ṇic; shortening of the penult by mitāṃ hrasvaḥ; loss of ṇi). Several rule-names and the clause on accent are clotted and marked [?].

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"indra — O Indra; te — your; dhiṣaṇā — mind; asya — this, of the praiser, which is my; stotre — in praise; yat — for which reason; ānaje — [has been] merged (with reverence); mahaḥ — of the great-souled; te — your; mahīm — extremely excellent; imāṃ dhiyam — this praise; pra bhare — I make, exceedingly; sasahim — one who conquers enemies; tam indram — that Indra; devāsaḥ — the priests who shine in the sacrificial acts; utsave ca — for their elevation; prasave ca — and for wealth such as (rain-water); śavasā — by the strength of praise; anu amadan — made glad in succession."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Indra, because your mind is merged in reverence in this my praise, which makes you glad, I make this praise, extremely excellent, and offer it to you, the great-souled. The priests who shine in the sacrificial acts, by the strength of their praise, made glad one after another that Indra who conquers enemies, for their own elevation and for wealth such as rain-water."

English Translation (as printed)

I address to you, who are mighty, this excellent hymn, because your understanding has been gratified by my praise : the gods have successively delighted that victorious Indra with the power (of praise) for the sake of prosperity and wealth.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 102.1 (Kannada)

"Dhiyam — though the word dhī is read among the thirteen names of intelligence (prajñā) (Ni. 3-[?]9 as read [?]), here the bhāṣya-author has given for this word the meaning stotra, 'praise'.

Utsave prasave — sū preraṇe: utsavārtham abhivṛddhyartham — for the sake of increase, for prosperity, or for the increase of wealth (śrī)."

original p. 316

"Sasahim — ṣaha abhibhave; śatrūṇām abhibhavitāram: one who overcomes, defeats the enemies.

Devāsaḥ — though the general sense of this word is 'deities', the bhāṣya-author here explains: karmasu dīvyanta ity devā ṛtvijaḥ — 'those who shine in the rites are devāḥ, priests': that is, since they shine, taking the chief place in the sacrificial and other acts, he has explained devāḥ or devāsaḥ as 'priests'. When Yāska gives the general sense of the word deva, he says: devo dānād vā dīpanād vā dyotanād vā dyusthāno bhavatīti vā — 'the deva is the giver, or the shining one, or the illuminating one, or the one who is in heaven': the sense is 'one who gives, who shines, or who is in heaven'. The bhāṣya-author, in the Ṛk"

स्वग्नयो हि वार्यं देवासो दधिरे च नः । svagnayo hi vāryaṃ devāso dadhire ca naḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]4-8 as read [?])

"— and in Ṛks like it, has explained the word devāsaḥ as the priests themselves: devāso dīpyamānā ṛtvijaḥ.

Śavasā — though the word śavas is read among the twenty-eight names of strength (Ni. 2-9 as read [?]), here the bhāṣya-author has given the meaning śavasā stutibhiḥ kīrtanabalena: 'by the strength that arises from doing the praise and the like'.

The first half of the Ṛk here addresses Indra directly and praises him: this kind of praise is called pratyakṣakṛta. The second half speaks of Indra generally, without address, as if he were not before us: this kind of praise is called parokṣakṛta. On this matter Yāska has explained thus —"

तद्यानि नामानि प्राधान्यस्तुतीनां देवतानां तद्दैवतमित्याचक्षते । यत्कामा ऋषिर्यस्यां देवतायामार्थपत्यमिच्छन्स्तुतिं प्रयुङ्क्ते तद्दैवतः स मन्त्रो भवति । ताः त्रिविधा ऋचः परोक्षकृताः प्रत्यक्षकृता आध्यात्मिकाश्च । तत्र परोक्षकृताः सर्वाभिर्नामविभक्तिभिर्युज्यन्ते प्रथमपुरुषैश्चाख्यातस्य । अथ प्रत्यक्षकृता मध्यमपुरुषयोगास्त्वमिति चैतेन सर्वनाम्ना । परोक्षकृताः प्रत्यक्षकृताश्च मन्त्रा भूयिष्ठा अल्पश आध्यात्मिकाः ॥ tad yāni nāmāni prādhānyastutīnāṃ devatānāṃ tad daivatam ity ācakṣate | yatkāmā ṛṣir yasyāṃ devatāyām ārthapatyam icchan stutiṃ prayuṅkte taddaivataḥ sa mantro bhavati | tāḥ trividhā ṛcaḥ parokṣakṛtāḥ pratyakṣakṛtā ādhyātmikāś ca | tatra parokṣakṛtāḥ sarvābhir nāmavibhaktibhir yujyante prathamapuruṣaiś cākhyātasya | atha pratyakṣakṛtā madhyamapuruṣayogās tvam iti caitena sarvanāmnā | parokṣakṛtāḥ pratyakṣakṛtāś ca mantrā bhūyiṣṭhā alpaśa ādhyātmikāḥ ‖ (Nirukta, Daivatakāṇḍa, adhyāya 7, khaṇḍa 1–3 [as printed: "adhyāya 7, khaṇḍa 1-3"]; the Sanskrit is given as read, some words clotted [?])

"— that is: among mantras there are many kinds, according to the sense: mantras of deities, mantras of praise, mantras of blessing, oath, curse, ... [the print lists:] śapatha, abhiśāpa, kaśmīdbhāva, paridevanā, nindā, praśaṃsā. Daivata mantra means a mantra that describes the greatness of deities; stuti means praise: a mantra that contains prayers; āśīḥ means blessing, a mantra that wishes for a good end; śapatha means a vow, abhiśāpa a curse, kaśmīdbhāva an account of an event or of the truth of a thing, paridevanā a lament, nindā blame, praśaṃsā praise, [dānastuti] and the like.

Among the many kinds mentioned above, the Ṛks that are daivata ('addressed to a deity') are of three kinds: parokṣakṛta, pratyakṣakṛta and ādhyātmika. Parokṣakṛta — since the deity who is praised is not before one, mantras that use, in praising, in the proper names and the verbs of that deity, the third person (third person both in subject and predicate — English in the original). Pratyakṣakṛta — Ṛks that praise, addressing the deity to be praised as if he were visibly present, with words such as 'you', 'your' in the second person (Second person — English in the original). Ādhyātmika — mantras that praise by using the first person (First person — English in the original). Of these three kinds of mantras, the parokṣakṛta and the pratyakṣakṛta are the more numerous; the ādhyātmika mantras are only a few. In accordance with this order, in a Ṛk of the present kind, the first half of the Ṛk is pratyakṣakṛta and the second half is parokṣakṛta." The Nirukta passage is given on p. 316 in the print and its explanation runs across the page break to p. 317; I have joined the Kannada explanation here as the print does at the head of p. 317.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 102.2) The print's wording is partly clotted; the above is the reading as given, with doubtful places marked [?]. The words of this tail: the first line completes asya (the accent of the case-ending by ūḍidam…); dyāvākṣāmā (a dvandva, with dyāvā for div, ḍā for the case-ending, and the accent of both members by devatādvandve ca); darśata (the affix tac by bhṛmṛdṛśi… [?]); sūryācandramasā (the dvandva with ānaṅ by devatādvandve ca; the accent of candramas); the prohibition of the double accent when a following member begins with an unaccented vowel; abhicakṣe (root cakṣ with kvip in the sense of the action; the dative in the sense of purpose); śraddhe (root dṛś … viś in the sense of the action); vitarturam (root tṝ 'to cross', in the intensive, with the Uṇādi kurac).

अस्येन्द्रस्य श्रवो यशः कीर्तिं सप्त इमं मे गङ्गे इत्यस्यामृचि प्राधान्येन प्रतिपादिता गङ्गाद्याः सप्तसंख्याका नद्यो बिभ्रति । धारयन्ति । वृत्रहननेनेन्द्रस्य यद्वृष्टेः प्रदातृत्वं तत्प्रभूतजलोपेता नद्यः प्रकटयन्तीत्यर्थः । अपि च द्यावाक्षामा द्यावापृथिव्यौ । पृथिवीत्यन्तरिक्षनाम । अन्तरिक्षं चास्य सूर्यात्मना वर्तमानस्येन्द्रस्य दर्शतं सर्वैः प्राणिभिर्दर्शनीयं वपुः । रूपनामैतत् । प्रकाशात्मकं रूपं धारयन्ति । किंच हे इन्द्र अस्मे अस्माकमभिचक्षे द्रष्टव्यानां पदार्थानामाभिमुख्येन प्रकाशनार्थं श्रद्धे कं श्रद्धार्थं । चक्षुषा दृष्टे हि वस्तुनीदं सत्यमिति श्रद्धोत्पद्यते । कमित्येतत्पादपूरणम् । तदुभयार्थं सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ वितर्तुरं परस्परव्यतिहारेण तरणं पुनःपुनर्गमनं यथा भवति तथा चरतः । वर्तेते । त्वमेव तद्रूपः सन्वर्तस इत्यर्थः ॥ अस्य । ऊदिदमिति विभक्ते- asyendrasya śravo yaśaḥ kīrtiṃ sapta imaṃ me gaṅge ity asyām ṛci prādhānyena pratipāditā gaṅgādyāḥ saptasaṃkhyākā nadyo bibhrati | dhārayanti | vṛtrahananendrasya yad vṛṣṭeḥ pradātṛtvaṃ tatprabhūtajalopetā nadyaḥ prakaṭayantīty arthaḥ | api ca dyāvākṣāmā dyāvāpṛthivyau | pṛthivīty antarikṣanāma | antarikṣaṃ cāsya sūryātmanā vartamānasyendrasya darśataṃ sarvaiḥ prāṇibhir darśanīyaṃ vapuḥ | rūpanāmaitat | prakāśātmakaṃ rūpaṃ dhārayanti | kiṃca he indra asme asmākam abhicakṣe draṣṭavyānāṃ padārthānām ābhimukhyena prakāśanārthaṃ śraddhe kaṃ śraddhārthaṃ | cakṣuṣā dṛṣṭe hi vastunīdaṃ satyam iti śraddhotpadyate | kam ity etat pādapūraṇam | tad ubhayārthaṃ sūryācandramasau vitarturaṃ parasparavyatihāreṇa taraṇaṃ punaḥpunargamanaṃ yathā bhavati tathā carataḥ | vartete | tvam eva tadrūpaḥ san vartasa ity arthaḥ ‖ asya | ūḍidam iti vibhakte- (the line continues on p. 320)

[…]दात्तत्वम् । द्यावाक्षामा । द्यौश्च क्षमा च । दिवो द्यावेति द्यावादेशः । सुपां सुलुगिति विभक्तेर्डादेशः । देवताद्वन्द्वे चेत्युभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । दर्शतं । भृमृदृशीत्यादिना तच् [?] । सूर्याचन्द्रमसा । सूर्यश्च चन्द्रमाश्च । देवताद्वन्द्वे चेति पूर्वपदस्यानङादेशः । सुपां सुलुगिति विभक्तेराकारः । चन्द्रमस्शब्दो दासीभारादित्वात्पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरेण मध्योदात्तः । अतो देवताद्वन्द्वे चेति प्राप्तस्योभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरस्य नोत्तरपदेऽनुदात्तादावपृथिवीति प्रतिषेधः । अभिचक्षे । चक्षिङ् प्रकाशार्थः सम्पदादिलक्षणो भावे क्विप् । तादर्थ्ये चतुर्थी । श्रद्धे । दृशिग्रहणात् धातोर्भावे विश् । चतुर्थ्येकवचन आतो धातोरित्याकारलोपः । उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । वितर्तुरं । तरतेर्यङ्लुगन्ताद् औणादिकः कुरच् । बहुलं छन्दसीत्यभ्यस्तत्वम् ॥ […]dāttatvam | dyāvākṣāmā | dyauś ca kṣamā ca | divo dyāveti dyāvādeśaḥ | supāṃ suluk iti vibhakter ḍādeśaḥ | devatādvandve cety ubhayapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | darśataṃ | bhṛmṛdṛśītyādinā tac [?] | sūryācandramasā | sūryaś ca candramāś ca | devatādvandve ceti pūrvapadasyānaḍādeśaḥ | supāṃ suluk iti vibhakter ākāraḥ | candramasśabdo dāsībhārādittvāt pūrvapadaprakṛtisvareṇa madhyodāttaḥ | ato devatādvandve ceti prāptasyobhayapadaprakṛtisvarasya notrapade 'nudāttādāv apṛthivīti pratiṣedhaḥ | abhicakṣe | cakṣiṅ prakāśārthaḥ saṃpadādilakṣaṇo bhāve kvip | tādarthye caturthī | śraddhe | dṛśigrahaṇāt dhātor bhāve viś | caturthyekavacana āto dhātor ity ākāralopaḥ | udāttanivṛttisvareṇa vibhakter udāttatvaṃ | vitarturaṃ | tarater yaṅluṅantād auṇādikaḥ kurac | bahulaṃ chandasīty abhyastatvam ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"asya — of this Indra; śravaḥ — the fame; sapta nadyaḥ — the seven rivers, Gaṅgā and the rest, too; bibhrati — make known (and carry); dyāvākṣāmā — heaven and earth; pṛthivī — the mid-air too; darśatam — [which in the form of the sun] charms all minds, becoming visible; vapuḥ — [Indra's] shining form; prakāśayanti — make manifest; indra — O Indra; asme — for us; abhicakṣe — in order that everything may become visible; śraddhe tam — and (after they have become visible) in order to produce faith in them; vitarturam — [their] eternal course, in the form of going and coming by their own movement; carataḥ — the sun and the moon and all the rest perform."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"The seven rivers, Gaṅgā and the rest, bear and make known the fame of Indra. Heaven and earth and the mid-air make manifest the form of that Indra, shining in the form of the sun, charming all minds. O Indra, so that all things may become visible to us, and so that faith may be produced in them once they have become visible, the sun, the moon and all the rest also carry out their works, going and coming in their eternal course."

English Translation (as printed)

The seven rivers display his glory ; heaven and earth, and sky display his visible form : the sun and moon, Indra, perform their revolutions, that we may see, and have faith in what we see.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 102.2 (Kannada)

"Śravaḥ — śravaḥ means fame: 'śravaś ca praśaṃsāṃ ca' [as read]: the Nirukta saying (Ni. 4-[?]2 as read [?]).

Asya śravo nadyaḥ sapta bibhrati — here 'the seven rivers' means the seven rivers named in the Ṛk imaṃ me gaṅge (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-75-5 as read [?]): Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, Śutudrī, Parūṣṇī, Asiknī and Marudvṛdhā. These seven rivers hold up the fame of Indra. That is, Indra, having pierced the clouds and checked the downpour of rain on the earth, killed Vṛtra and caused the rain-water to fall on the earth; by that water the seven rivers, Gaṅgā and the rest, fill with abundant water and flow, making manifest Indra's brave deeds, such as the slaying of Vṛtra, and so spread his fame: that is the chief intention. The matter of the slaying of Vṛtra as the cause for these rivers is supported by the Ṛks" Glosses, editorial and tentative: "The darkness, hard to cross, stood in the waters, within the bellies of Vṛtra, the mountain; Indra, the nadis fastened by the obstructor, all in the declivities he struck"; "That is the most sacrificial deed of this wonderful [god], the most beautiful of his works: when, in the recess, the four rivers, honey-streaming, he made swell".

अपामतिष्ठद्धरुणह्वरं तमोऽन्तर्वृत्रस्य जठरेषु पर्वतः । अभीमिन्द्रो नद्यो वव्रिणा हिता विश्वा अनुष्ठाः प्रवणेषु जिघ्नते ॥ apām atiṣṭhad dharuṇahvaraṃ tamo 'ntar vṛtrasya jaṭhareṣu parvataḥ | abhīm indro nadyo vavriṇā hitā viśvā anuṣṭhāḥ pravaṇeṣu jighnate ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-32-10 as read [?])

तदु प्रयक्षतममस्य कर्म दस्मस्य चारुतममस्ति दंसः । उपह्वरे यदुपरा अपिन्वन्मध्वर्णसो नद्यश्चतस्रः ॥ tad u prayakṣatamam asya karma dasmasya cārutamam asti daṃsaḥ | upahvare yad uparā apinvan madhvarṇaso nadyaś catasraḥ ‖ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-62-6 as read [?])

"— [and others] support this.

Dyāvākṣāmā — since gauḥ, gmā and the like, the first of the twenty-one names of the earth (pṛthivī), include the word kṣāmā (Ni. 1-1[?] as read [?]), dyāvākṣāmā means heaven and earth: the heavenly world and the earth.

Pṛthivī — since the word pṛthivī is read among the sixteen names of the mid-air beginning with ambara, viyat [as read, ?], pṛthivī means the mid-air. Therefore, in the words dyāvākṣāmā pṛthivī said here, the three — earth, mid-air, heaven — are meant.

Darśataṃ vapuḥ — darśanīyaṃ rūpam: 'a form fit to be seen', a beautiful form. Earth, mid-air and heaven, making manifest the beautiful form of Indra who illumines the world in the form of the sun, spread his greatness: that is the chief intention."

Special Topics of Rik 102.2, continued from p. 321 (Kannada)

"Abhicakṣe, śraddhe — since we see with the eyes, the belief arises that such things are true. Therefore, the sun and moon, which every day, rising and setting again and again, become visible to us, always appear to our eyes, so that we may directly have faith in the greatness of Indra. For us men, among the things that appear to our eyes — that is, among mountains, rivers, trees and the like — the belief arises naturally that they are true; in the worlds such as heaven, which do not appear to the eyes, there is not so much belief. Therefore the sun and moon appear to our eyes every day. Since Indra himself has established them in the mid-air, whenever we look at the sun and moon the greatness of Indra comes within the range of our memory. Though we cannot see Indra's greatness directly, by looking at the sun and moon, which are visible to us, we can easily infer and understand him: this is the chief intention.

Kam — Yāska, on this word —"

"— that is: the particles kam, īm, it, u have no fixed meaning of their own; they are used, in the lines of Ṛks that are bound by metre, to fill up one or two syllables that are wanting in the feet: so he has said.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 102.3) The print's geraya is a misprint for preraya; the word is read preraya [?].

हे मघवन् धनवन्निन्द्र सातयेऽस्माकं धनलाभाय तं स्म तमेव रथं प्राव । प्रेरय । वर्तय । नोऽस्माकं मनसा बुद्ध्या पुरुष्टुत बहुशः स्तुतेन्द्र ते तव स्वभूतं जैत्रं जयशीलं यं रथं संगमे शत्रुभिः सह संगमने आजा युद्धे सत्यनुमदाम । वयमनुक्रमेण स्तुमः । अपि च हे मघवन् त्वायद्भ्यस्त्वां कामयमानेभ्यो नोऽस्मभ्यं शर्म सुखं यच्छ । देहि ॥ अव । अव रक्षणगतिकान्तीत्यादिकत्वादवतिरत्र गत्यर्थः । संगमे । ग्रहवृदृनिश्चिगमश्च इति कर्मण्यप् । थाथादिनोत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । आजा । सुपां सुलुगिति सप्तम्या डादेशः । त्वायद्भ्यः । सुप आत्मनः क्यच् । प्रत्ययोत्तरपदयोश्चेति मपर्यन्तस्य त्वादेशः । व्यत्ययेन दकारस्यात्वम् । क्यजन्ताल्लटः शतृ । अदुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वे सति क्यचा सह्यैकादेश एकादेश उदात्तेनेति तस्योदात्तत्वम् ॥ he maghavan dhanavann indra sātaye 'smākaṃ dhanalābhāya taṃ sma tam eva rathaṃ prāva | preraya | vartaya | no 'smākaṃ manasā buddhyā puruṣṭuta bahuśaḥ stutendra te tava svabhūtaṃ jaitraṃ jayaśīlaṃ yaṃ rathaṃ saṃgame śatrubhiḥ saha saṃgamane ājā yuddhe saty anumadāma | vayam anukrameṇa stumaḥ | api ca he maghavan tvāyadbhyas tvāṃ kāmayamānebhyo no 'smabhyaṃ śarma sukhaṃ yaccha | dehi ‖ ava | ava rakṣaṇagatikāntītyādikatvād avatir atra gatyarthaḥ | saṃgame | grahavṛdṛniścigamaś ca iti karmaṇy ap | thāthādinottarapadāntodāttatvam | ājā | supāṃ suluk iti saptamyā ḍādeśaḥ | tvāyadbhyaḥ | supa ātmanaḥ kyac | pratyayottarapadayoś ceti mapayantasya tvādeśaḥ | vyatyayena dakārasyātvam | kyajantāl laṭaḥ śatṛ | adupadeśāl lasārvadhātukānudāttatve sati kyacā sahyaikādeśa ekādeśa udāttenēti tasyodāttatvam ‖

"O Maghavan, wealthy Indra! For sātaye — for our gaining of wealth — tam sma — that very chariot — prāva: send forth, set in motion. O Indra, much praised (puruṣṭuta) by our minds, by our understanding! Your own, jaitram — victorious — chariot, which, in saṃgame, in the meeting with enemies, in battle (ājā), we anumadāma — we praise in succession. And, O Maghavan, to us, tvāyadbhyaḥ — who desire you — give śarma, happiness." The grammatical tail is characterized: ava (the root av as a verb of motion here); saṃgama (ap in the sense of the object by grahavṛdṛniścigamaś ca, with the accent of the last member); ājā (the locative ending replaced by ḍā); tvāyat (denominative kyac with tva for the stem as before, then śatṛ, and the single-substitute accent).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"maghavan indra — O Indra, endowed with wealth; sātaye — (to us) for the gaining of wealth; tam sma rathaṃ — that chariot of yours; prāva — send quickly; naḥ — our; manasā — with mind (cordial); puruṣṭuta — O Indra, praised by us many times; te — your; jaitraṃ — which brings victory; yam — which chariot; saṃgame — which confronts enemies; ājā — [when] battle has come; anumadāma — we rejoice (seeing it in the field of battle); maghavan — O Indra, endowed with wealth; tvāyadbhyaḥ — to us who desire your help; naḥ — to us; śarma — happiness; yaccha — give."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Indra, endowed with wealth! Send your chariot quickly, so that we may gain wealth. We praise you many times with cordial mind. And as soon as we see, in the field of battle, your victorious chariot, which confronts the enemies when battle has come, we rejoice that victory is assured to us. O Indra, endowed with wealth, give happiness to us who desire your help."

English Translation (as printed)

Maghavan, despatch your chariot to bring us wealth ; that victorious car, which, Indra, who are much praised by us in time of war, we rejoice to behold in battle : O, Maghavan, grant happiness to those who are devoted to you.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 102.3 (Kannada)

"Sma — for the sake of the metre, the final letter of this word is lengthened in the Saṃhitā text. The word means eva, 'just': tam sma — tam eva, 'that very one'.

Pra ava — ava rakṣaṇagatikāntī…: since the root av has many senses, such as protection, [Sāyaṇa] says that here the sense of motion is to be taken. So prāva means 'send, dispatch'.

Saṃgame ājā — śatrubhiḥ saha saṃgamane ājā yuddhe: in the battle in which one meets enemies: in the battle that brings one face to face with enemies."

original p. 326

Special Topics of Rik 102.3, concluded from p. 325 (Kannada)

"Manasā puruṣṭuta — asmākaṃ buddhyā — 'with our understanding', that is, with the mind, with faith, praised many times.

Tvāyadbhyaḥ — tvāṃ kāmayamānebhyo no 'smākam: to us who desire you (Indra). This word occurs in the Ṛgveda only in this Ṛk; it is not found in the Mantras elsewhere either.

Sū. 6-4-105 as read]; since the verb stands at the beginning of the foot, the nighāta accent comes); sātaye (fixed by nipātana as acute on the last syllable by ūtiyūti… [Pā. Rik 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 102.4)

वयं जयेम त्वया युजा वृतमस्माकमंशमुदवा भरेभरे । अस्मभ्यमिन्द्र वरिवः सुगं कृधि प्र शत्रूणां मघवन्वृष्ण्या रुज ॥ ४ ॥

vayaṃ jayema tvayā yujā vṛtam asmākam aṃśam ud avā bhare-bhare | asmabhyam indra varivaḥ sugaṃ kṛdhi pra śatrūṇāṃ maghavan vṛṣṇyā ruja ‖ 4 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 102.4)

वयम् । जयेम । त्वया । युजा । वृतम् । अस्माकम् । अंशम् । उत् । अव । भरेऽभरे । अस्मभ्यम् । इन्द्र । वरिवः । सुऽगम् । कृधि । प्र । शत्रूणाम् । मघऽवन् । वृष्ण्या । रुज ॥ ४ ॥

vayam | jayema | tvayā | yujā | vṛtam | asmākam | aṃśam | ut | ava | bhare-bhare | asmabhyam | indra | varivaḥ | su-gam | kṛdhi | pra | śatrūṇām | magha-van | vṛṣṇyā | ruja ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 102.4) The print's text is read as given; kvip chandasi kvip is the print's wording, perhaps for kvip ca chandasi [?].

हे इन्द्र युजास्माभिर्युक्तेन सहायभूतेन त्वया वृतमावरणीयं शत्रुं वयं स्तोतारो जयेमु । अभिभवेम । अपि च भरेभरे संग्रामे संग्रामेऽस्माकमंशमस्मदीयं भागमुदव । शत्रुकृतपीडापरिहारेणोत्कृष्टं रक्ष । तथा हे इन्द्र वरिवो धनमस्मभ्यं सुगं सुगमनं सुप्रापं कृधि । कुरु । तथा हे मघवन् शत्रूणामस्मद्द्वेषकारिणां वृष्ण्या वृष्ण्यानि वीर्याणि प्र रुज । प्रभङ्गि । बाधस्वेत्यर्थः ॥ वृतं । वृङ् वरणे । क्विप्च्छन्दसि क्विप् । तुगागमः । सुगं । सुदुरोरधिकरण इति गमेर्डप्रत्ययः । कृधि । श्रुशृणुपृकृवृभ्य इति हेर्धिः । रुज । रुजो भङ्गे । तौदादिकः ॥ he indra yujāsmābhir yuktena sahāyabhūtena tvayā vṛtam āvaraṇīyaṃ śatruṃ vayaṃ stotāro jayemu | abhibhavema | api ca bhare-bhare saṃgrāme saṃgrāme 'smākam aṃśam asmadīyaṃ bhāgam udava | śatrukṛtapīḍāparihāreṇotkṛṣṭaṃ rakṣa | tathā he indra varivo dhanam asmabhyaṃ sugaṃ sugamanaṃ suprāpaṃ kṛdhi | kuru | tathā he maghavan śatrūṇām asmaddveṣakāriṇāṃ vṛṣṇyā vṛṣṇyāni vīryāṇi pra ruja | prabhaṅgi | bādhasvety arthaḥ ‖ vṛtam | vṛṅ varaṇe | kvip chandasi kvip | tugāgamaḥ | sugam | sudurorādhikaraṇa iti gamer ḍapratyayaḥ | kṛdhi | śruśṛṇupṛkṛvṛbhya iti herdhiḥ | ruja | rujo bhaṅge | taudādikaḥ ‖

"O Indra, we, the praisers, with you as our ally (yujā), united with us, would conquer (jayema) the enemy who is vṛtam — who is to be surrounded, [or] who besets us. And in battle after battle, udava — protect excellently — our portion, what belongs to us, by removing the oppression done by enemies. Likewise, O Indra, make varivas, wealth, sugam — easy to reach, easy to obtain — for us. And, O Maghavan, pra ruja — break, crush — the powers of the enemies who bear us hatred: oppress them, that is the sense." The grammatical tail is characterized: the form vṛta (root vṛ 'to choose, to cover', with kvip and the augment tuk); suga (root gam with ḍa when preceded by su/dur in the sense of the locus); kṛdhi (dhi for hi after śru, śṛ, pṛ, kṛ, vṛ); ruja (root ruj 'to break', of the tudādi class).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"indra — O Indra; yujā — (as our helper) joined with us; tvayā — by your help; vṛtam — [the enemy] who besets us; vayam — we (your devotees); jayema — may we conquer; bhare-bhare — in every battle; asmākam — our own; aṃśam — portion; udava — protect excellently; indra — O Indra; varivaḥ — wealth; asmabhyam — for us; sugam — easy to reach; kṛdhi — make; maghavan — O Indra, rich in wealth; śatrūṇām — of enemies; vṛṣṇyā — strengths; pra ruja — cause to be destroyed."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Indra, by your help, with you united with us, may we conquer the enemy who besets us. In every battle protect our portion so that the enemies' oppression does not reach it. O Indra, make wealth easy for us to reach. And, O Indra, rich in wealth, cause the strength of our enemies to be destroyed."

original p. 328

English Translation (as printed)

May we, having you for our ally, overcome our adversaries in every encounter ; defend our portion ; render riches easily attained by us ; enfeeble, Maghavan, the vigour of our enemies.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 102.4 (Kannada)

"Vayaṃ jayema tvayā yujā vṛtam — vṛṅ varaṇe: 'to cover, to enclose': the intention is that, by your help, we may conquer the enemy who comes and encloses us for the sake of fighting.

Asmākam aṃśam ut ava bhare bhare — protect our portion, that is, our houses and the like, our wealth, our sovereignty and other things that belong to us, so that they do not fall under the power of enemies in each battle. Since the word bhare is read twice, it suggests the sense 'in every battle'."

original p. 329

"Varivaḥ — since maghaṃ, reknaḥ and the like are read among the twenty-eight names of wealth, the word varivas is also read there (Ni. 2-[?] as read [?]): varivaḥ means wealth.

Sugaṃ kṛdhi — make wealth easy to obtain for us.

Vṛṣṇyā — heroism, or valour.

Ruja — rujo bhaṅge: 'to break': bhagnaṃ māḍu, nāśavāḍu: break, destroy: śatrūṇāṃ vṛṣṇyā pra ruja: check the valour (the pride) of the enemies: that is the intention.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 102.4)

Grammar page, noted briefly. It treats: jayema (root ji jaye; vidhiliṅ, first person plural, mas; loss of the s by nityaṃ ṅitaḥ [Pā. Sū. 3-4-99 as read]; yāsuṭ by yāsuṭ parasmaipadeṣūdātto ṅicca [Pā. Sū. 3-4-103 as read]; śap; guṇa of the root vowel; ay-substitution; iy-substitution for yās by ato yeyaḥ [Pā. Sū. 7-2-80 as read]; loss of y by lopo vyor vali [Pā. Sū. 6-1-66 as read]; nighāta); yujā (root yujir yoge; kvip by kvip ca [Pā. Sū. 3-2-76 as read]; in the instrumental, acute on the ending by sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ [Pā. Sū. 3-4-87 as read]; by śruśṛṇupṛkṛvṛbhyaś chandasi [Pā. Sū. 6-4-102 as read] the substitute dhi for hi; nighāta accent at the end of the verb)"

Rik 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 102.5)

नाना हि त्वा हवमाना जना इमे धनानां धर्तरवसा विपन्यवः । अस्माकं स्मा रथमा तिष्ठ सातये जैत्रं हीन्द्र निभृतं मनस्तव ॥ ५ ॥

nānā hi tvā havamānā janā ime dhanānāṃ dhartar avasā vipanyavaḥ | asmākaṃ smā ratham ā tiṣṭha sātaye jaitraṃ hīndra nibhṛtaṃ manas tava ‖ 5 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 102.5) The print's smākam eva is read as asmākam eva [?]; strini is the print's, perhaps ktini [?].

हे धनानां धर्तर्गोहिरण्यादिरूपाणां द्रव्याणां धारयितरिन्द्र विपन्यवः स्तोतारः । स्तोतृनामैतत् । स्तोतार इमे जना अवसा रक्षणेन हेतुना त्वा त्वां हवमाना आह्वयन्तो नाना हि । विभिन्नाः खलु । तेषां मध्येऽस्माकं स्माकमेव सातये धनदानाय रथमातिष्ठ । आरोह । हे इन्द्र निभृतमव्याकुलं तव मनश्चित्तं जैत्रं हि । जयशीलं खलु । शत्रूञ्जित्वास्मभ्यं धनं दातुं समर्थमित्यर्थः ॥ सातये । षणु दाने । स्त्रिनि जनसनखनां सन्झलोरिति आत्त्वं ॥ he dhanānāṃ dhartar gohiraṇyādirūpāṇāṃ dravyāṇāṃ dhārayitar indra vipanyavaḥ stotāraḥ | stotṛnāmaitat | stotāra ime janā avasā rakṣaṇena hetunā tvā tvāṃ havamānā āhvayanto nānā hi | vibhinnāḥ khalu | teṣāṃ madhye 'smākaṃ smākam eva sātaye dhanadānāya ratham ātiṣṭha | āroha | he indra nibhṛtam avyākulaṃ tava manaś cittaṃ jaitraṃ hi | jayaśīlaṃ khalu | śatrūñ jitvāsmabhyaṃ dhanaṃ dātuṃ samarthām ity arthaḥ ‖ sātaye | ṣaṇu dāne | strini janasanakhanāṃ sanjhaloḥ ity ātvaṃ ‖

"O dhartaḥ, upholder, bearer, of wealth in the form of cows, gold and the like! Indra! Vipanyavaḥ — praisers (this is a name for praisers); these praising people, for the sake of protection (avasā), calling you, are nānā — indeed varied, different. Among them, for our own sake, for the giving of wealth, mount your chariot, ascend. O Indra, your mind is nibhṛtam — undisturbed — jaitram — victorious, indeed: able, having conquered the enemies, to give wealth to us: that is the sense."

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"dhanānām — of wealth (in the form of cows, gold and the like); dhartaḥ — O Indra, the upholder; vipanyavaḥ — (your) devotees; ime janāḥ — these people (in the company of these people); avasā — with the object of obtaining protection; tvā — you; havamānāḥ — calling; nānā hi — are many (among them); asmākaṃ sma — for us; sātaye — for the giving of wealth; ratham — the chariot; ā tiṣṭha — mount; indra — O Indra; nibhṛtaṃ — undisturbed (smiling); tava — your; manaḥ — mind; jaitraṃ hi — is it not indeed victorious?"

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Indra, upholder of wealth in the form of cows, gold and the like! Many are those in the company of these your devotees who call you with the object of obtaining protection. Among all of them, mount your chariot in order to give wealth to us in particular. O Indra, is not your smiling mind victorious?"

English Translation (as printed)

Many are the men who call upon you for your protection : mount your car to bring wealth to us, for your mind, Indra, is composed, and resolved on victory.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 102.5 (Kannada)

"Vipanyavaḥ — since vipraḥ, ugraḥ and the like are read among the twenty-four [as read, ?] names of the wise (medhāvin), the word vipanyavaḥ is read there too (Ni. 3-[?]9 as read [?]); the sense of this word is 'intelligent'. The bhāṣya-author says 'praisers'."

original p. 332

"Nānā hi tvā havamānā janā ime vipanyavaḥ — now, gathered here, those who call you and praise you are of many kinds: that is, their wishes are of many kinds. All of them call you and praise you, each for his own protection and each for the desired object he wants.

Dhanānāṃ dhartaḥ — one who holds cows, gold and other wealth: that is, one who has them at hand in order to give them to praisers, one who holds them in his hand.

Asmākaṃ sātaye — we also are among the praising people. What we need is wealth.

Rathaṃ ā tiṣṭha — mount (and set out in) the chariot (quickly), in order to give us wealth.

Jaitraṃ hi indra nibhṛtaṃ manas tava — O Indra, your mind is undisturbed, set only on victory: that is the intention.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 102.6)

हे इन्द्र तव बाहू हस्तौ गोजिता जयेन गवां लम्भयितारौ । त्वं चामितक्रतुरपरिच्छिन्नज्ञानः सिमः श्रेष्ठः । तथा च शाट्यायनकम् । सिमु इति वै श्रेष्ठमाचक्षत इति । यद्वा । सिमः शत्रूणां बन्धकः । कर्मन्कर्मन् स्तोतॄणां कर्मणि कर्मण्युपस्थिते शतमूतिर्बहुविधरक्षणोपेतः खजंकरः । खजति मथ्नाति पुरुषानिति खजः संग्रामः । तस्य कर्ता । अकल्पः कल्पेनान्येन रहितः । स्वतन्त्र इत्यर्थः । ओजसा सर्वेषां प्राणिनां यदोजो बलमस्ति तेन सर्वेण प्रतिमानं प्रतिनिधित्वेन मीयमानः । यस्माद्देवगुणविशिष्ट इन्द्रोऽथातः कारणात्सिषासवो धनं लब्धुकामा जना वि ह्वयन्ते । विविधमाह्वयन्ति ॥ गोजिता । गा जयत इति गोजितौ । सुपां सुलुगिति विभक्तेराकारः । सिमः । षिञ् बन्धने । अस्मादौणादिको he indra tava bāhū hastau gojitā jayena gavāṃ lambhayitārau | tvaṃ cāmitakratur aparicchinnajñānaḥ simaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ | tathā ca śāṭyāyanakam | simu iti vai śreṣṭham ācakṣata iti | yadvā | simaḥ śatrūṇāṃ bandhakaḥ | karmankarman stotṝṇāṃ karmaṇi karmaṇy upasthite śatam ūtir bahuvidharakṣaṇopetaḥ khajaṅkaraḥ | khajati mathnāti puruṣān iti khajaḥ saṃgrāmaḥ | tasya kartā | akalpaḥ kalpenānyena rahitaḥ | svatantra ity arthaḥ | ojasā sarveṣāṃ prāṇinām yad ojo balam asti tena sarveṇa pratimānaṃ pratinidhitvena mīyamānaḥ | yasmād devaguṇaviśiṣṭa indro 'thātaḥ kāraṇāt siṣāsavo dhanaṃ labdhukāmā janā vi hvayante | vividham āhvayanti ‖ gojitā | gā jayata iti gojitau | supāṃ suluk iti vibhakter ākāraḥ | simaḥ | ṣiñ bandhane | asmād auṇādiko (the line continues on p. 334)

original p. 334

Characterized: the stem khajaṅkara ('maker of khaja, i.e. of war'; root khaj 'to churn', with khac and the augment mum by arurdviṣadajantasya mum, with the accent of the last member of a kṛt-ended compound); akalpa (accent of the last member by nañsubhyām); siṣāsu (root van/ṣaṇ with the desiderative san, optional absence of iṭ, with ā for the nasal and u by sanāśaṃsabhikṣa uḥ [Pā. Sū. 3-2-168, as read]).

[…]मुक् । खजंकरः । खज । मन्थे । पचाद्यच् । क्षेमप्रियमद्रेऽण् च । पा. ३-२-४४ । इति चशब्दस्यानुक्तसमुच्चयार्थत्वात् खजशब्दोपपदादपि करोतेः खच् । अरुर्द्विषदजन्तस्य मुम् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । अकल्पः । नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । सिषासवः । वन षण सम्भक्तौ । सनि सनीवन्तर्धेति विकल्पनादिडभावः । जनसनखनां सन्झलोरित्यात्त्वम् । द्विर्वचनादि । सनाशंसभिक्ष उः । पा. ३-२-१६८ । इत्युप्रत्ययः । सति शिष्टत्वादात्त्मस्यैव स्वरः शिष्यते ॥ […]muk | khajaṅkaraḥ | khaja | manthe | pacādyac | kṣemapriyamadre 'ṇ ca | Pā. 3-2-44 | iti caśabdasyāniktasamuccayārthatvāt khajaśabdopapadād api karoteḥ khac | arurdviṣadajantasya mum | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | akalpaḥ | nañsubhyām ity uttarapadāntodāttatvam | siṣāsavaḥ | vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau | sani sanīvantardheti vikalpanād iḍabhāvaḥ | janasanakhanāṃ sanjhaloḥ ity ātvam | dvirvacanādi | sanāśaṃsabhikṣa uḥ | Pā. 3-2-168 | ity upratyayaḥ | sati śiṣṭatvād ātmasyaiva svaraḥ śiṣyate ‖

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"; bāhū — your two arms; gojitā — which conquer [enemies] and win cows; amitakratuḥ — [your] knowledge is unmeasured; simaḥ — [you are] most excellent; or one who binds enemies; karman karman — in every sacrificial act; śatamūtiḥ — endowed with a hundred kinds of protection; khajaṅkaraḥ — the maker of war; akalpaḥ — independent, not subject to the control of others; indraḥ — Indra; ojasā — of the strength [of all beings]; pratimānam — the type, the standard; atha — for that very reason; siṣāsavaḥ — men who desire to obtain wealth; janāḥ — people; vi hvayante — call [Indra] in many ways."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Indra, your two arms conquer enemies and win cows. Your knowledge is unbounded. You are most excellent; you are endowed with a hundred kinds of protection in every sacrificial act; you are the maker of war; you are independent, not subject to the control of others. Indra is the standard of the strength of all beings. For that reason men who desire wealth pray to Indra and call him in many ways."

English Translation (as printed)

Your arms are the winners of cows, your wisdom is unbounded, you are most excellent, the granter of a hundred aids in every rite : the author of war, Indra is uncontrolled ; the type of strength ; therefore men, who are desirous of wealth, invoke him in various ways.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 102.6 (Kannada)

"Gojitā — śatrūṇāṃ parājayena gavāṃ lambhayitārau | gā jayata iti gojitau: the hands of Indra, who has the capacity, in battle, to defeat the enemies and win the cows that are with them."

original p. 335

"Amitakratuḥ — here the word kratu has the sense of knowledge (Ni. 4-[?]3 as read [?]): one whose knowledge is unmeasured; there is no end to Indra's knowledge anywhere: the intention is that he is exceedingly wise.

Simaḥ — ṣiñ bandhane: śreṣṭhaḥ, 'most excellent': 'the most excellent one'. This word is found in the Ṛgveda —"

तमित्पृच्छन्ति न सिमो वि पृच्छति स्वेनेव धीरो मनसा यदग्रभीत् । tam it pṛcchanti na simo vi pṛcchati svenēva dhīro manasā yad agrabhīt | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-145-1 as read [?])

सिमु उक्ष्णोऽवसृष्टाः अदन्ति स्वयं बलानि तन्वः शृणानाः । simu ukṣṇo 'vasṛṣṭāḥ adanti svayaṃ balāni tanvaḥ śṛṇānāḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-28-[?] as read [?]; the print's first word clotted [?])

यदेदयुक्त हरितः सधस्थादाद्रात्री वासस्तनुते सिमस्मै । yad edayukta haritaḥ sadhasthād ād rātrī vāsas tanute simasmai | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-115-[?] as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these. In these places the bhāṣya-author has given for the word simu the meaning 'all'. And tathā ca śāṭyāyanakam — simu iti vai śreṣṭham ācakṣata iti: 'as in the Śāṭyāyanaka, "they call the best simu"'. And yadvā simaḥ śatrūṇāṃ bandhakaḥ: 'or sima is the binder of enemies': the Śāṭyāyanins (the Sāmavedins) say that the word simu gives the sense 'most excellent'. Or, since the word sima is derived from the root ṣiñ with the sense 'to bind', the bhāṣya-author says the meaning is 'one who binds the enemies'. In this context simaḥ may also be taken as 'the most excellent among all men'.

Karman karman — in every act, in every sacrificial act; since the word karman is read twice, this means 'in every act': in the act performed by each praiser.

Khajaṅkaraḥ — khaja manthe: khajati mathnāti puruṣān iti khajaḥ saṃgrāmaḥ | tasya kartā: since the root khaj has the sense 'to churn, to oppress', khaja means the war that oppresses and harms men: khajaṅkara is the one who fights the enemies.

Akalpaḥ — kalpenānyena rahitaḥ | advitīyaḥ | svatantra ity arthaḥ: 'without any other [to compare]; without a second; independent'. Since no one is equal to him, he is without a second, or independent.

Śatamūtiḥ — bahuvidharakṣaṇopetaḥ: one who gives many kinds of protection to those who praise him. The word śata may be taken here in the sense 'many'.

Pratimānam ojasā — sarveṣāṃ prāṇinām yad ojo balam asti tena sarveṇa pratimānaṃ pratinidhitvena mīyamānaḥ: 'measured, as the representative of all the strength that there is in all living beings': whatever strength or capacity is in all beings, all of that is united in Indra" the sentence continues on p. 336

original p. 336

"[— all of that is united in Indra.] The strength of Indra alone is equal to the total strength and capacity of all living beings: that is the intention.

Siṣāsavaḥ — vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau | dhanaṃ labdhukāmāḥ: people who wish for wealth and the like.

Janā vi hvayante — vividham āhvayanti: 'they call in various ways': with praises and the like, and with the performance of sacrificial acts, they call Indra.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 102.6) grammar pages, pp. 336–337, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?]

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: gojitā (gā jayataḥ iti gojitau; the case-ending replaced by ā by supāṃ suluk… [Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 as read]); bāhū (bādhata iti bāhuḥ; the affix ku after the root bādh by ārtidṛśikamibhyaḥ… [Uṇ. Sū. 1-[?]2 as read, ?]; h for dh; final acute by the affix; dual); amitakratuḥ (amitāḥ kratavaḥ yasya saḥ; the accent of the first member by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam [Pā. Sū. 6-2-1 as read]); simaḥ (root ṣiñ bandhane; the Uṇādi affix mak; since it is kit, no guṇa; final acute by the affix); karman karman (the doubling by nityavīpsayoḥ [Pā. Sū. 8-1-4 as read]; the latter, taking the name āmreḍita, is unaccented by anudāttaṃ ca [Pā. Sū. 8-1-3 as read]; the locative ending dropped by supāṃ suluk…); khajaṅkaraḥ (root khaja manthe; ac of the pacādi class by nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ [Pā. Sū. 3-1-134 as read]; khaja; and by the ca of kṣemapriyamadre 'ṇ ca [Pā. Sū. 3-2-44 as read], which gathers what is not stated, khac after the root ḍukṛñ when khaja is the preceding word; guṇa of the root vowel because of the affix; raparatva; since it ends in a kit affix [khac is khit] the augment mum by arurdviṣadajantasya mum [Pā. Sū. 6-3-67 as read]; the form khajaṅkara; the accent of the last member by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt [Pā. Sū. 6-2-139 as read]); akalpaḥ (na vidyate kalpo yasya saḥ akalpaḥ; the accent of the last member by nañsubhyām [Pā. Sū. 6-2-172 as read])."

original p. 337

The grammar of Rik 102.6 concludes: siṣāsavaḥ (root vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau; san by dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samānakartṛkād icchāyāṃ vā [Pā. Sū. 3-1-7 as read]; no augment iṭ by sanīvantardha… [Pā. Sū. 7-2-49 as read], it being optional; ā for the nasal by janasanakhanāṃ sanjhaloḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-4-42 as read]; the doubling of the root by sanyaṅoḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-1-9 as read]; shortening in the reduplicative by hrasvaḥ [Pā. Sū. 7-4-59 as read]; i by sanyataḥ [Pā. Sū. 7-4-79 as read]; ṣ for s by ādeśapratyayayoḥ [Pā. Sū. 8-3-59 as read]; the san-ending form takes the name of a root by sanādyantā dhātavaḥ; then u by sanāśaṃsabhikṣa uḥ [Pā. Sū. 3-2-168 as read]; loss of the ā of san [i.e. of the final a] by ato lopaḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-4-48 as read]; the form siṣāsu; since the u-affix is sit-like [as printed], the accent of the stem remains; nominative plural); hvayante (root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; laṭ, third person plural; since a verb follows an indeclinable [vi], nighāta). The Rik is closed with ‖ 6 ‖ and a printed ornament.

6-4-94 | iti hrasvatvam | vācaṃyamapuraṃdarau ca | Pā. 6-3-69 | iti nipātanād am-am ‖

"O Maghavan, wealthy Indra! The śravaḥ — the food — that is given by you among the kṛṣṭiṣu — among men, the praisers — ud ririce — exceeds, is greater than, [food worth] a hundred. And more: it exceeds even what is more than a hundred. What need to say more? It exceeds even [food] in the thousands: that food given by you is inexhaustible. Furthermore, amātram — measureless, unlimited, impossible to reckon, surpassing in all qualities — you, mahī dhiṣaṇā, our great speech in the form of praise, titviṣe — makes bright, makes your qualities manifest. O puraṃdara — breaker of enemies' cities — Indra, thereafter, after the praise, you destroy the vṛtrāṇi — the enemies who obstruct." The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read: ririce (root ric in the passive liṭ); titviṣe (root tviṣ 'to shine'); jighnase (leṭ of han with the middle voice by vyatyaya, aḍāgama, loss of the penult by gamahana…, doubling, and i in the reduplicative); puraṃdara (khac after dṛ when pur precedes, by pūḥsarvayor dārisahoḥ [Pā. Sū. 3-2-41, as read]; shortening before khac; the augment am by vācaṃyamapuraṃdarau ca [Pā. Sū. 6-3-69, as read]).

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"maghavan — O Indra, rich in wealth; kṛṣṭiṣu — to men (your devotees); te — your (the one you give with your favour); śravaḥ — food; śatāt — than what a hundred people need; ut ririce — is greater; bhūyasaḥ — than even that, a number exceeding it; ut — is greater; ca — and; sahasrāt — than what a thousand people need; ut — is greater; amātraṃ — (beyond men's reckoning) tvā — you; mahī — great; dhiṣaṇā — (our) speech in the form of praise; titviṣe — makes manifest; puraṃdara — O Indra, destroyer of the cities of enemies; adha — after (our) praise; vṛtrāṇi — the enemies who obstruct; jighnase — you destroy."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Indra, rich in wealth, the food that you give with favour to your devotees among men is greater than what a hundred people need; it is greater than that, greater than the number that a thousand people need. Beyond men's reckoning, our great praise makes manifest and makes you shine. O destroyer of the cities of enemies, after our praise you destroy all our enemies by [your] extraordinary power."

original p. 339

English Translation (as printed)

The food, Maghavan, (which is to be given by you) to men, may be more than sufficient for a hundred, or for more, even, than a thousand : great praise has glorified you, who are without limit, whereupon you destroy your enemies.

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 102.7 (Kannada)

"Śravaḥ — since śravaḥ, andhaḥ, vājaḥ and the like are read among the twenty-eight names of food, śravaḥ means annam, 'food' (Ni. 2-[7?] as read [?]).

Kṛṣṭiṣu (tvayā dattaṃ yac chravastat) bhūyasaḥ sahasrāt ut ririce — the food given by Indra to men — a hundred portions, still more, even a thousand portions more — grows in plenty: that is, it does not quickly come to an end. Therefore.

Amātram — mātrāyeyattayā rahitaṃ parigaṇitum aśakyaḥ sarvair guṇair adhikam: 'of whom no measure can be made; surpassing in all qualities': one who is so many-sidedly endowed with qualities that one cannot say 'this much': greater than all. To you who are such an Indra —

Mahī dhiṣaṇā titviṣe — this great, or extensive, speech in the form of praise, which we make, makes your surpassing qualities manifest: that is, 'we praise your excellent qualities at length'.

Adha — for the sake of the metre, the final letter of this word is lengthened in the Saṃhitā text. Adha means anantaram, 'afterwards'.

Adha vṛtrāṇi jighnase puraṃdara — the prayer: 'after we have praised, destroy our enemies'.

Puraṃdara — śatrūṇāṃ purāṃ dārayitar indra: 'breaker of enemies' cities'. Concerning Indra's destroying the cities of the Dasyus, Śambara and the others —"

original p. 340

अभि सिध्मो अजिगादस्य शत्रून्वि तिग्मेन वृषभेणा पुरोऽभेत् । abhi sidhmo ajigād asya śatrūn vi tigmena vṛṣabheṇā puro 'bhet | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-33-13 as read [?])

उग्रो रयिं निरपः स्रोतसास्यजद्वि शुष्णस्य दृंहिता ऐरयत्पुरः । ugro rayiṃ nirapaḥ srotasāsyajad vi śuṣṇasya dṛṃhitā airayat puraḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-51-11 as read [?])

भिनत्पुरो नवतिमिन्द्र पूरवे दिवोदासाय महि दाशुषे नृतो वज्रेण दाशुषे नृतो । bhinat puro navatim indra pūrave divodāsāya mahi dāśuṣe nṛto vajreṇa dāśuṣe nṛto | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-130-7 as read [?])

दिवोदासाय नवतिं च नवेन्द्रः पुरो व्यैरच्छम्बरस्य । divodāsāya navatiṃ ca navendraḥ puro vy airac chambarasya | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-19-6 as read [?]; as quoted on p. 274)

पुराणि यश्चैत्ना शम्बरस्य वि नवतिं नव च देह्योऽहन् । purāṇi yaś caitnā śambarasya vi navatiṃ nava ca dehyo 'han | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-2 as read [?]; the print's second word clotted [?])

"— in many Ṛks like these, [Indra's breaking of cities] is described. The word puraṃdara is always used as an epithet of Indra —"

आलर्षि युध्म खजकृत्पुरंदर प्र गायत्रा अगासिषुः । ālarṣi yudhma khajakṛt puraṃdara pra gāyatrā agāsiṣuḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-2 as read [?])

स वृत्रहेन्द्रः कृष्णयोनीः पुरंदरो दासीरैरयद्धि । sa vṛtrahendraḥ kṛṣṇayonīḥ puraṃdaro dāsīr airayad vi | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-20-7 as read [?])

पुरंदरो वृत्रहा धृष्णुषेणः संगृभ्या न आ भरा भूरि पश्वः । puraṃdaro vṛtrahā dhṛṣṇuṣeṇaḥ saṃgṛbhyā na ā bharā bhūri paśvaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-3[?]-1[?] as read [?])

"— and in the Ṛks 3-30-[?]; 8-1-[?]; 8-6-[?]; 6-1[?]-[?]; 8-6[?]-[?]; 2-6[?]-3 and others as well, the word puraṃdara is meant as of Indra.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 102.7) grammar pages, pp. 340–341, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?]

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: ririce (root ricir virecane; liṭ in the passive; the middle-voice affix by bhāvakarmaṇoḥ [Pā. Sū. 1-3-13 as read]; third person singular, ta; eś for it by liṭas tajhayor eśirec [Pā. Sū. 3-4-81 as read]; doubling of the root; halādiśeṣa; the form ririce; since it stands at the beginning of the foot [as printed: ati…], nighāta)"

original p. 341

The grammar of Rik 102.7 continues: kṛṣṭiṣu (root kṛṣa vilekhane; ktic by ktic ktau ca saṃjñāyām [Pā. Sū. 3-3-174 as read]; ṭ for the t of the affix by the ṣṭutva rule; acute on the last syllable by the affix; locative plural); amātram (na vidyate mātrā yasya saḥ amātraḥ — 'he whose measure does not exist'; the accent of the last member by nañsubhyām [Pā. Sū. 6-2-172 as read]); titviṣe (root tviṣa dīptau; liṭ, third person singular; nighāta at the end of the verb); mahī (in the Saṃhitā, from mahatī, the loss of t by vyatyaya in the Veda); adha (the letter-interchange, tha → dha); jighnase (root han hiṃsāgatyoḥ; leṭ, second person singular; the middle voice by vyatyayo bahulam [Pā. Sū. 3-1-85 as read], se for it; aṭ by leṭo 'ḍāṭau [Pā. Sū. 3-4-94 as read]; śap replaced by śluḥ by bahulaṃ chandasi; doubling of the root by ślau [Pā. Sū. 6-1-10 as read]; halādiśeṣa; ku-to-c… kuhoś cuḥ [Pā. Sū. 7-4-62 as read]; loss of the penult a by gamahanajanakhanaghasāṃ lopaḥ kṅity anaṅi [Pā. Sū. 6-4-98 as read]; i for the a of the reduplicative by abhyāsāc ca [Pā. Sū. 7-3-55 as read]; nighāta); puraṃdara (root dṝ vidāraṇe; khac by pūḥsarvayor dārisahoḥ [Pā. Sū. 6-3-69 as read] the augment am is made by nipātana; in the vocative, the nighāta by āmantritasya ca [Pā. Sū. 8-1-19 as read]). The Rik is closed with ‖ 7 ‖ and a rule of dashes. ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 102.8)

त्रिविष्टिधातु प्रतिमानमोजसस्तिस्रो भूमीर्नृपते त्रीणि रोचना । अतीदं विश्वं भुवनं ववक्षिथाशत्रुरिन्द्र जनुषा सनादसि ॥ ८ ॥

triviṣṭidhātu pratimānam ojasas tisro bhūmīr nṛpate trīṇi rocanā | atīdaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ vavakṣithāśatrur indra januṣā sanād asi ‖ 8 ‖

त्रिविष्टिऽधातु । प्रतिऽमानम् । ओजसः । तिस्रः । भूमीः । नृऽपते । त्रीणि । रोचना । अति । इदम् । विश्वम् । भुवनम् । ववक्षिथ । अशत्रुः । इन्द्र । जनुषा । सनात् । असि ॥ ८ ॥

triviṣṭi-dhātu | prati-mānam | ojasaḥ | tisraḥ | bhūmīḥ | nṛ-pate | trīṇi | rocanā | ati | idam | viśvam | bhuvanam | vavakṣitha | aśatruḥ | indra | januṣā | sanāt | asi ‖ 8 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 102.8) The print's astrīn in the first clause stands for tisras trīn or the like; read tīn lokān [?]; and divyādiśākhyam is the print's reading of a clotted phrase [?].

हे नृपते नृणां पालयितरिन्द्र त्वमोजसः सर्वेषां प्राणिनां बलस्य प्रतिमानं प्रतिधिरसि । कीदृशं प्रतिमानम् । त्रिविष्टिधातु । धातुशब्दो रज्जुभागवचनः । यथा त्रिधातु पञ्चधातु वा शुल्वं करोतीति । यथा त्रिविष्टिस्त्रिगुणिता रज्जुर्दृढीयसी एवमिन्द्रोऽपि दृढतर इत्यर्थः । किंच त्वं तिस्रो भूमीरस्त्रीन् लोकान् त्रीणि रोचना त्रीणि तेजांसि दिव्यादिशाख्यमन्तरिक्षे वैद्युतरूपमग्निं पृथिव्यामाहवनीयादिरूपेण वर्तमानं पार्थिवमग्निं एवं त्रीन् लोकान् त्रीणि तेजांसि चाति ववक्षिथ । अतिशयेन वोढुमिच्छसि । अपि चेदं विश्वं सर्वं भुवनं भूतजातं चातिवोढुमिच्छसि । सर्वस्य जगतः पालनेन त्वमेव सर्वेषां निर्वाहको भवसीत्यर्थः । यस्माद्धे इन्द्र त्वं सनाच्चिरकालादारभ्य जनुषा जन्मना जन्मप्रभृत्यशत्रुः सपत्नरहितोऽसि ॥ त्रिविष्टिधातु । त्रिधा त्रिप्रकारेण विष्टया प्रवेशनेन विधीयते क्रियते इति त्रिविष्टिधातुस्त्रिगुणिता रज्जुः । विश प्रवेशने । स्त्रियां क्तिन् । ... [see p. 343] he nṛpate nṛṇāṃ pālayitar indra tvam ojasaḥ sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ balasya pratimānaṃ pratidhir asi | kīdṛśaṃ pratimānam | triviṣṭidhātu | dhātuśabdo rajjubhāgavacanaḥ | yathā tridhātu pañcadhātu vā śulvaṃ karotīti | yathā triviṣṭis triguṇitā rajjur dṛḍhīyasī evam indro 'pi dṛḍhatara ity arthaḥ | kiṃca tvaṃ tisro bhūmīr astrīn lokān trīṇi rocanā trīṇi tejāṃsi divyādiśākhyam antarikṣe vaidyutarūpam agniṃ pṛthivyām āhavanīyādirūpeṇa vartamānaṃ pārthivam agniṃ evaṃ trīn lokān trīṇi tejāṃsi cāti vavakṣitha | atiśayena voḍhum icchasi | api cedaṃ viśvaṃ sarvaṃ bhuvanaṃ bhūtajātaṃ cātivoḍhum icchasi | sarvasya jagataḥ pālanena tvam eva sarveṣāṃ nirvāhako bhavasīty arthaḥ | yasmāddhe indra tvaṃ sanāc cirakālād ārabhya januṣā janmanā janmaprabhṛty aśatruḥ sapatnarahito 'si ‖ triviṣṭidhātu | tridhā triprakāreṇa viṣṭyā praveśanena vidhīyate kriyate iti triviṣṭidhātus triguṇitā rajjuḥ | viśa praveśane | striyāṃ ktin | …

"O nṛpate — protector of men — Indra! You are the pratimāna, the counterpart, the representative, of the strength (ojas) of all living beings. What kind of counterpart? Triviṣṭidhātu: the word dhātu means a strand of a rope; as in 'he makes a three-stranded, five-stranded cord'. As a triviṣṭi — a rope of three strands — is the stronger, so Indra too is stronger: that is the sense. And more: you ati vavakṣitha — desire to bear exceedingly — tisro bhūmīḥ, the three worlds, trīṇi rocanā, the three lights: the fire in the form of lightning in the mid-air, the earthly fire existing on the earth in the form of the āhavanīya and the rest, [and the sun in heaven] — thus the three worlds and the three lights. And you desire to bear this whole world, all beings. By protecting the whole world, you alone are the sustainer of all. For, Indra, from of old (sanāt), by birth (januṣā), from your birth on, you are aśatru — without a rival."

original p. 343

Bhāṣya's grammatical tail of Rik 102.8, concluded (characterized; clotted in places) It treats: triviṣṭidhātu (root viś 'to enter', with ktin in the feminine, 'a thing made by entering', the threefold-twisted rope; the accent of the last member of a kṛt-ended compound); tisraḥ (the substitute tisṛ for tri in the feminine, and the acute on the first part by the rule on ṛ in the middle); vavakṣitha (root vah 'to carry', with the desiderative san and the middle-voice affix; no augment by the rule on the Veda); and januṣā (root jan, the Uṇādi usi). The Sanskrit of this tail is clotted in the print and is given in outline only [?].

॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)

"nṛpate — O Indra, protector of men; (tvam — you); triviṣṭidhātu — like a rope of three strands, strong; ojasaḥ — also of the strength [of all men]; pratimānam — you are the type, the counterpart; (and besides) tisraḥ bhūmīḥ — the three worlds, also; trīṇi rocanā — (the sun, lightning, and fire in the form of āhavanīya, etc.) these three lights, also; ati vavakṣitha — you desire to bear exceedingly (you are able); idaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanam — all this world of beings also (you are able to bear); indra — O Indra; (tvam — you); januṣā sanāt — from birth, always (for a very long time) [sanāt januṣā — from before your birth, for a very long time]; aśatruḥ — without enemies; asi — you are."

॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)

"O Indra, protector of men! As a rope woven of three strands is strong, so you are the counterpart of the strength of all men. And you desire to bear exceedingly the three worlds and the three lights, and you are able. You are able to bear together all this world of beings. O Indra, from your birth, and for a very long time, you are without an enemy who competes with you."

English Translation (as printed)

Strong as a thrice-twisted rope, you are the type of strength ; protector of men, that are more than able to sustain the three spheres, the three luminaries, and all this world of beings, Indra, who have from birth ever been without a rival.

original p. 344

॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 102.8 (Kannada)

"Idam uktaṃ bhavati — [Sāyaṇa:] sakalalokeṣu eteṣv ime ca bhuvane yatra sarveṣāṃ vastūnāṃ balam asti tasya triguṇaṃ balaṃ tvayi bhavatīti bhāvaḥ | imāś ca ye lokās tebhyaḥ sarvebhyo 'pi tvaṃ mahīyān bhavasi | ataḥ kāraṇān na ko 'pi tava śatruḥ kvāpi bhavatīti ca: that is: in all the worlds, in these worlds, in all things and in all living beings and men, whatever strength and capacity there is, thrice that is in you, Indra; you are greater than all these worlds. Therefore you have no enemy anywhere, ever: that is the intention.

Triviṣṭidhātu — dhātuśabdo rajjubhāgavacanaḥ | tridhā triprakāreṇa viṣṭyā praveśanena vidhīyate kriyata iti triviṣṭidhātus triguṇitā rajjuḥ | yathā tridhātu pañcadhātu vā śulvaṃ karotīti | yathā triviṣṭis triguṇitā rajjur dṛḍhīyasī evam indro 'pi dṛḍhatara ity arthaḥ: here the word dhātu must be understood to mean 'rope' — 'cord'. Tridhātu: three separate strands are joined, and each of them is twisted together into one strand to make one cord; to make a rope, two or three such thin strands are twisted into one cord; and then three such twisted strands [of a hundred-fold? as read [?]], as before, are twisted into a stronger rope; and, further, for a still stronger and more lasting rope, three such twisted strands are joined and twisted again. A rope so made is very strong: so Indra is endowed with great strength: that is the sense. Here there is a special point in the offering of a three-strand-twisted rope as a comparison to Indra's strength. In this very Ṛk, the words tisro bhūmīḥ and trīṇi rocanā — as in a rope with three strands, one strand pervades the others in whatever way — in the same way Indra's strength and capacity pervade tisro bhūmīḥ — the three worlds, earth, mid-air and heaven — and trīṇi rocanā — shining through the three kinds of fire.

Pratimānam ojasaḥ — Indra's strength is the representative of the strength that is in all beings: the intention is that it is equal to the sum (the whole) of the strength [of all].

Tisro bhūmīḥ — traya ime lokāḥ | dyauś ca pṛthivī cāntarikṣaṃ ca: the three worlds, earth, mid-air and heaven. The words tisro bhūmīḥ, which indicate the three worlds —"

तिस्रो भूमीर्धारयन्त्रीरुत द्यून्त्रीणि व्रता विदथे अन्तरेषाम् । tisro bhūmīr dhārayan trīr uta dyūn trīṇi vratā vidathe antar eṣām | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-27-8 as read [?])

original p. 345

तिस्रो द्यावो निहिता अन्तरस्मिन्तिस्रो भूमीरुपराः षड्विधानाः । tisro dyāvo nihitā antar asmin tisro bhūmīr uparāḥ ṣaḍvidhānāḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]4-[?] as read [?])

यस्य श्वेता विचक्षणा तिस्रो भूमीरधिक्षितः । yasya śvetā vicakṣaṇā tisro bhūmīr adhikṣitaḥ | (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?] as read [?])

"— occur in Ṛks like these.

Trīṇi rocanā — trīṇi tejāṃsi | divyādiśākhyam antarikṣe vaidyutarūpam agniṃ pṛthivyām āhavanīyādirūpeṇa vartamānaṃ pārthivam agniṃ: the three lights: the light in the form of the sun in heaven (in the sky), the light in the form of lightning in the mid-air, and the light in the form of fire — the āhavanīya and the rest — on the earth: these three kinds of light. Or: the three circles of light.

Ati idaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ vavakṣitha — the whole movable world that has the form of the worlds said above — earth, mid-air, heaven — and all beings, the three kinds of luminaries, sun, lightning and fire: you, Indra, you protect and hold up all with your strength and capacity: that is the intention.

Aśatruḥ indraḥ januṣā sanāt asi — O Indra, since your birth you have never had a rival, anywhere. Here 'enemy' means one who stands against you, who fights you with strength. Such a mighty enemy of yours did not exist, does not exist now, and will not exist hereafter: you have unrivalled valour: that is the intention.

॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 102.8) grammar pages, begun on p. 345, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?]

Grammar page, noted briefly.
